# Appendix E — Assumptions baked into tests and fixtures: all 114 findings
Eight readers by slice + an UNCONFIRMED hunter + a FakeDesk-fidelity audit; two skeptical verifiers per finding. Sorted by consensus severity; the two refuted items are at the end. 'Offline test' names the failing test the finder committed in its worktree (provenance only).

## E1. [high] (cfs-detector-fixtures, confirmed) Nobody touches the bus while ring_out runs: CFS tracks the master from its OWN writes (ses.master_db) and writes absolute levels, so the operator's fader or mute is never re-read after preflight.

**Encoded at:** tests/integration/test_cfs.py:319-358 (test_ring_out_closed_loop: no fset() during the run; asserts the fader writes are the monotone -19..-6 sequence); FakeDesk never moves a fader by itself; preflight checks mute/master once (src/x32mcp/provision.py:635-649).

**Code depends on it at:** src/x32mcp/cfs.py:1174 (nxt = ses.master_db + step), :1194-1195 (ses.master_db = after, where `after` is the REQUESTED value - desk.py:955-975 returns written=after, not a read-back, despite the comment at cfs.py:1186), :1280-1283 (BACKOFF final = ses.master_db - back, written with force=True 'lowering is always safe'), :1267-1273; no re-read of mix/on anywhere in _run_ringout.

**Reality:** The first thing a human does when a wedge howls is grab its master (or hit MUTE). HANDOVER §4a: Jim drives the desk from the panel/X32-Edit during tests; DESIGN/README: feedback_watch and ring_out run at soundcheck with an engineer at the desk. A muted bus opens the loop (research fx_routing_scenes.md §4 tap semantics: RTA post-EQ tap is pre-fader/pre-mute), so the detector sees 'no feedback' while muted.

**On a real desk:** Operator yanks Bus 1 from -13 to -60 (or -oo) to stop a howl; 1.5 s later CFS writes -12 (a +48 dB jump on the wedge, straight back past the howl point), then -11 ... and finally 'backs off' to target-3 with force=True. If the operator mutes instead, CFS raises blind to the target, reports DONE, and the un-mute lands 10-20 dB above the feedback onset. Verified offline: writes after the pull were [-13,-12,...,-6,-9], final_stage DONE (worktree test below).

**Offline test:** $SP/worktrees/assumptions-cfs-detector-fixtures/tests/integration/test_assumptions_cfs.py::test_operator_pulls_master_down_mid_ringout_is_not_overridden (FAILS today): fakedesk.set_value('/bus/01/mix/fader', -60) on a RAISE stage, assert no later fader write exceeds -60+step. Fix direction: _move_level already reads `before` (desk.py:991) - compare res['before_db'] with ses.master_db (and re-read mix/on) before every raise/backoff; abort without writing if they differ by > one report grid.

> **Verifier 1: CONFIRMED (high)** — Code citations check out exactly. cfs.py:1174 computes the next raise as `min(ses.master_db + ses.step_db, target)` from CFS's own bookkeeping; cfs.py:1194-1195 then sets `ses.master_db = after`, and `after` comes from `_write_master` (cfs.py:1114-1124) which returns `res["after_db"]`. In desk.py `_move_level` (948-978) `written = after if not superseded else ...` where `after` is `policy.clamp_level(...)` of the REQUEST (line 970), so `after_db` is the requested/clamped value, not a read-back — the comment at cfs.py:1186-1187 ('``after`` is the read-back rounded to the 0.1 dB report grid') is false. `superseded` only means another ramp task from this same Desk cancelled it (desk.py:897-921), not an external move. `set_level` does fetch `before` via `_leaf` (desk.py:991) and returns it as `before_db`, but CFS never looks at it. BACKOFF (cfs.py:1280-1283) writes `ses.master_db - back` absolute with force=True. CfsManager subscribes only to `connection.state` (cfs.py:522) and RTA frames; nothing in _run_ringout re-reads mix/fader or mix/on. Preflight reads master/mute exactly once (provision.py:631-645). There is no relative guard on the write path: policy.clamp_level (policy.py:254-273) is ceiling/floor only, check_relative is only called from adjust_level, Desk._write has no relative check, and the explicit comment in _move_level says the relative guard was removed from absolute moves on 2026-09-20. `_write_master` passes ramp_ms=0 and policy.ramp_steps returns `[end]` for ms<=0, so the re-raise is a single instantaneous write.

Test-side: test_ring_out_closed_loop (tests/integration/test_cfs.py:319-358) never touches the desk during the run and asserts the fader writes are exactly the monotone -19..-6 sequence plus a -9 backoff; no test in test_cfs.py perturbs the bus fader or mute mid-run (the only mix/on manipulation is in the preflight test at 191-196).

Repro verified: ran $SP/worktrees/assumptions-cfs-detector-fixtures/tests/integration/test_assumptions_cfs.py::test_operator_pulls_master_down_mid_ringout_is_not_overridden — FAILS at HEAD-equivalent code with writes after the pull = [-13.0, -12.0, -11.0, -10.0, -9.0, -8.0, ... -6.0, -9.0], final_stage 'DONE', desk fader ends at -9.0 after the operator set -60. Each of those is a +47..+54 dB instantaneous jump on the wedge.

Reality citations: HANDOVER §4a literally says Jim 'watches the front panel / X32-Edit and confirms' (the finding's 'drives' is a slight overstatement), but §4b directly records the operator moving the master by hand during the live CFS session ('he pushed the master higher, the next band up rang'). README 'Concurrent operators' (README.md:891-893) explicitly promises X32-Edit/front panel may be used at the same time, and README:784-787 says 'Emergency actions never go through the conversational path' — i.e. the designed emergency response IS a physical fader grab/mute, which ring_out then overrides. The fx_routing_scenes.md §4 citation is imprecise (§4.7 documents output-tap +M mute semantics, not the RTA tap), but the mute-case conclusion does not depend on it: a muted bus has no acoustic loop, so no ring can grow, the detector sees nothing, and CFS raises blind to the target and reports DONE at target-3 with no notches; un-muting lands there.

No fallback or mitigation was missed: cfs.stop() exists but is the conversational path the README says emergencies bypass; the 'master clamped' branch (cfs.py:1190-1193) compares against the requested value and can never fire on an external move. Severity high is justified: a wrong, un-ramped, safety-relevant write (+48 dB into a monitor wedge straight back past the howl point) that the suite certifies as correct.

> **Verifier 2: CONFIRMED (high)** — The assumption is real, encoded exactly where the finder says, and reproduces. _run_ringout (src/x32mcp/cfs.py:1146-1199) integrates the bus master purely from its own writes: nxt = min(ses.master_db + step, target) (cfs.py:1174), then ses.master_db = after (cfs.py:1194) where `after` comes from _write_master -> Desk.set_level -> _move_level, which returns written = the REQUESTED/clamped value, not a read-back (desk.py:970-974; the cfs.py:1186 comment 'after is the read-back' is false). _finalize_levels writes final = ses.master_db - back with force=True on the premise 'lowering is always safe' (cfs.py:1280-1283, _write_master docstring cfs.py:1116-1118) — but it is only 'lowering' relative to CFS's belief, not the desk. Nothing in _run_ringout re-reads mix/fader or mix/on; CfsManager subscribes only to connection.state and RTA frames (cfs.py:522, 920). Every write uses ramp_ms=0 -> policy.ramp_steps returns [to_db] (policy.py:439-440), i.e. an instantaneous absolute jump. The only ring_out integration test (tests/integration/test_cfs.py:319-358) never touches the fader mid-run and asserts the monotone -19..-6 then -9 sequence. I ran the finder's probe (worktree assumptions-cfs-detector-fixtures, tests/integration/test_assumptions_cfs.py::test_operator_pulls_master_down_mid_ringout_is_not_overridden): after the simulated operator pull to -60 dB the desk.write stream was [-13,-12,-11,-10,-9,-8,...,-6] then back-off -9, final_stage DONE, desk fader ends at -9.0 — a +47..+54 dB instantaneous re-raise of a wedge the human just pulled down.

Skeptical checks that did NOT rescue it: (1) The FakeDesk is not the culprit — FakeDesk.set() already models a front-panel move with /xremote push (fakedesk.py:432-442) and Desk invalidates its cache on push (desk.py:232, 282-284), so set_level's `before` read WOULD show the operator's -60; CFS simply never compares res['before_db'] with ses.master_db. The information to detect the conflict is already in hand and discarded, so this is not theoretical. (2) No documented 'hands off the master' contract mitigates it: the Tier-2 confirmation summary (server.py:1764-1770) and README §CFS only say 'Nobody may play or sing during the run'; README:741-743 itself states the human reflex to a ring is 'the fader, the mute or X32-Edit'. The only documented manual abort is feedback_watch_stop() (GIG_CHECKLIST.md:254) — an LLM tool round-trip of many seconds, useless against a howl, so the fader/mute IS the realistic abort at a gig. (3) HANDOVER §4b shows Jim drives the master by hand during live CFS tests and that a notch/verify cycle can leave a ring howling for seconds (up to 3 deepen x 1.5 s verify before ABORT) — exactly when an engineer grabs the fader. (4) The detector re-catching the ring afterwards does not undo the hazard: VERIFY passes falsely while the operator holds the fader down (acoustic loop broken by the fader, not the -3 dB notch), CFS marks the ring 'tamed', then slams the master back to howl-level+1 with no ramp; the mute variant climbs blind to target, reports DONE, and the un-mute lands at a level never ring-tested. The report's start/peak/end figures are CFS beliefs, not desk state. ring_out has not yet been run live (M7 was feedback_watch), so this is the next real-desk defect waiting.

Severity high per the rubric: a wrong absolute write derived from stale belief about desk state, on the one tool whose job is to push a live wedge toward feedback, overriding a human safety action, forced past show-mode clamps on the 'back-off'. Fix is cheap (compare before_db / re-read mix/on before each RAISE/BACKOFF; abort without writing, or never write above the observed level).

## E2. [high] (cfs-detector-fixtures, confirmed) The GEQ only changes through CFS: 'cuts only, never shallower' is validated against the controller's cached gains (preflight snapshot + own writes), never against the desk, and set_geq_band writes without reading.

**Encoded at:** tests/test_detector.py:364-370 (validate_cut stand-in fed the controller's own `current`), tests/integration/test_cfs.py:240-296 (nobody touches /fx/5/par during the watch); FakeDesk GEQ pars only change via OSC.

**Code depends on it at:** src/x32mcp/cfs.py:401-416 (_DeskGeqWriter.gains seeded from `existing`, validate_notch(self.gains.get(band,0), new)), :886-889 (existing read ONCE at preflight), src/x32mcp/detector.py:567-571 (_apply: current = self._gains), src/x32mcp/policy.py:405-416 (validate_notch trusts caller's current_db), src/x32mcp/desk.py:1403-1431 (set_geq_band: no read-before-write).

**Reality:** feedback_watch is armed during soundcheck while the engineer works the same monitor GEQ by hand (that is what the GEQ-on-insert is for); ring_out sessions last minutes after the preflight read. REVIEW_BRIEF §3 asks exactly 'can CFS² be induced to boost?'.

**On a real desk:** Engineer pulls 2.5 kHz to -12 dB on the console after CFS cut it to -3; the ring persists; CFS 'deepens' -3 -> -6 and writes -6 dB over the engineer's -12: a +6 dB BOOST on the wire into the band that is ringing, with policy reporting nothing. Verified offline: fakedesk par/22 ended at -6.0 after being set to -12 (test fails with 'a boost of +6.0 dB'). Conversely a band the engineer reset to 0 is jumped to -9 in one write.

**Offline test:** …/test_assumptions_cfs.py::test_engineer_deepens_a_geq_band_by_hand_cfs_must_not_boost_it (FAILS today). Fix direction: _DeskGeqWriter.set_band_gain reads the par (Desk.get_geq bands or a leaf GET, cache invalidated by the /xremote push) and validates against min(cached, desk); NotchController.plan should be re-seeded from the read value.

> **Verifier 1: CONFIRMED (high)** — All citations check out and there is no fallback. (1) src/x32mcp/cfs.py:398-416: _DeskGeqWriter seeds self.gains = dict(existing) and set_band_gain calls policy.validate_notch(self.gains.get(band, 0.0), gain_db) then desk.set_geq_band — the 'current' value is the controller's own shadow, never the desk. (2) cfs.py:886-889: `existing` is built once from pf.geq.bands_db (the preflight read) and handed to both NotchController and _DeskGeqWriter; grep of cfs.py shows no later get_geq/bands_db read, no on_update subscription, no reseed during WATCH or ring_out. (3) detector.py:567-571: _apply computes new = max(notch_max_db, self._gains[band] + step) from the same shadow. (4) policy.py:405-422: validate_notch only compares new_db against the caller-supplied current_db (its own docstring/message says 'raising a band … is a boost; CFS² only deepens cuts', so the design intent is on-the-wire monotonic deepening). (5) desk.py:1403-1431 set_geq_band reads the /fx/N section only for the type, computes raw=(dB+15)/30 and _write()s; desk.py:871-884 _write has no read-before-write. Desk._on_push (desk.py:282) invalidates the read cache on /xremote pushes, but CFS never consults that cache after arming, so a console/X32-Edit edit of /fx/5/par/NN is invisible to it — contrary to DESIGN.md §0 item 6 'Desk is the source of truth'. Tests encode the assumption exactly as claimed: tests/test_detector.py:364-369 validate_cut is fed the controller's own current; tests/integration/test_cfs.py:240-296 nobody touches /fx/5/par during the watch. REVIEW_BRIEF.md §3 (line 123) does ask 'Can it be induced to boost'; BRIEF.md:80 defines feedback_watch as the mode where the 'human drives gain', i.e. concurrent operator activity on the same bus is the designed use case, and hand-cutting the wedge GEQ during ringing is standard practice. Reproduced against unmodified src (worktree assumptions-cfs-detector-fixtures has no src diff vs a408a2a): the probe test fails with 'CFS wrote -6.0 dB over the engineer's -12 dB (a boost of +6.0 dB)' — CFS raised a ringing band on a monitor wedge by 6 dB (up to +9 dB possible, e.g. engineer at -12, shadow at 0 → writes -3) while policy reported nothing. That is a wrong autonomous write into the band that is feeding back — the rubric's 'high'. The converse (engineer resets to 0, CFS jumps it to -9 in one write, and reports/validate_ringout_eqs then describe cuts that do not match what happened) is the medium-grade tail of the same defect.

> **Verifier 2: CONFIRMED (high)** — Reproduced and traced. The 'cuts only, never shallower' invariant is enforced against session-long shadow state, never the desk. _open_session (src/x32mcp/cfs.py:886-889) reads the GEQ bands ONCE from the preflight and seeds both NotchController._gains (detector.py:528-534) and _DeskGeqWriter.gains (cfs.py:407); every later notch is planned as current=self._gains.get(band) + step (detector.py:567-569) and validated by policy.validate_notch(self.gains.get(band,0), new) (cfs.py:413 -> policy.py:405-416, which trusts the caller's current_db); Desk.set_geq_band -> Desk._write (desk.py:1403-1431, 871-884) writes the absolute par with no read-before-write and no relative check. Nothing retires that shadow state: CfsManager subscribes only to connection.state and frames (cfs.py:522, 920); Desk._on_push (desk.py:282) invalidates the Desk read cache on /xremote pushes but the writer never consults the Desk cache. So any console-side change to the ring-out GEQ during an armed session is invisible to CFS and is overwritten by an absolute value computed from stale numbers.

Skeptic's case considered and rejected: (1) 'the engineer would not touch that GEQ' — an X32 mix bus has exactly one insert point, so the GEQ CFS inserts IS the wedge GEQ; 'GEQ on faders' is the standard monitor-engineer reflex, and feedback_watch is explicitly the mode where the human drives the wedge during soundcheck (README:234, 710) and is even allowed in show mode (GIG_CHECKLIST.md:274). (2) 'the written value is still ≤ −3 dB absolute, so never a boost above flat' — the hazard policy exists to prevent is raising gain at a frequency that is ringing; writing −6 over the engineer's −12 (or −3 over −15 on a band untouched at preflight: +12 dB) does exactly that, at the instant the detector has just confirmed the band is ringing, on a live wedge/IEM, and policy raises nothing. (3) 'already mitigated by the 2 s cache / xremote' — README principle 5 (README.md:137-139) promises no shadow state beyond the 2 s cache; this is minutes-long shadow state outside it, so the finding also contradicts the project's own contract. (4) Research does not excuse it: transport.md §4 (CONFIRMED) says console parameter changes are pushed to /xremote clients, so the real desk both permits and announces the hand edit; the FakeDesk simply never had anyone touch /fx/5/par during a test (test_cfs.py:240-296), and the unit test feeds validate_cut the controller's own `current` (test_detector.py:364-370).

Real-gig failure: feedback_watch on a wedge; ring at 2.5 kHz; CFS cuts band 22 to −3; still rings, engineer pulls band 22 to −12 on GEQ-on-faders; engineer raises the master further (the point of the mode); 2.5 kHz re-rings; CFS 'deepens' −3→−6 and writes 0.3 to /fx/5/par/22: +6 dB into the ringing band → howl in the performer's wedge, report/notch log claims a 3 dB deepening, policy silent. Subsequent deepen caps at −9, permanently 3 dB shallower than the engineer set, and CFS then 'cannot deepen' (ring_out: ABORT). REVIEW_BRIEF §3 (line 123-127) names 'can CFS² be induced to boost' as the highest-value class ('the part that protects someone's hearing'). Rubric: wrong write + safety → high; no downgrade warranted because there is no mitigation on any path and the trigger is an ordinary operator action, not an adversarial one.

Offline test exists and fails today: worktree assumptions-cfs-detector-fixtures, tests/integration/test_assumptions_cfs.py::test_engineer_deepens_a_geq_band_by_hand_cfs_must_not_boost_it → 'CFS wrote -6.0 dB over the engineer's -12 dB (a boost of +6.0 dB)'. Fix direction is sound: read the par (leaf GET ≈ one RTT, or Desk cache kept fresh by /xremote) in _DeskGeqWriter.set_band_gain and validate/plan against min(cached, desk); re-seed NotchController from the read; optionally treat an external change to the session's GEQ as a reason to pause/abort.

## E3. [high] (cfs-detector-fixtures, confirmed) The RTA source, once written at arm time, is applied and stays on the bus for the whole session; a failed /-stat/rtasource read-back is informational.

**Encoded at:** src/x32mcp/fakedesk.py:1094-1101 (_mirror_rta_stat: instant, unconditional mirror), tests/integration/test_cfs.py:252 (asserts res['rta']['verified'] and 146); no test changes /-prefs/rta/source, presses solo, or changes the console screen mid-session.

**Code depends on it at:** src/x32mcp/meters.py:926-941 (mismatch after 2 reads is only log.warning; result.verified=False), src/x32mcp/cfs.py:910-917,928-929 (_arm proceeds and merely publishes rta_verified), no re-read of /-stat/rtasource anywhere in cfs.py (grep), no /-stat/screen/METER/page write (meters.md §5.3 'safe practice') anywhere.

**Reality:** meters.md §5.3: /meters/15 is 'simply the console's RTA, whatever it is currently analysing'; encoder 6 on the METERS/RTA page, X32-Edit, Solo Priority (bit 5 can be re-ticked on the panel), and possibly the displayed PEQ/GEQ page (UNCONFIRMED) all change it; §6.15 /-stat/rtasource may be stale after a console reset; whether /-prefs/rta/source alone switches the live analyser vs /-action/setrtasrc is UNCONFIRMED - code depends on it with no fallback beyond a warning.

**On a real desk:** Someone presses an RTA encoder or solos a channel while ring_out raises a wedge: the detector now analyses Ch01/the solo bus, sees nothing, and CFS raises the wedge master to the target blind and reports DONE. Verified offline: /-prefs/rta/source set to 2 on the first RAISE -> desk stat=98 (Ch01 post), report DONE at -6 from -19 with no abort.

**Offline test:** …/test_assumptions_cfs.py::test_rta_source_hijacked_mid_ringout_stops_the_raise (FAILS today). Make _arm refuse when verified is False (with an /-action/setrtasrc retry), subscribe to /-stat/rtasource pushes (conn.on_update) and HOLD/ABORT on change, re-clear Solo Priority, and force /-stat/screen to METER/RTA per meters.md §5.3.

> **Verifier 1: CONFIRMED (high)** — All citations check out. (1) Fake: src/x32mcp/fakedesk.py:1094-1101 `_mirror_rta_stat` mirrors /-prefs/rta/source→/-stat/rtasource instantly and unconditionally; it ignores options bit 5 and solo state, so the fake cannot model a Solo-Priority or console-side hijack, and its /meters/15 content is source-independent (fakedesk.py:39-43, 944-946: RTA frames come from SyntheticRta regardless of source). tests/integration/test_cfs.py:252 asserts verified/146 only at arm; grep of tests/ finds no test that changes /-prefs/rta/source or /-stat/rtasource mid-session. tests/test_meters.py:683-692 explicitly certifies that an unverified read-back does not raise. (2) Code: meters.py:926-937 — mismatch after verify_attempts is only log.warning + verified=False; cfs.py:910-917 `_arm` catches only RtaSourceError/NotConnected and proceeds; cfs.py:928-929 merely publishes rta_verified; ring_out (cfs.py:637-720) never inspects ses.rta.verified; _run_ringout (cfs.py:1146-1197) raises to target purely on absence of detections; grep confirms no read of /-stat/rtasource anywhere in cfs.py, Desk._on_push (desk.py:282-284) only invalidates cache, and no /-stat/screen write exists anywhere in src/. (3) Research: meters.md §5.3 says verbatim '/meters/15 takes no source argument … The stream is simply the console's RTA, whatever it is currently analysing', encoder 6 = source, 'Solo Priority (bit 5) overrides everything while any solo is active', GEQ/PEQ-page behaviour 'remains UNCONFIRMED … Safe practice: put the console on the METERS/RTA tab (/-stat/screen/screen ,i 1 … /-stat/screen/METER/page ,i 4)'; §6.15 stale-after-reset warning present. Minor overreach: the research marks setrtasrc↔prefs interaction and the GEQ-page case UNCONFIRMED, not 'prefs alone switches the analyser' (prefs is the primary VERIFIED-CORRECTED recipe, and M7 on the real desk worked via prefs); and a plain solo is already mitigated because set_rta_source clears bit 5 at arm (claimant acknowledges re-tick needed). These do not change the core: the only fallbacks are a log line and 'RTA NOT verified' in the tool summary; nothing stops or re-points during the session. (4) Independently reproduced in worktree verify-rta-hijack-repro (commit d13aa70, tests/integration/test_rta_hijack.py): setting /-prefs/rta/source=2 on the first RAISE → fakedesk /-stat/rtasource=98 (Ch01 post), ring_out continues -19→-6 dB, final_stage DONE, aborted False, and the report's rta block still says verified True / stat_actual 146 — the report lies about what the analyser was watching. Severity high per rubric: with the analyser re-pointed (one encoder turn or one click in X32-Edit on the console's single global RTA, realistic during a minutes-long ring_out_system), CFS drives RAISE writes on a live wedge/main bus from a blind detector up to target/ceiling with no notching — CFS acts on garbage with a direct acoustic-safety consequence, and reports DONE/verified.

> **Verifier 2: CONFIRMED (high)** — Core claim holds and reproduces: CFS computes `rta.verified`, publishes it, and then raises a live bus master to the 0 dB ceiling regardless; nothing re-checks the analyser source for the rest of the session; the FakeDesk makes verification impossible to fail and its /meters/15 content is source-independent, so no test can see the consequence.

(1) Arm-time, unverified-but-proceed — CONFIRMED, this is the part that would bite. set_rta_source (meters.py:887-888) writes /-prefs/rta/source and /pos with X32Connection.set, which is fire-and-forget with no ack and no retry (connection.py:520-530, 'no ack exists'). If that one datagram is lost (venue WiFi / a tablet walked onto the stage — the wedge ring-out use case) the analyser stays wherever it was (factory default source 0 = dynamic/selected channel, pre-EQ). The code then reads /-stat/rtasource twice, sees the mismatch, and only log.warning + verified=False (meters.py:926-937; the unit test tests/test_meters.py:683-691 literally certifies 'unverified … do_not_raise', and meters.py:24-25 documents 'a mismatch is logged, never raised'). cfs._arm (cfs.py:910-929) has no branch on ses.rta.verified beyond publishing rta_verified; ring_out then runs _run_ringout (cfs.py:1147-1198), whose raise loop has no frame-content sanity check at all — no detection ⇒ raise step, dwell, repeat to target (default target = bus_fader_max_db/master_ceiling_db = 0 dB, device.yaml:725,830), then BACKOFF 3 dB and DONE. Reproduced with the earlier probe (worktree verify-rta-unverified, tests/integration/test_cfs.py::test_probe_ring_out_arms_with_unverified_rta): rta={'stat_expected':146,'stat_actual':168,'verified':False}, final DONE, max_master -6.0 (= target), report warnings None; the report summary (cfs.py:1373-1376) reads 'no feedback detected; DONE' — the unverified source appears only in the nested rta dict, after the master has already been raised. On a real wedge whose GBF onset is below the target this is an automated, unsupervised gain raise into sustained feedback that the tool then leaves standing at max−3 dB and reports as clean. That is 'CFS acts on garbage' with a signal the code already had in hand; the fix (re-write / /-action/setrtasrc retry, refuse RINGOUT when still unverified) is trivial. In feedback_watch mode the same gap is medium (human raises by hand; tool claims protection it does not have, summary does say 'RTA NOT verified', server.py:1645).

(2) Mid-session hijack — CONFIRMED as a gap, but I rate this half medium and partly theoretical. grep confirms no re-read of /-stat/rtasource, no conn 'update' subscription for /-prefs/rta/*, and no /-stat/screen write anywhere in cfs.py; the finder's test (assumptions-cfs-detector-fixtures …::test_rta_source_hijacked_mid_ringout_stops_the_raise) fails today: source→2 at the first RAISE, desk stat=98, CFS raises −19→−6 and reports DONE. Caveats: (a) Solo hijack is already mitigated — bit 5 is cleared at arm (meters.py:899-903); re-ticking Solo Priority mid-run is contrived. (b) The finder's own example (hijack to Ch01 when Ch01 is the wedge mic) would NOT be blind on a real desk: a mic→bus→wedge loop rings on the mic channel too, so the detector would still see it; only a hijack to an unrelated/quiet strip (encoder 6 turned, X32-Edit on a second device, Monitor with nothing solo'd) blinds it. (c) The console-screen dependency (PEQ/GEQ page changing what /meters/15 carries) is UNCONFIRMED in meters.md §5.3 in both directions; the code ignores the documented 'safe practice' (force METER/RTA page) but whether that matters is unknown — worth a hardware check because 'select the vocal channel and look at its EQ while ringing out' is exactly what engineers do by reflex.

(3) Overstated plank: 'whether /-prefs/rta/source alone switches the live analyser is UNCONFIRMED — code depends on it with no fallback'. HANDOVER §4b (M7, fw 4.x, Main LR) shows the prefs write did drive the real analyser (CFS caught real feedback; auto-gain/POST-insert effects were measurable), so in practice that item is resolved; it does not change the verdict.

FakeDesk encodes the belief exactly as stated: _mirror_rta_stat is instant and unconditional (fakedesk.py:1094-1101) so verified can never be False in integration tests (test_cfs.py:252 asserts it True), and _meter_values returns the one global SyntheticRta frame whatever /-prefs/rta/source says (fakedesk.py:943-946), so even a wrong source still 'detects' in every test. Offline test path is as the finder proposes: make the fake able to drop/lag the prefs write and to switch the synthetic frame content with the source, then assert ring_out refuses/aborts.

Severity kept at high because the dominant path (lost arm-time write → known-unverified → automated raise to 0 dB → DONE 'no feedback') is a wrong write left in place plus a lying report, triggered by ordinary UDP loss, with zero operator window in the two-call ring_out flow; the mid-session half alone would be medium.

## E4. [high] (desk-policy-server, confirmed) The ≤2 s node cache is a safe base for relative moves because /xremote pushes invalidate it whenever anyone else moves a control.

**Encoded at:** tests/integration/conftest.py + every test: ≤2 xremote clients on a lossless in-memory socket; tests/integration/test_desk.py:104-121 proves push invalidation only in that world; fakedesk.py:98,850-853 does model the 4-client cap ('no room', silent) but no test registers 4 others first.

**Code depends on it at:** src/x32mcp/desk.py:1007 (adjust_level reads `before` via _leaf -> _read_sections cache hit ≤ read_cache_ttl_s, desk.py:316-319) and desk.py:1009 base+delta; also desk.py:991 (set_level before), 1019 (set_mute was_muted), server.py get_* summaries; X32Connection never learns whether its /xremote registration took (no ack exists).

**Reality:** transport.md §2 (CONFIRMED, DOC 446-455): the desk pushes to 'maximum four active clients'; a fifth /xremote is silently ignored (§4.1 emulator 'no room for new clients'). §2/§9.7: plain UDP, no ack, pushes are lost silently on Wi-Fi. A gig routinely has X32-Edit + an iPad + musicians' monitor-mix phone apps = 4+ clients. Red test test_relative_move_uses_a_fresh_base_when_pushes_do_not_arrive: musician pulls his send -10 -> -40 on his phone, model 'adjust_send +3' within 2 s of a read -> desk writes -7.0: '+33 dB' into his ears.

**On a real desk:** In-ear/wedge level jumps of tens of dB from adjust_send/adjust_fader computed on a stale base whenever we are the 5th client or a push datagram was lost; was_muted/summaries lie; the ±6 dB relative guard is defeated because the delta is applied to a fictional starting point.

**Offline test:** Pre-register 4 dummy client addresses in fakedesk.clients (or drop the push), prime the cache with get_sends, fakedesk.set_value the send to -40, adjust_send +3 -> assert desk value -37 (fails today: -7). Fix direction: relative moves must GET the leaf fresh (one round trip) instead of trusting the cache; detect missing registration (e.g. probe with a second socket) and warn.

## E5. [high] (desk-policy-server, confirmed) Once a ramp/restore/ring-out is running, nothing else needs to stop it: the only competing mover is another of our own ramps, and panic() is 'the last word'.

**Encoded at:** tests/integration/test_desk.py:214-224 (only a newer *own* ramp supersedes); test_desk.py:359-405 and test_server_tools.py:243-247 call panic() with nothing in flight; tests call ring_out/restore/set_fader strictly sequentially (direct function calls hide that an MCP client is turn-based).

**Code depends on it at:** src/x32mcp/desk.py:922-946 _run_ramp writes precomputed steps regardless of pushes; desk.py:282-284 _on_push only invalidates cache; desk.py:1184-1223 panic() touches neither self._ramps nor CFS nor a running restore; nodes.py:1201-1227 restore lines re-write whole '/bus/NN/mix ON …' sections (unmute); server.py:1733-1737 ring_out and 1242 restore hold the tool call for minutes while DESIGN §0.5 promises ~2 s per tool.

**Reality:** transport.md §4.1 (DOC): the desk pushes the operator's fader moves to us, i.e. we are told when a human counter-moves and ignore it. MCP clients deliver panic() only between tool calls, so during a 60 s ramp, a whole-desk restore (~40 s at 50 lines/s) or a ring_out (minutes) the model cannot issue panic at all; and when panic does run concurrently, the in-flight writer keeps going (red tests test_operator_pulling_the_fader_down_mid_ramp_wins: engineer yanks bus 1 to -oo at 0.7 s, ramp drags it back to 0.0 dB; test_panic_cancels_running_ramps: ramp keeps climbing after panic, superseded False).

**On a real desk:** Engineer pulls a howling wedge down on the desk -> the server pushes it back up 20 ms later for the rest of the ramp (motor fader fights the hand; on a Rack the X32-Edit fader snaps back). panic() during a restore is undone by the restore's next '/bus/07/mix ON 0.0' line; panic during ring_out mutes the bus, the detector then hears silence, RAISE continues to the 0 dB ceiling, DONE backs off 3 dB and leaves the wedge at -3 dB for whoever unmutes it.

**Offline test:** As in the red tests: (a) start set_level(bus.1, 0, ramp_ms=2000) from -40, fakedesk.set_value(fader,-oo) mid-ramp, assert final -oo/superseded; (b) panic() mid-ramp must cancel self._ramps, abort CFS and cancel a running restore; (c) assert ring_out/restore return within the §0.5 budget (run as a background session like feedback_watch) so panic stays reachable.

(2) feedback_watch_stop (server.py:1674) aborts a ring-out but panic() does not call it and it has the same turn-based reachability problem. (3) panic-vs-own-ramp is latent rather than audible (panic mutes the output; the ramp leaves the fader hot for whoever unmutes), and restore only re-unmutes bus mix sections that were in the plan. (4) The long-running tools are a documented, deliberate deviation from §0.5 (docstrings say 'up to several minutes'), but the dashboard is read-only (DESIGN §17: inbound WS ignored; webui.py:355) so there is no out-of-band stop. Why this bites at a real gig (skeptic's weighing): README §'device is the source of truth' and GIG_CHECKLIST.md:10-11,77-78 make the physical fader/mute or X32-Edit THE emergency reflex and panic() only a backstop. That reflex is exactly what the code overrides. (1) Ramps: default 300 ms is harmless, but the tool accepts 0..60000 ms (server.py:888) and M5 actually used 12-15 s ramps on the real desk (HANDOVER §4a:99-100,124); for the remainder of such a ramp the operator's pull-down is rewritten every 20 ms (motor fader fights the hand / X32-Edit fader snaps back; DSP value zips between the two = audible). Measured: bus 1 yanked to -oo at 0.7 s of a 2 s ramp ends at 0.0 dB, superseded=False. (2) Ring-out, the procedure that deliberately provokes feedback and whose detector is known to miss a plateaued howl (REVIEW_BRIEF §1): operator pulls the howling wedge master to -oo; within one dwell (1.5 s default) the server writes it straight back to howl-level+1 dB in ONE UNRAMPED STEP (-oo -> -14 dB measured) and keeps raising to the target; report says DONE. (3) Operator (or panic) mutes the bus mid-run: the loop is broken so the detector hears nothing, RAISE runs to the target, DONE backs off 3 dB and the report certifies a level that was never acoustically tested; the master is parked at target-3 behind the mute for whoever unmutes it (measured: DONE, max -6, end -9, bus still muted, no warning). These are wrong writes against a human safety action -> high.

Parts I downgrade: the 'panic() is unreachable / not the last word' framing is weaker than stated. With the stdio transport (server.py:1949) and a single LLM client, panic() cannot be issued while set_fader/ring_out/restore is pending anyway, and the reachable interrupt — MCP cancellation (Esc) — is handled correctly: desk.py:907-910 cancels the ramp task and cfs.py:706-710 unwinds the ring-out with a back-off. panic() racing a plain ramp is audibly benign (the mute holds; the ramp writes a different address). restore_plan (nodes.py:1201-1227) is computed once from a diff, so it only re-unmutes a bus whose mix section already differed at plan time, and real restores were 3 sections/9 ms (HANDOVER §4a) — low. DESIGN §0.5's '~2 s per tool' vs minutes-long ring_out/restore is a documented, deliberate exception (tool docstrings say so), though GIG_CHECKLIST.md:254 ('call feedback_watch_stop() mid-run') does encode the false belief that a second tool call can be made while ring_out is in flight. None of these caveats touch the operator-override hazard, which stands on its own.

## E6. [high] (fakedesk-fidelity, confirmed) Writing side A (par 01-31) of a dual-mono GEQ2 selected as FXnL on Main LR equalises the whole Main LR signal, and side B (FXnR) of that slot is then free for another bus.

**Reality:** fx_routing_scenes.md §2.1: GEQ2/TEQ2 are dual — 'side A (= L input)', 'side B (= R input)'; §3.4: 'a stereo effect needs both FXnL and FXnR inserted (e.g. main L/R uses the pair automatically when /main/st/insert/sel = FXnL … UNCONFIRMED whether sel then reads FXnL)' and an insert point serves ONE strip. HANDOVER §4b defect 4: with GEQ2 in FX5 on Main LR a -15 dB PRE cut moved the RTA only -5.9/-6.0/-3.9 dB — that is 20·log10((1+10^(-15/20))/2) ≈ -4.6 dB, the signature of one leg cut and a mono-summed analyser, not a -15 dB cut on both legs. HANDOVER 'Desk facts': Jim's desk already has GEQ2 in FX5 inserted on Main LR, so plan_setup will reuse 5A for main and lend 5B to the first monitor bus.

**On a real desk:** ring_out('main') notches only the LEFT PA stack: the right stack keeps full gain at the ringing frequency (ring persists or only ~3 dB of system headroom is gained), VERIFY sees ≤-3.3 dB for a -9 cut → deepens to -9 on L only → audible L/R tonal imbalance for the audience, budget burned, run aborted. ring_out_system([1,'main']) on Jim's desk: bus 1 gets FX5R = the GEQ leg carrying Main R — either the desk refuses/reassigns (validate fails at the gig) or every monitor notch is cut into the right PA stack (wrong write heard by the room). Probe test_probe_main_lr_gets_a_stereo_geq_or_both_sides fails today ({'A':'main','B':None} on GEQ2).

**Offline test:** Model main/st (and /config/buslink-ed bus pairs) in FakeDesk as two legs: RTA attenuation = -20·log10((10^(gA/20)+10^(gB/20))/2) with gA from par 1-31 and gB from par 33-63 for dual types (both = par 1-31 for GEQ/TEQ), and mark (slot,B) as owned by main.st when sel=FXnL. Add: ring_out('main') on a fresh fake must load GEQ (stereo) or write both sides and must verify a full-depth drop; plan_setup(["main", 1]) must not allocate slot-of-main side B to bus 1. Reproduce M7: -15 dB on side A only → RTA ≈ -4.6 dB.

(3) Research: fx_routing_scenes.md §2.1 table: GEQ2/TEQ2 par 01-31 = 'side A (= L input)', par 33-63 = 'side B (= R input)'; GEQ/TEQ = 'L/R linked'. §3.4: 'a stereo effect (GEQ, TEQ, ...) needs both FXnL and FXnR inserted (e.g. main L/R uses the pair automatically when /main/st/insert/sel = FXnL … UNCONFIRMED whether sel then reads FXnL)'; §13 item 6 lists 'Whether selecting FXnL on a stereo strip (main/st, stereo-linked bus) auto-inserts the FXnR side' as UNCONFIRMED. The claimant's reading of that as the one-leg/coherent-sum signature (20*log10((1+10^-0.75)/2) = -4.6 dB) is a plausible inference, not something the handover states; music noise and GEQ filter shape are confounders, but a ~-5 dB reading for a -15 dB cut at band centre is hard to explain with both legs cut, so it is supportive. Caveats that do not rescue the code: the M7 run did tame rings with side-A-only cuts (cutting one leg still lowers loop gain a few dB, often enough for marginal feedback), so 'ring persists' is the pessimistic case; the realistic outcome is roughly a third of the intended dB effect, L/R tonal imbalance, VERIFY (decay_verify_db=6, device.yaml:820) under-reading linear drops (-9 dB one leg ≈ -3.4 dB summed) and deepening/aborting, and near-zero effect when the feedback path is via the right stack. The side-B lending is an unambiguous wrong-write hazard: on Jim's desk plan_setup(['main',N]) inserts bus N on FX5R, so either the desk refuses/reassigns (setup fails at the gig) or every monitor notch for bus N is cut into the Main R PA leg. Severity high per the brief's scale (wrong write heard by the room; CFS acting on a wrong physical model of the mains).

> **Verifier 2: CONFIRMED (high)** — The claim is that the code (and the FakeDesk that certifies it) treats Main LR as a mono strip: one side of a dual-mono GEQ2 is assumed to equalise the whole Main LR signal, and the other side of that slot is assumed free for another bus. I verified every leg of it.

1. Research ground truth (authoritative over code): fx_routing_scenes.md §2.1 (VERIFIED from DOC p.104 + X32GEQ2cpy.c) — GEQ2/TEQ2 par 01-31 = side A '= L input', par 33-63 = side B '= R input'; GEQ/TEQ = 'L/R linked'. §3.4: 'a stereo effect (GEQ, TEQ, ...) needs both FXnL and FXnR inserted (e.g. main L/R uses the pair automatically when /main/st/insert/sel = FXnL ...)' — only the sel read-back is UNCONFIRMED, not the fact that a stereo strip consumes the L/R pair. This is also standard X32 practice: Dual GEQ on the LR bus = independent left/right graphics, Stereo GEQ = linked. There is no plausible real-desk behaviour in which writing only par 01-31 of a GEQ2 EQs both legs of Main LR — that is precisely what distinguishes GEQ2 from GEQ. So the FakeDesk behaviour does NOT match what research says the desk does → not refutable on fidelity grounds.

2. FakeDesk encodes the wrong belief: fakedesk.py:1103-1134 _refresh_cuts resolves the RTA-source strip (main/st for source 72), reads its insert/sel, and for sel=FX5L (side_b False) applies par 01-31 gains as 100% attenuation of every RTA band. No notion that /main/st is stereo, no L/R legs, no /-insert ownership. So a side-A-only notch 'verifies' at full depth on the fake.

3. Code depends on it, with zero Main-LR special-casing: provision.py:433-509 plan_setup treats main.st like any mono bus (load_type = first fx_types_dual = GEQ2; pairs it A/B with another bus; 'partial reuse' 466-478 lends the other side of main's dual slot); provision.py:405-412 validate only objects to sharing for *stereo* types; desk.py:1403-1431 set_geq_band writes par_a_first.. for side A only; cfs.py:887-889/_DeskGeqWriter:410-416 binds the session writer to ins.side. grep for family=="main" in cfs.py finds only master-fader handling.

4. Ran the existing probe worktree (verify-stereo-main, tests/integration/test_verify_stereo_main.py) against the FakeDesk: plan_setup(['main',3]) fresh → loads GEQ2 in FX5, main.st=FX5L (A), bus.3=FX5R (B) of the SAME slot; with Main LR already on FX5L/GEQ2 (Jim's real desk per HANDOVER 'Desk facts') plan_setup(['main',3]) → bus.3 gets FX5R; plan_setup([1,2,3,'main']) → main.st gets FX6**R** (side B of bus 3's GEQ2) — so CFS's main-stage cuts would go to par 33-63 while, on a real desk, bus 3's side-A graph would sit on Main L. validate_ringout_eqs says ok=True for all of these. tests/integration/test_cfs.py:136-138 asserts exactly this shape ({main.st: FX6L} on a GEQ2 load) and test_server_tools.py:655-658 drives ring_out_system ending on 'main'.

5. Real-desk corroboration: HANDOVER §4b defect 4 — with GEQ2 in FX5 on Main LR, a −15 dB PRE cut moved the Main RTA only −5.9/−6.0/−3.9 dB. A −15 dB cut on both legs read by a 1/10-octave band at the GEQ centre should show ≈ −13..−15 dB; one leg cut with a summed analyser predicts 20·log10((1+10^(−15/20))/2) = −4.6 dB (coherent) / −2.9 dB (incoherent) — the observation sits right there. The handover took '−6 dB' as proof the cut was visible and never asked why it was not −15. M7's 'successful catch' was very likely a left-stack-only notch.

Skeptical weighing: no safety hazard (cuts only, ≤ −9 dB), and monitor buses (mono) are unaffected. But for the 'main' stage — which ring_out_system ends on by design and which is the exact configuration of the only real desk tested — CFS writes notches into one PA stack only, VERIFY measures through a summed analyser that can never show the commanded depth (so it deepens to max on a misleading reading and burns budget), the report claims Main LR is rung out while the other stack has zero notches (feedback returns in the show at 'handled' frequencies, plus audible L/R tonal asymmetry), and the planner can cross-wire a monitor bus onto Main's other GEQ side (either a spurious validation failure at the gig if the desk enforces one-owner, or monitor notches landing in the FOH PA if it does not — desk behaviour UNCONFIRMED §3.4, and the code has no fallback). That is a wrong write to the FOH system plus CFS acting on a measurement that cannot reflect the write → high stands. Fix direction is clear and cheap: for main.st (and buslink-ed bus pairs) load GEQ (stereo) or write both sides of a GEQ2, mark (slot,B) owned when a stereo strip selects FXnL, refuse FXnR-only on a stereo strip; make FakeDesk model two legs (RTA atten = −20·log10((10^(gA/20)+10^(gB/20))/2)) so today's tests fail.

## E8. [high] (meters-rta, confirmed) Every RTA band always carries broadband energy tens of dB above the −128 floor, so 'prominence = level − median(±3 neighbours)' is a bounded, meaningful number (≈10–50 dB) and the 12 dB / 25 dB thresholds discriminate something.

**Encoded at:** src/x32mcp/meters.py:595-600,617-618 (SyntheticRta defaults: base −25 dB@100 Hz → −55 dB@10 kHz, ±3 dB noise, ±2 dB wobble; measured min over 2000 frames = −64.0 dB, never −128) and :694-700 (a tone leaks into ±1 band at −10 dB only); tests/test_detector.py:88-93 floor −30…−52 dB; the only flat-floor stream (_plateaued_ring, test_detector.py:480-491) uses −85.

**Code depends on it at:** src/x32mcp/detector.py:278-288 (prominences: plain median of neighbours, −128 treated as a level) and :361-366 (override: prominence ≥ 25 dB for ≥ 6 frames emits at confidence 0.7 regardless of growth); device.yaml detector prominence_db 12, min_level_db −45, override 25/6.

**Reality:** meters.md §4.2/§6.3: 'RTA silence = 0x8000 = −128.0 dB exactly'; HANDOVER §4a: on the real desk '/meters/15 … values were all floor'. With neighbours at −128 any tone above the −45 gate has prominence ≥ 83 dB (script: a held −40 dB tone in a silent room → prominence 88, override fires at frame 5 = 300 ms; the identical tone over the synthetic floor is not even a candidate). HANDOVER §4b's '60 dB-prominent 8 kHz ring' is unreachable in the synthetic model (cap −3 vs base ≈ −54).

**On a real desk:** In the quiet room a ring-out requires, the override path is 'any isolated narrowband sound ≥ −45 dBFS for 300 ms': a whistle, a phone tone, a projector/HVAC whine, a flute or a sine check from the system tech gets a −3 dB GEQ cut (feedback_watch writes immediately). Conversely every threshold fitted in tests (12/25 dB) was fitted against a floor 40–70 dB hotter than reality, so none of the prominence numbers transfer.

**Offline test:** Add SyntheticRta(level_100hz_db=-128, level_10khz_db=-128, noise_db=0) ('silent room') and a 'preamp hiss' variant (−100 dB flat); feed a held non-growing −40 dB tone and assert no detection within 2 s (fails today at 300 ms); make prominences() clamp neighbours to max(level, noise_floor_estimate) or use a trimmed mean over a wider window and re-fit thresholds on both floors.

> **Verifier 1: CONFIRMED (high)** — All citations check out and the behaviour reproduces exactly.

Encoded assumption (verified): src/x32mcp/meters.py:595-600 defaults noise_db 3, wobble_db 2, level_100hz_db -25, level_10khz_db -55, leak_db 10; :617-618 builds the -15 dB/decade base; :694-700 leaks a tone only into the +/-1 bands at -leak_db. Measured over 2000 default frames: min -64.0 dB, max -9.5 dB - never within 60 dB of the -128 floor. Every SyntheticRta in the suite and in FakeDesk (fakedesk.py:301, :1333; test_meters.py; integration/test_cfs.py:408; webui.py:571) uses those defaults. tests/test_detector.py:88-93 local floor is -30 - 0.22*i (+bumps, +/-3 dB) = -30..-52 dB; notes there are defined as 'above_floor_db' 18-20 (test_held_note_not_detected :215-224, test_plateau_and_transient_do_not_detect :299-305), and the only flat-floor fixture _plateaued_ring (:480-491) uses -85 with the 'safe held vocal note' pinned at 15 dB prominence (:512-522). So the safety property 'a held note is never notched' is only ever certified at prominence < 25 dB, a number that exists only because the fixture floor sits a few dB under the signal.

Code dependence (verified): detector.py:278-288 prominence = level - median(+/-3 neighbours) with -128 treated as an ordinary level; :361-366 override emits at confidence_threshold once prominence >= 25 dB for >= 6 frames regardless of growth; device.yaml:783,797,812-813 = 12 / -45 / 25 / 6. cfs.py:1040-1041 (WATCH) calls _notch -> writer.set_band_gain immediately; RINGOUT queues to pending and _notch_and_verify (cfs.py:1200-1219) also writes at once, and with the PRE insert a -6 dB cut on an external held tone reads as a 6 dB 'decay' and verifies as tamed.

Reality (verified): meters.md line 469 (sec 6.3) 'RTA silence = 0x8000 = -128.0 dB exactly', line 304 (sec 4.2) floor/no-signal = -128; HANDOVER sec 4a line 97-98 '/meters/15 ... values were all floor/zero because the desk was silent'; HANDOVER sec 4b line 159 'A 60 dB-prominent 8 kHz ring' on the real desk (so the real analyser is selective enough for single-band prominences of tens of dB), and sec 4b line 171-174: two of four real notches were spent on 40/80 Hz non-feedback content. The detector.py:349-360 rationale ('musical content is harmonically spread, so tens of dB of prominence in a single band is feedback by construction') does not hold for a +/-0.3-octave window: harmonics are >= 1 octave (10 bands) away, so a whistle, sine line-check, phone tone, flute/organ/synth note is exactly as locally prominent as a ring.

Reproduction with device.yaml config: silent room (all -128) + held -40 dB tone with -50 dB +/-1 leak -> prominence 88.0, detection at frame index 5 (ts 0.25 s, frames=6, slope 0.0, conf 0.70); -100 dB hiss floor -> prominence 60, same frame; a -44 dB tone (1 dB over the gate) -> prominence 84, same frame; SyntheticRta(level_100hz_db=-128, level_10khz_db=-128, noise_db=0)+inject_note(1000,-40) -> fires at frame 10 (after the 5-frame rise); the identical inject_note over the default floor never fires (max prominence 6.4 dB); a capped 8 kHz ring over the default floor tops out at 53.7 dB prominence, so the M7 60 dB case is unreachable in the model.

Fallbacks checked: cfs._calibrate_floor (cfs.py:824-877, active via device.yaml floor_margin_db 8) only raises min_level_db to max(-45, floor+8); with a -128 or -100 floor the gate stays -45, so it does not touch this path. No frequency window, harmonic/bandwidth check, or operator confirmation sits between a detection and the GEQ write. Notch budget (6) and -9 dB max bound the damage but do not prevent the wrong write; wasting budget on non-feedback is precisely the M7 failure. Minor overstatement: HVAC/projector whine rarely reaches -45 dBFS, and the 25 dB override threshold came from the real-desk observation rather than synthetic fitting - but the 'held note is safe below 25 dB' half was fitted only on hot floors. Severity high per rubric: CFS writes GEQ cuts to a live bus on non-feedback input and reports it as feedback caught/tamed.

> **Verifier 2: CONFIRMED (high)** — Reproduced against the shipped detector + device.yaml (prominence 12, min_level -45, override 25 dB / 6 frames). A dead-steady -40 dBFS narrowband tone (±1-band leak at -10) over a flat floor fires the override at frame 5 (250 ms) with slope 0.0 for EVERY plausible real-desk floor: -128 (prom 88), -100 preamp hiss (prom 60), -85 = the M7-measured neighbour level at 8 kHz (prom 45); even a -44 dB tone 1 dB over the gate fires (prom 41). The identical -40 dB held note injected into the product emulator (meters.SyntheticRta defaults, as used by FakeDesk fakedesk.py:301/1333, webui demo and every integration test) has prominence 5.6 dB and never even qualifies; over that floor the override needs a tone >= -15 dBFS at 1 kHz, >= -28.6 at 8 kHz and >= -0.2 dBFS (i.e. impossible) at 100 Hz. Worse than the finding states: the synthetic base spectrum (-25 @100 Hz ... -40 @1 kHz ... -44 @2 kHz) sits ABOVE min_level_db -45 for every band below ~2 kHz, so on the FakeDesk the level gate gates nothing and prominence does all the discriminating, while on the real desk (HANDOVER §4b: a real ring was 60 dB prominent; meters.md §6.3: silence is exactly -128) prominence is always saturated and the -45 gate is the ONLY discriminator. The two regimes are inverted, so every FakeDesk/integration demonstration of detector selectivity (test_detector.py:215 held note 'not detected' at +20 dB over a -30..-52 floor; :512 'override needs real prominence' at 15 dB) certifies a regime that does not exist on hardware; the 12/25 dB numbers were never exercised against a realistic floor except the single hand-built -85 stream at :480, which only checks the positive case.
Skeptical discounting applied: (1) the '-128 silent room' premise is overstated for CFS operation (mics open, master raised: M7 saw ~-85 at HF with quiet music, -51.7 peak at 48 Hz) — but the conclusion is floor-independent for any real floor <= ~-70, so it stands. (2) Several of the listed triggers (phone in the audience, HVAC, projector whine) are unlikely to clear -45 dBFS at a pre-fader bus tap; the realistic triggers are a whistle / sine or pink-band check from the system tech and DI/amp mains hum (50/100/150 Hz, stationary, perfectly narrowband) during ring_out, and near-sine sustained programme (organ, synth/808 bass, flute, falsetto vowels, bass fundamentals 20-30 dB over the bed per REVIEW_REPORT §1.3) during feedback_watch, which is intended for live use. (3) Not mitigated: cfs._calibrate_floor (cfs.py:824-877) only raises the level gate, never touches prominence, and in production it is called from _open_session (cfs.py:890) BEFORE _arm starts the frame source (cfs.py:923), so with LiveMeters idle it returns unchanged after the 0.3 s first-frame timeout (its only test, test_cfs.py:645-696, pre-starts a hand-rolled source) — HANDOVER §4b itself records this ordering problem as the reason calibration was 'backed out'; there is no frequency window; rta decay/peakhold are not forced. (4) Overlap: docs/REVIEW_REPORT.md §1.2(a)/(c) and §1.3 already state the override emits 'for all 95 testable bands at >= 25 dB prominence' and list near-sine programme sources, so the override half of this is known to the lead reviewer; the genuinely new, testable part is the emulator-floor inversion (gate inert / prominence decisive on the fake, the reverse on hardware). Consequence on a real desk is an unrequested GEQ write to Main LR or a wedge bus within 300 ms of any steady tone over the gate, deepening -3 -> -6 -> -9 once per 1 s cooldown while it persists, VERIFY failing (a PRE cut of a non-regenerative tone drops the RTA only by ~the cut, < decay_verify_db 6) and, in ring_out, ABORT 'not tamed' with a 6 dB master back-off; budget (6) burned so later genuine feedback is not caught — the same class as the M7 40/80 Hz budget loss. Cuts-only, bounded to -9 dB and snapshot-protected, so no safety hazard, but it is a wrong write on the PA acting on a misread, which the rubric maps to high. Offline test as proposed is valid and fails today: SyntheticRta(level_100hz_db=-100, level_10khz_db=-115, noise_db=1) (or -128/-128/0), inject_note(1000, -40), assert no Detection within 40 frames -> fires at frame 5.
