Nothing reads /-insert/fx*L|R to reconcile, nothing loads GEQ/TEQ for main.st, nothing writes both sides for a stereo strip. The only mitigation is incidental: if the operator pre-loads a stereo GEQ/TEQ and inserts it on main, plan_setup reuses it (provision.py:460) and set_geq_band handles stereo types — but the tool's own provisioning never produces that, and DESIGN.md §14 (line 605 "dual-mono pairs buses (L, R) on one slot") carries the same assumption.

Fake/tests: fakedesk.py:1103-1131 _refresh_cuts picks side A/B from insert/sel alone and attenuates every RTA band by that one side's pars even when the RTA-source strip is /main/st (module doc fakedesk.py:39-44 says so explicitly), so a side-A-only notch fully kills a synthetic ring on the mains; tests/integration/test_cfs.py:136-138 asserts plan_setup([1,2,'main']) yields main.st {sel: FX6L} on a GEQ2 type-load with side B None; no test models L/R.

Empirical probe (worktree wt/verify-stereo-main, commit eab3ba1, tests/integration/test_verify_stereo_main.py, all pass = current behaviour): plan_setup(desk, ['main', 3]) -> type_loads [{slot 5, GEQ2}], inserts main.st FX5L + bus.3 FX5R, allocation sides {A: main, B: 3}; with main already on FX5L/GEQ2 (the HANDOVER §4b studio setup) plan_setup(['main', 3]) hands bus 3 FX5R; plan_setup([1,2,3,'main']) (a typical monitors+mains prep) gives main.st **FX6R** — side B of a dual-mono GEQ2 whose side A is Bus 3.

Real-desk consequence: with GEQ2 in the slot (Dual GEQ = two independent mono graphs — standard X32 behaviour, which is why operators are told to use Stereo GEQ/TEQ on LR), CFS's 'main' stage notches Main L only; the right PA stack keeps its full loop gain, VERIFY sees a partial drop, the notch is deepened to -9 dB on L only (lopsided mains, ring not reliably killed). HANDOVER §4b is circumstantially consistent: on the GEQ2-on-Main-LR setup a -15 dB PRE cut moved the RTA only -5.9/-6.0/-3.9 dB, close to what a one-side cut looks like through a mono-summed analyser (~-4.6 dB coherent) and far from a both-sides -15 dB cut (~-14 dB at the centre 1/10-oct band). The planner additionally allocates FXnR of main's slot to another bus (or puts main on FXnR of a bus's slot): under the research's model that insert point is already main R's, so either the desk drops/steals an insert (main loses its ring-out cuts, or validation fails spuriously) or the other bus's par 33-63 notches land on Main R — a wrong write to a strip not under test. That is CFS acting on a wrong signal-path model at the mains stage plus a potentially wrong write, so 'high' per the rubric is justified (the second scenario's exact outcome hinges on UNCONFIRMED desk behaviour, but every branch is bad and the first scenario is plain FX-rack physics).

Offline test proposal is sound: give FakeDesk stereo awareness for /main/st (L through side A, R through side B, RTA = power sum so an A-only cut caps at ~3 dB), mark (slot,'B') used when a stereo strip selects FXnL, then assert plan_setup(['main']) loads GEQ/TEQ or writes both sides, plan_setup(['main',3]) never allocates main's FXnR, and a closed-loop ring on main dies after one -3 dB step — all fail today.

> **Verifier 2: CONFIRMED (high)** — The finding is real and reachable through the headline flow, not theoretical.

1. What the research says (authoritative over code): fx_routing_scenes.md §2.1 table — GEQ2/TEQ2 par 1-31 = side A "(= L input)", par 33-63 = side B "(= R input)"; GEQ/TEQ = "L/R linked". §3.4: "a stereo effect (GEQ, TEQ, ...) needs both FXnL and FXnR inserted (e.g. main L/R uses the pair automatically when /main/st/insert/sel = FXnL ...)" — only the sel read-back is UNCONFIRMED (§13 item 6), not the fact that a stereo strip consumes both slot inputs. An FX slot is a 2-in/2-out processor; Main LR cannot be squeezed through one mono graph. With a *Dual* GEQ the two graphs are independent (that is the whole GEQ2-vs-GEQ distinction; Maillot's X32GEQ2cpy A->B tool exists for exactly this situation). So writing par 1-31 on a GEQ2 inserted on Main LR equalises Main L only.

2. Where the code depends on it, with no fallback: provision.py:437 load_type = fx_types_dual[0] = "GEQ2" for every target including main.st (a stereo GEQ is never loaded for the mains; module doc lines 19-21 even say a stereo GEQ found in a free slot is *replaced* by GEQ2); provision.py:466-479 treats the other side of a dual slot that one of "our" strips sits on as free and hands it to the next bus — including when that strip is main.st; provision.py:483-497 pairs main.st with a bus on one slot (main can even land on side B = FXnR); desk.py:837-842/_insert_side derives a single side from sel and cfs.py:885-895/414 writes only that side via set_geq_band (desk.py:1418-1425: par 1-31 or 33-63, never both for a dual type); validate_ringout_eqs (provision.py:400-411) only warns about a shared *stereo* GEQ, never about a dual GEQ on a stereo strip whose other side is claimed.

3. Where the fake encodes the belief: fakedesk.py:1103-1131 _refresh_cuts picks side A/B from insert/sel alone and applies that one side's 31 gains to every SyntheticRta band even when the RTA-source strip is main.st — i.e. the emulator models "GEQ2 graph A EQs the whole Main LR", so every closed-loop test on main passes. tests/integration/test_cfs.py:136-138 asserts plan_setup([1,2,"main"]) puts main.st on FX6L of a GEQ2 with side B unallocated (free for a later bus).

4. Reproduced offline (worktree verify-stereo-main, tests/integration/test_verify_stereo_main.py, 2 passed): plan_setup(["main", 3]) on a fresh fake -> type_loads [{slot 5, GEQ2}], inserts main.st=FX5L and bus.3=FX5R, allocation sides {A: main, B: 3}. With the M7 studio state (GEQ2 in FX5 already on Main LR) plan_setup(["main", 3]) reuses main and again hands FX5R to bus 3; validate_ringout_eqs(["main"]) returns ok=True, reasons=[] for a GEQ2 side A on the stereo main.

5. Skeptical checks that do NOT refute it: (a) M7 (HANDOVER §4b) rang out Main LR through "GEQ2 already in FX slot 5, inserted on Main LR" and notches audibly killed rings — but ring-out rings are marginal by construction (gain raised until it just rings), so halving the loop through one stack is enough to stop them; and the same session's PRE measurement of a -15 dB cut read only -5.9/-6.0/-3.9 dB on the RTA, which is far short of -15 and consistent with only one leg of the stereo pair being cut (not proof, but it points the same way). (b) The desk's OSC reaction to a second strip selecting an in-use insert point is UNCONFIRMED (§13 item 5) — but both candidate behaviours are bad here: either bus 3 steals FX5R from Main R (mains lose half their ring-out EQ mid-gig) or both own it and bus 3's CFS notches (par 33-63) land on the right PA stack. (c) Harm is bounded (cuts only, <= 9 dB, narrow) so nobody gets hurt — but the rubric's "wrong write / CFS acts on garbage" is met: monitor-wedge notches written into Main R's EQ, and VERIFY on the mains judging a cut the R leg never received, deepening L to -9 dB while R keeps ringing (lopsided mains, tool reports success). This is the default planner output whenever main is provisioned with an odd number of buses or already holds a GEQ2 (the actual M7 desk), and ring_out_system's default plan ends on "main" (cfs.py:1411), so it bites at an ordinary small gig (3 wedges + mains).

Severity kept at high: wrong writes to a strip not under test plus a silently half-effective mains ring-out on the primary supported path; not mitigated anywhere (no stereo type load for main, no A->B mirroring, no validation reason, planner actively reallocates the R side).

## E12. [medium] (cfs-detector-fixtures, confirmed) RTA frames keep flowing for the whole run, so 'no detection during the dwell' means 'no feedback' - the RAISE loop never checks frame age.

**Encoded at:** src/x32mcp/fakedesk.py:944-946 (the fake streams /meters/15 unconditionally while leased); tests/integration/conftest.py:21 (watchdog_s=1.0 so any silence becomes a connection loss within 1 s - the real config took 14 s, HANDOVER §4a); no test stalls only the meter stream.

**Code depends on it at:** src/x32mcp/cfs.py:1126-1133 (_dwell just sleeps), :1147-1197 (_run_ringout raises whenever pending is empty; never consults ses.last_ts / ses.frames), src/x32mcp/meters.py:418-420 (LiveMeters.last_rx_age_s exists but nothing reads it), :437-452 (a failed renew is only logged).

**Reality:** meters.md §1.3/§6.6: the stream is a 10 s lease renewed by fire-and-forget UDP every 5 s; §6.7 'frame rate … may be variable according to console's ability'; HANDOVER §4a: DEGRADED only 14 s after the cable came out; meters.md §5.3: /meters/15 content changes with the displayed page (UNCONFIRMED). Any of these silences or repoints the analyser without touching control traffic.

**On a real desk:** Meter datagrams stop (Wi-Fi burst loss, lease lapse, cable out < 14 s): CFS keeps adding +1 dB per 1.5 s with a blind detector, reaches the target, reports 'no feedback detected; DONE' while the wedge howls; when a cable comes back the next absolute write is a +N dB jump. Verified offline: with frames dropped from -18 dB on and a ring injected, report = 'master -20 -> -9 (highest -6), 0 notches, no feedback detected; DONE'.

**Offline test:** …/test_assumptions_cfs.py::test_ring_out_does_not_raise_while_the_analyser_is_silent (FAILS today): shadow LiveMeters._on_blob to drop blobs after a RAISE, inject a ring, assert aborted and max_master <= level at blinding. Fix: refuse to raise (HOLD, then ABORT after ~1 s) when clock()-ses.last_ts > ~3 frame periods; same guard in feedback_watch status.

> **Verifier 1: CONFIRMED (high)** — Core claim verified by code reading and by reproduction. (1) Code: cfs.py:1126-1132 `_dwell` only waits on ses.wake/timeout; cfs.py:1147-1197 `_run_ringout` raises whenever `ses.pending` is empty and never consults `ses.last_ts`/`ses.frames` (last_ts is used only for frame ordering at :1028-1032, frames only for the report at :1391); CfsState (:214-238) exposes no frame count/age; `_calibrate_floor` (:848-866) silently returns when no frames arrive rather than refusing to arm; meters.py:418-420 `LiveMeters.last_rx_age_s` is read nowhere in src (the only other `last_rx_age_s` is X32Connection's own field, connection.py:106/458); meters.py:441-455 `_run/_send_request` log-and-continue on a failed renew. (2) Fake/fixtures: fakedesk.py:913-924 streams every leased meter unconditionally and :943-946 always has an RTA frame to send; its only faults are `drop_next` (replies only, not streams, :793-798) and `silent` (all traffic, :772-786) — there is no way to stall only /meters/15; tests/integration/conftest.py:21 sets watchdog_s=1.0 (product default 12.0, connection.py:248; HANDOVER §4a line 118: 'DEGRADED 14 s after the cable came out'); the only mid-ring-out fault test (test_cfs.py:370-396) uses total silence and asserts connection_lost. (3) Research citations are accurate: meters.md §1.3 (10 s lease, 5 s resend 'tolerates one lost datagram'), §6.6, §6.7 ('may be variable according to console's ability to fulfill requests… Don't derive timing from packet arrival'), §5.3 (which analysis /meters/15 carries while a GEQ/PEQ page is displayed is UNCONFIRMED). README.md:808-811 even documents a Wi-Fi tablet host for CFS² and says 'expect the desk's watchdog/DEGRADED handling to cover Wi-Fi hiccups' — the watchdog covers total silence only, not meter-stream loss. (4) Reproduction: ran the claimant's probe (worktree assumptions-cfs-detector-fixtures, src identical to a408a2a) — with LiveMeters._on_blob dropping blobs from the -18 dB RAISE on and a 2.4 kHz ring injected, ring_out returned final_stage DONE, max_master_db -6.0, summary 'master -20.0 -> -9.0 dB (highest -6.0), 0 notch(es), no feedback detected; DONE' — 12 blind +1 dB raises. One sub-claim is overstated and should be dropped: the 'cable out < 14 s keeps adding +1 dB… +N dB jump when it returns' trigger does NOT hold, because every raise goes Desk.set_level → `_leaf(address)` (desk.py:991) and the previous write invalidated that section (desk.py:883 → :275-278), so the raise needs a /node reply; on a dead link it times out in ~1.5 s (0.5 s × 3) → DeskError TIMEOUT (desk.py:355-360) → `_lose_connection` (cfs.py:1180-1182). Total link loss therefore costs at most the in-progress dwell, and ses.master_db only advances on successful writes so no jump accumulates. The finding stands for meter-only silence (lease lapse after two consecutive lost fire-and-forget renews, meter-datagram burst loss on Wi-Fi while 3-attempt control requests survive, desk throttling frames) — the RAISE automaton has no liveness check on its only sensor and reports 'no feedback detected; DONE' (and ring_out_system proceeds to the next bus). Severity high: blind gain raise on a live bus with open mics up to the ceiling plus a false all-clear report; fix is cheap (HOLD then ABORT when clock()-ses.last_ts exceeds a few frame periods, refuse the first RAISE until a frame has arrived, surface frame age in CfsState/feedback_watch).

> **Verifier 2: PARTIAL (medium)** — The code claim is correct: src/x32mcp/cfs.py:1147-1197 (_run_ringout) raises whenever ses.pending is empty and _dwell (:1126-1133) just sleeps; nothing consults ses.last_ts/ses.frames or LiveMeters.last_rx_age_s (meters.py:418-420, read by nobody), and ring_out() (:637-720) starts RAISE right after _arm without waiting for a first frame. The slice's probe test genuinely FAILS today ('master -20 -> -9 (highest -6), 0 notches, no feedback detected; DONE'). But the probe manufactures PERMANENT meter-only silence by monkey-patching LiveMeters._on_blob, and the finding's headline real-world triggers do not produce that:

1. 'Cable out < 14 s' / Wi-Fi burst / PSU (TOTAL silence): REFUTED as a blind-raise mechanism. Every RAISE goes Desk.set_level -> _leaf(address) -> /node read (desk.py:991, 1229; the previous write invalidated the cached section at desk.py:883/275), so with production timeouts (0.5 s x 3, watchdog 12 s) the very next step fails with DeskError TIMEOUT and cfs.py:1180-1182 calls _lose_connection -> ABORT + raw restore. Verified offline at production CONN opts: fakedesk.silent=True at -17 dB -> 'ABORT desk write failed while raising: TIMEOUT: no /node reply for /bus/01/mix', ZERO fader writes attempted after the silence, max_master == level at silence, while conn.state was still 'connected' (i.e. this does NOT depend on the test conftest's 1 s watchdog). GIG_CHECKLIST.md:256 already covers the cable pull during RAISE. And with the cable out the raises could not reach the desk anyway, so 'the wedge howls' is wrong for that case.

2. Meter-ONLY silence while control traffic works: the FakeDesk already models the real 10 s lease (fakedesk.py:900-924, meters.md §1.3) and LiveMeters re-requests every 5 s, so on a real desk the only mechanisms are lost /meters request datagrams: (a) the FIRST request lost -> no frames until the 5 s renew; (b) TWO consecutive renews lost -> ~5 s lapse. Both verified offline at the default 1500 ms dwell: (a) 4 dB raised blind (-20 -> -16) before the first frame, a ring injected at ARM grew unseen for ~5 s, then was caught and notched on the first frames (DONE, 1 notch); (b) 5.05 s frame gap, 3 dB blind (-12 -> -9), ring injected in the gap caught on resumption (DONE, 1 notch). So the realistic consequence is a bounded 3-4 dB / ~5 s blind window in which a ring can build louder and longer than necessary before the prominence override catches it - not 'DONE while the wedge howls'. Probability: single/double loss of a specific small UDP datagram - essentially nil on the documented wired-LAN deployment (README:289), plausible on the Wi-Fi/Termux host README:806-811 explicitly contemplates for CFS², where the README's stated belief 'expect the desk's watchdog/DEGRADED handling to cover Wi-Fi hiccups' is exactly wrong for meter-lease hiccups (control traffic keeps _last_rx fresh, so the watchdog never sees a meter-only gap). meters.md §6.7 (variable frame rate) slows frames, does not stop them; §5.3 (page repoints /meters/15, UNCONFIRMED) changes content while frames keep flowing, so a frame-age guard would not catch it - separate issue. A permanent blind run would need every renew lost while every /node read succeeds (no mechanism), or frames rejected wholesale by the len(values)!=100 check (cfs.py:1023-1027) - but 100 bands is VERIFIED on this FW 4.13 desk (HANDOVER §4a) and fw 4.06 (meters.md §6.13).

Net: a real, cheaply fixable gap (require a first frame before the first RAISE; HOLD/ABORT when clock()-ses.last_ts exceeds a few frame periods; surface frame age in state()/feedback_watch), but the high-severity framing rests on the cable-out scenario, which the read-before-write TIMEOUT path already defuses with zero blind writes. Downgraded to medium: bounded wrong writes (+3-4 dB over ~5 s, during a ring-out with the engineer at the desk, caught on resumption) under a low-probability network condition on a secondary deployment.

## E13. [medium] (cfs-detector-fixtures, confirmed) Feedback grows at 'a few to ~30 dB/s' (a fixed rate injected by fiat, independent of the fader), so anything rising faster than 60 dB/s is a note onset and a -3 dB cut kills 'any ring slower than 60 dB/s'.

**Encoded at:** src/x32mcp/meters.py:572-578 + :714-718 (SyntheticRta: constant growth_db_per_s, `level -= cut` per frame, loop_period_s defaults to the 50 ms frame = a 17 m loop), src/x32mcp/fakedesk.py:44 ('bus fader/mute deliberately not coupled to ring growth'), tests/test_detector.py:232,257-258,285,331 (rings at 10-15 dB/s), tests/integration/test_cfs.py:262,333,409 (15-20 dB/s injected at -34..-30 dB), src/x32mcp/detector.py:45-48 docstring.

**Code depends on it at:** src/x32mcp/detector.py:103 (growth_max_db_per_s=60), :335-339 (onset guard zeroes growth and truncates the window), :341-342 (growth_min 6), :361-367 (only the 25 dB/6-frame override remains); device.yaml:802-803.

**Reality:** Loop physics: growth rate = excess loop gain / loop delay tau. tau = distance/343 m/s + ~1 ms desk latency: a wedge at 1.5 m is ~5 ms, FOH at 8 m ~25 ms. One 1 dB ring_out step past unity therefore grows at 200 dB/s (wedge) / 40 dB/s (FOH); even 0.3 dB of excess on a wedge is 60 dB/s. HANDOVER §4b#2: the successful M7 catch came through the override, not the growth path - consistent with real growth lying outside the 6..60 window.

**On a real desk:** On monitor wedges (the primary ring-out target, buses 1-16) every ring scores growth 0; it is emitted only by the override after 6 frames >= 25 dB prominent, i.e. at -10..0 dBFS on the RTA - a full-scale howl for 300-650 ms per notch, three times per ring-out (offline run: notches at RTA levels -10, -5, -5 dB). With override_prominence_db: 0 (documented knob) a 70 dB/s or 200 dB/s ring is NEVER detected and sits at clip. Probe: rate 70/100/200 dB/s -> detected only via override at -24/-20/0 dBFS.

**Offline test:** …/tests/test_assumptions_detector.py::test_a_short_loop_ring_is_scored_as_feedback_not_as_a_note_onset[tau,excess] and ::test_override_off_a_wedge_ring_is_never_detected_at_all (FAIL today); integration: …/test_assumptions_cfs.py::test_ring_out_against_a_loop_whose_growth_follows_the_fader (LoopCoupledRing: growth=(fader-onset)/tau, fakedesk.rta.loop_period_s=tau so the cut acts as (excess-cut)/tau) FAILS for tau=5 ms (notch at -10 dBFS). Make FakeDesk couple ring growth to the RTA-source bus fader this way permanently.

> **Verifier 1: CONFIRMED (high)** — All citations check out. detector.py:103 sets growth_max_db_per_s=60; detector.py:335-339 (the onset guard) truncates the growth window to the last sample and forces slope=0 whenever the LS slope exceeds 60 dB/s; :341-342 then scores growth 0; so confidence is capped at w_p+w_s=0.5<0.7 and the only remaining path is the override at :361-367 (>=25 dB prominent for >=6 frames). The docstring at detector.py:45-48 states the belief verbatim ("nothing regenerative rises this fast … feedback in a ring-out grows at a few to ~30 dB/s"). Nothing in docs/research/*.md or DESIGN §12 supports that number (DESIGN only specifies the +15 dB/s test ring; growth_max is an undocumented 'extension'). The synthetic sources encode it by fiat: meters.py SyntheticRta grows at a constant inject_ring(growth_db_per_s) independent of any fader, loop_period_s defaults to the 50 ms frame period (meters.py:613, docstring :572-578 'one −3 dB GEQ step kills any ring slower than 60 dB/s'), fakedesk.py:44 says 'The bus fader/mute is deliberately *not* coupled to ring growth', tests/test_detector.py:232,257-258,285 use 10-15 dB/s, tests/integration/test_cfs.py:262,333,409 inject 15-20 dB/s; no test anywhere feeds a ring faster than 60 dB/s (grep growth_max/onset in tests: none). Physics: regenerative growth rate ≈ excess loop gain (dB) / loop transit time; a wedge at ~1.5 m gives τ≈5-6 ms so even 0.3-0.5 dB of excess after a 1 dB ring_out step (cfs.py default step_db=1.0) is 60-100 dB/s — squarely in the 'onset' bucket. I reproduced offline with the product SyntheticRta + device.yaml config: 15/30/50 dB/s rings are caught by the growth path at ≈-30..-25 dBFS (conf 0.84-1.0); 70/100/200 dB/s rings are caught only when confidence is lifted to exactly 0.70 by the override, at -11/-5/0 dBFS (start -60, cap 0); with override_prominence_db=0 (device.yaml documents '0 disables the override') 70/100/200 dB/s rings are NEVER detected in 200 frames and sit at the cap. cfs.py _run_ringout/_notch_and_verify (1146-1215) HOLDs the master where it is (no back-off on detection), so on a real wedge the howl sits at limiter/clip for the 6 override frames plus write latency before the first -3 dB notch lands. No fallback the claimant missed: the override is the fallback and the claimant accounted for it. Minor caveats: the HANDOVER §4b#2 citation is only 'consistent with' (the handover attributes the M7 miss to a plateaued ring, not explicitly to fast growth), the exact dBFS numbers depend on start level, and very gentle unity crossings (<0.3 dB excess) on a wedge would still fall inside the 6..60 window — so 'every ring' is slightly overstated, but the majority case on short loops is as described. Severity high is defensible: on the primary ring-out target (monitor buses) the default config lets each ring reach full scale before acting (safety/hearing at a gig), and a documented knob (override=0) makes fast rings undetectable while the master keeps rising.

> **Verifier 2: CONFIRMED (medium)** — The assumption is real, is encoded exactly where the finding says, and the detector's growth path depends on it. SyntheticRta rings grow at a constant injected rate (meters.py:714-718, `r.level += r.growth*period_s - cut*period_s/loop_period_s`, loop_period_s defaulting to the 50 ms frame = a ~17 m loop; docstring 572-578 '−3 dB kills any ring slower than 60 dB/s'); fakedesk.py:44 states outright that 'the bus fader/mute is deliberately not coupled to ring growth'; every detector/CFS fixture injects 10–20 dB/s (test_detector.py:232,257-258,285; test_cfs.py:262,333,409,541). The detector then hard-codes growth_max_db_per_s=60 (detector.py:103) with an onset guard that zeroes growth and truncates the window for anything faster (335-339), and its docstring (45-48) asserts 'regenerative feedback in a ring-out grows at a few to ~30 dB/s'. That is a belief about the room, not the desk: for a regenerative loop the level gains the excess loop gain e once per loop delay τ, so R = e/τ; τ is ~5–6 ms for a wedge at 1.2–1.5 m (incl. ~0.8 ms converter latency), ~10 ms for tops at 3 m, ~25 ms only for distant FOH. ring_out's own +1 dB steps leave e uniformly in (0,1] dB, so on a wedge ~70 % of rings exceed 60 dB/s (e > 0.3 dB), on 3 m tops ~40 %; only long FOH paths land in the 6–60 window the fixtures certify. Real-desk evidence agrees: HANDOVER §4b #2 — the 8 kHz ring sat at confidence exactly 0.50 (growth 0) for 15 s and the successful catches came through the prominence override, not the growth term; the lead reviewer's REVIEW_REPORT §1.3 reaches the same conclusion ('the M7 false negative is the typical case, not a corner'). Nothing in meters.md (§1: 50 ms nominal frames; §5.1 decay affects fall only) suggests the analyser would slow the observed rise. My own probe against the shipped detector + device.yaml confirms the behaviour: rings at 10–60 dB/s are emitted by the growth path 2–5 frames after qualifying at −32…−24 dBFS (conf 0.72–1.0); at 70/100 dB/s the onset guard fires and emission comes only from the override at confidence exactly 0.70 with the band already at −11 / −5 dBFS; at 150/200 dB/s at the cap (−3 or 0 dBFS); with override_prominence_db: 0 (documented as a valid setting in device.yaml) 100 and 200 dB/s rings are never emitted at all (70 dB/s was eventually emitted at the cap via a window artefact, so the finding's 'never at 70' is slightly overstated, as is 'every ring on a wedge' — it is most, not all). Real-gig consequence: wedges are the primary target (README:216 promises detection 'in under 100 milliseconds'; README:234/725 'David's wedge', 'every wedge bus'), and on them the weighted growth term (w=0.5, the designed primary discriminator) is dead; each ring blooms to full PA level and is notched ~300 ms after reaching 25 dB prominence, i.e. ~0.5–0.7 s of loud-to-clipping howl per notch, up to budget times per bus, while the test suite certifies a quiet catch at −30 dBFS. Severity downgraded from high to medium: with shipped defaults the override does catch it, the −3 dB step reliably breaks a loop whose excess is ≤1 dB (reality decays faster than the fake's 50 ms loop model, so VERIFY is if anything conservative), no wrong or unsafe write is made, ring-out is a pre-show procedure where rings are expected, and the total-miss case requires the non-default override=0. It is nonetheless a genuine instance of the class the brief asks for (a fixture encoding room physics by fiat, code correctness depending on it), and the proposed offline test (couple FakeDesk ring growth to (fader−onset)/τ with loop_period_s=τ; assert detection before −20 dBFS for τ=5 ms) would fail today.

## E14. [medium] (cfs-detector-fixtures, confirmed) The analyser has no ballistics: a killed ring drops by the full amount on the very next frame, so VERIFY (>= 6 dB below the notch-time level on 2 consecutive frames within 1.5 s) measures the loop, not the meter - and /-prefs/rta/decay and /peakhold can be left wherever the operator had them.

**Encoded at:** src/x32mcp/meters.py:702-712 (SyntheticRta._compute: memoryless), src/x32mcp/fakedesk.py:159-160 (state carries rta/decay 1.0, rta/peakhold OFF, rta/det RMS but _meter_values :944-946 applies none of them), tests/integration/test_cfs.py:354-356 (VERIFY ok, drop >= 6 within a frame or two of a -3 dB cut).

**Code depends on it at:** src/x32mcp/cfs.py:1221-1252 (_verify_decay), :1200-1219 (a failed VERIFY deepens -6, -9 then ABORTs 'not tamed'), src/x32mcp/detector.py:115-117 (decay_verify_db 6 / 1.5 s / 2 frames), src/x32mcp/meters.py:860-941 (set_rta_source forces autogain=0 and det=PEAK but never writes rta/decay or rta/peakhold).

Lead note: set_rta_source never sets decay/peakhold. Code depends on the UNCONFIRMED fast fall with no fallback.

**On a real desk:** Operator left Peak Hold on (or decay at 8-16 s) on the METERS/RTA page: after a correct -3 dB notch the bar does not fall 6 dB within 1.5 s, VERIFY fails, CFS writes -6 then -9 into a band that was already tamed (6 dB of needless cut in the wedge mix), then ABORTs the ring-out and backs the master off 6 dB - every run, every bus. Long decay also holds transients as plateaus for the 6-frame override.

> **Verifier 2: PARTIAL (medium)** — Code facts all check out; the physical premise is an (honestly labelled) inference, and the stated consequence is overstated and in the safe direction, so PARTIAL at medium rather than CONFIRMED/high.

CONFIRMED in code: (1) SyntheticRta._compute (src/x32mcp/meters.py:702-712) has no display ballistics at all -- each frame is base+noise+rings-cuts, memoryless; the only "decay" is the loop model in _advance (:714-718: ring level -= cut dB per frame at the default loop_period_s=period_s, i.e. 60 dB/s for a 3 dB cut). (2) FakeDesk carries /-prefs/rta/decay=1.0, peakhold=OFF, det=RMS, autogain=ON in state (fakedesk.py:159-160) but _meter_values for type 15 (:944-946) just returns rta.last_frame -- none of decay/peakhold/det/autogain/gain touch the stream, so the M7 autogain defect could not have been caught either and nothing in the suite can exercise these prefs. (4) VERIFY (cfs.py:1221-1252, defaults detector.py:115-117 / device.yaml:820-822) needs >=6 dB below the notch-time level on 2 consecutive frames within 1.5 s, i.e. silently requires the bar to release faster than ~4 dB/s; a fail deepens -3 -> -6 -> -9 and the 4th plan returns None -> 'not tamed' ABORT (cfs.py:1070-1079, 1200-1219, 1160-1163). test_cfs.py:354-356 certifies ok/drop>=6 after one -3 dB step only because the fake has no ballistics.

Reality: meters.md 5.1 documents decay (logf 0.25..16, 'adjustable decay time', unit UNCONFIRMED) and peakhold (OFF,1..8) as RTA prefs; 4.2 marks 'do display prefs affect /meters/15' UNCONFIRMED; HANDOVER 4b#1 settled the one tested member of that class (autogain) as YES, and the code itself already treats det -- added in the same firmware drop as decay/peakhold (5.3) -- as reaching the stream. No source proves decay/peakhold reach /meters/15 (peak hold in particular may well be a client-drawn overlay; the blob has only 100 values), so this is inference, but per the brief an unhedged dependency on an UNCONFIRMED item is a finding, and the fix (write decay->0.25, peakhold->0 in set_rta_source, report both) is two lines of the pattern already used for autogain/det.

Skeptical downgrade: I built the offline probe the finding proposes (worktree wt/verify-rta-ballistics, tests/integration/test_rta_ballistics.py, commit 40f1f18: a display stage on the FakeDesk RTA driven by its own /-prefs/rta/decay and /peakhold, modelled as linear release of D s per 40 dB and an N-second hold -- an assumed model). Results with the exact test_ring_out_closed_loop scenario: decay 1 or 4 -> one -3 dB notch, DONE; decay 16 alone -> VERIFY fails once (2.6 dB drop), passes at -6 dB: ONE needless 3 dB step, no abort; peakhold 3 -> -9 dB then passes (6 dB needless); peakhold 8, or peakhold 2 + decay 16 -> three failed VERIFYs, ABORT 'not tamed', master backed off to -18. So 'deepens to -9 and ABORTs every run, every bus' only holds if peak hold reaches the stream with a long hold (the less likely premise); long decay alone costs one extra step. Every error is in the conservative direction (more cut, master lowered, run stopped) -- nobody is endangered and CFS is not raising gain on garbage; the gig-level harm is a duller wedge and a ring-out tool that spuriously reports an untamable ring on a desk whose engineer (plausibly -- peak hold is a common manual ring-out habit) left those prefs up. That is 'tool fails spuriously / reports wrong state at a gig' = medium. M7 on the real desk saw notches verify, consistent with Jim's desk sitting at benign defaults, which is exactly the operator-dependence the finding names. Also already raised by the lead in docs/REVIEW_REPORT.md 1.2(c).

## E15. [medium] (cfs-detector-fixtures, confirmed) Bus masters are independent: writing /bus/01/mix/fader moves only Bus 1.

**Encoded at:** src/x32mcp/fakedesk.py:675-684 (_store has no link ganging; /config/buslink/* and /config/linkcfg/fdrmute are stored but inert), no test in tests/integration/test_cfs.py sets a bus link; preflight (src/x32mcp/provision.py:627-663) never reads /config/buslink or linkcfg.

**Code depends on it at:** src/x32mcp/cfs.py:1115-1124 (_write_master on ses.target only), :1174-1197 (raise loop), :1324-1359 (_restore_master restores one bus), src/x32mcp/provision.py:627-663 (no link check, mic discovery for one bus).

**Reality:** scales_params.md §10: /config/buslink/1-2..15-16 ON/OFF with /config/linkcfg/fdrmute selecting whether linked pairs share fader+mute (desk default ON). Stereo wedge pairs and IEM mixes are routinely linked odd/even buses; the console gangs the partner's fader on any control source, OSC included (engineering knowledge of the desk; not contradicted by research, not modelled by the fake).

**On a real desk:** ring_out(1) on a linked 1-2 pair raises Bus 2's wedge in lock-step while the RTA watches Bus 1 only: Bus 2 (different mic in front of it) rings unseen and CFS keeps stepping; its GEQ side (FX5R) is never notched; the report claims Bus 2 was untouched. ring_out_system then rings out Bus 2 and drags Bus 1 (already at its end level) up again.

**Offline test:** Teach FakeDesk._store to mirror mix/fader and mix/on to the partner when /config/buslink/<pair> and /config/linkcfg/fdrmute are ON (and push the partner leaf); add test: link 1-2, ring_out(1) -> expect preflight blocker 'Bus 1 is linked to Bus 2' (or a paired session that watches/notches both sides); today Bus 2's fader ends at Bus 1's end level with no mention in the report.

> **Verifier 1: CONFIRMED (high)** — Citations check out. docs/research/scales_params.md §10 (lines 638-639) lists `/config/buslink/1-2..15-16` OFF/ON and `/config/linkcfg/hadly|eq|dyn|fdrmute` as "what a stereo link shares" — i.e. fader+mute are a shared parameter of a linked pair; device.yaml:441-442 itself comments "linking re-syncs the pair's parameters". The research does not separately verify that an OSC fader write gangs the partner (the claimant correctly labels that engineering knowledge; the only link-related research item is fx_routing_scenes.md §13 #6, UNCONFIRMED, about inserts on stereo-linked buses), but link ganging is implemented in the console firmware for every control source and is standard desk behaviour, and the brief explicitly admits physical/engineering common sense as a source. The one embellishment is "(desk default ON)" for fdrmute, which §10 does not state (it is the factory default, but not research-cited) — minor, not load-bearing.

Fake/test side verified empirically: FakeDesk (src/x32mcp/fakedesk.py:675-684 `_store`) has no link logic anywhere (grep for 'link' in fakedesk.py finds only the `mono/link` default); with `/config/buslink/1-2`=1 and `/config/linkcfg/fdrmute`=1 set, writing /bus/01/mix/fader to -5 dB leaves /bus/02/mix/fader at 0.0 and muting bus 1 leaves bus 2 on. The fake also defaults linkcfg/* to 0 (OFF), unlike a real desk. No test under tests/integration (test_cfs.py, test_desk.py, test_fakedesk.py, test_patches_desk.py) mentions a link; the only link test is set_channel_config's chlink write (test_server_tools.py:459). The fake's own scene 2 names bus 01/02 "Wedge L"/"Wedge R" — exactly the pair an operator would link.

Code side verified: cfs.py:1115-1124 `_write_master` writes only ses.target via Desk.set_level; the raise loop 1174-1197 reads back only that bus; `_restore_master` 1324-1359 raw-writes/reads one address; `_finalize_levels` 1254-1292 leaves the target at raised-minus-margin on DONE; provision.preflight 627-663 reads strip/GEQ/mics/master for one bus and never reads /config/buslink or linkcfg; nothing in cfs.py or provision.py references links at all (grep). No fallback exists that the claimant missed.

Consequence on a real desk with an odd/even linked pair (side fills, stereo wedges, stereo IEM): ring_out(N) drags bus N±1's master up step-for-step, unmonitored by the RTA (source = bus N) and unprotected by notches (only the FX L side for bus N is cut; dual-mono GEQ2 sides are independent per provision.py:20), DONE leaves the partner permanently raised, and the report/events name only bus N — an unintended write to a bus the tool never named, i.e. the rubric's "wrong write / safety" class. Offline test proposal (teach FakeDesk._store to mirror mix/fader+mix/on to the partner when buslink pair and linkcfg/fdrmute are ON, push the partner leaf, default linkcfg to ON; assert preflight blocks or the session handles both sides) is sound and would fail today.

> **Verifier 2: CONFIRMED (medium)** — The factual claims hold. (1) FakeDesk encodes bus independence: src/x32mcp/fakedesk.py:675-686 (_store) writes exactly one address; there is no chlink/buslink/linkcfg handling anywhere in fakedesk.py (grep 'link' hits only the 'mono/link' default at :153). Demonstrated in-process: with /config/buslink/1-2=ON and /config/linkcfg/fdrmute=ON, set_value('/bus/01/mix/fader', -5.0) leaves /bus/02/mix/fader at 0.0 and muting bus 1 leaves bus 2 on. FakeDesk also defaults linkcfg/* to OFF. (2) No product code reads bus links: grep for buslink/linkcfg over src/ returns nothing; preflight (src/x32mcp/provision.py:627-663) checks GEQ, mics, mute, -inf master, start level only; _write_master (cfs.py:1115-1124), the raise loop (:1174-1197), _finalize_levels and _restore_master (:1324-1359) address ses.target alone; the only link-aware code is set_channel_config writing /config/chlink (server.py:1357-1407). No integration test sets a bus link (tests/integration/test_server_tools.py:459 only asserts the chlink value was stored). (3) Research: scales_params.md §10 (lines 638-639) documents /config/buslink/1-2..15-16 and /config/linkcfg/hadly|eq|dyn|fdrmute as 'what a stereo link shares'; fx_routing_scenes.md §13 item 6 explicitly lists stereo-linked-bus insert behaviour as UNCONFIRMED, and §3.4 (line 303) notes stereo strips take the FXnL/FXnR pair — so the research itself flags linked buses as an unverified area and the code has no fallback (no blocker, no warning). Desk-side ganging of fader+mute for linked pairs regardless of control source (surface, X32-Edit, OSC) is standard X32 behaviour (the link lives in the console's parameter engine; remote apps rely on it) and nothing in research contradicts it, so the FakeDesk does NOT match the real desk here — not refutable.
Skeptical downgrade of severity from high to medium: the precondition is a non-default operator configuration (buslink pairs default OFF); the commonest linked-bus use, stereo IEM mixes, has no acoustic loop and would rarely carry a ring-out GEQ; when a linked wedge/side-fill pair is rung out, the partner is raised only to the same level as the target (never past min(policy ceiling, master_ceiling_db, target_gain_db)), back-off/restore writes gang the partner back down the same way, and a ring in the unwatched loop that bleeds into the watched bus ends in VERIFY-fail -> deepen -> ABORT + abort_backoff rather than an unbounded climb; it happens at soundcheck under a Tier-2 confirmation with the engineer present. What remains real and unmitigated: an unrequested level change on a bus outside the session, notches spent on the wrong GEQ side (or none on FXnR), a partner wedge left at max-3 dB with un-notched rings going into the show, ring_out_system re-raising the already-finished partner, and a report that never mentions Bus 2 — i.e. the tool reports wrong state and can misbehave at a gig with stereo-linked monitors, but bounded and conditional rather than a default-path safety failure. The proposed offline test (teach FakeDesk._store to mirror mix/fader+mix/on to the odd/even partner when buslink/<pair> and linkcfg/fdrmute are ON, then expect a preflight blocker/warning 'Bus 1 is linked to Bus 2') is the right shape and would fail today.

## E16. [medium] (cfs-detector-fixtures, confirmed) RTA dB values are absolute: -45 dB (min_level_db), the 8 dB floor margin and the M7 numbers (-51.7 floor, -25 howl) mean the same thing on every desk, so only autogain needs forcing - the manual /-prefs/rta/gain can stay wherever it is.

**Encoded at:** src/x32mcp/fakedesk.py:159 ('rta/gain': 24.0 in state) vs :944-946 (never applied to the frames); SyntheticRta levels are generated directly in 'RTA dB'; tests/test_detector.py floors -30..-52 and tests/integration streams sit comfortably above -45.

**Code depends on it at:** src/x32mcp/detector.py:99,382 (min_level_db gate), device.yaml:797 (-45, 'one room's number'), src/x32mcp/cfs.py:870-876 (floor+margin gate), src/x32mcp/meters.py:906-916 (clears autogain, never reads/writes rta.get('gain_param') - there is none in device.yaml:758-766).

**Reality:** meters.md §5.1: /-prefs/rta/gain linf 0..60 dB in 6 dB steps; §5.3 (X32 manual): 'when [Auto Gain is] disabled, the gain can be manually adjusted … for comparing absolute frequency band levels'; §4.2: whether gain shifts /meters/15 is UNCONFIRMED but 'probably does'; HANDOVER §4b#1 proved the display-gain stage (autogain) does reach the stream. With autogain forced OFF the stream sits at whatever manual gain the desk holds (Jim's desk: unknown; fake: 24).

**On a real desk:** A desk left at gain +60: every band reads 36+ dB hotter than at M7 -> floor rumble and walk-in music clear the -45 gate everywhere and the 40/80 Hz false-notch failure (§4b#3) returns, spending the budget; a desk at 0 dB when M7 was at +24: a ring must be 24 dB louder in the room before it even qualifies. Reports/detection_log levels are not comparable between gigs.

**Offline test:** Make FakeDesk add state['/-prefs/rta/gain'] (when autogain is 0) to every SyntheticRta value before encoding, clamp to [-128,0]; parametrise test_feedback_watch_closed_loop over gain 0/24/60 -> expect identical behaviour because set_rta_source pinned gain to a declared value (add rta.gain_param + RtaSourceResult.gain_set); today detection latency/false positives change with the gain.

> **Verifier 1: CONFIRMED (medium)** — Both halves of the claim hold. (1) Encoded: src/x32mcp/fakedesk.py:159 seeds state 'rta/gain': 24.0 and 'rta/autogain': True, but _meter_values (fakedesk.py:944-946) returns self.rta.last_frame/tick() values untouched — neither manual gain nor autogain is ever applied to the type-15 frames, so no test can observe a gain-dependent stream. SyntheticRta (meters.py ~559-598) and tests/test_detector.py:88-93 generate levels directly in a fixed 'RTA dB' frame (-30 tilted floor; synthetic base -25@100 Hz..-55@10 kHz). (2) Depended on: device.yaml:797 min_level_db -45 (comment at :790-796 explicitly says it is 'one room' calibrated from M7's -51.7/-25 readings); detector.py:99 default and detector.py:382 gate `vals[i] >= cfg.min_level_db` (the >=25 dB prominence override also only applies to candidates that passed this gate); cfs.py:870-876 `gate = max(cfg.min_level_db, floor + margin)` — calibration only ever RAISES the gate; meters.py:906-916 set_rta_source clears autogain and sets det=PEAK but never touches /-prefs/rta/gain, and device.yaml rta: block (758-767) has source/pos/options/stat/autogain/det params only — no gain_param. grep confirms no other code reads or writes rta/gain. (3) Research: meters.md §5.1 table (line 395) '/-prefs/rta/gain float linf [0,60,6] dB'; §5.3 (line 446) quotes the manual 'when disabled, the gain can be manually adjusted … for comparing absolute frequency band levels'; §4.2 (line 307) 'UNCONFIRMED: whether the reported dB is affected by /-prefs/rta/gain / autogain … gain/autogain probably do shift them — test with a known tone'; HANDOVER §4b#1 (lines 154-156) confirms autogain did move every band of the live stream (337 false detections), so the display gain stage is upstream of /meters/15 and manual gain almost certainly offsets it too. Per the brief, depending on an UNCONFIRMED item without a fallback is itself a finding. Fallback check: _calibrate_floor is a partial mitigation only — it runs in _open_session (cfs.py:890) BEFORE _arm starts the frame source and before set_rta_source (cfs.py:900-923), bails after 0.3 s with no frame (cfs.py:852-858), and can never lower the gate, so a desk whose manual gain is below M7's leaves real rings under -45 and undetected (including the established-feedback override), while a hotter desk either inflates candidates or, if calibration did run, pushes the gate toward the 0 dB clip ceiling; report levels are not comparable across desks either way. Minor imprecision: SyntheticRta's HF end (-55 dB) is not 'comfortably above -45', but that does not affect the finding. Medium is right: the tool mis-detects/misses at a gig depending on an operator-set encoder; a wrong GEQ write additionally needs growth or 25 dB prominence, so not automatically 'high'. Fix/test as proposed: model gain (+autogain) in FakeDesk._meter_values, add rta.gain_param and pin it in set_rta_source, parametrise the closed-loop test over gain 0/24/60.

> **Verifier 2: CONFIRMED (medium)** — The finding holds up on every checkable point. (1) The product never reads, writes or reports /-prefs/rta/gain: set_rta_source (src/x32mcp/meters.py:860-960) writes source/pos, clears Solo Priority, forces autogain=0 and det=PEAK, and returns RtaSourceResult with no gain field; device.yaml rta: (758-766) declares no gain_param; grep for 'rta/gain' in src/ hits only the fake's state dict and node field lists. Forcing autogain OFF hands the analyser to whatever manual gain (linf 0..60 dB, meters.md §5.1) the desk's global prefs hold — a value the code neither knows nor pins. (2) The detector's only absolute threshold, min_level_db (detector.py:97, gate at :382 `vals[i] >= cfg.min_level_db`), is -45 in device.yaml (~797), a constant derived from one session's readings (-51.7 floor / -25 howl, HANDOVER §4b#3) at one unknown gain state; the prominence override is also behind this gate, so it does not rescue a deafened detector. (3) The would-be mitigation, _calibrate_floor (cfs.py:824-877), is dead in production: it runs inside _open_session (cfs.py:890) before _arm starts the LiveMeters (cfs.py:923), so no frame arrives within _FLOOR_FIRST_FRAME_S=0.3 s and the fixed -45 stands (the only test of it, tests/integration/test_cfs.py:660-695, pre-starts a fake Room source and calls _calibrate_floor directly). No frequency window exists either (no min_hz/max_hz anywhere), so -45 absolute is the sole defence against the 40/80 Hz false notches and the sole quiet-ring gate. (4) The fake encodes the blind spot: fakedesk.py:159 holds 'rta/gain': 24.0 and 'rta/autogain': True as inert leaves; _meter_values (fakedesk.py:944-946) returns SyntheticRta values untouched, so neither autogain (which is exactly why M7 defect #1 passed 934 tests) nor manual gain can ever perturb a test; no test references rta/gain beyond node-field ordering (tests/test_nodes.py:231, test_descriptor.py:437, test_device_yaml.py:348). Skeptical caveats, which are why this stays medium rather than high: whether gain reaches /meters/15 is formally UNCONFIRMED (meters.md §4.2) — but §4b#1 proved the same encoder's autogain mode does reach the stream and the manual (§5.3) describes manual gain as the alternative setting of that same display-gain stage, so the inference is strong, and the brief counts unfallbacked dependence on an UNCONFIRMED item as a finding; and /-prefs are global console prefs that persist on Jim's own X32 Rack, so on the same untouched desk gig-day scale equals M7 scale. It bites on any other desk, after a reset, or the moment an engineer (or X32-Edit) nudges encoder 4 on the RTA page — common during soundcheck, and more likely once Claude has switched their autogain off. Consequences are real, not cosmetic: gain above M7's → walk-in music/rumble clears -45 and the 40/80 Hz false notches return (wrong GEQ writes on mains, budget spent); gain 24 dB below M7's → a howl 4 dB louder than the one M7 already called 'missed' never qualifies, so feedback_watch sits silent and ring_out keeps raising the master into audible feedback before any cut. Fix is cheap (add rta.gain_param, pin a declared gain in set_rta_source, report gain_set; make FakeDesk add state['/-prefs/rta/gain'] offset/autogain normalisation to frames and parametrise the closed-loop test over 0/24/60). Verdict: CONFIRMED, medium.

## E17. [medium] (cfs-detector-fixtures, confirmed) The spectrum's background is a noisy continuum some tens of dB under any peak, so 'prominence >= 25 dB for 6 frames' singles out an established howl.

**Encoded at:** tests/test_detector.py:88-93 (floor -30-0.22*i +-1.5), :480-493 (_plateaued_ring floor -85), src/x32mcp/meters.py:598-599,707 (base -25..-55 +-3 dB noise) - no synthetic frame ever contains the value -128.0.

**Code depends on it at:** src/x32mcp/detector.py:278-288 (prominence = level - median(neighbours)), :361-367 (override: >= 25 dB for >= 6 frames emits regardless of growth), device.yaml override_prominence_db 25 / override_persistence_frames 6.

**Reality:** meters.md §4.2/§6.3: RTA silence is exactly 0x8000 = -128.0; §2.2: level meters bottom out at exactly -128; HANDOVER §4a: on the real desk 'values were all floor/zero because the desk was silent'; §4b#2: the real ring was '60 dB-prominent' - i.e. its neighbours were pinned at the floor. Against a pinned floor every audible isolated band is 60-90 dB 'prominent'; the 25 dB threshold fitted to that observation carries no information.

**On a real desk:** During a quiet ring_out (the recommended condition) any steady narrow-band sound >= -45 dB is notched within 300 ms with zero growth: a tuner/reference tone, a phone notification, a keyboard's held organ note (fundamental AND each harmonic are separately 'isolated' -> several notches), LED-wall/PSU whine near 15 kHz. Probe: steady -40 dB tone amid -128 -> notched at frame 5 with prominence 88 dB; 440 Hz organ + harmonics -> bands 45 and 55 both notched.

**Offline test:** …/tests/test_assumptions_detector.py::test_prominence_against_a_pinned_floor_makes_any_isolated_tone_an_established_howl (FAILS today). Make SyntheticRta pin quiet bands to exactly -128 (base well below -128+noise outside injected content) so every detector test runs against a real floor; cap prominence at (level - max(neighbour, noise_floor_estimate)) or require the override to see a non-floored local background / harmonic-family absence (REVIEW_BRIEF §1).

> **Verifier 1: CONFIRMED (medium)** — All citations check out and the failure reproduces exactly as claimed.

Encoded assumption (verified): tests/test_detector.py:87-92 floor_db = -30-0.22*i + bumps + 3*sin, ±1.5 dB noise (a continuum at -30..-52 dB); tests/test_detector.py:480-493 _plateaued_ring uses a flat -85 floor and the tests pick the peak's prominence directly (60 dB 'howl' vs 15 dB 'held note') rather than deriving it from a physical tone level over a physical floor; src/x32mcp/meters.py:598-599 SyntheticRta base -25 dB@100 Hz .. -55 dB@10 kHz, :707 ±noise_db(3) + wobble — no synthetic frame ever reaches -128 except via cuts; FakeDesk (fakedesk.py:301) uses that same SyntheticRta. No detector/CFS test feeds a -128 background.

Code dependence (verified): detector.py:278-288 prominence = level - median(±3 neighbours); detector.py:361-367 override emits when prominence >= override_prominence_db and frames >= override_persistence_frames regardless of growth; device.yaml:812-813 sets 25 dB / 6 frames, min_level_db -45 (line 797). The in-code justification (detector.py:352-356, device.yaml:810) 'musical content is harmonically spread, so tens of dB of prominence in a single band is feedback by construction' is physically wrong for this measure: harmonics of a note land +10, +16, +20 bands away, outside the ±3-band median window, so each partial of any tonal sound over a quiet background is individually 'isolated'. cfs._consume (cfs.py:1034-1043) passes detections straight to _notch (watch) or HOLD->NOTCH (ring_out) with no further discrimination.

Research (verified): meters.md §4.2 '-128.0 (0x8000 … the floor / "no signal")', §6 gotcha 3 'RTA silence = 0x8000 = −128.0 dB exactly', §2.2 level meters bottom out at exactly -128 dBFS; HANDOVER §4a 'values were all floor/zero because the desk was silent'; §4b#2 '60 dB-prominent 8 kHz ring'; GIG_CHECKLIST.md:41 'Stage empty and silent; ring out each wedge' confirms quiet ring-out is the recommended condition. (Minor overreach: the claimant infers the M7 ring's neighbours were pinned at -128; §4b says quiet music was playing, so that is unproven — not load-bearing.)

Reproduction with the shipped device.yaml config: steady -40 dB tone at band 45 amid -128 -> Detection at frame 5 (6th frame, 300 ms), prominence 88.0 dB, slope 0.0, confidence 0.70; 440 Hz note with harmonics (-35/-41/-45/-50) -> bands 45, 55 and 61 all emitted (three separate notches). The claimant's test tests/test_assumptions_detector.py::test_prominence_against_a_pinned_floor_makes_any_isolated_tone_an_established_howl in worktree assumptions-cfs-detector-fixtures FAILS today exactly as stated.

Mitigation the claimant did not mention: cfs._calibrate_floor (cfs.py:824-878, floor_margin_db 8) raises min_level_db to (loudest band during the 2 s arm sample)+8, so a steady source already present and loudest at arm time (e.g. PSU/LED-wall whine) is gated out; 'any steady narrow-band sound >= -45 dB' is therefore overstated. It does not cover the principal scenarios (tuner tone, phone notification, held note, anything starting after arm or >8 dB above the arm-time peak), and in watch mode notches are applied with no VERIFY. In ring_out, VERIFY runs after the write; with the PRE insert the RTA measures the cut, so the notch is deepened to -6 dB and 'passes', leaving a wrong cut and spending budget (or deepens to -9 and aborts the run spuriously). Damage is bounded (cuts only, <= -9 dB, <= 6 bands), so medium is the right severity rather than high.

> **Verifier 2: CONFIRMED (medium)** — The mechanism is real, reproducible offline, and contradicted by the project's own real-desk observations; I keep it at medium rather than high only because the resulting wrong writes are bounded (cuts only, -3 dB steps, -9 dB max, per-bus budget) and ring_out is procedurally run on a silent stage.

1. The fixtures do encode a loud continuum background that the real desk does not have. tests/test_detector.py SyntheticRta.floor_db (l.87-92) is -30-0.22*i (+bumps, +-1.5 noise) = -30..-52 dB; src/x32mcp/meters.py SyntheticRta (l.598-599 defaults level_100hz_db=-25, level_10khz_db=-55, noise 3; l.707 clamp) is -25..-55 dB and is what FakeDesk serves on /meters/15 (fakedesk.py:301). Reality: HANDOVER 4a - silent desk reads floor (-128, meters.md 6.3 / 4.2: 0x8000 exactly); HANDOVER 4b#3 - WITH background music playing the loudest band on the real desk was -51.7 dB, i.e. the real bed sits 25-70 dB below the synthetic one. HANDOVER 4b#2 - the real ring was 60 dB prominent as computed by this very prominence code, which proves the real analyser's +-2/+-3 neighbours of a steady tone sit at the (very low) background, not on filter skirts.

2. Code correctness depends on it. detector.py:361-367 emits any candidate with prominence >= 25 dB for >= 6 frames regardless of growth (device.yaml 812-813), justified by the comment 'musical content is harmonically spread, so tens of dB of prominence in a single band is feedback by construction'. That is false for the +-3-band median: harmonics 1-3 of any pitched note are 10, 6, 4 bands apart, so each is an isolated single band whose prominence = note level - inter-harmonic background. Every 'held note must not be notched' test places the note 15-20 dB above the synthetic floor (test_held_note_not_detected above_floor_db=20, test_plateau_and_transient 18/20, test_the_override_needs_real_prominence_not_just_patience 15 dB) - i.e. under the 25 dB override only because the fixture floor is loud. The 25 dB threshold was fitted between fixture notes (<=20) and the one real ring (60); real notes are not bounded at 20.

3. Probe with device.yaml config (min_level -45, override 25/6): steady -40 dB tone amid -128 -> emitted at frame 5, prominence 88, slope 0; same amid a realistic -95 preamp/room floor -> prominence 54.6, emitted frame 5; held 440 Hz note with harmonic series at -30 amid -100 -> bands 45 (442 Hz, 70 dB), 55 (884 Hz, 64 dB) and 61 (1.34 kHz, 37 dB) all emitted at frame 5; a sung note at -25 dBFS over an M7-like quiet music bed (-73 dB at 440 Hz) -> bands 45/55/61 emitted at 46/44/28 dB prominence, re-emitted each cooldown (-> -6, -9). Zero growth in every case.

4. Real-gig consequence. The finder framed it around ring_out with stray tones (tuner, phone, PSU whine) - those are partly marginal against the -45 dBFS gate and GIG_CHECKLIST l.41 asks for a silent stage. The stronger bite is feedback_watch, whose documented use (README l.231: 'I'm bringing up David's wedge - catch anything that rings') has a live performer on the mic: any sustained vowel/organ/flute note in a sparse passage is notched at its fundamental and low harmonics within 300 ms, the singer hears the wedge go hollow at their own pitch, and 3 of the 6 budget bands are gone before anything rings - the same 'budget spent before the real feedback' failure that ended M7. README l.227-228's claim that growth protects sustained vocal notes is no longer true once prominence >= 25, and the tests certify it only against the fixture floor. Also during ring_out an engineer's own 'two... twooo' check or a keyboardist noodling into the bus triggers it.

5. Not refutable as 'FakeDesk matches research': research says silence is exactly -128 and the handover says real backgrounds are <= -52 even with music; the fakes never go below ~-60 and never emit -128. Not already mitigated: min_level_db -45 does not help (performer signal is well above it), no frequency window exists yet (grep: none in device.yaml/detector.py/cfs.py), and raising the override threshold cannot separate a 46-70 dB-prominent note from the 60 dB ring - only a harmonic-family/stability test can, which is what REVIEW_BRIEF 1 asks for (so the area is partially anticipated, but the specific fixture-floor mechanism that makes the override look safe is a valid new instance of the 2 class).

Offline test as proposed is right: give SyntheticRta (both copies) a real floor (quiet bands pinned to -128 or a -90..-100 preamp floor, notes/harmonics at realistic absolute levels) and add held-note/organ-note streams asserting no detection - they fail today.

## E18. [medium] (cfs-detector-fixtures, confirmed) The ring-out GEQ is flat when a session starts, and any cut already on it is a previous CFS notch that should be deepened in preference to opening the ringing band.

**Encoded at:** tests/integration/test_cfs.py:141-154 (provision() loads a fresh GEQ2 and asserts flat / [0.0]*31 before every closed-loop test), tests/test_detector.py:444-453 (existing cuts only ever AT the detected band).

**Code depends on it at:** src/x32mcp/detector.py:529-536 (every existing band < 0 dB becomes a Notch), :556-562 (plan: nearest existing notch within merge_adjacent_bands=1 is deepened before the target band is considered), src/x32mcp/cfs.py:886 (existing = all 31 preflight gains), provision preflight only WARNS 'GEQ already carries cuts' (provision.py:655-658) and knows matched_session but cfs ignores it.

**Reality:** A monitor GEQ inserted on a wedge bus normally already carries the engineer's house curve (LF rumble cuts, a presence dip) - that is why FX slot 5 'already holds a GEQ2' on Jim's desk (HANDOVER §4a 'Desk facts'). Those cuts are not feedback notches and sit on arbitrary bands adjacent to where rings occur.

**On a real desk:** Engineer's -4 dB at 2 kHz, ring at 2.5 kHz: CFS writes 2 kHz -> -7, VERIFY fails, 2 kHz -> -9, VERIFY fails, only then 2.5 kHz -> -3. Two wasted HOLD/VERIFY cycles (3 s of ringing while the master is held up) and the engineer's curve mangled by 5 dB on a band that was not ringing. Verified with NotchController(existing={21:-4}): plan sequence [(21,-7),(21,-9),(22,-3),(22,-6)].

**Offline test:** Unit: NotchController(cfg, geq, validate, budget=6, existing={21:-4.0}); plan(det at 2500 Hz) must return band 22 at -3 first (fails today). Integration: fset('/fx/5/par/21', (15-4)/30) before feedback_watch, inject 2400 Hz ring, assert the first cfs.notch is band 22. Fix: only treat existing cuts as mergeable notches when preflight matched them to a CFS report (geq.matched_session), otherwise record them as foreign gains (still the base for cuts-only validation) and never deepen them by adjacency.

> **Verifier 1: CONFIRMED (medium)** — Code citations check out exactly. src/x32mcp/detector.py:529-536 turns every `existing` band with db<0 into a Notch (session_id="", detections=0); plan() at :552-562 sorts self._notches by distance to the target band and deepens the first one within cfg.merge_adjacent_bands (default 1, detector.py:114 / device.yaml:819) that _can_deepen and _affordable, before ever considering the target band. cfs.py:886 builds `existing` from all 31 preflight bands_db with no provenance filter, and `matched_session` is computed in provision.py:341-362/417 but never read by cfs.py (grep: only provision.py and server.py display it). provision.py:656-659 only appends a warning for a non-flat GEQ; module doc (provision.py:19-21) confirms a slot already holding GEQ2 is 'used as is' (not reloaded/flattened), so foreign cuts survive into the session. Reproduced empirically with the repo venv: NotchController(DetectorConfig(), ISO31, validate, budget=6, existing={21:-4.0}) planning four detections at 2500 Hz yields [(21,-7.0),(21,-9.0),(22,-3.0),(22,-6.0)] — the engineer's 2 kHz cut is driven to -9 before the ringing 2.5 kHz band is touched. In ring_out mode each wasted step costs a decay_verify_s=1.5 s VERIFY window (cfs.py:1200-1219, detector.py:116), so ~3 s of extra ringing; in feedback_watch mode (no VERIFY) it costs two cooldown re-detections. Test-side encoding is as cited: tests/integration/test_cfs.py:141-154 provisions a fresh GEQ2 and asserts flat/[0.0]*31, and tests/test_detector.py:444-453 only exercises pre-existing cuts located exactly at the detected band (22 @ 2400 Hz), never a foreign cut on an adjacent band. Reality citation: HANDOVER §4a (line 137-138) does say 'FX slot 5 already holds a GEQ2 (CFS² provisioning should reuse it)'; it does not literally say that GEQ carried a house curve — that part is the claimant's inference — but the underlying claim (a monitor/main GEQ on a working desk routinely carries non-feedback cuts on arbitrary bands) is sound live-audio common sense, which the task accepts as a source. DESIGN.md:536 documents the adjacent-merge as intended, but that is precisely the baked-in assumption (all existing cuts are prior CFS notches), not a fallback. Mitigations are partial only: cuts-only policy and the -9 dB cap bound the damage, and preflight warns; nothing prevents the wrong-band write. Medium is appropriate: a wrong write to a non-ringing band plus delayed suppression of the real ring, bounded and warned about, not a safety/boost issue.

> **Verifier 2: CONFIRMED (medium)** — The code does exactly what the finding says. NotchController.__init__ (src/x32mcp/detector.py:529-536) turns every pre-existing band gain < 0 dB into a Notch, and plan() (detector.py:551-565) walks self._notches sorted by distance to the target band and deepens the nearest one within merge_adjacent_bands (default 1, detector.py:114 / DESIGN.md:279) BEFORE it even considers opening the target band. CfsManager._open_session (cfs.py:886-888) feeds it `existing` = all 31 preflight gains with no provenance, and cfs.py never references matched_session (grep: only provision.py and server.py do). I reproduced the claimed sequence with the repo's venv: NotchController(DetectorConfig(), iso31, ..., budget=6, existing={21:-4.0}) planning a 2500 Hz detection five times yields [(21,-7.0),(21,-9.0),(22,-3.0),(22,-6.0),(22,-9.0)]; likewise existing={7:-6,8:-3} with a 125 Hz ring yields [(8,-6),(8,-9),(9,-3),...]. In ring_out mode _notch_and_verify (cfs.py:1200-1219) re-plans after each failed 1.5 s VERIFY, so the two wrong-band writes cost two full verify windows (~3 s of sustained ringing at HOLD) plus one budget unit, and leave the operator's 2 kHz band 5 dB deeper than they set it; in watch mode the detector re-emits once per cooldown_s=1 s, so a growing howl during a show runs ~2 s longer before the ringing band is touched. The report then lists band 21 as a CFS notch.

The assumption is genuinely baked into the fixtures: every closed-loop integration test starts from provision() (tests/integration/test_cfs.py:83-85), which loads a fresh GEQ2 over DES2 and is asserted flat / [0.0]*31 (test_cfs.py:152-154); the only non-flat GEQ any integration test sees is CFS's own previous notch (test_cfs.py:291-295, matched_session). The unit test test_existing_notches_and_policy_rejection (tests/test_detector.py:444-453) goes further and positively encodes the behaviour: existing={22:-6,10:-2,5:+3} — a -2 dB cut (off CFS's -3 dB grid, so necessarily foreign) and a +3 dB boost (CFS never boosts) — and asserts that a 200 Hz ring 'would need budget' on band 10, i.e. merges into the foreign 160 Hz cut rather than opening band 11.

Skeptical checks that did not refute it: (1) 'By design' — DESIGN.md:536 says plan 'merges into an adjacent existing notch', but the design's premise is that cuts on the ring-out GEQ are ring-out notches; that premise is the operator/desk assumption under review, and the intended deployment contradicts it: plan_setup reuses whatever GEQ/TEQ is already inserted on the bus (test_cfs.py:159-160 plan2.reuse; provision.py module doc), validate_ringout_eqs accepts any curve including boosts with ok=True (provision.py:396-421, flat is informational), and HANDOVER §4a explicitly directs 'FX slot 5 already holds a GEQ2 (CFS² provisioning should reuse it)'. A monitor/main GEQ that an engineer already inserted is, in normal live practice, carrying a curve. (2) Mitigation — preflight does warn 'GEQ already carries cuts' (provision.py:656-659) but does not say CFS will deepen them, and nothing blocks or changes behaviour; matched_session is computed and then ignored by cfs. (3) Physics — on a real GEQ2 an extra 3-5 dB at the adjacent 1/3-octave band bleeds ~1-2 dB into the ringing band, so in ring_out (1 dB raise steps, loop gain barely over unity) the first wrong-band cut might even pass VERIFY; that does not rescue the tool, it just changes the failure to 'engineer's band mangled, ringing band never notched, rings again on the next raise'. The FakeDesk cannot show either variant today because SyntheticRta.set_geq_gain (meters.py:661-667) is a brick-wall ±1/6-octave model and every fixture GEQ is flat. (4) Likelihood — requires a foreign cut within ±1 ISO band of a ring; with a typical 5-8-band house curve that neighbourhood covers half the GEQ, and wedge/58 feedback clusters in the same 250 Hz-5 kHz region engineers cut, so this is a realistic gig event, not a corner case.

Severity stays medium rather than high: writes are cuts only, capped at -9 dB, on a band that was already cut, reversible from the pre-write snapshot, and the correct band is reached within 2-3 s; rather than low because it is a wrong write to settings the operator owns, misreported as CFS's own, with audible extra feedback time in watch mode and wasted budget (HANDOVER §4b already shows budget exhaustion is what ends real sessions). The proposed offline test (unit: existing={21:-4}, det 2500 Hz must plan band 22 first; integration: fset /fx/5/par/21 before feedback_watch, inject 2400 Hz, assert first cfs.notch is band 22) fails today and the proposed fix (only merge into cuts that preflight matched to a CFS report; treat others as foreign base gains) is sound.

## E19. [medium] (desk-policy-server, confirmed) A DCA fader is a 'channel-side offset', so dca.N gets the channel ceiling (+5 dB) at Tier 1 with no confirmation.

**Encoded at:** src/x32mcp/policy.py:13-15 (docstring decision) + policy.py:243-252 level_ceiling_db (dca -> ch_fader_max_db); tests/test_policy.py:131 expects (dca.3, 7.0) -> 5.0; FakeDesk meters (_strip_level, fakedesk.py:926-938) never apply DCA gain to members so no test can observe the effect; tests/integration/test_desk.py:96-97 only reads dca.2.

**Code depends on it at:** src/x32mcp/desk.py:399-401 (_level_param maps dca -> /dca/N/fader, Tier MIX), desk.py:948-955 _move_level clamps with policy kind 'fader' for family dca; server.py set_fader/adjust_fader/mute/unmute accept 'dca.N' as Tier 1.

**Reality:** fx_routing_scenes.md §5.2 (VERIFIED): grp/dca membership exists on ch, auxin, fxrtn, bus, mtx, main/st AND main/m. A DCA at +5 dB adds +5 dB to every member — including Main LR (whose own fader is Tier 2, ceiling 0 dB) and wedge buses (ceiling 0 dB = the ring-out margin, device.yaml:725 'also the ring-out ceiling'). DCA mute/unmute likewise acts on members. Red test: worktree wt/assumptions-desk-policy-server tests/integration/test_assumptions_desk.py::test_dca_holding_main_lr_is_not_a_tier1_backdoor -> after_db 5.0.

**On a real desk:** set_fader('dca.1', +5) or two adjust_fader('dca.1', +5..+6) calls raise Main LR / rung-out wedges 5-11 dB above their policy ceilings with no confirmation token; the audience/monitors get exactly the move the Tier-2 gate and bus ceiling exist to prevent, and unmute('dca.N') can open a DCA-muted PA. get_strip also reports muted:false / fader 0.0 for members a DCA is muting or holding at -oo (desk.py:449-451 reads mix/on only), so discover_mics/preflight see DCA-killed mics as live.

**Offline test:** FakeDesk: honour grp/dca in _strip_level (member level += DCA dB, member silent when /dca/N/on==0). Test: fakedesk.set('/main/st/grp/dca',1); fakedesk.set('/bus/01/grp/dca',1); desk.set_level('dca.1', +5) must be GUARDED (member is Tier 2) or clamped to min(member ceilings)=0 dB; today writes +5.0 (red test above fails).

> **Verifier 1: CONFIRMED (high)** — All citations check out. policy.py:13-15 docstring literally says "``dca`` the channel ceiling (a DCA fader is a channel-side offset, +10 dB top like a channel)" and policy.py:243-252 level_ceiling_db falls through to ch_fader_max_db (+5) for family dca; tests/test_policy.py:131 encodes (Target("dca",3), 7.0 -> 5.0, limit 5.0). desk.py:415 (_level_param) maps dca to /dca/N/fader; device.yaml:273-274 gives /dca/N/on and /dca/N/fader tier: 1, and the guarded globs (device.yaml:708-720) do not cover /dca/*, so _move_level (desk.py:948-955) never raises GUARDED and only applies clamp_level -> +5. server.py:881-935 set_fader/adjust_fader/mute/unmute accept dca.N as Tier 1 with docstrings advertising "DCAs clamp at +5 dB". Nothing in desk.py/policy.py reads grp/dca membership (grep: only fakedesk default grp/dca=0), and FakeDesk._strip_level (fakedesk.py:929-940) computes member levels from the member's own mix/on + mix/fader only, so no test can observe a DCA acting on Main LR or a bus. Research fx_routing_scenes.md §5.2 (line 487-488, VERIFIED) confirms /dca/N/fader has the channel fader law (+10 top) and grp/dca membership exists on ch, auxin, fxrtn, bus, mtx, main/st, main/m; a DCA is by definition a VCA-style dB offset on its members, so +5 on a DCA holding Main LR or a rung-out wedge bus adds +5 dB on top of strips whose own ceilings are 0 dB (device.yaml:723-725, bus 'also the ring-out ceiling') and whose own faders are Tier 2 (main). The claimant's red test reproduces: desk.set_level('dca.1', +5.0) with /main/st/grp/dca=1 and /bus/01/grp/dca=1 returns after_db 5.0, no GUARDED, no clamp to 0. No fallback was missed; in fact device.yaml:274 itself declares `clamp: {max: 0}  # group master; 0 dB ceiling` for the DCA fader, but ParamSpec.clamp is never called on the write path (grep: only descriptor.py defines it), so the descriptor's own 0 dB intent is silently overridden by policy's +5 — an internal contradiction that strengthens the finding. Minor looseness: the '5-11 dB' figure is imprecise (a single set_fader gives +5 over the member ceiling; +10 effective on a channel already at +5), and get_strip reporting muted:false for a DCA-muted member mirrors the desk's own mix/on (the real desk also leaves mix/on=1), so that sub-point is medium at most. Core claim — Tier 1, unconfirmed +5 dB (and mute/unmute) write that acts on Tier-2 Main LR / 0 dB-ceiling buses via DCA membership, unobservable in the FakeDesk — is a wrong-write/safety issue: high.

> **Verifier 2: PARTIAL (medium)** — Core claim reproduced and accurate; severity and peripheral claims overstated.

CONFIRMED parts: (1) policy.py:243-252 level_ceiling_db gives family 'dca' the channel ceiling (+5 dB) and /dca/N/fader is Tier 1 (device.yaml:272-273, not in the guarded globs at device.yaml:709-721); desk.py:_move_level only checks the tier of the DCA's own address and never reads any member's grp/dca, so nothing in desk/policy/server is membership-aware (grep for grp/dca in desk.py/policy.py/server.py: zero hits). (2) Research fx_routing_scenes.md §5.2 (VERIFIED) puts grp/dca on ch, auxin, fxrtn, bus, mtx, main/st and main/m, and the DCA fader uses the channel fader law to +10 dB — so on a real desk a DCA offset lands on Main LR (Tier 2, ceiling 0) or a bus master (ceiling 0 = ring-out ceiling) if they are members. (3) Ran the finder's red test against unmodified src (worktree assumptions-desk-policy-server has no src diff vs main): with /main/st/grp/dca=1 and /bus/01/grp/dca=1, desk.set_level('dca.1', +5.0) returns after_db 5.0, no GUARDED, no confirmation. (4) FakeDesk._strip_level (fakedesk.py:929-938) reads only the strip's own mix/on and mix/fader, so no meter/test can ever observe a DCA acting on members. (5) Extra corroboration the finder missed: device.yaml:273 itself declares the DCA fader `clamp: {max: 0}` with the comment 'group master; 0 dB ceiling (DESIGN silent)', while policy.py's docstring (lines 13-15) fills the same silence with +5 and never consults ParamSpec.clamp_max — the two authors disagree and tests/test_policy.py:131 certifies the +5 reading; server.py:882 docstring advertises 'DCAs clamp at +5 dB ... Tier 1'.

DOWNGRADED because: default grp/dca is 0 on every strip (fakedesk.py:132 and a factory scene), so the Tier-2/bus-ceiling bypass needs a non-default membership the operator created; Main LR on a DCA is uncommon practice (buses/FX returns on DCAs is more common); the move is operator-requested, ramped, capped at +5, and adjust_fader keeps the ±6 dB relative guard, so worst case is +5 dB on members, not 5-11 dB; a real scene in the research corpus parks /dca/1/fader at +10.0 (scales_params.md:297), i.e. DCAs above unity are normal engineering practice, so this is a policy-design gap ('DESIGN silent') rather than a wrong belief about the protocol. The DCA mute sub-claim is weaker still: per fx_routing_scenes.md §5.1/§7 a DCA mute only removes members' main contribution unless /-prefs/dcamute=1, and BRIEF §4 guards mute groups but never mentions DCAs. The get_strip/discover_mics sub-claim is cosmetic: every console reports channel mute and DCA mute separately, and mic discovery uses pre-fade input meters which a DCA does not touch.

Net: a real, untested hole — a Tier-1 DCA write can add up to +5 dB to a Tier-2 Main LR or a 0-dB-ceiling wedge bus without a token when those strips are DCA members, and device.yaml's own 0 dB DCA ceiling is silently ignored — but conditional on non-default membership and bounded at +5, so medium (gate bypass under specific config), not high. Offline test as proposed is sound: make FakeDesk apply DCA gain/mute to members in _strip_level and assert set_level('dca.N', >0) is guarded or clamped to min(member ceilings) when any member is main/bus/mtx; simplest code fix is to honour device.yaml's clamp max 0 for dca in level_ceiling_db (or read members' grp/dca and escalate to Tier 2 when main is a member).

**Encoded at:** device.yaml:578-706 declares no /outputs/{main,aux,p16,aes,rec}/NN nodes at all; fakedesk.py:943-975 meters model strips only, no physical outputs; tests/integration/test_desk.py:359-369 and test_server_tools.py:243-247 equate 24 mix/on==0 with success; server.py:127-129 INSTRUCTIONS 'use it whenever the user says stop / kill it / mute everything'.

**On a real desk:** User says 'kill it', tool answers 'PANIC: 24 outputs muted in 0.4 ms (sent)' while front fills tapped EQ-> from Main LR and the drummer's P16 direct-out feed keep carrying the fault at full level; a scene recall that repatched outputs cannot be undone by restore_snapshot because /outputs was never captured.

Red test test_descriptor_knows_output_taps... fails today.

Because panic is the designated never-blocked safety backstop and REVIEW_BRIEF:121-122 asks exactly "is there any state in which it fails to silence the outputs", a false "outputs muted" on common rigs (front fills/delays tapped EQ->/PRE, P16/IEM from direct outs, AES50/card input blocks) is a safety-class defect: severity high stands (a medium argument exists only for factory-default POST rigs, and that default is itself UNCONFIRMED).

The FakeDesk does with the 24 writes exactly what research says the real desk does; nothing the code reads diverges. (b) No wrong write, no CFS-on-garbage: panic under-covers in non-default routings, it never writes something harmful. (c) Real-gig consequence is narrower than the finding paints: the target rig (BRIEF.md:9,22 — X32 Rack + SD16, IEM mixes from SD16 bus outs, PA on Main) is all master-fed and M5 verified 24/24 muted live (HANDOVER.md:114); on X32s generally, speaker feeds (mains, wedges, fills/delays off a matrix) are POST from a master (factory pos assumed POST, §13 item 13), so muting the masters breaks any acoustic feedback loop regardless of what a DirectOut or PRE tap keeps carrying — what survives is the un-looped source into personal P16/IEM mixers (listener has a local volume knob) or record/broadcast feeds.
