## E21. [medium] (desk-policy-server, confirmed) Strips are independent: writing bus 1's fader/mute/send moves bus 1 only (the fake stores /config/{ch,bus,aux,mtx}link and linkcfg/* as inert flags).

**Encoded at:** src/x32mcp/fakedesk.py _DEFAULTS (no link coupling anywhere; grep 'link' finds only mono/link); tests/integration/test_server_tools.py:452-465 sets chlink 1-2 ON and asserts nothing about ch 2; no test writes a linked partner.

**Code depends on it at:** src/x32mcp/desk.py:948-981 _move_level/_ramp report one target; desk.set_mute/set_send likewise; cfs.py:1122 raises the ring-out master with set_level on one bus while the RTA/GEQ side (FXnL) covers that bus only.

**Reality:** scales_params.md §10 (638-639): /config/buslink/1-2…, chlink, auxlink, mtxlink ON/OFF with /config/linkcfg/hadly|eq|dyn|fdrmute selecting what a stereo link shares (fdrmute = fader+mute). On a linked pair the desk applies our fader/mute/send write to the partner too; whether it pushes the partner's new value to OSC clients is not covered by the research (UNCONFIRMED) — if not, our cache for the partner is also stale. fx_routing_scenes.md §13 item 6: insert behaviour on linked buses UNCONFIRMED.

**On a real desk:** ring_out('bus.1') on linked wedges 1-2 raises Wedge R in lock-step with nobody watching it and notches only FX5L (side A) — Wedge R rings on, VERIFY fails, notch deepens to -9, ABORT; set_fader('bus.1') / set_send(ch,1) reports one strip moved while two did; adjust on bus 2 may compute from a stale cache.

**Offline test:** FakeDesk: when /config/buslink/N-M (chlink…) is ON and linkcfg/fdrmute ON, mirror fader/on/send writes to the partner and push it. Tests: set_level('bus.1',-10) must report partner bus.2 (red test test_linked_bus_partner_move_is_reported fails); preflight/ring_out on a linked bus must refuse or treat the pair (GEQ on both sides).

> **Verifier 1: CONFIRMED (medium)** — Both citations check out and the code has no fallback. (1) Research: docs/research/scales_params.md §10 lines 638-639 read exactly as quoted — `/config/chlink|auxlink|fxlink|buslink|mtxlink/N-M` enum OFF/ON and `/config/linkcfg/hadly|eq|dyn|fdrmute` enum OFF/ON "(what a stereo link shares)"; docs/research/fx_routing_scenes.md §13 item 6 (line 749) lists insert behaviour on a stereo-linked bus as UNCONFIRMED. No research or handover text describes link coupling further, and the claimant correctly flagged the partner-push question as UNCONFIRMED rather than asserting it. That an X32 stereo link with the Fader/Mute link preference on gangs the pair's fader, mute and sends at firmware level (any control path, including remote) is standard desk behaviour and follows from §10's "what a stereo link shares"; nothing in DESIGN/HANDOVER/README scopes linked strips out. (2) Fake: src/x32mcp/fakedesk.py builds /config/*link/* and linkcfg/* as plain descriptor params in _build_initial_state (lines ~470-500) and FakeDesk.set (432-442) stores/pushes only the written address — grep 'link' in fakedesk.py hits only 'mono/link' (153); there is no partner mirroring anywhere. The only test touching a link, tests/integration/test_server_tools.py:450-462 (test_set_channel_config_dance), turns chlink 1-2 ON and asserts nothing about ch 2; no other test under tests/ writes buslink/chlink (only descriptor/yaml parse tests mention them). (3) Code dependence: desk.py _move_level (948-981) and set_level/set_send (985-996, 1026-1027) and set_mute (1015-1024) read/write/report exactly one address and one target; cfs.py _write_master (1114-1123) raises the ring-out master with set_level on the single session bus while provision.preflight (provision.py:627-663) checks GEQ/mics/mute/master only — no /config/buslink read anywhere in src (grep 'link' in cfs.py/desk.py/policy.py/provision.py: zero hits; server.py only writes chlink). setup_ringout_eqs loads dual GEQ2 with one side per bus (provision.py:19-20, 437), so on a linked bus pair ring_out notches side A only while the firmware raises both masters. Failure mode as described (tool reports one strip moved while two did; partner cache possibly stale; ring-out on a linked monitor pair raises the unwatched partner and cannot notch it) is a wrong-state/spurious-failure class, not a wrong write by our code → medium is the right severity. Offline test proposal (make FakeDesk mirror fader/on/send writes to the partner when the pair's link and linkcfg/fdrmute are ON, then assert set_level('bus.1') reports bus.2 and preflight refuses/handles a linked bus) is sound and would fail today.

> **Verifier 2: CONFIRMED (medium)** — The encoded assumption is real and nothing in the product code is aware of stereo links. FakeDesk.set()/ _commit()/_side_effects() (src/x32mcp/fakedesk.py:432-441, 815-820, side-effects handler) store and push exactly one address; the only side effects modelled are the RTA-stat mirror, scene recall and scene-field capture. /config/{ch,aux,fx,bus,mtx}link/* and /config/linkcfg/* exist in the fake purely as descriptor-derived flags with no coupling. The one test that turns a link on (tests/integration/test_server_tools.py:450-462) asserts only that /config/chlink/1-2 == 1 and never touches ch 2. Outside fakedesk, 'link' appears in src only in server.set_channel_config (writes the flag) and a provision.py comment about stereo GEQ types; Desk._move_level (desk.py:948-981), set_mute/set_send, provision.preflight (provision.py:629-652: checks mics, mute, master -inf/warn only) and CfsManager._write_master (cfs.py:1115-1124) all treat the addressed strip as the only thing that moves.

Skeptical check of the 'reality' side: docs/research only lists the addresses (scales_params.md §10 lines 638-639: buslink/chlink... ON/OFF, linkcfg/hadly|eq|dyn|fdrmute = 'what a stereo link shares') and flags insert behaviour on linked strips as UNCONFIRMED (fx_routing_scenes.md §13 item 6). It does not state in so many words that an OSC write to one side is applied to the partner, so that part rests on engineering knowledge of the X32 rather than the repo's verified ground truth. But it is the standard, well-known behaviour of this console family: X32 links are absolute and enforced in the desk's parameter engine regardless of control source (surface, X32-Edit, Mixing Station, MIDI, OSC all send one side and the desk gangs the pair), and fdrmute=fader+mute sharing is literally what the documented flag means. The FakeDesk therefore does NOT match the real desk here; it matches Maillot's emulator, which is a parameter store with the same omission. So this is not refutable on 'fake == research' grounds.

Would it bite at a gig? Two consequences, weighed separately:
(1) set_fader/set_mute/set_send on a linked strip report one strip while two moved. Physically this is what the operator who linked them wants; the LLM's report is merely incomplete, and the partner's cache staleness is bounded by read_cache_ttl_s = 2 s (desk.py:212) even if the desk does not push the partner leaf to the writing client. On its own this is low.
(2) ring_out on one side of a linked bus pair is the real problem. Linked bus pairs that get rung out are not exotic: side-fills L/R and stereo keyboard/drum-fill wedges are routinely a linked pair, and the repo's own GravelAxe fixture scene puts 'Wedge L'/'Wedge R' on bus 1/2 (fakedesk.py _SCENES[2]) — the archetypal linked pair — with the link inert. With buslink/1-2 ON and fdrmute ON (the usual reason to link buses), every RAISE step of ring_out('bus.1') lifts bus 2's master to the same dB. Mics sent to a linked bus pair go to both sides (the send becomes a stereo send), so Wedge R has its own live loop, un-instrumented: the RTA is on bus 1 and the GEQ2 side A is inserted on bus 1 only (or, per UNCONFIRMED item 6, side B may be auto-inserted on bus 2 but is never written). Whichever loop has less margin rings first; a Wedge R ring reaches the mic, shows on bus 1's RTA, gets notched on FX5 side A (no effect on the bus-2 loop), fails VERIFY (decay_verify_s 1.5 s), is deepened to -6 then -9, and the session ABORTs with 'not tamed' after ~4.5 s of howl, leaving a pointless -9 dB hole in Wedge L's GEQ and a report that blames bus 1. Even if Wedge L rings first and is tamed, continued raising eventually excites Wedge R and ends the same way, so a linked pair can essentially never be rung out to target by this tool, and preflight gives no hint why. Mitigations that keep this from being 'high': it happens in a supervised pre-show procedure where rings are expected, the partner never exceeds the level the session intends for the target (absolute link), master_ceiling_db/target still bound it, and the ABORT back-off (and cfs_abort/panic) lower the partner too through the same link, so there is no unbounded or unrecoverable hazard; cuts stay cuts-only, <= -9 dB, on the correct strip. That is squarely 'CFS acts on garbage / tool fails and misreports at a gig' rather than a safety escape — medium, as the finder rated.

Offline test proposal is sound and cheap: give FakeDesk link coupling (when /config/buslink/N-M (chlink, auxlink, mtxlink) is ON and linkcfg/fdrmute ON, mirror mix/fader, mix/on and mix/NN/level|on writes to the partner and push the partner leaf), then (a) a red test that set_level('bus.1', -10) reports/moves bus.2, and (b) a red test that preflight/ring_out on a linked bus either blocks ('bus 1-2 are stereo-linked: unlink or ring out the pair') or provisions/writes both GEQ sides. The cheapest product fix is a preflight blocker/warning that reads /config/buslink/N-M (one cached read), which also sidesteps the UNCONFIRMED insert-on-linked-strip question.

## E22. [medium] (desk-policy-server, confirmed) A scene recall can be verified by polling /-show/prepos/current, and the desk's show control is SCENES (FakeDesk default) so the pointer means a scene.

**Encoded at:** src/x32mcp/fakedesk.py:158 show_control 'SCENES', :154 prepos/current 0, :1141-1156 _recall_scene always moves the pointer and applies instantly; tests/integration/test_desk.py:466-500 and test_server_tools.py:281-296 never recall the scene that is already current and never lose the goscene datagram; nodes.py:708-713 _scene_of labels every snapshot from prepos/current with no show_control check.

**Reality:** fx_routing_scenes.md §6.4: the reply to /-action/goscene is UNCONFIRMED, whereas `/load ,si scene N` -> `/load ,si scene 1|0` is VERIFIED (DOC p.52) and is what Maillot's tools use; DOC fn.39-41: 'not necessarily fully completed when the status is returned' (so reads right after must not be cached as post-recall truth). §6.2: the pointer indexes cues/snippets unless show_control==SCENES. Red test test_recall_of_the_current_scene_is_not_reported_verified_without_evidence: desk ignores goscene, tool still says verified True.

**On a real desk:** 'Reset to the soundcheck scene' (re-recall of the current scene, the commonest use) reports 'verified' even if the datagram was lost or the desk refused; on the CUES desk every recall is 'cannot be verified'; list_snapshots/diff label snapshots with scene = name of scene[cue index].

**Offline test:** FakeDesk: option to ignore/delay goscene and to answer /load with 0/1; test recall of the current index with goscene swallowed -> verified must not be True; test under show_control=CUES that recall is still positively confirmed (use /load status + the xremote burst) and that DeskState.scene is None/annotated.

> **Verifier 1: CONFIRMED (medium)** — All citations check out and the core defect reproduces. (1) Research: docs/research/fx_routing_scenes.md §6.4 (line 553) marks the reply to `/-action/goscene` UNCONFIRMED while `/load ,si scene N` -> `/load ,si scene 1|0` is VERIFIED (DOC p.52) and §13 item 10 (line 753) says `/load` "returns a 0/1 status and is what Maillot's tools use"; line 566 quotes DOC fn.39-41 "not necessarily fully completed when the status is returned"; §6.2 (line 502) says the pointer indexes whichever list `/-prefs/show_control` selects; transport.md line 340/639 says SETs have no ack, "silence = ignored or lost", confirm by observation. No fallback exists for this case (no xremote-burst check, no /load status). (3) Fake/tests: fakedesk.py:158 defaults show_control 'SCENES', :154 prepos/current 0, _recall_scene at :1143-1157 always applies goscene instantly; test_desk.py:466-500 and test_server_tools.py:287-296 only ever recall a scene different from the current one under SCENES (the one same-index recall, test_desk.py:512, runs under CUES where verified is None). FakeDesk already implements `/load` with a 0/1 reply (fakedesk.py:1186-1199) but desk.py never uses it. (4) Reproduced: the claimant's red test in worktree assumptions-desk-policy-server (tests/integration/test_assumptions_desk.py:168) swallows goscene, re-recalls scene 1 while current==1, nothing on the fake desk changes, and recall_scene returns verified: True — FAILS today as claimed. (5) CUES sub-claim: accurate but honestly handled — desk.py:1258-1262/1287-1288 return verified=None plus a note (tested at test_desk.py:503-518), so on the real desk every recall reads 'NOT verified — check the desk' even when it worked; the tool does not lie there, it just can never verify, although a VERIFIED status path (/load) exists. (6) nodes.py:708-713 `_scene_of` confirmed: labels DeskState.scene from prepos/current with no show_control (not in any /node section) and no -1 guard, feeding dump/snapshot/list_snapshots (server.py:870,1190,1203) — on a CUES desk snapshots carry scene[cue-index] names (low, cosmetic). > **Verifier 2: PARTIAL (medium)** — Three sub-claims, judged separately.

(A) Vacuous 'verified' on re-recall of the current scene — CONFIRMED. desk.py:1251-1289: recall_scene reads previous=/-show/prepos/current, fires one fire-and-forget datagram (/-action/goscene via _write -> conn.set, desk.py:871-884, no reply, no retry), then polls conn.get('/-show/prepos/current') until it equals idx. When previous == idx the first poll matches immediately, so verified=True carries zero evidence that the desk received or acted on goscene. This is deliberately designed, honestly reported, and tested with the fake flipped to CUES (test_desk.py:503-519 test_scene_pointer_is_not_trusted_unless_show_control_is_scenes). The FakeDesk default SCENES (fakedesk.py:158) is therefore not an untested assumption. Using /load's status for positive confirmation under CUES is a valid enhancement, not a wrong belief the tests certified; on Jim's desk the result is a nuisance caveat (HANDOVER §4a already says flip to SCENES), i.e. low.

(C) nodes.py:708-713 _scene_of labels every DeskState/snapshot from prepos/current with no show_control check — CONFIRMED by reading (state.scene feeds only snapshot metadata/summaries: nodes.py:745,793,822; server.py:870,1190,1203). On a CUES desk snapshots get scene={cue-list index, name of scene[that index]}, and a -1 pointer yields {index:-1,name:''}. Nothing writes or restores based on it — cosmetic, low.

Minor fidelity note supporting (A): FakeDesk moves the pointer even for an empty slot (fakedesk.py:1144-1145 before the has-data check) and regardless of show_control; real behaviour for both is undocumented. Server blocks empty slots (server.py:1131-1132) so that path is mitigated.

Net: the core claim (verification is vacuous for same-index recalls and rests on an UNCONFIRMED command with no real fallback, while a VERIFIED /load status goes unused) stands at medium; the CUES and snapshot-label parts are already-mitigated/cosmetic. Offline test as the finder proposes is sound: give FakeDesk an option to ignore/delay inbound goscene (not just drop replies) and answer /load 0|1; assert recall of the current index with goscene swallowed is not verified=True; optionally assert DeskState.scene is None/annotated when show_control != SCENES.

**Encoded at:** src/x32mcp/nodes.py:111 _RESTORE_EXCLUDED_FAMILIES {show,stat,prefs,action}; fakedesk.py:159 rta/autogain True + meters.set_rta_source now flipping it, but no test diffs after restore; test_server_tools.py:344-347 'diff == 0 after restore' runs in a test that never touched /-prefs; server.py:117 INSTRUCTIONS 'restore_snapshot undoes'.

Red test test_restore_of_the_pre_write_snapshot_undoes_the_rta_prefs_we_changed: after restore the diff still lists 'Prefs RTA autogain on → off', 'source MAIN → BUS01', 'det RMS → PEAK', 'Status rtasource 168 → 146'.

**Offline test:** The red test: set_rta_source through the snapshotting writer, desk.restore(pre_write), diff_states == [] (fails). Direction: CfsManager/get_rta save and restore the /-prefs/rta section on stop, or restore_plan includes /-prefs/rta; make the preview count only what restore_plan will write.

> **Verifier 1: CONFIRMED (medium)** — Both halves of the claim check out against HEAD a408a2a. Nothing else does either: cfs._disarm has no RTA-prefs restore (only invalidate('/-prefs/rta') at cfs.py:916), and grep finds no other autogain/det write path. Research citation is accurate: meters.md §5.3 (line 446) quotes the manual that Auto Gain is 'recommended for most situations to ensure meaningful readings' and that rta/source can be dynamic (follow selected channel) — these are the operator's global console preferences, not scene data, so no scene recall puts them back. DESIGN.md:419 does document that restore excludes -prefs, but INSTRUCTIONS (server.py:117) tells the model 'restore_snapshot undoes' and README:531 describes get_rta's prefs writes as snapshot-before-write with no caveat, so the exclusion is an undisclosed hole rather than a mitigated one. I ran the claimant's red test in their worktree (no src changes vs a408a2a) and it fails exactly as stated: after desk.restore(pre_write) diff_states still lists 'Status rtasource 168 → 146', 'Prefs RTA autogain on → off', 'Prefs RTA source MAIN → BUS01', 'Prefs RTA det RMS → PEAK'. Severity medium is right: no unsafe audio write, but the tool misreports (preview counts unwritable items, post-restore diff never clean, inviting restore loops) and leaves the engineer's console RTA permanently altered (auto-gain off, PEAK, pinned to a wedge bus instead of following the selected channel) with no tool path to put it back short of raw OSC.

> **Verifier 2: CONFIRMED (medium)** — Reproduced. INSTRUCTIONS (server.py:117) tell the model 'restore_snapshot undoes', and get_rta's result (server.py ~1511 rta_info) does not even surface autogain_cleared/detector_set_peak, so neither model nor operator is told the console's RTA settings were changed. The only test asserting a clean diff after restore (tests/integration/test_server_tools.py:344-347) never touches /-prefs, so the suite certifies 'undo' on a footprint that excludes our own RTA writes. Ran the slice's red test (worktree assumptions-desk-policy-server, tests/integration/test_assumptions_desk.py:139-161): FAILS on HEAD with remaining diff ['Status rtasource 168 → 146', 'Prefs RTA autogain on → off', 'Prefs RTA source MAIN → BUS01', 'Prefs RTA det RMS → PEAK'] — exactly as claimed. ## E24. [medium] (desk-policy-server, confirmed) The analyser behind /meters/15 has no ballistics: whatever /-prefs/rta/decay, peakhold, det, gain, autogain say, a notched band drops instantly (SyntheticRta), so VERIFY's 6 dB-in-1.5 s rule measures acoustics.

**Encoded at:** src/x32mcp/fakedesk.py:159-160 stores rta/decay 1.0, peakhold OFF, det RMS, autogain True, gain 24 and fakedesk.py:943-946 feeds /meters/15 straight from SyntheticRta ignoring all of them (grep: 'decay'/'peakhold' appear nowhere in meters.py logic); this is also why M7 defect #1 (autogain) was invisible and why its fix is still unverifiable offline.

**Code depends on it at:** src/x32mcp/meters.py:860-941 set_rta_source writes source/pos/options/autogain/det but never decay or peakhold (lead's lead confirmed); cfs.py:1222-1229 _verify waits decay_verify_s=1.5 s for decay_verify_db=6 (device.yaml:820-822) and deepens/aborts on failure.

**Reality:** meters.md §5.1 (VERIFIED): /-prefs/rta/decay logf 0.25…16 (presumably s), peakhold OFF/1…8, det RMS/PEAK all shape the RTA the desk streams; §5.3: which analysis /meters/15 carries while a PEQ/GEQ page is displayed (on the desk or X32-Edit) is UNCONFIRMED. An operator who likes slow meters (decay 4-16 s) or has peak-hold on makes a killed ring linger on the meter for seconds.

**On a real desk:** Notch works acoustically, band falls slowly on the RTA -> VERIFY fails -> deepen -3 -> -6 -> -9 -> 'cannot deepen' -> ABORT with a needlessly deep cut and a spent budget; with peak-hold on, every notch 'fails'. CFS acts on display ballistics, not sound.

**Offline test:** Give SyntheticRta/FakeDesk a per-band release model driven by /-prefs/rta/decay and a hold driven by peakhold (and normalisation when autogain is ON); tests: set decay=8 -> ring_out must still verify (or set_rta_source must force decay=0.25, peakhold=OFF and restore them on stop); today set_rta_source leaves both untouched.

> **Verifier 1: CONFIRMED (medium)** — Both halves of the finding check out against the code at a408a2a. (1) Encoded: src/x32mcp/fakedesk.py:159-160 seeds "rta/gain": 24.0, "rta/autogain": True, "rta/det": "RMS", "rta/decay": 1.0, "rta/peakhold": "OFF", and fakedesk.py:944-946 (`if mtype == RTA_METER_TYPE: frame = self.rta.last_frame or self.rta.tick(); return list(frame.values)`) streams SyntheticRta frames verbatim. The only /-prefs/rta/* the emulator acts on are source/pos (stat mirror, fakedesk.py:1083-1101) and source (cut coupling, _refresh_cuts fakedesk.py:1103-1135); decay, peakhold, det, gain, autogain are stored-and-ignored. SyntheticRta (meters.py:558-670) has no release/hold model: a cut is applied as `level -= c` per frame (docstring meters.py:572-578), i.e. instantaneous. A repo-wide grep finds no writer of /-prefs/rta/decay or /-prefs/rta/peakhold anywhere in src/ (only descriptor entries device.yaml:566-567,704), and no test touches autogain/det/decay/peakhold behaviour (tests only assert the node field order: test_nodes.py:231-232, test_descriptor.py:437, test_device_yaml.py:348) — so the side-claim that M7 defect #1's fix (autogain off / det PEAK) is unverifiable offline is also true: not even the write is asserted. (2) Depends: meters.py:860-941 set_rta_source writes source, pos, options bit 5, autogain=0 (912-916) and det=1 PEAK (918-923) but never decay or peakhold; cfs.py:1221-1254 _verify_decay waits cfg.decay_verify_s for a drop >= cfg.decay_verify_db on decay_verify_frames consecutive frames, values 6 dB / 1.5 s / 2 from device.yaml:820-822 (defaults detector.py:115-117); on failure _notch_and_verify (cfs.py:1200-1219) deepens and ultimately returns False -> abort path. No adaptive window, no ballistics normalisation, no restore — no fallback the claimant missed. provision.py:292-296 independently documents the identical failure shape for a blind VERIFY ("can never verify decay and drives every ring to the -9 dB maximum whether the cut worked or not"). (3) Research: meters.md §5.1 (lines 379-380, 401-403) VERIFIES the parameters and ranges exactly as cited (decay logf 0.25*64**f, 0.25..16, unit UNCONFIRMED 'presumably seconds'; peakhold enum OFF,1..8; det RMS/PEAK); §5.3 line 453 does mark the /meters/15 content while a PEQ/GEQ page is displayed as UNCONFIRMED, as cited. One nuance: the research does not itself VERIFY that decay/peakhold shape /meters/15 — §4.2 line 307 marks even gain/autogain's effect on the stream UNCONFIRMED with 'best inference: values are the analyser output as displayed'. But HANDOVER §4b defect #1 (lines 154-156) is real-desk confirmation that a display pref (auto-gain) does normalise the streamed bands, and the code's own det=PEAK write (meters.py:918 'RMS blunts a narrow tone… PEAK tracks the onset') already presumes detector ballistics reach the stream; decay is the release ballistic of that same detector. So at minimum the code depends on an UNCONFIRMED item (operator's decay/peakhold being benign) with no fallback, which the brief defines as a finding, and the available real-desk evidence points the claimant's way. The 'peak-hold makes every notch fail' sub-claim is the most speculative part (peak-hold may be an overlay marker not carried in the stream), but the decay case alone sustains the finding. Severity medium is right: consequence is spurious VERIFY failure -> needless deepening to -9 dB and budget burn / ABORT (cuts-only, bounded), i.e. the tool fails spuriously and over-cuts at a gig rather than an unsafe write.

> **Verifier 2: PARTIAL (medium)** — Mechanism confirmed in code, consequence plausible but partly speculative; overlaps an observation already in the repo.

CONFIRMED parts: (1) FakeDesk stores rta/decay 1.0, peakhold OFF, det RMS, autogain True, gain 24 (src/x32mcp/fakedesk.py:159-160) and _meter_values() returns SyntheticRta frames verbatim for /meters/15 (fakedesk.py:943-945) — none of the /-prefs/rta/* values influence the stream; SyntheticRta has no release model at all (a cut is `level -= c` per frame, meters.py:572-578, i.e. 60 dB/s). (2) No product code touches decay/peakhold: grep of src/ finds /-prefs/rta/decay|peakhold only in the FakeDesk default table; set_rta_source (meters.py:860-941) writes source, pos, options bit5, autogain, det only. (3) VERIFY is a pure display-timing rule: _verify_decay waits decay_verify_s=1.5 s for decay_verify_db=6 dB on 2 consecutive frames (cfs.py:1221-1253, device.yaml:820-822); failure deepens -3→-6→-9 (deepening is free of budget, detector.py NotchController._affordable) then _run_ringout aborts 'not tamed' and backs the master off 6 dB (cfs.py:1157-1163). (4) Not mitigated anywhere: GIG_CHECKLIST.md never mentions decay/peak hold. (5) VERIFY has never run on hardware: the successful M7 catch (HANDOVER §4b) was Jim pushing the master by hand, i.e. feedback_watch, which notches without verify (cfs.py:1040-1041); so no real-desk datum contradicts or supports the 1.5 s rule. (6) Precedent that display prefs reach the OSC stream is real: HANDOVER §4b defect 1 / commit f43f10c — autogain ON normalised /meters/15 on FW 4.13 (337 false detections), resolving meters.md §4.2's UNCONFIRMED note in the 'display-processed' direction. Operator scenario is realistic: engineers routinely set long decay / peak hold on the RTA precisely to ring out by eye, so a desk arriving with those settings is not exotic.

OVERSTATED / UNPROVEN parts (why PARTIAL, not CONFIRMED): (a) The finding cites 'meters.md §5.1 (VERIFIED)' as saying decay/peakhold/det shape the streamed RTA; §5.1 only verifies the parameter table and ranges. Whether decay is applied desk-side before streaming is inference (strong, by the autogain precedent), and the decay unit itself is UNCONFIRMED ('presumably seconds', §5.1). (b) 'With peak-hold on, every notch fails' is speculative: /meters/15 carries exactly 100 bar values with no room for separate held peaks, so peak hold is plausibly a UI overlay line that never enters the stream. (c) Magnitude: a notch that breaks a loop collapses the band by tens of dB acoustically; unless 'decay 16' means slower than ~4 dB/s of bar release, even slow settings still show 6 dB inside 1.5 s, so the spurious deepen/ABORT needs the extreme end of the range AND desk-side ballistics. At the factory/FakeDesk default (1.0) it almost certainly passes. (d) REVIEW_REPORT.md:85-93 (§1.2c) already records the same uncontrolled decay/peakhold gap (for the detector's persistence/override terms); this finding extends it to VERIFY and to the FakeDesk blind spot rather than discovering it.

Severity: medium, conditional. Worst realistic outcome is a spurious VERIFY failure → needlessly deep −9 dB cut at a correct frequency, ring_out ABORT and a 6 dB master back-off at soundcheck (tool fails spuriously at a gig); cuts-only and master-lowering, so not a safety/high item. (The detector-side effect of long decay — stale transients satisfying the 25 dB/6-frame override and producing false notches — would be the higher-severity path, but that is REVIEW_REPORT §1.2c's claim, not this finding's.) Fix is cheap and the offline test proposed is right: give FakeDesk's /meters/15 a release/hold stage driven by state['-prefs/rta/decay'|'peakhold'|'autogain'] and assert ring_out still verifies at decay=16 / peakhold=8, or that set_rta_source forces decay→0.25, peakhold→OFF (read-back verified, restored on stop) alongside the existing autogain/det writes.

## E25. [medium] (desk-policy-server, confirmed) Under firmware-4 user routing the UIN blocks sit diagonally (UIN1-8 on inputs 1-8 …), so channel source INk reads /config/userrout/in/k; and computing the head amp is as good as asking the desk.

**Encoded at:** tests/integration/test_desk.py:704-731 only places UIN1-8 on routing/IN/1-8 (the diagonal case seen on Jim's desk); FakeDesk has no /-ha/NN/index.

**Code depends on it at:** src/x32mcp/desk.py:751-768: on a UIN* block token it reads f'/config/userrout/in/{src:02d}' (src = channel source number) instead of userrout/in/((block-20)*8+off); whole algorithm desk.py:717-784 is the UNCONFIRMED §12.4 recipe with no cross-check; consumers: desk.set_phantom(target) (48 V) and provision.py:582 'physical mic' classification.

**Reality:** scales_params.md §12.4 (UNCONFIRMED algorithm) indexes `userrout_in[(r - 20) * 8 + off]` — the UIN block number matters; §12.3 (VERIFIED, DOC p.43): the console itself publishes the resolved mapping read-only at /-ha/00..39/index ('Prefer querying /-ha/NN/index over computing'; -1 = no head amp). Red test test_headamp_follows_a_non_diagonal_uin_block: routing/IN/1-8=UIN9-16, userrout/in/09=33 -> expected head amp 32, code returns 0.

**On a real desk:** With UIN9-16 patched onto inputs 1-8 (or any AES50/card shuffle done in the user-in table), set_phantom('ch.1') puts 48 V on local XLR 1 instead of the stage-box input actually feeding ch 1, and discover_mics calls card/USB feeds 'physical' or real mics 'not physical'.

**Offline test:** FakeDesk: compute and serve /-ha/NN/index from its routing state; Desk: read /-ha/{ch-1:02d}/index first and fall back to the algorithm only when it times out; keep the red test (non-diagonal UIN) plus a test that the two agree on the diagonal case.

(2) Code: src/x32mcp/desk.py:722-784 implements the §12.4 recipe (docstring itself says "§12.4 (UNCONFIRMED…)"), but the UIN branch at desk.py:760-764 does `patch = await self._leaf(f"/config/userrout/in/{src:02d}")` where src is the channel source index 1..32 — it ignores which UIN block token (UIN1-8/9-16/17-24/25-32) the input block carries, so it is only right on the diagonal (block b <- UIN block b), which is exactly the one configuration seen on Jim's desk (HANDOVER.md:139-141) and the only one the suite tests (tests/integration/test_desk.py:710-740 sets routing/IN/1-8=UIN1-8 only; no other UIN test exists). Consumers confirmed: desk.py:1363 set_phantom(target) resolves idx via headamp_index_for and writes /headamp/NNN/phantom (guarded); provision.py:582 `physical = (await desk.headamp_index_for(c)) is not None` drives mic classification. (3) Reproduced: the slice's red test tests/integration/test_assumptions_desk.py:185-190 (routing/IN/1-8=UIN9-16, userrout/in/09=33, userrout/in/01=1) fails today with `assert 0 == 32` exactly as claimed; an independent repro worktree (verify-uin-crossblock-repro) also shows set_phantom('ch.N') returning the wrong headamp (4 instead of 0) and In 9-16<-UIN1-8 returning 16 instead of 32. Physics/firmware semantics agree with §12.4 over the code: the routing_in enum has four distinct UIN block tokens mirroring A1-8/A9-16/…, so "Inputs 1-8 <- User In 9-16" means input 1 hears user-in slot 9. 4. Skeptical weighting of the gig consequence. (a) set_phantom is NOT an MCP tool (server.py exposes no phantom/headamp tool) and /headamp/*/phantom is a guarded Tier-2 glob (DESIGN §guarded, desk.py:1369 guarded=True), so the '48 V on the wrong XLR' path is Python-API-only and confirmation-gated — that keeps this out of 'high'. (b) The live consumer is provision.py:582 `physical = headamp_index_for(c) is not None`, which drives `include` (line 591), the 'no preamp (not a physical input)' note (596-597), preflight's hard blocker 'no candidate mics' (provision.py:645) and the ring-out 'plan expects mics … not routed' warning (cfs.py:690). Under a non-diagonal bank, discover_mics reads the wrong user-in slot: a stage-box mic whose wrongly-read slot holds a card/USB value (Jim's own table is '1 129 130 33 …', so such slots exist on his desk) is reported 'not a physical input' and excluded — if it is the only open mic, start_ringout refuses with PREFLIGHT_FAILED at the gig for a false reason; conversely a USB playback channel can be listed as a mic. Any aux-in mic patched via User In is always 'no preamp' today. That is squarely 'tool reports wrong state / fails spuriously at a gig' = medium. (c) Mitigations that stop it being worse: Jim's desk is diagonal (HANDOVER §4a validated ch4 -> slot 04 -> 33 -> 032), non-diagonal banks are uncommon, and server instructions make the operator confirm the discover_mics list before feedback_watch — but the preflight blocker and include flag are automated, so human review does not rescue the spurious block.

Net: CONFIRMED as stated; severity medium is right (not high because the unsafe write is not on the MCP surface and is confirmation-guarded; not low because a legal FW-4 routing makes discover_mics/preflight lie or block, and the VERIFIED /-ha node that would make this exact is never read). Offline test as proposed is sound: have FakeDesk compute /-ha/NN/index from routing+userrout (including aux 32..39), declare /-ha in device.yaml, make headamp_index_for read /-ha/{n:02d}/index first (treat -1 as None) and fall back to the §12.4 formula with `(r-20)*8+off` and the aux UIN branch only on timeout; keep the non-diagonal and aux-in red tests plus an agreement test on the diagonal case.

## E26. [medium] (desk-policy-server, partial) A strip's audible state is its own mix/on and mix/fader: 'unmuted, fader 0.0 dB' means signal can pass.

**Encoded at:** src/x32mcp/fakedesk.py:926-938 _strip_level uses only the strip's own on/fader (no DCA, no mute-group, no LR-assign, no source) and every FakeDesk strip boots ON at 0.0 dB assigned to LR (fakedesk.py:113-114); test_desk.py:73-97 assert exactly those defaults.

**Code depends on it at:** src/x32mcp/desk.py:449-451 get_strip muted/fader_db; server.py:_strip_summary 'unmuted'; provision.py:582-583 (mic is live if unmuted+routed+preamp) and preflight 'bus is muted' checks read the same fields.

**Reality:** fx_routing_scenes.md §5.2/§11 item 5: /dca/N/on 0 mutes members and the DCA fader offsets them without touching the members' mix/on or mix/fader (member mute LEDs flash, values unchanged); §11 item 2: mute groups (/config/mute/K + grp/mute) mute members ('post-fader sends only unless /-prefs/hardmute'), semantics of hardmute/dcamute UNCONFIRMED (§13 item 14). HANDOVER §4b already saw the sibling problem (7 'live' candidates, 1 real mic).

**On a real desk:** get_channel says 'Ch 4 unmuted, fader 0.0' for a vocal the engineer killed with DCA 'VOX' or mute group 'BAND OFF'; discover_mics/preflight include dead mics and ring_out raises a bus whose only 'open mic' is DCA-muted — no ring ever comes, it runs to the 0 dB ceiling and reports a clean ring-out that is 9+ dB hotter than reality once the DCA comes up.

**Offline test:** FakeDesk: fold DCA on/fader and active mute groups into _strip_level; Desk.get_strip: add effective_muted / dca / mute_groups fields from grp/* + /dca/N + /config/mute; test: fakedesk.set('/ch/04/grp/dca',1); fakedesk.set('/dca/1/on',0) -> get_channel(4) must report it silenced; today muted:false.

> **Verifier 1: PARTIAL (medium)** — Core assumption CONFIRMED, failure story and one research citation overstated -> PARTIAL.

What checks out (verified in code and by a probe test run against the FakeDesk):
- FakeDesk encodes 'audible = own mix/on + own fader': src/x32mcp/fakedesk.py:929-940 _strip_level reads only {prefix}/mix/on and {prefix}/mix/fader; defaults at fakedesk.py:117-118 boot every strip mix/on True, fader 0.0, mix/st True and every DCA on True fader 0.0; fakedesk.py:132 boots grp/dca=0, grp/mute=0. The fake is a parameter store: writing /dca/1/on 0 or /config/mute/1 1 changes nothing on member strips (probe: /ch/05/mix/on stays 1). tests/integration/test_desk.py:53-80 (claimant wrote 'test_desk.py:73-97'; right file is under tests/integration/) assert those defaults (muted False, fader 0.0 for ch/main/dca).
- Code depends on it: desk.py:450-452 get_strip derives muted solely from mix/on (dca: 'on') and fader_db from mix/fader; the strip dict has no dca/mute-group/effective fields at all (probe printed the key list). server.py:466 _strip_summary prints 'unmuted'. provision.py:567/587 discover_mics: muted=strip['muted']; include=(not muted) and sending and physical; for main targets (573-575) send_on/send_db come from lr_assigned/fader_db only. preflight (provision.py ~631-648) uses strip['muted'] for the bus-muted blocker. grep: nothing in src/ reads grp/dca, /dca/N/on|fader, /config/mute/K, /-prefs/dcamute or /-prefs/hardmute for effective state (discover_mics reads grp/mute only as the 'group 6 = stage mics' membership hint, never the group's ON state). No fallback missed.
- Probe (worktree wt/verify-dca-mute, commit a0b78ba, tests/integration/test_zz_dca_probe.py): ch4 in DCA1 with /dca/1/on=0, ch5 in mute group 1 with /config/mute/1=1 -> get_channel(4/5) both muted:False fader 0.0, discover_mics('main') includes both with no notes. Passes today, i.e. the blind spot is real.
- Research: fx_routing_scenes.md s11 item 5 ('DCA fader//dca/N/on 0 only affects members' main contribution unless /-prefs/dcamute = 1'), s11 item 2 ('Mute groups mute post-fader sends only unless /-prefs/hardmute = 1'), s13 item 14 (semantics UNCONFIRMED) and HANDOVER s4b (7 candidates, 1 real mic) are quoted accurately.

What does not check out:
- s5.2 does NOT say a DCA mute leaves members' mix/on/mix/fader untouched or that 'member mute LEDs flash, values unchanged' - that is the claimant's general X32 knowledge, not the cited text. s5.2 only lists /dca/N/on|fader and grp/dca membership; the separateness is implied (and by the definition of a DCA for the fader), not stated.
- The headline gig failure ('ring_out raises a BUS whose only open mic is DCA-muted - no ring ever comes') contradicts the research's own default semantics: with dcamute=0 (default) a DCA mute removes only the MAIN contribution, so the member still feeds the monitor bus and the ring does come. The scenario holds for ring_out('main') (bus_target accepts main.st; M7 was run on Main LR) and for desks with dcamute=1, not for the general bus case as written.
- The mute-group half is the weakest: s5.1's hardmute description (with Hard Mutes OFF, un-muting a group un-mutes a channel that was muted by its own MUTE) implies the default desk writes group mute/unmute through to the member's own mix/on, in which case get_strip would read muted:True correctly; the doc marks this UNCONFIRMED, so it is an open question rather than an established defect. The FakeDesk cannot express either behaviour.

Net: a genuine baked-in assumption (DCA layer invisible to get_strip/discover_mics/preflight, fake reproduces it, tests certify it) with a real consequence on Main LR ring-outs and misleading 'unmuted, fader 0.0' summaries for DCA-killed strips; but the research citation is embellished and the bus failure narrative is wrong under the documented default. Severity medium (tool reports misleading state; mains preflight can pass with no audible mic -> ramp to ceiling, false clean report), not high.

> **Verifier 2: PARTIAL (medium)** — Half of this finding survives; the other half is unsupported by the research and its headline gig scenario is wrong at factory prefs.

CONFIRMED PART (DCA): A DCA mute/fader is an overlay that never touches members' mix/on or mix/fader (real X32: member MUTE LEDs flash, values unchanged — general X32 knowledge; the research only documents the addresses, §5.2). Desk.get_strip (desk.py:439-451) derives `muted` solely from mix/on and exposes no grp/dca, /dca/N/on or /dca/N/fader; discover_mics (provision.py:566-584) uses that `muted`, and for bus='main' uses the channel fader_db/lr_assigned (573-575) as the 'send'; it reads grp/mute only as a membership convention (582-584) and never reads /config/mute/K, grp/dca, /dca/N/*, or /-prefs/dcamute. FakeDesk has no DCA/mute-group signal model at all (fakedesk.py:132 defaults only; _strip_level 929-938 own on/fader only), and no test exercises DCA or /config/mute interplay (test_cfs.py:210-234, test_desk.py:77-78). Probe run today against FakeDesk: ch1 in DCA1 with /dca/1/on=0 and /dca/1/fader=-oo -> get_channel(1) = muted False, fader 0.0, no DCA field; discover_mics('main') includes ch1 as live with no DCA note. On a real desk that channel contributes nothing to Main LR, so discover_mics('main')/preflight('main') over-report live mics and ring_out on Main LR (ring_out_system's last stage) can pass preflight with zero acoustically open mics, climb to master_ceiling_db 0 (device.yaml:830), back off 3 dB and report a 'clean' result that was never tested against open mics — feedback risk when the DCAs come up. DCAs muted/parked at -oo is the normal idle state of a show desk, and the state is cheaply readable, so this is a genuine, fixable gap.

REFUTED / OVERSTATED PARTS: (1) Bus ring-out scenario: per fx_routing_scenes.md §5.1 (line 482) and §11 item 5 (line 711), with /-prefs/dcamute=0 (default) a DCA mute only removes members from the MAIN mix; bus sends (and certainly pre-fader wedge sends, which a DCA fader cannot reach by definition) stay live. So for the primary workflow — ringing out monitor buses — a DCA-muted vocal still feeds the wedge, discover_mics(bus) include=True is correct and rings do come; the 'no ring ever comes on the bus' story only holds on desks with dcamute=1 or post-fader monitor sends. (2) Mute groups: the research never says mute groups leave members' mix/on untouched — the cited '§11 item 2 / LEDs flash, values unchanged' text does not exist for mute groups; §13 item 14 marks hardmute/dcamute semantics UNCONFIRMED. Real X32 mute groups most likely drive the members' own mutes (solid-lit MUTE buttons; the 'Hard Mutes' preference only makes sense if group release rewrites member mutes), in which case get_strip.muted already reflects them and discover_mics correctly excludes/annotates them ('muted on the desk but mute group 6 lists it'). Even under the finding's reading, §11 item 2 (line 708) says mute groups kill post-fader sends only, so pre-fader wedges would again still be live. At most this half is an UNCONFIRMED item to check on hardware (does /config/mute/6=1 flip /ch/NN/mix/on?), not an established defect. (3) get_channel 'unmuted' for a DCA-muted strip is literally the strip's own switch state (what X32-Edit shows under the flashing overlay) — incomplete, not false; get_strip('dca.1') reports the DCA correctly. (4) The 'dead candidate counted live' class is already documented (HANDOVER §4b lines 185-188; README:534 'include is a suggestion to confirm'), and Main LR ring-out is Tier-2 confirmed with an engineer watching the main fader move.

Net: keep as a medium, but rescoped to 'discover_mics/preflight/get_strip ignore DCA state (grp/dca, /dca/N/on, /dca/N/fader, /-prefs/dcamute) — wrong live-mic report for the Main LR stage (any prefs) and for buses only when dcamute=1 or sends are post-fader'. Offline test that fails today: fakedesk.set('/ch/01/grp/dca',1); set('/dca/1/on',0) (or '/dca/1/fader',-inf); assert discover_mics(desk,'main') marks ch1 not included / noted 'DCA 1 muted' and get_channel(1) reports dca membership + effective mute; for mute groups, first verify on hardware whether /config/mute/K rewrites member mix/on, then teach FakeDesk the observed behaviour.

## E27. [medium] (fakedesk-fidelity, confirmed) The /meters/15 stream is the raw analyser output, unaffected by the RTA display prefs the operator left set (/-prefs/rta/decay, /peakhold, /gain), so a killed ring vanishes from the RTA within one frame and levels are absolute.

**Encoded at:** src/x32mcp/fakedesk.py:159-160 (defaults rta/gain 24, autogain ON, decay 1.0, peakhold OFF are stored) but fakedesk.py:943-946 streams SyntheticRta frames that never read any /-prefs/rta/* leaf; src/x32mcp/meters.py:714-718 (_advance: a cut of c dB lowers the ring by c dB PER FRAME, no fall-rate limit, no peak hold, no gain offset). tests/integration/test_cfs.py:281-284 (l2 < l1-3 within 0.4 s) and test_fakedesk.py:425-427 rely on the instant fall.

**Code depends on it at:** src/x32mcp/meters.py:888-923 set_rta_source forces source/pos/options bit5/autogain/det but never writes decay, peakhold or gain; src/x32mcp/cfs.py:1221-1252 _verify_decay requires a 6 dB drop on 2 consecutive frames within decay_verify_s=1.5 (device.yaml:820-822) or deepens the notch to -6/-9 and then aborts the ring-out; src/x32mcp/detector.py:120-123 override (>=25 dB prominent for 6 frames) re-emits a peak-held dead ring every cooldown_s; device.yaml:794 min_level_db -45 is an absolute gate that a manual display gain (0..60 dB, autogain now forced OFF) shifts wholesale.

**Reality:** meters.md §5.1: /-prefs/rta/decay is logf [0.25..16] ('adjustable decay time'), /peakhold enum {OFF,1..8}, /gain linf 0..60 dB (used when autogain is off). meters.md §4.2: 'UNCONFIRMED whether the reported dB is affected by /-prefs/rta/gain/autogain … best inference: values are the analyser output as displayed'. HANDOVER §4b defect 1 proved autogain (a display setting) DOES reach /meters/15, so decay/peakhold/gain almost certainly do too. Code depends on an UNCONFIRMED item with no fallback and no normalisation.

**On a real desk:** Engineer's RTA has peak hold on or a long decay (common for room tuning): CFS notches a ring, the acoustic ring dies but the displayed band falls at the decay rate / is held → VERIFY sees <6 dB in 1.5 s → deepens to -6, -9 (wasted cuts audible as a hole in the wedge), then 'not tamed' → ABORT, master backed off 6 dB mid-soundcheck; in feedback_watch the held peak keeps satisfying the 25 dB override every cooldown_s and drives the band to -9 and burns the budget. With manual gain at +40 the whole display sits 40 dB hot: every music peak clears the -45 gate; at gain 0 a real ring may sit under the gate until it is loud. Probe test_probe_set_rta_source_normalises_display_ballistics (worktree wt/fakedesk-fidelity fd2c0d3) fails today: peakhold '8', decay 16, gain 60 survive set_rta_source.

**Offline test:** Give SyntheticRta a display stage driven by FakeDesk state: per-frame fall limited to (period_s/decay_s)*K dB, peak-hold of N s, +gain dB offset when autogain==0, normalise-to-max when autogain==1 (fakedesk._meter_values reads /-prefs/rta/{decay,peakhold,gain,autogain}). Then (a) run test_ring_out_closed_loop with fakedesk.set_value('/-prefs/rta/peakhold','8') and decay 16 before arming — today it would abort/deepen to -9; (b) assert set_rta_source writes peakhold OFF, decay <=1 s, gain to a known value and reports *_cleared flags like autogain_cleared.

> **Verifier 1: CONFIRMED (high)** — All cited text and code check out. (1) FakeDesk stores rta/gain 24, autogain True, decay 1.0, peakhold OFF as inert defaults (src/x32mcp/fakedesk.py:159-160) and its /meters/15 path returns SyntheticRta frame values verbatim (fakedesk.py:943-946 `_meter_values`: `frame = self.rta.last_frame or self.rta.tick(); return list(frame.values)`); the only /-prefs/rta/* leaves the fake reacts to are source/pos (fakedesk.py:1083-1084 `_side_effects`, 1096-1109 `_mirror_rta_stat`/`_refresh_cuts`). A write to decay/peakhold/gain merely sets `_cuts_dirty` (fakedesk.py:682) and changes nothing in the stream. (2) SyntheticRta has no display stage: `_advance` (meters.py:714-718) drops a ring by `cut*period_s/loop_period_s` per frame, which the docstring (meters.py:573-577) states is literally `level -= c` per frame with the default loop_period_s=period_s — no fall-rate limit, no hold, no gain offset; `_compute` (meters.py:702-712) likewise applies cuts instantly. (3) set_rta_source (meters.py:860-941) writes source, pos, clears options bit 5, forces autogain 0 and det PEAK, verifies /-stat/rtasource — and never touches /-prefs/rta/decay, /peakhold or /gain; grep over src/ finds no other writer (device.yaml:758-766 rta section lists only source/pos/options/stat/autogain/det params). (4) Dependents: cfs.py:1221-1252 `_verify_decay` needs decay_verify_db=6 on decay_verify_frames=2 consecutive frames within decay_verify_s=1.5 (device.yaml:820-822); on failure `_notch_and_verify` (cfs.py:1200-1219) deepens and `_run_ringout` (cfs.py:1157-1163) sets abort_reason 'not tamed' → ABORT with abort_backoff_db. detector.py:33-34,120-123,361-367,417,431: a band ≥25 dB prominent for ≥6 frames is emitted regardless of growth and re-emitted once per cooldown_s, and in WATCH mode each emission calls `_notch` (cfs.py:1040-1041) → deepens to notch_max_db -9. min_level_db -45 (device.yaml:794) is an absolute gate. (5) Reality citations are accurate: meters.md §5.1 table (lines 395-403) gives gain linf 0..60, decay logf [0.25,16,19] 'adjustable decay time', peakhold enum OFF,1..8; line 446 quotes the manual that manual gain applies when autogain is disabled; §4.2 line 307 marks raw-vs-displayed as UNCONFIRMED with best inference 'as displayed'; HANDOVER §4b defect 1 (lines 154-156) confirms autogain — a display pref — did reach /meters/15 on the real desk (337 false detections). So the code relies on an UNCONFIRMED property (instant, absolute, un-held /meters/15) with no fallback, while its own M7 evidence points the other way. The project's own comment at provision.py:292-296 describes exactly the predicted failure mode when the detector cannot see a cut land: 'it can never verify decay and drives every ring to the -9 dB maximum whether the cut worked or not'. (6) The claimant's probe reproduces: running tests/integration/test_fidelity_probes.py::test_probe_set_rta_source_normalises_display_ballistics in worktree wt/fakedesk-fidelity (fd2c0d3, tests-only on top of a408a2a) FAILS today — `assert '8' == 'OFF'` — peakhold 8 / decay 16 / gain 60 survive set_rta_source. The lead reviewer independently built the same fix in worktree lead-rta-ballistics (7b0c07d 'Force the RTA's decay and peak-hold at arm time'). Caveats (do not change the verdict): (a) meters.md flags only gain/autogain explicitly as UNCONFIRMED; that decay and peakhold also shape /meters/15 is the claimant's extrapolation from 'as displayed' + the M7 autogain result — strong for decay (analyser ballistics), weaker for peakhold (could be a separate overlay trace on the console screen). (b) 'burns the budget' is overstated: NotchController budget counts distinct GEQ bands, so a peak-held dead ring is driven to -9 but consumes one band, not the budget. (c) The gain-offset sub-claim misses a partial mitigation: cfs.py:824-877 `_calibrate_floor` raises the gate floor+8 dB from measured frames — but it runs in `_open_session` before `_arm` starts the frame source (cfs.py:577-578, 684/697) and bails after _FLOOR_FIRST_FRAME_S=0.3 s with no frame (cfs.py:852-857), so in the normal path the gate stays absolute -45, and it can only raise, never lower, so gain 0 dB still hides quiet rings. Test path nit: the cited test_fakedesk.py is tests/integration/test_fakedesk.py:425-427 (content matches). Severity high per the rubric: if the inference holds and an engineer left long decay / peak hold on (common for room tuning), CFS writes unnecessary -6/-9 dB cuts and aborts a ring-out with a 6 dB master back-off mid-soundcheck — CFS acting on display artefacts, the same class as M7 defect 1; the fix (write decay/peakhold/gain at arm time and report *_cleared flags; give SyntheticRta a prefs-driven display stage so the closed-loop tests can fail) is cheap.

> **Verifier 2: CONFIRMED (medium)** — The substance is real and verified on HEAD a408a2a: (1) set_rta_source (src/x32mcp/meters.py:888-939) writes source, pos, options bit 5, autogain=0 and det=PEAK but never touches /-prefs/rta/decay, /peakhold or /gain; (2) the FakeDesk stores all of these leaves (fakedesk.py:159-160) yet _meter_values (fakedesk.py:943-946) streams SyntheticRta frames that read none of them — not even autogain, the pref M7 already proved reaches /meters/15 — so no test can express the failure; the only pref-driven RTA behaviour in the fake is the GEQ-cut mirror (_refresh_cuts, fakedesk.py:1103-1135). (3) SyntheticRta._advance (meters.py:714-718) drops a cut ring by c dB per frame with no fall-rate limit, and test_cfs.py:281-284 / test_fakedesk.py:425-427 assert that instant fall. (4) CFS depends on neutral ballistics/absolute levels: _verify_decay needs 6 dB in 1.5 s on 2 consecutive frames (cfs.py:1221-1252, device.yaml:820-822) else deepens -6/-9 then aborts; the override (detector.py:361-367, 25 dB/6 frames) re-emits any held prominent band each cooldown; min_level_db -45 (device.yaml:797) is an absolute gate applied before the override (detector.py:382). meters.md §4.2/§5.1/'Still UNCONFIRMED' explicitly flag whether gain/autogain shift /meters/15 as UNCONFIRMED, and HANDOVER §4b defect 1 shows the sibling display pref (autogain) does — so this is code depending on an UNCONFIRMED item with no fallback, exactly the class the brief asks for. The probe test in wt/fakedesk-fidelity (fd2c0d3) fails today (peakhold '8', decay 16, gain 60 all survive set_rta_source), and the lead reviewer independently wrote the same fix in wt/lead-rta-ballistics (7b0c07d, not on main).

Downgraded from high to medium on real-world consequence: every resulting action is fail-safe — cuts only, bounded at -9 dB on the dedicated ring-out GEQ, and an ABORT backs the master OFF 6 dB; nothing raises gain on garbage. It also needs a non-default operator state (long decay / peak hold on / manual gain ≠ the value Jim's desk had when autogain was forced off — factory manual gain appears to be 24 dB per the emulator's /-prefs/rta init, matching the fake), and whether decay and especially peak-hold reach the stream is unproven (the /meters/15 blob carries only the 100 bar values, so peak markers may well be UI-side; decay, an averaging constant, is more likely DSP-side like autogain). The gain sub-case is the strongest (near-certain given autogain) but is half-mitigated: _calibrate_floor (cfs.py:824-877, floor_margin_db 8 active) raises the gate when the display runs hot; only the cold direction (manual gain below Jim's) is unmitigated, delaying detection by the offset (experiment: -24 dB → ring caught 1.25 s / ~25 dB later; -36 → never; +36..+60 → clipping at 0 dBFS defeats the override). Net effect at a gig: over-deep notches, spurious VERIFY failures/aborts mid-soundcheck, watch-mode budget burned on dead held peaks, or late/loud catches — tool fails spuriously / acts sub-optimally, not an unsafe write. Offline test as proposed is right: give SyntheticRta a display stage (fall-rate from decay, hold from peakhold, +gain offset when autogain==0, normalise when autogain==1) driven by FakeDesk state, then run test_ring_out_closed_loop with peakhold 8/decay 16 pre-set and assert set_rta_source neutralises and reports them.

## E28. [medium] (fakedesk-fidelity, confirmed) Acoustic feedback grows at ~15-20 dB/s from a quiet start, so anything rising faster than 60 dB/s is an 'onset' (music transient), not a ring.

**Encoded at:** src/x32mcp/fakedesk.py:1285 (/-fake/ring defaults growth 15 dB/s, start -45 dB = exactly the gate); fakedesk.py:1338/1356 CLI --ring-growth 15; src/x32mcp/meters.py:633 inject_ring(cap -3); every closed-loop test injects 15-20 dB/s from -34..-45 dB (tests/integration/test_cfs.py:264, 333; test_fakedesk.py:413; test_server_tools.py CFS test). detector.py:48 asserts 'regenerative feedback in a ring-out grows at a few to ~30 dB/s' with no source.

**Code depends on it at:** src/x32mcp/detector.py:103 growth_max_db_per_s=60 and :334-338 (slope > max → candidate history reset every frame, growth never accrues); device.yaml:801-806 growth_min 6/ref 20; the only remaining path is the plateau override (25 dB × 6 frames, detector.py:120-123), i.e. detection ≥300 ms after the ring stops growing — at clip.

**Reality:** Physics: a regenerating loop multiplies by its open-loop gain g once per loop transit τ, so growth ≈ 20·log10(g)/τ dB/s. FOH mains at 8-10 m: τ≈25-30 ms → 0.5-1 dB excess = 17-40 dB/s (the case the fixtures model). A wedge at 1-1.5 m from an SM58 (the primary ring_out use case, monitor buses): τ≈4-6 ms incl. ~1 ms console latency → 0.5 dB excess ≈ 80-120 dB/s, 1 dB (one ring_out step_db, device.yaml:825) ≈ 170-250 dB/s. REVIEW_BRIEF §1 sets the success criterion 'every ring within ~300 ms'. Measured offline on HEAD: growth 15→ detected 2.05 s after onset at -11.8 dB; 80 → 0.6 s at -12 dB; 150 → 0.45 s at the -3 dB cap (script in this run); probe test_probe_wedge_speed_feedback_is_caught_before_clip fails: a 120 dB/s ring is first detected at -1.0 dB, its clip plateau.

**On a real desk:** On a wedge ring-out each 1 dB raise that crosses unity produces a >60 dB/s onset: the detector discards it as a transient, the wedge howls to full scale in <0.5 s, and the notch arrives only ≥300 ms after the plateau (plus write latency) — the performer takes a full-level squeal in the face on every band; in feedback_watch during a show the same happens whenever a singer cups the mic or walks in front of the wedge. Hearing-safety class, and it is invisible on the fake because no fixture ever grows faster than 20 dB/s.

**Offline test:** Replace SyntheticRta's free 'growth_db_per_s' with a physical ring model: parameters loop_delay_ms and excess_db (level += excess_db·period/loop_delay per frame; a cut c_eff changes excess to excess-c_eff), default loop_delay 5 ms for bus targets / 25 ms for main. Add detector streams at 60, 120, 250 dB/s from -70 dB with cap -1 and assert detection while the band is still < -10 dB and within 300 ms of crossing the gate; today all fail (onset guard). Also make /-fake/ring take loop_delay/excess so test_ring_out_closed_loop exercises a wedge-speed ring.

> **Verifier 1: CONFIRMED (high)** — Citations check out. detector.py:45-48 docstring asserts (unsourced; nothing in docs/research/*.md covers feedback growth rate) that 'regenerative feedback in a ring-out grows at a few to ~30 dB/s' and that anything faster than growth_max_db_per_s is 'a note onset or a swell'; detector.py:103 sets growth_max_db_per_s=60 (device.yaml does not override it); detector.py:335-338 deletes all but the last sample of the growth window whenever ≥3 samples slope >60 dB/s, so a ring that keeps rising faster than 60 dB/s alternates 1→2→3 samples→reset and never scores growth; without growth confidence caps at 0.3+0.2=0.5<0.7, leaving only the override (prominence ≥25 dB for ≥6 frames, device.yaml:810-811 / detector.py:122-123). Every fixture encodes the slow-ring belief: fakedesk.py:1285 (/-fake/ring default 15 dB/s from -45), fakedesk.py:1338/1356 (--ring-growth 15), meters.py:633, tests/integration/test_cfs.py:262,333 (20 dB/s), :409,:541 (15), test_fakedesk.py:413 (15), test_server_tools.py:617 (20), test_meters.py (6-15), test_detector.py add_ring default 15 and all uses 10-15 dB/s. No test stream exceeds 20 dB/s. cfs.py has no independent clip/runaway fallback — notches are driven only by detections.

I reproduced the dependency offline with the shipped device.yaml DetectorConfig and meters.SyntheticRta (ring from -70 dB, cap -1): there is a cliff exactly at the guard. Music-like default background: 59 dB/s → caught by growth path at -25.7 dB (conf 1.0); 61 dB/s → override only, at -15.1 dB, 0.9 s after gate; 80 → -10 dB; 120 → -1.0 dB (the cap, i.e. clip); 250 → cap. Quiet background (-70/-95 dB base): 59 dB/s → caught 0.10 s after crossing the -45 gate at -37.5 dB; 61 → 0.25 s at -27.3 dB (conf exactly 0.70 = override); 120 → -10 dB; 250 → -1 dB cap. So a wedge-speed ring is caught 10-45 dB louder than a slow one, at or near full scale for ≥120 dB/s.

Physics/engineering: loop growth ≈ excess-gain(dB)/loop-transit-time; README.md:65,216,234-236 make monitor wedges the primary ring_out/feedback_watch target and even promise '<100 ms' detection; a wedge 1-1.5 m from the mic plus ~1 ms console latency gives τ≈4-6 ms, so ring_out's own 1 dB step (device.yaml:826) that crosses unity yields ~170-250 dB/s and even 0.3 dB excess exceeds 60 dB/s. Real-desk corroboration: HANDOVER §4b item 2 — the real 8 kHz ring was never emitted by the growth path (sat at 0.50 for 15 s); only the override has ever caught real feedback.

One inaccuracy that does not change the outcome: the override is not a 'plateau' detector — it fires 6 frames (~250-300 ms) after the band first qualifies provided prominence ≥25 dB, whether or not the ring has stopped growing. But at wedge speeds the ring has climbed 30-60 dB in those 6 frames (and in a music background the 25 dB prominence requirement, halved by the ±1-band leak entering the 6-neighbour median, delays it further), so the practical claim — first notch arrives with the wedge at -15..0 dBFS, performer takes a full-level squeal per band — holds. Severity high: safety-class (hearing) miss in the primary use case of an automated procedure that deliberately provokes feedback, invisible offline because no fake/fixture can grow faster than 20 dB/s by default and none is ever asked to.

> **Verifier 2: PARTIAL (medium)** — Core claim CONFIRMED and reproduced; consequence narrative overstated, so PARTIAL with severity downgraded to medium.

What holds: (1) Every ring fixture in the suite grows 10-20 dB/s (tests/test_detector.py:82 default 15, :232/:257/:258/:285/:343; tests/integration/test_cfs.py:262,333 20 dB/s, :409,:541 15 dB/s; test_server_tools.py:617 20 dB/s; test_fakedesk.py:413 15 dB/s), the FakeDesk /-fake/ring default is 15 dB/s from -45 (src/x32mcp/fakedesk.py:1285) and the CLI default is 15 (fakedesk.py:1356); DESIGN.md:541 specifies the acceptance ring as '+15 dB/s from -40 dB'. detector.py:48 asserts 'regenerative feedback in a ring-out grows at a few to ~30 dB/s' with no citation and docs/research/*.md contains nothing at all on growth rate (no 'dB/s' anywhere in research/) — so growth_max_db_per_s=60 (detector.py:103) is an unverified belief about the room, exactly the class sought. (2) Physics: loop growth R = excess/loop-delay; a wedge at 1-1.5 m (tau 4.5-8 ms incl. console/DSP latency) with ring_out's 1 dB steps (device.yaml:825) gives R uniformly in 0..125-220 dB/s, i.e. >60 dB/s on roughly half to 70% of threshold crossings; only FOH-length paths stay under 60. (3) Mechanism verified in code: detector.py:333-339 resets the growth window whenever the 3-sample slope exceeds 60, so growth never accrues and the weighted score caps at 0.5; the only emitting path is the override (detector.py:369-375). (4) Reproduced on HEAD with the shipped device.yaml on a ring-out-realistic quiet floor (2.5 kHz ring from -70 dB, cap -1): 15/20/40/59 dB/s -> detected at frame 3, 100 ms after crossing the -45 gate, at -43..-37 dBFS via growth; 80/120/200/300 dB/s -> growth path never fires, override emits at frame 6 = 250 ms after the gate at -22 / -10 / -1(clip) / -1(clip) dBFS. Same rings with the guard disabled: 100 ms at -34 / -28 / -20 / -10 dBFS. So the guard costs 150 ms and 12-20 dB of extra howl on the physically typical wedge ring and lets rings >= ~180 dB/s (excess >~0.9 dB on a close wedge) reach bus full scale before the cut. (5) Real-desk corroboration: HANDOVER §4b / commit f43f10c — the growth path never caught the real 8 kHz howl in either run; 'the override is what made the successful catch possible'.

What does not hold: (a) 'the only remaining path is the plateau override ... detection >=300 ms after the ring stops growing — at clip' is mechanically wrong: the override needs frames>=6 since first qualification plus current prominence>=25, not a plateau, so detection lands 250 ms after gate crossing regardless — inside REVIEW_BRIEF §1's own '~300 ms' criterion and well before clip for 60-150 dB/s. (b) 'full-level squeal in the face on every band' only applies to the fastest ~10-30% of close-wedge crossings; typical is a cut at -25..-5 dBFS instead of -38..-28. (c) The finding's own probe result ('120 dB/s first detected at -1.0 dB') is an artefact of meters.SyntheticRta's default -46 dB background at 2.5 kHz (qualification becomes prominence-limited at -34 dB), not a ring-out floor; on a quiet floor 120 dB/s is caught at ~-10 dBFS. (d) The mid-show feedback_watch scenario is outside README:741's declared scope (soundcheck assistant, not a show-time suppressor). (e) No wrong write results: correct band, cuts only, -3 dB steps, VERIFY passes (a 3 dB cut against <=1 dB excess decays at hundreds of dB/s).

Severity: not 'high' — CFS does not act on garbage or write the wrong thing, and the miss is bounded (override catches within 250 ms). It is a real, untested degradation of the one timing the design promises (<100 ms detect->cut, BRIEF.md:75, README:216) in the tool where the server, not a human, holds the wedge fader, producing howls 12-20 dB louder than designed and full-scale at excess->1 dB on close wedges: medium, bordering high for that sub-case. Side note from probing: with the override present the guard buys little (a 120 dB/s swelling note >=25 dB prominent is emitted at frame 6 anyway), so the offline test proposed (loop_delay/excess ring model in SyntheticRta and /-fake/ring, streams at 60/120/250 dB/s asserting detection <-10 dBFS within 300 ms of the gate) is the right regression to add; today 120 lands at exactly -10.0 and 200+ at clip.

## E29. [medium] (fakedesk-fidelity, confirmed) The RTA frame source is already streaming when a CFS session opens, so arm-time noise-floor calibration measures the room.

**Encoded at:** tests/integration/test_cfs.py:645-697 builds a Room FrameSource, calls room.start() FIRST, assigns cfs._frames and calls the private cfs._calibrate_floor directly — the only test of the feature; the FakeDesk-backed tests never notice because LiveMeters is idle at that point and calibration silently returns the unchanged config.

**Code depends on it at:** src/x32mcp/cfs.py:890 (_open_session → _calibrate_floor) runs before cfs.py:578/697 _arm → self._frames.start() (cfs.py:920); cfs.py:852-858 bails out after _FLOOR_FIRST_FRAME_S=0.3 s with no frame ('the source is idle, skip calibration'); device.yaml:784-800 documents min_level_db as 'calibrated UP at arm time'.

**Reality:** HANDOVER §4b 'Also outstanding': calibration 'must run after the frame source starts (_open_session runs before that, and also on ring_out's preflight where frames never start)'. With the production LiveMeters (meters.py:422-441: no request is sent until start()) no /meters/15 frame can arrive during _open_session, so on a real desk the gate is always the fixed -45 dB single-room number (REVIEW_BRIEF 'right for the wrong reason'). Probe test_probe_floor_calibration_runs_on_the_production_arming_path fails today: after feedback_watch(1) on the fake, cfs._floor_db was never set.

**On a real desk:** In any room louder than Jim's studio (pub PA with walk-in music, festival stage) the -45 dB gate sits below the ambient spectrum: bass notes/HVAC rumble become candidates, notches are spent on 40-80 Hz before the first real ring (exactly the M7 failure), and the operator believes the shipped 'calibration' protects them because the test suite says it works.

**Offline test:** Delete the direct-call test and assert through the public path: arm feedback_watch on the FakeDesk with fakedesk.rta base spectrum raised (level_100hz_db=-30) and require cfs.state/report to carry floor_db and a raised gate; move _calibrate_floor into _arm after self._frames.start() (and skip it on the pending/preflight call). Add a FakeDesk 'room_floor_db' knob so integration tests run in loud and quiet rooms.

> **Verifier 1: CONFIRMED (medium)** — Both citations check out and the behaviour reproduces independently.

Code ordering (verified at HEAD a408a2a): CfsManager._open_session calls `cfg = await self._calibrate_floor(cfg)` at src/x32mcp/cfs.py:890; the only production start of the frame source is `await self._frames.start()` at cfs.py:923 inside _arm, which feedback_watch calls at cfs.py:578 (after _open_session at 577) and ring_out at cfs.py:697 (after _open_session at 684). _calibrate_floor subscribes and waits _FLOOR_FIRST_FRAME_S=0.3 s for a first frame, then `return cfg` unchanged (cfs.py:852-858). The default frame source is LiveMeters (cfs.py CfsManager.__init__: `frames if frames is not None else LiveMeters(...)`), and LiveMeters registers its on_blob handler and sends the /meters request only in start() (meters.py:422-427, 437-446) — before start() `_emit` can never fire. Nothing else starts cfs.frames: DashboardServer only subscribes ('Frame source lifecycle is the caller's', webui.py:22, 296-298), get_rta uses its own LiveMeters when CFS is idle (server.py:1512-1519), and _disarm stops frames between sessions. So on the production path calibration is always skipped; device.yaml:797-800 nevertheless ships it enabled (floor_margin_db: 8, 'Calibrated UP at arm time', 'floor_margin_db 0 disables calibration').

Test encoding: tests/integration/test_cfs.py:645-697 is the only test of the feature; it builds a Room source, `await room.start()` first, assigns `cfs._frames = room`, and calls the private `cfs._calibrate_floor(cfg)` directly — it never exercises _open_session/_arm ordering. Git history confirms the inconsistency: 56c34a7 added _calibrate_floor + test + yaml keys; 60b86d5's message says the calibration was 'Backed out' but its diff touches only device.yaml (min_level_db -60 → -45), so the dead-on-arrival code and its green test remain at HEAD.

Docs: HANDOVER.md:176-179 (§4b 'Also outstanding') says verbatim it 'must run *after* the frame source starts (`_open_session` runs before that, and also on `ring_out`'s preflight where frames never start)'; HANDOVER item 3 / REVIEW_BRIEF.md:178 'right for the wrong reason' for the -45 constant — both quoted accurately.

Reproduction: the claimant's probe (fakedesk-fidelity worktree, test_probe_floor_calibration_runs_on_the_production_arming_path) fails as stated (`_floor_db` None after feedback_watch(1)). My own independent probe (worktree verify-floor-calib-repro, commit 9ec3a01, tests/integration/test_verify_floor_calib.py) through the public feedback_watch path on the FakeDesk shows: room peak seen after arm = -10.9 dB (the fake's default base spectrum is loud), detector gate = -45.0 unchanged, _floor_db unset, no 'room floor' log line; a control test that starts cfs.frames (the production LiveMeters) first and then calls _calibrate_floor raises the gate (floor -10.0 → gate -2.0), proving the only defect is ordering (and incidentally that there is no cap, as HANDOVER also warns). No fallback was missed: the only fallback is the static single-room -45 dB constant, which is exactly the claimant's point.

Minor nits that do not change the verdict: the frames.start() line is 923 not 920; `self._floor_db/_gate_db = None` initialisers sit misplaced inside CfsError.__init__ (cfs.py:122-123) rather than CfsManager, so CfsManager has no _floor_db attribute until a calibration succeeds. Severity medium is appropriate: behaviour on a real desk degrades to the known fixed-gate M7 behaviour (room noise/walk-in music above -45 dB becomes candidates and can spend notches at 40-80 Hz) while the suite certifies a calibration that never runs; it is not a new unsafe write beyond the bounded -9 dB GEQ cuts.

> **Verifier 2: CONFIRMED (medium)** — The assumption is real and encoded exactly as claimed. src/x32mcp/cfs.py:890 calls _calibrate_floor inside _open_session; _arm only starts the frame source afterwards at cfs.py:923. The production source is LiveMeters, which subscribes to blobs and sends the /meters request only inside start() (meters.py:422-427); before that _emit is never reached, so no subscriber (including the calibration grab) can see a frame. _calibrate_floor therefore always hits the _FLOOR_FIRST_FRAME_S=0.3 s timeout (cfs.py:855-858) and returns the unchanged config: on a real X32 the candidate gate is always the fixed device.yaml min_level_db -45, even though device.yaml:798 has floor_margin_db: 8 (calibration nominally enabled) and device.yaml:784-786 says the gate is 'Calibrated UP at arm time'. The dashboard only subscribes to cfs.frames and never starts it (webui.py:296-298; server.py:163), rta_snapshot uses its own LiveMeters (server.py:1512), and a previous session's _disarm stops the source, so there is no production path on which frames are flowing at _open_session time. The only test of the feature (tests/integration/test_cfs.py:645-697) starts a hand-rolled Room source FIRST, swaps it into cfs._frames and calls the private cfs._calibrate_floor directly, so it certifies the arithmetic while encoding the assumption that frames are already streaming; the FakeDesk-backed tests (which use the default LiveMeters over the fake, test_cfs.py:70-71) never notice because calibration silently no-ops. Empirically confirmed: the probe test_probe_floor_calibration_runs_on_the_production_arming_path (fakedesk-fidelity worktree) fails on HEAD a408a2a — after feedback_watch(1) through the public path, cfs has no measured _floor_db. HANDOVER §4b and commit 60b86d5 state exactly this ('it must run after the frame source starts (_open_session runs before that, and also on ring_out's preflight where frames never start)') and claim the change was 'backed out' — but 60b86d5 only touched device.yaml; the 56c34a7 code, the enabled floor_margin_db and the green test named test_candidate_gate_is_calibrated_to_the_room_noise_floor all remain, so the suite advertises a protection that never runs. Extra evidence of the half-back-out: cfs.py:122-123 initialise self._floor_db/_gate_db inside CfsError.__init__ (indentation slip), not CfsManager.

Skeptical weighing: (1) No tool output lies — floor_db/gate_db are never surfaced in state/report/feedback_watch return, only in a log line that never fires; the 'operator believes calibration protects them' harm is via docs/tests/commit history, not tool output. (2) HANDOVER §4b already lists it as outstanding, so it is known to the author, though the task's calibration list does not include it and the misleading green test is squarely the REVIEW_BRIEF §2 class. (3) The proposed fix (move after _frames.start()) is necessary but not sufficient: as written calibration has no cap, so in a pub with walk-in music at -30 dB it would gate at -22 dB and deafen the detector to the -25 dB howl M7 actually missed — HANDOVER flags the cap requirement too; it must also be skipped on ring_out's pending/preflight call. (4) Real gig consequence stands: with no frequency window implemented (detector.py has none; HANDOVER names it as the next change) the fixed -45 gate is one room's number ('right for the wrong reason', HANDOVER §4b item 3); any venue whose loudest RTA band exceeds ~-53 dB lets ambient LF content become candidates and CFS can spend -3..-9 dB GEQ notches on 40-80 Hz rumble/bass before a real ring — the M7 failure #3 repeats, bounded and restorable but a wrong write. (5) Side effect: every _open_session stalls 0.3 s waiting for a frame that cannot arrive (feedback_watch and both ring_out calls) — cosmetic. Medium is appropriate: not high because the dead code itself writes nothing wrong and the residual risk is the documented fixed-gate limitation; not low because the suite positively certifies a safety-relevant feature that is inert on the only production path and the config file claims it is active.

## E30. [medium] (fakedesk-fidelity, confirmed) Whatever /-prefs/rta/source we wrote is what /meters/15 analyses for the whole session; nobody and nothing else (solo, console screen, X32-Edit, a second engineer) redirects the analyser, and the /-stat/rtasource read-back can be trusted because it always matches.

**Encoded at:** src/x32mcp/fakedesk.py:943-946 (type-15 frames come from SyntheticRta regardless of /-prefs/rta/source, /-stat/solosw/*, /-stat/screen/* or /config/solo; only the CUTS follow the source strip, :1109-1119); fakedesk.py:1094-1101 _mirror_rta_stat computes /-stat/rtasource with the very formula production checks against (src/x32mcp/meters.py:826-830 rta_stat_expected) — verification cannot fail on the fake. tests/integration/test_fakedesk.py:383-400, test_cfs.py:252 (stat_actual==146) certify the mirror against itself.

**Code depends on it at:** src/x32mcp/cfs.py:907-929 _arm proceeds when ses.rta.verified is False (only published as rta_verified); no subscription to /-stat/rtasource or /-prefs/rta/source pushes during the session (cfs.py has no reference to solosw/screen); meters.py:925-935 verify_attempts=2 × 0.1 s.

**Reality:** meters.md §5.3: Solo Priority 'replaces the RTA source with the monitor solo bus whenever a channel solo is active' (bit 5 is cleared once at arm, but the operator can re-tick it); 'Which of the three analyses /meters/15 carries when a PEQ or GEQ page is displayed on the console (or on a remote client) remains UNCONFIRMED … Safe practice: put the console on the METERS/RTA tab … or at least do not leave an FX GEQ page showing'; §6 gotcha 15: /-stat/rtasource may be stale after a console reset; source 0 = dynamic selected-channel mode. During a ring-out the engineer is very likely to open exactly the FX5 GEQ page to watch the cuts.

**On a real desk:** Engineer opens the GEQ page or solos the kick with Solo Priority back on, or X32-Edit's RTA view rewrites the source: the detector now analyses a different signal and writes notches into the monitor bus GEQ for peaks that are not in that bus (wrong writes, budget gone, real ring later missed); a failed source write is logged and the session arms anyway, notching bus 3's GEQ from Main LR's spectrum.

**Offline test:** Make FakeDesk's type-15 content depend on the resolved source: per-strip SyntheticRta (or silence for strips with no ring), honour /-stat/solosw + options bit 5 (solo hijack) and a '/-stat/screen/FX page showing' switch that swaps in the GEQ-overlay analysis; compute /-stat/rtasource from an independent table and allow a 'stale after reset' mode. Tests: arming with an unverified source must refuse (or re-write via /-action/setrtasrc); a mid-session push of /-stat/rtasource≠expected or a solo must pause notching and raise a warning event.
