HANDOVER §4a/§4b record no contrary real-desk observation. Minor overstatement: claimant says verified is 'only published as rta_verified' — it is also in the tool result/report — but that is reporting, not a fallback. Severity kept at medium (agreeing with claimant): the consequence is wrong GEQ writes / budget burned on a foreign spectrum, but it needs a lost datagram, a stale stat, or operator/second-client interference (and the GEQ-page redirect is itself UNCONFIRMED), and Solo Priority is proactively cleared.

> **Verifier 2: PARTIAL (medium)** — What holds up: (1) FakeDesk's /meters/15 content is source-blind — fakedesk.py:943-946 returns SyntheticRta's frame for type 15 whatever /-prefs/rta/source says; only the GEQ cuts follow the source strip (_refresh_cuts, :1103-1109). The fake has no /-stat/solosw, no /-stat/screen/*, no Solo-Priority semantics at all (grep: zero hits), so none of the meters.md §5.3 redirections (solo hijack via options bit 5, GEQ-overlay analysis while an FX GEQ page is displayed, dynamic source 0/1) can be exercised offline. (2) Product code relies on an item meters.md §5.3 marks UNCONFIRMED ('Which of the three analyses /meters/15 carries when a PEQ or GEQ page is displayed … remains UNCONFIRMED … Safe practice: put the console on the METERS/RTA tab via /-stat/screen/screen ,i 1 + /-stat/screen/METER/page ,i 4') without the documented fallback: nothing in src/ or device.yaml references /-stat/screen, and cfs.py never re-reads or subscribes to /-stat/rtasource or /-prefs/rta/source after _arm (cfs.py:911-929). During a ring-out the engineer opening the GEQ page to watch the cuts is the expected behaviour, and in ring_out_system leaving bus 1's FX-slot GEQ page open while the run moves to bus 2 (different slot) is a realistic way to have the detector watch the wrong bus while cfs raises bus 2's master — if the UNCONFIRMED behaviour goes the wrong way. (3) _arm proceeds on verified=False and ring_out (automated, raises the master) has no gate on it; only feedback_watch's summary says 'RTA NOT verified' (server.py:1645) and the cfs.state event carries rta_verified.

What does not hold up / is mitigated: the /-stat/rtasource mirror (fakedesk.py:1094-1101) is not a self-certifying fiction — it implements exactly the mapping meters.md §5.2 documents as VERIFIED (Bus N post = 146+N−1, Main post 168, Monitor 72) and the real desk at M7 armed with RTA verified on Main LR (HANDOVER §4b, no verification defect among the four found). The unverified path is unit-tested with a non-mirroring fake (tests/test_meters.py:683-693) and 'mismatch is logged, never raised' is an explicit design decision (meters.py:25), so 'verification cannot fail on the fake' is only true of the integration FakeDesk, not the suite. Solo hijack needs the operator to re-tick Solo Priority on the RTA prefs page after arm (set_rta_source clears bit 5, meters.py:903-906) — unlikely mid ring-out. In the standard single-bus topology (GEQ inserted on the target bus = RTA source) the GEQ overlay by default analyses 'the bus in which the EQ is inserted' (§5.3 bit-2 row), i.e. the same bus, so the claimed 'notches for peaks that are not in that bus' does not follow from merely opening that page; the realistic effect there is a tap difference (pre-GEQ overlay → cut not measurable → VERIFY deepens a false-positive notch), and a genuine ring still dies acoustically at any tap (HANDOVER §4b item 4). Reaching 'unverified but armed' on a real desk needs a lost fire-and-forget UDP write (connection.py:520-530) or the post-reset stale stat of gotcha 15 — possible, not common on a wired LAN.

Net: a genuine fidelity gap plus a missing fallback for an UNCONFIRMED protocol behaviour, with a plausible (not certain) wrong-bus/blind-detector outcome in ring_out_system; the mirror/verification half of the finding is refuted. Medium stands on the UNCONFIRMED-without-fallback rule and the ring_out_system scenario; it is not high because every damaging path is contingent on unverified console behaviour or unusual operator action, and the operator is at the desk with stop/panic.

## E31. [medium] (fakedesk-fidelity, confirmed) A scene recall changes a handful of names/colours, completes instantly, and never touches FX slot types, inserts, GEQ bands, routing or the bus being rung out; nobody presses GO on the desk during a CFS session.

**Encoded at:** src/x32mcp/fakedesk.py:166-177 (_SCENES differ only in config/name and config/color), :564-580 (_build_scenes = current state + names), :1142-1157 (_recall_scene applies synchronously inside the goscene handler and sets /-show/prepos/current first); show_control default 'SCENES' (:158). tests/integration/test_desk.py:466-524, test_server_tools.py:286-320, test_fakedesk.py:454-495 verify recall by the instantly-updated pointer.

**Code depends on it at:** src/x32mcp/desk.py:1251-1288 recall_scene polls /-show/prepos/current for 2 s (reply to goscene UNCONFIRMED) and invalidates the cache; src/x32mcp/cfs.py (whole session) holds fx_slot/side/sel and NotchController gains captured at preflight (cfs.py:884-889) with no subscription to /-show/prepos/current, /fx/N/type or */insert/sel pushes; desk.py:1417-1424 set_geq_band re-reads /fx/N type through a 2 s TTL cache.

**Reality:** fx_routing_scenes.md §6.1-6.4: a scene stores ~the whole console (effects rack, inserts, routing, headamps subject to scene/param safes); recall = 'highlighting + GO on the desk; honours scene safes'; §13 items 10-11: goscene reply and prepos numbering UNCONFIRMED; HANDOVER §4a: the real desk boots with prepos -1, sits in CUES, holds scenes 'Studio Sept 26'/'molecules' with real content, and a PSU fault reboots it ('state may not survive'). Engineers recall scenes/snippets per song during shows — the feedback_watch use case.

**On a real desk:** Song-change snippet or scene GO mid-watch: FX5 becomes the band's vocal reverb or the GEQ is reset flat; CFS still believes band 22 is at -3, its next 'deepen' writes -6 into a slot that may no longer be a GEQ (set_geq_band catches a type change only after the cache TTL/push; a GEQ reset to flat is not caught at all — existing-gain bookkeeping is now 3-9 dB off and validate's matched_session lies); a recall that moves the monitor master invalidates ses.master_db so BACKOFF/ABORT writes an absolute level computed from stale state (could RAISE the bus).

**Offline test:** FakeDesk scene realism switch: scenes 1/2 carry different /fx/5..8 types, */insert blocks, GEQ pars, bus faders and routing; recall applies over ~800 ms in chunks with pushes, optional 'GET stalls during load'; show_control default CUES and prepos -1 at boot. Test: during feedback_watch, fakedesk recall of a scene that changes /fx/5/type or zeroes /fx/5/par must pause/abort the session with a cfs.abort reason within 1 s and never write a par afterwards; a recall that moves /bus/01/mix/fader must re-base ses.master_db before any back-off.

> **Verifier 1: CONFIRMED (high)** — Core claim — a CFS session captures fx_slot/side/sel, GEQ band bookkeeping and master_db once at preflight and never reconciles them with desk-side changes (scene/snippet GO, operator), so a recall mid-session makes CFS act on stale state — is confirmed by code reading AND by three repro tests run against the unmodified FakeDesk (worktree $SP/worktrees/verify-scene-recall-midsession-repro, commit 7ae914d, tests/integration/test_scene_recall_midsession.py; all 3 'pass' because they only print, but the printed behaviour is the defect):

1. GO scene 1 during feedback_watch (fake reverts FX5 GEQ2->DES2, bus-1 insert FX5L->OFF, pars flat, bus fader -20->~0): CFS stays in WATCH, publishes no cfs.abort, every later detection logs 'notch write failed ... NOT_A_GEQ: FX slot 5 holds DES2' and the ring is never cut; worse, NotchController.plan() mutates _gains/_touched BEFORE the write (detector.py:567-584, cfs.py:1070-1086 never rolls back), so cfs.state reports phantom notches band 22 = -9 dB and band 25 = -9 dB with budget_left 4 while the desk holds DES2 with flat pars — status/dashboard lies and budget is burnt on nothing.
2. GO on a scene that keeps FX5=GEQ2 but flat pars: after a real -3 dB notch, recall resets par22 to 0.5 raw; next ring -> CFS 'deepens' -3 -> -6 and writes -6 absolute onto a flat band; bookkeeping never sees the reset (validate_notch is checked against the stale 'current', _DeskGeqWriter.gains cfs.py:397-416). Had the scene carried a deeper cut the write would raise that band.
3. ring_out bus 1 from -20 dB; at RAISE -15 the bus master is pulled to -60 on the desk: CFS's next RAISE writes -14 dB ABSOLUTE with ramp_ms=0 (+46 dB in one step on a wedge bus), carries on to -6, BACKOFF to -9, final_stage DONE, abort_reason None, report never mentions it. Mechanism: _run_ringout nxt = ses.master_db + step (cfs.py:1174-1176), _finalize_levels final = ses.master_db - back written with force=True (cfs.py:1280-1285), and Desk._move_level deliberately has no relative guard on absolute moves (desk.py:959-965); set_level reads before_db but CFS never compares it to ses.master_db.

Citations verified: fakedesk.py:166-177 (_SCENES = names/colours only), :564-577 (_build_scenes = boot state + names), :1142-1157 (synchronous _recall_scene, pointer stored first), :158 show_control SCENES default, prepos 0 at :154; desk.py:1251-1288 recall_scene polls prepos 2 s; cfs.py:884-896 session built from preflight; cfs.py:522 the only event subscription is connection.state; desk.py:1417 set_geq_band reads /fx/N via _section (TTL 2 s, push-invalidated via _on_push :282). Research: fx_routing_scenes.md §6.3 scene safes bits (Effects, Mix Buses, Routing, Out Patch...) and §6.4 'Equivalent to highlighting + GO on the desk; honours scene safes', 'load ... not necessarily fully completed when the status is returned'; §6.2 'Every parameter that changed on recall is also pushed'; §13 items 10-11 UNCONFIRMED as stated. HANDOVER §4a: desk in CUES, scenes 0 'Studio Sept 26'/1 'molecules', FX5 already GEQ2, PSU fault reboots — as stated.

Caveats (do not change the verdict): (a) 'prepos -1 at boot' is not in HANDOVER §4a; it is a real-desk observation recorded in tests/integration/test_desk.py:656 docstring and is already handled+tested (current_scene -> index None). (b) CUES show_control is already handled by recall_scene/current_scene (desk.py:1258-1262, test_desk.py:507-524), so the 'goscene reply UNCONFIRMED / CUES default' parts are mitigated, not defects. (c) The fake is more capable than the finding says: because scenes snapshot boot state, a recall in the FakeDesk DOES revert FX types, inserts, GEQ pars and bus faders changed since boot (demonstrated); what is missing is scene-to-scene content variation, recall latency/chunking, and any test that fires a recall (or external fader move) during a live CFS session. (d) set_geq_band caught the type change immediately via the push, not only after TTL.

Severity raised to high (claimant said medium): item 3 is a wrong, un-ramped +46 dB write to a monitor bus and item 1 is CFS acting on garbage (phantom notches, burnt budget, untamed ring, no abort) — both match the brief's 'high' definition. The trigger need not even be a scene: an engineer grabbing the wedge fader because it howls produces item 3 identically.

> **Verifier 2: PARTIAL (medium)** — Core claim CONFIRMED, several sub-claims wrong or already mitigated.

CONFIRMED (reproduced offline, worktree $SP/worktrees/verify-scene-recall-midsession-repro, tests/integration/test_scene_recall_midsession.py, commit 0a641e6): a CFS session captures fx_slot/side/sel, the GEQ gains and master_db once at preflight (cfs.py:884-897 _open_session; _DeskGeqWriter.gains cfs.py:401-417; NotchController._gains detector.py:526-536) and nothing reconciles them with desk-side changes — no subscription to /-show/prepos/current, /fx/N/type, /fx/N/par/* or */insert/* pushes anywhere in cfs.py. A front-panel GO (fakedesk.set('/-action/goscene', n), which the existing FakeDesk already handles like the real desk: full stored state applied + pushed) during feedback_watch produced three concrete misbehaviours:
 (1) Scene reverts FX5 GEQ2->DES2 and clears the bus insert: every subsequent detection logs 'notch write failed NOT_A_GEQ' (Desk.set_geq_band desk.py:1417-1424 caught the type change because the /fx/5/type push invalidated the cache — so NO par write reached the non-GEQ effect; that part of the finding's failure story did not happen), but the session neither aborts nor publishes cfs.abort, cfs.state.mode stays WATCH, and because NotchController._apply commits gains/touched before the write (detector.py:567-572) and cfs._notch never rolls back on a failed write (cfs.py:1071-1086), cfs.state.notches and the saved report claim band 22 = -9 dB and band 25 = -9 dB that were never written and budget drops 6->4. The operator's dashboard says the bus is protected with two deep cuts; the desk has no GEQ at all. Tool lies about protection at a gig = medium.
 (2) Scene keeps the rack but reloads the GEQ flat: CFS belief -3, desk 0, next detection writes -6 in one step. Bounded, still a cut = low.
 (3) Scene reloads the GEQ with a deeper cut than the session knows (band 22 = -9 from a previous ring-out) and the ring reappears: CFS writes -6 then -9, i.e. the wire effect of the first 'cut' is a +3 dB RAISE of a ringing band while it rings, published as cfs.notch depth -6. policy.validate_notch (policy.py:405-422) checks 'no boost' against CFS's own bookkeeping, never the desk, so the cuts-only invariant holds only if nobody else touches that GEQ. Absolute gain can never exceed 0 dB and the relative raise is at most back to CFS's belief, so it is bounded; and it needs a mid-session external GEQ change. Note the same root cause is hit by the far more common case of the engineer grabbing the ring-out GEQ in X32-Edit during the show (two hands on one control), which makes this more than theoretical.
Realism: feedback_watch is the during-the-show mode; cue/scene/snippet GO between songs or at band changeover is normal X32 practice (the test desk itself sits in CUES mode, HANDOVER §4a), and fx_routing_scenes.md §6.1/6.3 confirms a scene carries the effects rack, inserts and bus processing subject to safes. For ring_out (a 1-2 minute soundcheck procedure the operator started) a GO is operator self-sabotage; the stale-master BACKOFF concern (cfs.py:1280-1284 writes ses.master_db - back with force=True) is real in code but writes a level at or below what the room heard seconds earlier — low.

REFUTED / already mitigated sub-claims: (a) 'FakeDesk scenes differ only in names/colours and recall never touches FX types, inserts, GEQ, routing or the bus' — wrong: _build_scenes (fakedesk.py:564-577) stores the full boot-time non-/- state per scene, and my repro shows a recall reverting /fx/5/type, /bus/01/insert/sel|on, /fx/5/par/* and the bus fader (-20 -> 0 dB). The fake needs no 'scene realism switch' for this; the gap is purely that no test presses GO (or touches the GEQ) while a session runs. (b) show_control default SCENES vs the real desk's CUES — Desk.recall_scene/current_scene already handle non-SCENES (desk.py:1257-1262, returns verified=None + note) and tests/integration/test_desk.py:503-517 covers it. (c) goscene reply UNCONFIRMED (§13 item 10/11) — recall_scene does not depend on a reply; it polls prepos for 2 s and degrades to verified=False, i.e. it has the required fallback. (d) 'recall completes instantly' — the fake is synchronous, the real desk streams the change (DOC fn.39-41), but recall_scene invalidates the whole cache and later pushes keep invalidating; worst case is a torn read immediately after recall — cosmetic.

Net: the operator assumption 'nothing outside CFS changes the ring-out GEQ / FX slot / insert during a session' is genuinely baked in (zero tests, zero code defence beyond the per-write type check), reproducible today, and at a gig yields a silently useless watch with a lying state/report and, in the deeper-cut case, a bounded wrong-direction write. That is medium (tool reports wrong state; conditional unsafe-direction write), not high, and the fake-fidelity framing of the finding is largely incorrect.

## E32. [medium] (fakedesk-fidelity, confirmed) The head amp behind a channel can be computed from config/source + routing blocks (+ userrout for UIN) and the computation is correct because the test's expected values come from the same inference.

**Encoded at:** FakeDesk stores /config/routing/*, /config/userrout/* and /headamp/* as unrelated leaves and models no /-ha/NN/index (scales_params.md §12: the desk's read-only 'actual headamp used as source for a given input'); its FW-4.06 identity ships FW-2.x style 'AN1-8' routing defaults (fakedesk.py:136-145) unless a test rewrites them; tests/integration/test_desk.py:710-740 and test_cfs.py:210-236 assert headamp_index_for against hand-derived numbers from the same §12.4 algorithm.

**Code depends on it at:** src/x32mcp/desk.py:722-783 headamp_index_for (block_base table, AUX ranges (1,0),(4,32),(7,80), PLAY routswitch branch, UIN→userrout 1..128 mapping verified on ONE channel of one desk); desk.py:1352-1370 set_phantom(target) resolves a strip to that index and writes /headamp/NNN/phantom; provision.discover_mics 'physical' verdict (provision.py:576).

**Reality:** scales_params.md §12.4: the algorithm is 'inferred, not stated in the PDF — mark UNCONFIRMED and validate against /-ha/NN/index on a real desk'; §17 repeats it; HANDOVER §4a defect 5: the first contact with FW-4.x user routing made EVERY channel resolve to None, and the fix was validated for ch 1-4 on one X32 Rack (local 1, card, card, AES50-A 1). AUX-in blocks, AES50-B, PLAY (virtual sound-check) mode and userrout values 33-128 on other stage-box layouts remain unverified; the desk offers the authoritative answer for inputs 00-39 and the code never reads it.

**On a real desk:** set_phantom('ch.12', on) on a desk whose AUX/AES50-B/user routing differs from the inference switches 48 V on the WRONG preamp: a phantom thump through an open channel into the PA, 48 V onto a ribbon mic or a keyboard DI on another musician's input, while the intended condenser stays dead; discover_mics counts card returns as mics or drops real ones.

**Offline test:** Give FakeDesk an independent, table-driven /-ha/NN/index (computed from a routing matrix written from the DOC lists, not from desk.py's function) including S16/AES50-B and PLAY layouts; make headamp_index_for read /-ha/NN/index first and fall back to the inference only when it is -1/unavailable, and assert both agree across a sweep of routing permutations; require set_phantom to read back /headamp/NNN and the strip's /-ha index before reporting success.

> **Verifier 1: CONFIRMED (medium)** — Both citations hold and there is no fallback the claimant missed.

Research/handover text checks out verbatim: scales_params.md §12.3 (lines 773-784) documents `/-ha/[00..39]/index` as the desk's read-only "actual headamp used as source for a given input" and says "Prefer querying /-ha/NN/index over computing"; §12.4 (785-787, 834) marks the compute-it-yourself algorithm "inferred, not stated in the PDF — mark UNCONFIRMED and validate against /-ha/NN/index on a real desk" and "still UNCONFIRMED as an algorithm"; §17 (line 1049) repeats "the console's own /-ha/NN/index is authoritative". HANDOVER §4a defect 5 (lines 127-129, 139-142) confirms the FW-4.x user-routing failure and that the fix was observed only on X32RACK-Jim ch 1-4 (local 1, card, card, AES50-A 1 → 032).

Code checks out: desk.py:722-783 headamp_index_for implements the §12.4 inference (block_base table 742-749, UIN→`/config/userrout/in/{src:02d}`-1 at 764-768, AUX ranges (1,0),(4,32),(7,80) at 775-778, PLAY routswitch at 737) and its own docstring says "§12.4 (UNCONFIRMED…)"; desk.py:51-53 header repeats "UNCONFIRMED algorithm… pass an int head-amp index to bypass it" — an acknowledged risk, not a runtime fallback. `grep '/-ha'` over device.yaml, src/ and tests/ returns nothing: the descriptor does not even declare /-ha/NN/index, Desk never reads it, FakeDesk (fakedesk.py) has no such leaf and stores /config/routing/*, /config/userrout/* and /headamp/* as independent leaves (defaults fakedesk.py:135-145, identity FW "4.06" at :289). set_phantom (desk.py:1352-1371) resolves a target through headamp_index_for and writes /headamp/NNN/phantom with no read-back of /headamp/NNN or /-ha. provision.discover_mics uses `physical = headamp_index_for(c) is not None` (provision.py:582, claimant said 576) and preflight turns "no physical candidates" into a PREFLIGHT_FAILED blocker (provision.py:643-645), so CFS arming depends on the inference. Tests encode the same inference: test_desk.py:567-568 ("routing IN 1-8 = AN1-8 -> head amp 004 (scales_params.md §12.4)"), test_desk.py:710-740 (only the identity layout IN/1-8=UIN1-8 seen on the one real desk), test_cfs.py:215/232 (CARD9-16 → not physical).

Per the brief's own rule ("code that depends on an UNCONFIRMED item without a fallback is a finding") this qualifies, and it goes beyond known defect 5: the fix is still inference-only, and I found a concrete divergence even from the research algorithm — §12.4 indexes `userrout_in[(r-20)*8+off]` (block-relative) while desk.py:765 reads `userrout/in/{src}`; they agree only when IN block b is assigned UIN block b (the only case tested). With IN/9-16=UIN1-8 (legal, fx_routing_scenes.md §4.3 VERIFIED enum 0..23 for every block) ch 9 resolves through the wrong userrout slot, flipping physical/non-physical in discover_mics or pointing set_phantom at another preamp. AUX-in on UIN1-2/1-4/1-6 returns None (safe-side but drops real mics).

Caveats (why medium, not high): set_phantom is NOT exposed as an MCP tool (server.py defines no phantom tool; only the Python Desk API and tests call it), so the "48 V on the wrong preamp at a gig" path is not operator-reachable today; the operator-facing failure is discover_mics/preflight mis-classifying inputs (spurious "no candidate mics" PREFLIGHT_FAILED, or card returns counted as mics — HANDOVER §4b already notes discover_mics over-reports). The AN/A/B block→index branches rest on individually VERIFIED enum order (§4.3) and index ranges (§12.2), so those are low-risk; the genuinely unverified parts are UIN cross-block, AUX-in, AES50-B, PLAY and userrout values 33-128 on other stage-box layouts. "FW-2.x style AN1-8 defaults" is a loose characterization (AN1-8 is also a valid FW-4 factory state), but the substantive point — the fake cannot arbitrate the inference because it models no /-ha — stands.

Offline repro committed in worktree <review-worktrees>/verify-ha-index-authority (commit 8f91660, tests/integration/test_ha_index_authority_repro.py): 3 tests fail today — (1) FakeDesk has zero /-ha/* leaves; (2) spying the fake's GET and /node handlers during headamp_index_for('ch.1') + set_phantom(ch.1) shows only `node ch/01/config`, `node config/routing`, `node config/routing/IN`, `node config/routing/PLAY` (plus the pre-write snapshot sweep) — no /-ha read; (3) with an injected authoritative `/-ha/00/index = 7` disagreeing with AN1-8 routing, set_phantom(ch.1) still writes /headamp/000/phantom ("48 V went to head amp 0 per the UNCONFIRMED inference; the desk's own /-ha/00/index said 7").

> **Verifier 2: CONFIRMED (medium)** — The facts of the finding check out, and an offline repro shows the inference is not merely UNCONFIRMED but demonstrably diverges from the research doc's own algorithm in two routing layouts; the FakeDesk cannot expose any of it because it models routing, userrout and headamps as unrelated leaves and has no /-ha/NN/index at all.

1. Code depends on the UNCONFIRMED §12.4 inference and never consults the desk's authoritative answer. scales_params.md §12.3 (VERIFIED, PDF p.43): `/-ha/00..39/index` is read-only 'actual headamp used as source for a given input … Prefer querying /-ha/NN/index over computing'. §12.4 and §17 (line 1049): the compute-it-yourself algorithm is 'inferred, not stated in the PDF — mark UNCONFIRMED and validate against /-ha/NN/index on a real desk'. `grep -rn '/-ha' src/ device.yaml` → nothing: desk.py:722-783 headamp_index_for is the only resolver, device.yaml declares no /-ha node, fakedesk.py has no /-ha and its FW-4.06 'X32' identity ships classic AN1-8 routing (fakedesk.py:135-139). HANDOVER §4a defect 5 validated the UIN fix on exactly one desk for ch1→local 1 and ch4→AES50-A 1 (=032); AUX blocks, AES50-B, PLAY/routswitch, and non-default UIN layouts were never seen.

2. The tests encode the same inference. test_desk.py:567-571 (IN05 under AN1-8 → 4), test_desk.py:710-740 (UIN1-8 on block 1-8 with userrout/in/01..04 → 0/None/None/32; AN1-8 → ch4=3) and test_cfs.py:222-229 (physical_input) all assert numbers hand-derived from §12.4 against a FakeDesk that has no independent notion of which preamp feeds which input, so any error in the inference is invisible.

3. Concrete divergence found (stronger than the finding states). §12.4 indexes the user-in patch by the UIN block assigned to the routing block: `userrout_in[(r-20)*8 + off]`. desk.py:764 instead reads `/config/userrout/in/{src:02d}` — indexed by the input number. They agree only when routing block b selects UIN block b (the default 1-8→UIN1-8 … layout Jim's Rack has). Repro (worktree verify-uin-crossblock-repro, tests/integration/test_uin_crossblock_repro.py, run today, 4 failed): IN/1-8=UIN9-16, userrout/in/09=1 (local 1), userrout/in/01=5 → headamp_index_for('ch.1') returns 4 (doc: 0) and Desk.set_phantom(ch.1,on) writes /headamp/004/phantom=1 while /headamp/000 stays 0 — 48 V on local XLR 5, the mic on ch.1 stays dead; IN/9-16=UIN1-8 ('custom bank of 8', a realistic FW4 use of per-block UIN), userrout/in/01=33 → ch.9 resolves to 16 (local 17) instead of 32 (AES50-A 1); IN/AUX=UIN1-2 → auxin.1 resolves None although §12.4 resolves it via userrout (desk.py:775-781 has no UIN branch for aux; fails safe as NOT_SUPPORTED).

Skeptical downgrades / mitigations: (a) Desk.set_phantom(target) is NOT exposed as an MCP tool or via the web UI at HEAD (no 'phantom' in server.py/webui.py; only DESIGN §13:579 and the Desk API), so the 'phantom thump / 48 V on a ribbon' gig scenario is latent, not reachable by the LLM today — this keeps it out of 'high'. (b) discover_mics (provision.py:582) only uses None-vs-not-None and iterates ch strips only, so for classic AN/A/B block routing and the default UIN layout its verdict is right regardless of the exact index; it goes wrong only when a cross-block UIN layout makes the wrongly-read userrout slot flip local/AES50 vs card/USB (card return counted as a mic → CFS rings out against playback, or a real mic dropped → 'no candidate mics' blocker). (c) The block-base table for AN/A/B follows the PDF's verbatim index ranges (§12.2 VERIFIED) and positional enums (§10 VERIFIED), so the residual risk there is genuinely theoretical. Net: a tool that can report wrong state at a gig under plausible non-default FW-4 routing, plus a latent wrong-preamp phantom write in the Desk API, with zero test coverage possible on the current FakeDesk → medium, as the finding says; not high.

Offline test as proposed is right: give FakeDesk a table-driven /-ha/NN/index derived from its own routing/userrout leaves (from the DOC lists, not desk.py), add it to device.yaml, make headamp_index_for read /-ha first and fall back to inference only on -1/timeout, sweep routing permutations (incl. cross-block UIN, aux UIN, PLAY, AES50-B) asserting agreement, and have set_phantom(target) refuse when /-ha and the inference disagree.

## E33. [medium] (meters-rta, confirmed) ring_out may keep raising the bus master on its dwell timer whether or not any RTA frame has arrived — the analyser stream is assumed to be always flowing and fresh (as the FakeDesk's perfectly periodic asyncio stream is).

**Encoded at:** src/x32mcp/fakedesk.py:913-925 (_meter_stream: one frame every interval, never late, never lost) + src/x32mcp/meters.py:723-727,753-760 (SyntheticRta ticks on a virtual clock, ts = t0 + i*period); every CFS integration test (tests/integration/test_cfs.py:262,333,409,541) therefore runs RAISE with frames guaranteed.

**Code depends on it at:** src/x32mcp/cfs.py:1153-1198 (_run_ringout: `nxt = min(master+step, target)` → _write_master → _dwell(dwell_ms) loops on time alone; nothing consults ses.frames / ses.last_ts / LiveMeters.last_rx_age_s); cfs.py:1028 additionally drops every frame whose wall-clock ts <= last_ts, so an NTP step backwards (LiveMeters stamps with time.time(), meters.py:392) silently deafens the detector while RAISE continues.

**Reality:** meters.md §1.2/§6.7: 'Update cycle … may be variable according to console's ability to fulfill requests … Don't derive timing from packet arrival'; §1.3/§6.6: the stream is a 10 s lease renewed by our own UDP datagram every 5 s (two lost renewals = a multi-second gap); §5.3: /meters/15 may carry something else while a GEQ/PEQ page is displayed (UNCONFIRMED). HANDOVER §4a: DEGRADED is only declared ~14 s after the cable is pulled — RAISE at 1 dB/1.5 s adds ~9 dB in that window. GIG_CHECKLIST puts the tablet on Wi-Fi.

**On a real desk:** A Wi-Fi stall / lost renew / busy console during RAISE: the detector receives nothing, so no detection can ever pause the loop, and the server walks the wedge master up to the target (default ceiling 0 dB) through the onset of a howl that nobody is measuring. Repro: with a frame source that delivers zero frames, ring_out(1, target −14) raised −20 → −14 dB and reported 'target reached' with frames=0.

**Offline test:** Committed (fails today): tests/integration/test_assumptions_meters_rta.py::test_ring_out_does_not_raise_blind in worktree wt/assumptions-meters-rta — CfsManager(frames=FixtureSource([])) then ring_out; assert max_master_db stays at start when frames==0. Better: give FakeDesk a `stall_meters(seconds)` fault and assert RAISE pauses (and ABORTs with 'no RTA frames for N s') whenever last frame age > ~3×period; use a monotonic clock for LiveMeters ts.

> **Verifier 1: CONFIRMED (high)** — Both citations hold and the defect reproduces. (1) Code: src/x32mcp/cfs.py `_run_ringout` (lines ~1145-1198 at HEAD a408a2a) pops pending detections, checks target/budget, writes `min(master+step, target)`, then `_dwell(dwell_ms)`; the only loop exits are a detection outcome, target reached, budget spent, a write/policy error, or abort_reason. Nothing reads `ses.frames`, `ses.last_ts`, `ses.frame_event` or `LiveMeters.last_rx_age_s` (meters.py:419 defines it; grep shows no consumer anywhere in src/ outside meters.py/connection.py). `_consume` (cfs.py:1017-1034) additionally drops frames whose length != 100 (one warning, then silent) and frames with `ts <= last_ts`; LiveMeters stamps with `time.time` by default (meters.py:392) and CfsManager builds it with that default (cfs.py:508), so a backward wall-clock step deafens the detector while RAISE continues. The only frame-presence check in the module is `_calibrate_floor` (cfs.py:850-868), which on no frames just returns the configured gate and proceeds. The report carries `frames` as a bare number with no warning and the run finishes DONE 'target reached'. (2) Fake/fixtures: fakedesk.py:913-921 `_meter_stream` sends one datagram every `interval_s` until lease expiry, never late or lost; SyntheticRta stamps `t0 + frame_index*period` (meters.py:723-725) and its `_run` paces perfectly (753-760); the cited test_cfs.py lines 262/333/409/541 all inject rings into a streaming RTA, and no test anywhere starves the frame source during RAISE. (3) Research: meters.md §1.2 line 73 quotes the DOC 'may be variable according to console's ability to fulfill requests. Timeout is 10 seconds'; §1.3 lines 104-105 give the 10 s lease / resend-every-5 s practice ('tolerates one lost datagram' — i.e. two lost renewals is a multi-second outage); §6.6/§6.7 lines 472-473 'Frame rate is nominal … Don't derive timing from packet arrival'. HANDOVER.md line 118 confirms DEGRADED only after 14 s. (4) Repro: the claimant's committed test wt/assumptions-meters-rta tests/integration/test_assumptions_meters_rta.py::test_ring_out_does_not_raise_blind fails today exactly as described: `AssertionError: raised to -14.0 dB with no RTA frames at all (None)` — bus 1 master driven −20 → −14 dB with frames==0, abort_reason None, i.e. DONE 'target reached'. One overstatement noted but not disqualifying: for a total link loss (cable pull) the blind window is shorter than the claimed ~9 dB/14 s, because each raise step first re-reads the fader section from the desk (desk.py:991 `_leaf`, cache invalidated by the previous write at desk.py:883) and a read TIMEOUT (~500 ms per HANDOVER) routes to `_lose_connection` (cfs.py:1180-1181). That mitigation does not cover the finding's actual class — a meter-only stall with a healthy control path (lost renew datagrams/lease lapse, console shedding meter frames under load, /meters/15 blob of unexpected length, backward clock step) — where RAISE walks the live bus to the target (default ceiling 0 dB) with a deaf detector and then reports a clean ring-out. That is CFS acting on no data with real fader writes on a live wedge: high per the rubric.

> **Verifier 2: PARTIAL (medium)** — The encoded assumption is real and the repro is genuine: `_run_ringout` (src/x32mcp/cfs.py:1153-1198) raises on `_write_master` + `_dwell` alone; nothing on the RAISE path consults `ses.frames`, `ses.last_ts` age or `LiveMeters.last_rx_age_s`, and ARM→RAISE does not even wait for a first frame. I ran the committed test (wt/assumptions-meters-rta, tests/integration/test_assumptions_meters_rta.py::test_ring_out_does_not_raise_blind) against HEAD: with `FixtureSource([])` ring_out(1, target −14) went −20 → −14 dB, final_stage DONE, abort_reason None, frames=0, summary '… no feedback detected; DONE'. The FakeDesk stream (fakedesk.py:913-925) is perfectly periodic and has no meters-only fault (only `silent` both ways, `drop_next` on replies, latency), and SyntheticRta ticks a virtual clock, so no test ever runs RAISE without frames. So a sensor-liveness interlock is missing from the one automated gain-raising loop, and the report certifies headroom ('no feedback detected') that was never measured.

But the claimed real-desk consequence is overstated, so I downgrade from high:
1. Any condition that blocks ALL inbound datagrams (cable pull, PSU cut, Wi-Fi power-save/roam stall on the host, inbound firewall) does NOT produce a blind climb to the ceiling. Every raise step is `Desk.set_level` → `_leaf(address)` (desk.py:988) and the previous write invalidated that cache entry (desk.py:883/275), so each step begins with a wire `/node` read of the fader; when nothing comes back `_unreachable` raises TIMEOUT/NOT_CONNECTED (desk.py:355-360) in ~0.5 s and `_run_ringout` routes that to `_lose_connection` (cfs.py:1181-1182) → ABORT + restore of the start level. This is exactly what tests/integration/test_cfs.py:370-401 (silent mid-RAISE) exercises and what HANDOVER §4a measured ('reads timed out in ~500 ms'). The finding's '14 s to DEGRADED → +9 dB' arithmetic is therefore wrong for ring-out: the loop's own read fails one step in, long before the watchdog. And with the link down the raise writes never reach the desk anyway, so nobody hears anything.
2. What survives is a meters-ONLY gap while /node round-trips still work. Realistic triggers: one lost UDP `/meters` request datagram (the initial one at ARM → up to 5 s with zero frames; or two consecutive lost 5-s renewals → ≤5 s gap, meters.md §1.3/§6.6), or the console thinning frames under load (§1.2/§6.7 — a rate drop, not a blackout). On the documented topology (PC and desk on one LAN; the Wi-Fi tablet is only the HTTP dashboard client, GIG_CHECKLIST pre-show) UDP loss is ~0; on a Wi-Fi-hosted laptop it is plausible but bounded by the 5 s renew cadence: ≤3-4 dB unobserved at the defaults (1 dB / 1500 ms), after which frames resume and the detector (with the M7 prominence override) catches any ring that bloomed in the gap and HOLD pauses the raise. Context is soundcheck with the engineer's hand on the fader (checklist golden rule). Unpleasant, not a walk to 0 dB.
3. The NTP clause (LiveMeters stamps time.time(), meters.py:392; cfs.py:1028 drops ts <= last_ts) is correct code-reading but theoretical for a ~1-minute procedure; a backwards step deafens only for the step size.
4. meters.md §5.3 (GEQ/PEQ page changes what /meters/15 carries) yields garbage frames, not missing ones — a different finding.

Net: CONFIRMED as a missing interlock + misleading DONE report (the tool can say 'no feedback detected' for a window in which it was deaf, and never refuses to raise before its first frame), REFUTED as 'server walks the wedge to the ceiling through a howl' on any realistic real-desk fault, because the per-step fader read already acts as an inbound-liveness gate. Medium: spurious/misleading result and a few dB of unmeasured raise at a gig under packet loss; cheap fix (gate RAISE on last-frame age ≤ ~3×period, abort 'no RTA frames for N s', monotonic clock for ts, flag frames/elapsed in the report) and cheap offline test (add an inbound-request drop / meters-only stall fault to FakeDesk).

**On a real desk:** (a) Peak-hold left on by the engineer: a notched band's bar never falls, every VERIFY fails, every ring is driven to −9 dB and ring_out ABORTs with a 6 dB back-off — three writes and an abort for a ring the first −3 dB cut killed (exactly the path tests/integration/test_cfs.py:403-430 exercises as 'untamable'). Decay at 8–16: same, intermittently. (b) Manual gain differs per desk by up to 60 dB, so the fitted −45 dB gate means 'room noise qualifies' on one desk and 'a −50 dB onset is ignored until it is a howl' on another; the M7 numbers (−51.7 floor, −25 howl) embed Jim's gain setting.

**Offline test:** Committed (fails today): test_set_rta_source_pins_display_processing — asserts set_rta_source writes gain/decay/peakhold to known values. ## E35. [medium] (meters-rta, confirmed) A GEQ inserted POST is visible to the RTA's post-EQ tap, and an already-inserted GEQ can be reused for ring-out whatever its insert position — the M7 fix (PRE) only applies to inserts provisioning creates.

**Encoded at:** src/x32mcp/fakedesk.py:1103-1135 (_refresh_cuts applies the GEQ to the SyntheticRta whenever insert/on and sel point at a GEQ — insert/pos and /-prefs/rta/pos are never consulted); tests/integration/test_fakedesk.py:409-437 (test_geq_notch_kills_ring_closed_loop provisions `insert ON POST FX5L` and asserts the RTA sees −6/−9 dB); FakeDesk default insert/pos is POST (fakedesk.py:129).

**Reality:** HANDOVER §4b #4 (real X32, M7): a −15 dB cut through a POST insert moved the RTA by −0.2/+0.4/+1.2 dB; the same cut PRE read −5.9/−6.0/−3.9 dB. HANDOVER §4a: Jim's desk already holds GEQ2 in FX5 inserted on Main LR ('CFS² provisioning should reuse it') — the reuse path.

CONFIRMED parts:

Running the finder's committed repro in worktree assumptions-meters-rta: test_fakedesk_post_insert_is_invisible_to_the_rta FAILS with "fake RTA shows 15.0 dB of a POST-insert cut" — i.e. the emulator reports a -15 dB POST cut as -15 dB at the RTA where the real desk (HANDOVER §4b #4) read -0.2/+0.4/+1.2 dB. That is exactly the class of assumption the brief asks for, and it means a regression of _RINGOUT_INSERT_POS back to POST would pass the whole suite.
(2) The reuse path ignores pos. provision.py:458-463: when the bus already inserts a GEQ/TEQ slot, plan_setup records InsertInfo with the existing pos and only queues {"on": True} if bypassed — never a pos write. validate_ringout_eqs (provision.py:384-421) has no pos check; the module doc (provision.py:29-31) even says "An insert at PRE is accepted", i.e. POST is the assumed norm. The finder's test_reused_post_insert_is_flagged FAILS today (plan.inserts empty, reasons empty). HANDOVER §4a documents that Jim's desk already holds GEQ2 in FX5 inserted on Main LR and §4b #4 says that insert was POST, so setup_ringout_eqs('main') on the tested desk takes precisely this path and leaves it POST while reporting ok.

REFUTED/overstated part (why not high):
The failure narrative "ring_out cannot measure any of its cuts ... otherwise every ring escalates to -9 dB and aborts" repeats the provision.py:292-297 comment, which the project itself walked back. HANDOVER §4b #4 and the ddcfeb1 commit message: "Narrower than first claimed: when a notch breaks the loop the ring stops acoustically and the RTA sees it wherever it taps, which is why cuts audibly worked ... What POST costs is the ability to measure a cut directly, so decay verification is inferring from the loop rather than observing the filter." cfs VERIFY (cfs.py:1221-1253, detector.py:115-117) requires the notched RTA band to drop >= 6 dB below the ring's level-at-notch within 1.5 s on 2 consecutive frames. A -3 dB first GEQ step cannot produce a 6 dB direct reading even PRE (M7 measured only ~6 dB of a -15 dB PRE cut), so in both positions VERIFY effectively passes only when the ring collapses acoustically — which it does at any tap when the notch breaks the loop, and when it does not break the loop, deepening is the correct response either way. The RTA data with a POST insert is true acoustic data, not garbage; no wrong write, no level goes up, no safety path is affected. Real residual cost of POST reuse: marginal/plateaued rings or misdetected non-loop tones deepen to -9 dB and ABORT where PRE might have passed on the direct reading (spurious soundcheck failure / over-notching), ringout_status/preflight say OK on a configuration the project has declared wrong, and the emulator cannot police the M7 fix. That is "tool reports wrong state or fails spuriously at a gig" = medium.

Note on the proposed offline fix: making _refresh_cuts skip attenuate() unless insert/pos==PRE would also remove the ring's loop-gain decay in SyntheticRta (meters.py:714-718 ties both effects to the same _cuts dict), which is physically wrong — a POST GEQ is still in the acoustic loop. A faithful fake needs two paths: "visible at the tap" (PRE insert with rta/pos POST only; base spectrum/notes and direct dip) versus "reduces loop gain" (PRE or POST; ring decay).

## E36. ## E37. [medium] (meters-rta, confirmed) Feedback grows linearly at 6–20 dB/s from a quiet start (fakedesk `/-fake/ring` default 15 dB/s), so a slope above growth_max_db_per_s = 60 dB/s is 'a note onset, not a ring'.

**Encoded at:** src/x32mcp/fakedesk.py:1285 and :1356 (default growth 15 dB/s), src/x32mcp/meters.py:633 (inject_ring: constant dB/s ramp independent of the bus master or loop delay); all test rings 6–20 dB/s (test_meters.py:394,416; test_cfs.py:262,409; test_server_tools.py:617).

**Code depends on it at:** src/x32mcp/detector.py:103 (growth_max_db_per_s 60: faster growth restarts the growth window → growth_score 0) with w_growth 0.5 — leaving only the 25 dB/6-frame override; cfs RAISE step 1 dB / dwell 1.5 s (device.yaml ringout).

**Reality:** Physics: regenerative growth rate ≈ excess loop gain (dB) per loop transit. A vocal mic 1–2 m from a wedge has a 3–6 ms acoustic path (+~1 ms console), so +1 dB over unity after a RAISE step grows at ~150–300 dB/s; only reverberant/room-mode loops (effective τ ≈ RT60/13.8 ≈ 50–100 ms) give the 10–20 dB/s the fixtures model. Script: a 100 dB/s synthetic ring is emitted only via the override at frame 6 (confidence exactly 0.70), by which time it has risen 30 dB to the cap.

**On a real desk:** The primary use case (SM58 into wedges) produces rings the growth term classifies as onsets; detection waits for the override (300 ms) while the ring climbs to clip — the room hears a full howl before every cut, and REVIEW_BRIEF §1's 'detect within ~300 ms' is met only at full scale. (Overlaps the §1 discriminator work, but the fixture default is what hid it.)

**Offline test:** Model the ring in SyntheticRta/FakeDesk as loop physics: level += (master_db + geq_at_ring − unity_db) × period/loop_delay with loop_delay 5 ms and 80 ms variants, coupled to the FakeDesk bus fader; run ring_out and assert detect→cut happens before the band exceeds, say, −20 dBFS for the 5 ms loop (fails today).

> **Verifier 1: CONFIRMED (medium)** — All citations check out and the code has no fallback the claimant missed other than the one they already named (the 25 dB / 6-frame override).

Encoded assumption (verified): src/x32mcp/fakedesk.py:1285 `on, growth, start = True, 15.0, -45.0` and :1356 `--ring-growth default=15.0`; src/x32mcp/meters.py:633 `inject_ring(freq_hz, growth_db_per_s, start_db=-45, cap_db=-3)` with meters.py:717 `r.level += r.growth*period_s - cut*period_s/loop_period_s` — a constant dB/s ramp with no coupling to the bus master (FakeDesk._refresh_cuts at fakedesk.py:1103-1134 couples only GEQ gains into the RTA, never the fader). Every ring in the suite is 6–20 dB/s: tests/test_meters.py:394,416,438,457,468 (15/6/15/15/15), tests/integration/test_cfs.py:262,333 (20), :409,:541 (15), tests/integration/test_server_tools.py:617 (20), tests/integration/test_fakedesk.py:413 (15), tests/test_webui.py:223 (15); tests/test_detector.py's own generator defaults `rate_db_s=15.0` (line 81) and its ring tests use 10–15 dB/s (lines 231, 258-259, 291). DESIGN.md:541 canonises the '+15 dB/s from −40 dB' ring.

Code dependence (verified): src/x32mcp/detector.py:103 `growth_max_db_per_s: float = 60.0  # faster than this is an onset, not a ring`, applied at detector.py:335-339 (slope > 60 → window trimmed to last sample, slope forced 0 → growth 0); w_growth 0.5 (detector.py:107, device.yaml:805) so without growth confidence caps at 0.5 < 0.7 and only the override (detector.py:361-367; device.yaml:812-813, 25 dB / 6 frames) can emit. The module docstring states the belief outright (detector.py:45-48: 'nothing regenerative rises this fast … Regenerative feedback in a ring-out grows at a few to ~30 dB/s'). growth_max is a code 'extension' absent from DESIGN §12 and device.yaml, i.e. an unreviewed prior. Ring-out step/dwell: device.yaml:826-827 step_db 1.0, dwell_ms 1500. There is no RTA-level clip guard in the RAISE/HOLD/NOTCH loop (cfs.py:1160-1198, 1200-1219): on detection the master is merely held, not backed off, until VERIFY fails.

Reality: neither docs/research nor HANDOVER records a measured growth rate, so this rests on loop physics, which is standard: growth rate ≈ excess loop gain (dB) / loop transit time. A close vocal-mic→wedge loop is ~4-6 ms (1.5 m + ~1 ms console), so after a 1 dB RAISE step the excess is in (0,1] dB → 0–200 dB/s, i.e. most crossings exceed 60 dB/s; even the M7 rig (SM58 → Alto tops on Main LR, ~3-5 m, 10-15 ms) gives ~65-100 dB/s per dB of excess. The RTA is forced to PEAK det (HANDOVER §4b defect 1) and cfs feeds raw frames unsmoothed (cfs.py:1034), so a fast rise is seen as fast. HANDOVER §4b corroborates indirectly: the only successful real catch came via the override ('This is what made the successful catch possible'), never via the growth path.

Reproduced offline with the shipped DetectorConfig (device.yaml) against meters.SyntheticRta: 15/40/59 dB/s rings are emitted by the growth path 100–350 ms after crossing at ≈−28 dBFS; 80/100/300 dB/s rings are emitted only by the override at confidence exactly 0.70, 250 ms after crossing, at −9/−5/−3 dBFS (the cap); 200 dB/s is emitted at the cap via an artefactual 20 dB/s slope from the trimmed window. So for the primary use case the detector waits ~300 ms while the ring runs to full scale, and BRIEF.md:75's '<100 ms detect→cut' / REVIEW_BRIEF §1's '~300 ms' are met only at clip. The existing integration tests would still pass with a 200 dB/s ring (override fires within their 1 s budget), which is exactly how the fixture hid it. Side note supporting the proposed offline test: the synthetic cut model (meters.py:717) makes a −3 dB notch unable to stop any ring growing faster than 60 dB/s (growth×period > cut), which is also non-physical — a loop 1 dB over unity is killed by any cut > 1 dB regardless of how fast it was howling — so modelling the ring as (master + geq − unity)/loop_delay is the right fix for the fixture.

Severity medium as claimed: no wrong write results (the eventual −3 dB cut is correct and sufficient), but during server-driven ring_out and during feedback_watch the room hears a full-scale howl for ≥300 ms + write + verify before every cut, and the growth term — half the confidence weight — is structurally blind to the common case. Physics estimate carries some uncertainty (a minority of crossings land <0.3 dB over unity and do grow <60 dB/s), which keeps it below high.

> **Verifier 2: CONFIRMED (medium)** — The assumption is real, encoded exactly where cited, physically wrong for the stated primary use case, exercised by no fixture, and only accidentally mitigated.

1. Encoded: every ring the suite or emulator can produce is a constant 6–20 dB/s ramp from a quiet start (fakedesk.py:1285 `/-fake/ring` default 15 dB/s; :1356 `--ring-growth` default 15; meters.py:633 inject_ring = linear dB/s independent of any fader/loop; tests use 15/6/20/15 dB/s at test_meters.py:394,416, test_cfs.py:262,333,409,541, test_server_tools.py:617; test_detector.py's local SyntheticRta defaults rate_db_s=15 and never exceeds 20). No test injects a ring faster than 60 dB/s. The detector hard-codes the belief: detector.py:103 `growth_max_db_per_s = 60.0  # faster than this is an onset, not a ring`, detector.py:336 'Onset guard: nothing regenerative rises this fast', and the module docstring (detector.py:45-49) asserts 'Regenerative feedback in a ring-out grows at a few to ~30 dB/s' with no research citation. device.yaml does not override it, so 60 dB/s ships. The same worldview is baked into the fake's cut model: SyntheticRta.loop_period_s defaults to the 50 ms frame period (an implied 17 m loop path; fakedesk.py:301/1333, webui.py:571 and all integration tests use the default), and its docstring states 'one −3 dB GEQ step kills any ring slower than 60 dB/s'.

2. Reality: nothing in docs/research or HANDOVER measures growth rate, so this rests on loop physics, which is unambiguous: above threshold a linear loop grows at excess-gain/loop-delay dB/s. Vocal mic 1–1.5 m from a wedge + ~1 ms console = τ≈4–7 ms; ring_out's own +1 dB step (device.yaml:826) leaves excess e∈(0,1] dB, so growth is 0–250 dB/s and P(growth>60 dB/s)=1−60τ ≈ 60–75 % for wedges (≈4–40 % for FOH tops at 3–5 m). The finding's '150–300 dB/s' assumes the full 1 dB excess (typical is about half that) but the conclusion — most near-field ring-out howls exceed the guard — stands. Circumstantial real-desk support: at M7 the growth term never caught the real SM58→Alto ring; HANDOVER §4b says the prominence override 'is what made the successful catch possible'. The X32 RTA in PEAK mode has no attack smoothing that would hide a fast rise (meters.md §5.1: decay/peakhold are fall-side only).

3. Verified numerically against the shipped detector + device.yaml (min_level −45): rings of 15/30/50/59 dB/s are emitted by the growth path 2–4 frames (100–200 ms) after first qualifying, at ≈−25 dBFS; rings of 70/100/150/300 dB/s get growth_score 0 every frame (window truncated each time 3 samples accumulate) and are emitted only by the 25 dB/6-frame override, 5 frames (250 ms) after qualifying, at −13.5 dBFS (70) and at the −3 dB cap for ≥100 dB/s, confidence exactly 0.70, override=True. (200 dB/s fires at frame 6 via a fluke 20 dB/s slope across the truncation+cap, also at the cap.) And the fake cannot host the realistic case: a 150 dB/s synthetic ring is NOT tamed by a −3 dB GEQ cut with the default loop_period_s (stays at −3.0), but collapses to −128 within 10 frames with loop_period_s=0.005 — i.e. a realistic fast-ring fixture added today would make ring_out deepen to −9 and abort 'not tamed', the opposite of what a real 0.5 dB-excess loop does.

4. Consequence at a gig: in ring_out the server itself raises the master into feedback and then HOLDs it there while it notches (cfs.py:1153-1197 — no back-off on detection). For the wedge case the ring is discarded as a 'note onset', climbs 25–45 dB to amp limiting/0 dBFS, and is cut ~250–300 ms after qualifying plus write latency: a full-scale howl through the wedge at the musician before every notch, versus ≈−15 to −25 dBFS if the growth path (w=0.5, the intended primary discriminator) were allowed to see it at frame 3. feedback_watch has the same blind spot and additionally needs 25 dB prominence over programme. Before the M7 override existed this guard made fast rings completely undetectable while the master kept stepping up every 1.5 s; today the override bounds it, which is why this is not high.

5. Skeptic's discount: no wrong write, no garbage acted on, detection does occur and the real cut works; the guard-attributable delta is ~3 frames/≈150 ms and 15–30 dB of howl, and REVIEW_BRIEF §1 already flags growth as a weak feature (though neither the brief nor HANDOVER identifies that the onset guard rejects real rings — that is new). Medium is the right level: the tool behaves worse than designed in its primary use case in the mode where the server drives gain, every fixture hid it, and the emulator's cut model would actively mislead anyone who tried to test it. Offline test as proposed (loop-physics ring coupled to the bus fader with 5 ms and 80 ms τ; assert detect→cut before −20 dBFS for τ=5 ms) fails today and is the right regression.
