- src/x32mcp/fakedesk.py:129 `_DEFAULTS`: every strip starts `insert/on False, insert/pos POST, insert/sel OFF`; every provisioning test in tests/integration/test_cfs.py:124-170 starts from that virgin state, and the only pre-existing inserts ever exercised are GEQs the code itself wrote. So the suite encodes "the buses you ring out carry no insert you didn't put there".
- src/x32mcp/provision.py:453-465: a target whose insert resolves to no FX slot (desk.py:190-194 `_insert_side` maps AUX1..6 -> (None,None)) or to a non-GEQ/TEQ type falls through to `need.append(t)`; :494-506 then emits `{"sel": "FX5L", "on": True, "pos": "PRE"}` for it; SetupPlan.to_dict (provision.py ~line 200) and plan.blockers carry no record of the current sel/type; apply_setup :508-529 writes it and the per-insert `writes` entry has no `was` (contrast type_loads, which DO carry `current_type`/`was` — the code already knows the pattern and omits it for the riskier resource).
- server.py:1564-1575 `_plan_summary` -> Tier-2 action_summary. Probe output with bus1=FX7L(LIM) ON, bus2=AUX1 ON: blockers=[], reuse={}, summary "load GEQ2 into FX slot 5 (currently DES2); insert FX5L on bus.1 PRE; insert FX5R on bus.2 PRE"; after apply bus1 sel=FX5L, bus2 sel=FX5R, result ok=True. Same for Main LR with LIM in FX8 inserted: "insert FX5L on main.st PRE", limiter unpatched. The finder's committed test (worktree assumptions-routing-fx-provision, test_plan_does_not_silently_evict_an_existing_non_geq_insert) fails today exactly as claimed.
- Research agrees a strip has exactly one insert point (fx_routing_scenes.md §3.1/§3.4) and that AUXn is a physical outboard loop (§3.2); the project's own real scene file shows inserts in use on a real desk (`/ch/01/insert ON PRE FX4L`, `/main/st/insert ON PRE FX8L` — note: that line is in scales_params.md:446, not transport.md §6.3 as cited; transport.md:457 only has the ch01 line). No policy/descriptor rule protects a non-OFF insert (policy.py has no insert logic; device.yaml only marks /*/insert/* Tier 2). Worse, the "step zero" tool actively funnels into the eviction: validate_ringout_eqs on an AUX-inserted bus says "no FX insert on Bus 2 (insert/sel is 'AUX1'); run setup_ringout_eqs" (provision.py:396).

WHY NOT REFUTED: the FakeDesk does match the real desk here (last write to insert/sel wins) — this is not an emulator lie. But REVIEW_BRIEF §2's class explicitly includes "a fixture, fake, DEFAULT or assertion that encodes something about … the operator", and the all-OFF default plus virgin-desk fixtures are exactly that; the code's non-destructiveness depends on it, and DESIGN §14's careful "a slot is free iff no strip inserts it" shows the intent was never to displace existing processing — the bus's own insert point simply wasn't considered.

WHY MEDIUM, NOT HIGH:
1. The write is Tier-2 gated and the summary is accurate, just incomplete ("insert FX5L on bus.1") — an engineer who knows their desk can catch it; it is not a wrong value to a wrong address.
2. Fully recoverable from the automatic pre-write snapshot (restore_snapshot) once noticed; validate_ringout_eqs/get_bus before setup do show the existing sel/type.
3. Precondition frequency on ring-out targets is modest: by far the most common pre-existing insert on a wedge bus or Main LR of an X32 is a GEQ/TEQ, which the reuse path handles. Outboard AUX loops on an X32 are rare; the headline IEM-limiter case requires someone to request a ring-out GEQ on an IEM bus (no acoustic loop — an odd request, though an LLM told "set up all monitor buses" could make it). The most credible mainline hit is a LIM/CMB on the Main LR insert as PA protection being swapped out before ring_out_system raises the mains — real, safety-adjacent, but many rigs limit downstream (speaker DSP) and ring_out clamps the master via master_ceiling_db.
4. HANDOVER §4b's real rig (GEQ2 in FX5 on Main LR) would not have hit it.
So: a genuine silent-destructive-write defect with a safety tail, cheap to fix (carry `replaces: {sel, fx_type, on}` into plan.inserts/summary/writes, or block when current sel != OFF and not a GEQ), but at a typical gig it is gated, visible to a careful operator, and recoverable — medium.

## E39. [medium] (routing-fx-provision, confirmed) With firmware-4.x user routing, channel source InNN is patched by /config/userrout/in/NN — i.e. routing block k always selects user-in block k — and the (UNCONFIRMED) hand-computed head-amp algorithm is as good as asking the desk.

**Encoded at:** tests/integration/test_desk.py:725-740 (only the aligned case IN/1-8 = UIN1-8 is exercised; M5 desk was aligned too, HANDOVER §4a); src/x32mcp/fakedesk.py:136-139 (routing defaults) and the fake has no /-ha/NN/index, so nothing can contradict the algorithm.

**Code depends on it at:** src/x32mcp/desk.py:764-768 (`patch = await self._leaf(f"/config/userrout/in/{src:02d}")` — indexed by the channel's In number, ignoring WHICH UIN block the routing block selected), :776-779 (aux branch drops UIN1-2/4/6 entirely), :722-780 as a whole reimplements the mapping; consumers: desk.py:1362-1369 set_phantom(target) writes /headamp/NNN/phantom at the computed index; provision.py:582 physical_input.

**Reality:** scales_params.md §12.4 (explicitly 'inferred, not stated in the PDF — mark UNCONFIRMED and validate against /-ha/NN/index'): for a UIN block r on channel block b the user input is `(r-20)*8 + off + 1`, so /config/routing/IN/9-16 = UIN1-8 feeds ch 9 from userrout/in/01, not /09 (fx_routing_scenes.md §4.10 says the same). §12.3: the console provides `/-ha/[00..39]/index` read-only, 'returns the actual headamp used as source … -1 when internal (card)' — 'Prefer querying /-ha/NN/index over computing'. The code depends on the UNCONFIRMED algorithm with no /-ha fallback or cross-check.

**On a real desk:** On any desk whose Routing>Inputs page maps e.g. 'Inputs 9-16 <- User In 1-8' (a legal, one-encoder setting), set_phantom('ch.9') switches 48 V on the wrong XLR/stage-box socket (whatever userrout/in/09 names) — a ribbon mic or unbalanced source can be on it, and the intended condenser stays dead; discover_mics/physical_input and every 'head amp behind this channel' report are equally wrong. Same for aux-ins patched through UIN1-2/4/6 (always 'no preamp').

**Offline test:** Make FakeDesk serve /-ha/NN/index computed from its own routing/userrout state (it is the authority), then assert Desk.headamp_index_for == fakedesk /-ha for randomised routings; minimal repro committed as test_headamp_user_routing_block_not_aligned_with_channel_block (IN/9-16=UIN1-8, userrout/in/01=33, /09=9 -> expects 32, code returns 8).

> **Verifier 1: CONFIRMED (high)** — Every citation checks out and the repro fails today.

Code (HEAD a408a2a): src/x32mcp/desk.py:722-780 `headamp_index_for` reimplements the channel->head-amp mapping. In the UIN branch (desk.py:764-768) it reads `/config/userrout/in/{src:02d}` where `src` is the channel's In number (b*8+off+1) and never looks at WHICH UIN block token (`UIN1-8` vs `UIN9-16` …) the routing block selected — `tok.upper().startswith("UIN")` is the only use of the token. The aux branch (desk.py:776-779) iterates only r in 1..9 (AN/A/B) and returns None for r=13..15 (UIN1-2/1-4/1-6). No `/-ha/NN/index` exists anywhere in src/ or device.yaml (grep: zero hits), so there is no cross-check or fallback; the docstring itself says '§12.4 (UNCONFIRMED …)'.

Research: scales_params.md §12.4 (lines 785-838) — explicitly 'inferred, not stated in the PDF — mark UNCONFIRMED and validate against /-ha/NN/index' — gives `userin_to_ha(userrout_in[(r - 20) * 8 + off])` for a UIN block and `userrout_in[a]` for UIN1-2/4/6 aux; fx_routing_scenes.md §4.10 (line 450) independently says `User In 8*(v-20)+o+1 -> then /config/userrout/in/<that>`. §12.3 (lines 773-783): `/-ha/[00..39]/index` read-only 'returns the actual headamp used as source', 'Prefer querying /-ha/NN/index over computing'. The code both depends on the UNCONFIRMED algorithm and deviates from it (indexes by channel In number instead of by selected UIN block), and is only equivalent when block k selects UIN block k. The code's reading is also physically incoherent: if block 9-16 always followed userrout/in/09..16, the four distinct UIN options per block would be meaningless; every other option (e.g. A1-8 on Inputs 9-16 -> ch9 <- AES50-A 1) is block-relative.

Tests/fake: tests/integration/test_desk.py:725-740 only exercises IN/1-8 = UIN1-8 (the aligned case, matching the M5 desk per HANDOVER §4a lines 139-141, whose evidence is ch1-4 on block 1-8 only); fakedesk.py:136-139 defaults all blocks to AN*, and the fake serves no /-ha, so nothing can contradict the algorithm.

Consumers verified: desk.py:1352-1369 `set_phantom(target)` resolves via `headamp_index_for` and writes `/headamp/NNN/phantom` at the computed index (guarded write, but the confirmation summary would show the wrong index with nothing for the operator to check it against); provision.py:582 `physical = (await desk.headamp_index_for(c)) is not None` drives discover_mics inclusion/notes (MCP tool `discover_mics`, server.py:1618) — a real AES50 mic behind a non-aligned UIN block whose same-numbered userrout slot says card/USB is dropped as 'not a physical input', or a card feed is treated as a mic, so CFS acts on a wrong mic set.

Repro: claimant's worktree assumptions-routing-fx-provision, tests/integration/test_assumptions_routing_fx.py:50-61 (IN/9-16=UIN1-8, userrout/in/01=33, /09=9) — ran it: `assert 8 == 32` FAILED, exactly as claimed.

Nuances (do not change the verdict): set_phantom is a Desk-layer API per DESIGN §13 (docs/DESIGN.md:579) and is not currently registered as an MCP tool in server.py, so the 48 V-on-wrong-socket path is via the Python API/scripts rather than the LLM surface; phantom is Tier-2 (device.yaml guarded '/headamp/*/phantom') so a confirmation step exists but cannot catch a wrong index; the hazard needs a non-aligned UIN selection, which is legal and one encoder click away but less common than aligned. Severity kept high: wrong guarded write in the product's Desk contract plus CFS mic discovery acting on a wrong classification, with dependence on an UNCONFIRMED algorithm and no /-ha fallback.

> **Verifier 2: CONFIRMED (medium)** — The defect is real and reproduces exactly as stated; I downgrade severity from high to medium on reachability grounds.

1. The code deviates from BOTH research docs, not just from an UNCONFIRMED guess. scales_params.md §12.4 (`userrout_in[(r - 20) * 8 + off]`) and fx_routing_scenes.md §4.10 (`elif 20<=v<=23: User In 8*(v-20)+o+1 -> then /config/userrout/in/<that>`) both say the UIN *block enum* picks which 8 user-in slots feed the channel block. desk.py:764-768 instead indexes `/config/userrout/in/{src:02d}` by the channel's In number, which is only right when routing block k selects UIN block k. The routing enum (fx_routing_scenes §4.3, VERIFIED from DOC p.21 + X32CfgMain.h) offers all four UIN blocks (20..23) on every IN/PLAY position, so 'Inputs 9-16 <- User In 1-8' is a legal one-encoder setting; this is the same positional semantics every other block source (AN/A/B/CARD) has, so the research reading is not in serious doubt even though §12.4 as a whole is tagged UNCONFIRMED. The aux branch (desk.py:776-779) also silently drops UIN1-2/1-4/1-6 (aux enum 13..15), which §12.4 resolves via userrout_in[a].
2. Nothing offline can contradict it: fakedesk.py:135-139 defaults every block to aligned AN*, the fake serves no `/-ha/NN/index` (grep: no `-ha` anywhere in src/ or device.yaml), and tests/integration/test_desk.py:725-740 only exercises IN/1-8=UIN1-8 (aligned, as Jim's M5 desk happened to be). §12.3 explicitly says 'Prefer querying /-ha/NN/index over computing'; the code has no /-ha read or cross-check, so it depends on an UNCONFIRMED algorithm (and mis-implements it) with no fallback — squarely the class the brief asks for.
3. Reproduced: the slice's committed test (worktree assumptions-routing-fx-provision, tests/integration/test_assumptions_routing_fx.py:50-61: IN/9-16=UIN1-8, userrout/in/01=33, /09=9) fails today with `assert 8 == 32`.

Why medium, not high: the physically dangerous consequence (48 V on the wrong XLR) requires Desk.set_phantom(<target>) (desk.py:1352-1370), which is a public, DESIGN §13-listed, guarded library method that HANDOVER §4a says was exercised at M5 — but it is NOT exposed as an MCP tool (server.py has no phantom/headamp tool; webui.py, cfs.py, patches.py never call it). So at a gig, through the product's LLM/dashboard surface, nobody can trigger the wrong phantom write. The gig-time consumer is provision.py:582 (`physical = headamp_index_for(c) is not None`) feeding discover_mics/preflight/ring_out inclusion: that boolean is wrong only when the decoy userrout slot differs in kind from the real one (e.g. Inputs 25-32 <- User In 1-8 patched to Card 1-8 for a DJ/USB feed while userrout/in/25-32 still hold their default Local 25-32 -> the card feed is classed as a live mic and rung out against; or the reverse -> a real mic excluded / spurious 'no candidate mics' PREFLIGHT_FAILED). That is 'tool reports wrong state / CFS includes or excludes the wrong channel' on a minority (non-aligned UIN or aux-via-UIN) configuration — medium. It would become high the moment set_phantom(target) or a 'which preamp/socket is this channel' report is surfaced as a tool.

Fix/test direction is as the finding says: index userrout by `(uin_block-20)*8+off+1` (and `a+1` for aux UIN1-2/4/6), and better, read `/-ha/{ch-1:02d}/index` on a real desk and fall back to the algorithm only when it is absent; make FakeDesk compute and serve /-ha from its own routing/userrout state so randomised-routing property tests can pin Desk.headamp_index_for to it.

## E40. [medium] (routing-fx-provision, confirmed) The bus (or Main) master fader and mute control what the wedge/PA hears: raising /bus/NN/mix/fader provokes feedback, backing it off or restoring it removes it, muting silences it — so preflight only needs to check 'muted' and 'master at -oo', and BACKOFF/ABORT-restore/panic are effective safety actions.

**Encoded at:** src/x32mcp/fakedesk.py: no /outputs/* model at all (state built from device.yaml, which declares no /outputs, /config/routing/OUT is a bare enum with defaults :145) and module doc :44 'The bus fader/mute is deliberately not coupled to ring growth' — tests inject rings on a timer keyed to the RAISE stage (tests/integration/test_cfs.py:328-334, 380-386), so fader->SPL causality is never exercised; test_desk.py:360-371 counts 24 mix/on writes as 'panic mutes 24 outputs'.

**Code depends on it at:** src/x32mcp/provision.py:646-649 (preflight blockers: bus muted, master -inf — meaningful only if the output follows fader/mute); src/x32mcp/cfs.py:1119-1125 (_set_master drives RAISE/BACKOFF and the abort restore), :1254 ff (_finalize_levels backoff = the 'untamable ring' safety action); src/x32mcp/desk.py:1184-1220 panic (docstring concedes 'POST-tapped' only).

**Reality:** fx_routing_scenes.md §4.7: each physical/AES50/P16 output taps its source at pos {IN/LC, IN/LC+M, <-EQ, <-EQ+M, EQ->, EQ->+M, PRE, PRE+M, POST}; 'taps without +M are not affected by the strip's mute'; IN/LC…PRE are pre-fader. §11: muting masters 'does not silence outputs whose pos is IN/LC, <-EQ, EQ-> or PRE'. §13 item 13: factory default pos 'assumed POST' is UNCONFIRMED. A real console scene (transport.md §6.3, Saddleback X32) reads `/outputs/main/01 4 PRE OFF` — output 1 = MixBus 1 tapped PRE-fader, no +M. The descriptor does not even declare /outputs/*/src|pos, so the code cannot look. Also common: PA driven from matrices or M/C with Main->Mtx sends tapped pre-EQ/IN/LC (UNCONFIRMED where the PRE insert sits relative to those taps).

**On a real desk:** On a wedge output tapped PRE/EQ->: ring_out raises the master 1 dB at a time to the ceiling with zero acoustic effect, finds no feedback and reports 'target reached, no rings' — a certified-safe monitor that was never tested; if a ring does start (talker at the mic), BACKOFF and the connection-loss restore do nothing while the report says the master was backed off 6 dB, and panic()'s bus mute leaves that wedge screaming. Preflight's 'bus muted'/'-oo' blockers are likewise about a control that is not in the path.

**Offline test:** Declare /outputs/{main,aux,p16}/NN/{src,pos} in device.yaml, give FakeDesk per-output taps and couple SyntheticRta ring growth to the tapped level (POST: follows fader+mute; PRE: ignores both); add preflight blocker tests: bus 1 on /outputs/main/01 src=4 pos=PRE -> preflight must refuse ('Bus 1 feeds XLR 1 pre-fader: the master cannot ring it out') and panic must report outputs it cannot silence. Fails today (no such read exists).

> **Verifier 1: CONFIRMED (high)** — Both halves of the claim check out. (1) Research: fx_routing_scenes.md §4.7 (lines 405-408) states verbatim that /outputs/<group>/NN/pos is a 0..8 enum {IN/LC, IN/LC+M, <-EQ, <-EQ+M, EQ->, EQ->+M, PRE, PRE+M, POST} and 'Taps without +M are not affected by the strip's mute; +M variants and POST are muted with the strip' (VERIFIED); §11 option 1 (lines 706-708) says muting main/bus/mtx masters 'does not silence outputs whose /outputs/*/NN/pos is IN/LC, <-EQ, EQ-> or PRE (no +M), nor DirectOut taps', and option 3 says killing PRE/DirectOut taps needs the input-channel mutes the code deliberately omits (HANDOVER:114-115 'Input channels are deliberately untouched'); §11 line 714 and §13 item 13 (line 758) flag the factory-default POST tap as UNCONFIRMED; transport.md §6.3 line 457 lists the real-desk (FW 2.x Saddleback scene / Maillot SetSceneParse.c excerpt) line `/outputs/main/01 4 PRE OFF` = XLR tap 1 carries MixBus 1 pre-fader, no +M — so the assumption is violated in the wild. (2) Code: device.yaml declares no /outputs family at all (only /config/routing/OUT block enums at :437-440), src/ has zero references to '/outputs' apart from the panic docstring, and fakedesk.py has no output-tap model (defaults at :145 are just the routing/OUT block enums; module doc :44 'The bus fader/mute is deliberately not coupled to ring growth'). provision.preflight (provision.py:646-649) blocks only on 'bus muted' and 'master is -oo'; cfs._run_ringout (cfs.py:1147-1197) raises the master step by step and, absent detections, ends with reason 'target reached' -> _finalize_levels (cfs.py:1254-1293) BACKOFF/DONE, with no check that the master is in the acoustic path; _write_master (cfs.py:1115-1124, the claimant's '_set_master 1119-1125') is the only lever for RAISE/BACKOFF/abort-restore; desk.panic (desk.py:1184-1221) sends 24 mix/on 0 and the server reports 'PANIC: 24 outputs muted' (server.py:1064-1073) — the docstring concedes 'Silences every POST-tapped output (§11 option 1)' but nothing user-facing (README:204, :621, tool description) carries the caveat and nothing reads the taps. Tests: tests/integration/test_cfs.py:328-333 and :380-385 inject the ring / cut the PSU from an on_stage callback keyed to stage=='RAISE' and master_db thresholds, i.e. fader->SPL causality is scripted, never modelled; tests/integration/test_desk.py:360-371 (claimant wrote tests/test_desk.py) equates 24 mix/on==0 with 'panic mutes 24 outputs'. No fallback exists anywhere (no /outputs read is even possible through the descriptor; GIG_CHECKLIST has no 'verify output taps are POST' step). Real-desk M7 test (HANDOVER §4b) ran on Main LR into tops, presumably factory POST taps, so it never exercised this. Consequence on a PRE/EQ->/<-EQ/IN/LC-tapped wedge: ring_out moves a fader outside the loop, reports 'master A -> B dB, 0 notches, no feedback detected; DONE' (cfs.py:1373-1376) for a monitor whose gain-before-feedback was never probed; if a ring is running, ABORT back-off and the connection-loss restore are inert while reported as done; panic() leaves that output (and any DirectOut-fed output) live while reporting success. Nuance for severity: in the PRE case the tool's own writes are acoustically inert rather than harmful, and panic's POST-only scope is acknowledged in a docstring — but the safety action silently failing while reporting '24 outputs muted', plus CFS driving and reporting on a control that is not in the loop, with the relevant default explicitly UNCONFIRMED and a real scene showing PRE, meets the brief's 'safety / CFS acts on garbage' bar. Minor citation slips (function name/lines in cfs.py, test file path) do not change the substance.

> **Verifier 2: CONFIRMED (medium)** — Facts check out. (1) Nothing in the product can see an output tap: `grep outputs src/x32mcp/*.py` is empty; device.yaml declares /config/routing/OUT blocks (:437-440) but no /outputs/{main,aux,p16}/NN/{src,pos}; fakedesk.py:44 states 'The bus fader/mute is deliberately not coupled to ring growth', and the ring-out integration tests inject the ring from a stage callback keyed on master_db (tests/integration/test_cfs.py:328-333, 380-385), so fader->room causality is never modelled or exercised. (2) The code depends on it: provision.py preflight blockers 'bus is muted' / 'master is -oo' (:640-643), cfs.py _write_master (:1115-1124) drives RAISE and the BACKOFF/ABORT back-off in _finalize_levels (:1254-1290), desk.py panic (:1184-1220) mutes masters only. (3) Research contradicts the implicit POST assumption: fx_routing_scenes.md §4.7 (VERIFIED) 'Taps without +M are not affected by the strip's mute', IN/LC..PRE are pre-fader; §4.10 gives the exact bus->output recipe including 'If /outputs/main/11/pos is 6 (PRE) the feed ignores the bus mute'; §11 says master mutes do not silence IN/LC/<-EQ/EQ->/PRE or DirectOut taps; §13 item 13 factory POST is UNCONFIRMED; and transport.md §6.3 quotes a real console scene `/outputs/main/01 4 PRE OFF` alongside `/bus/01/mix OFF 0.0` — a real church desk running MixBus 1 to XLR 1 pre-fader with the bus master muted, i.e. exactly the configuration where preflight would wrongly block on 'muted', and after unmuting ring_out would raise the master to target with zero acoustic effect and report DONE/no rings. REVIEW_REPORT.md:144-148 also concedes the bus RTA tap is upstream of the fader, so the tool has no way to observe that its raise reached the room except by feedback onset — the certification is unfalsifiable on a PRE tap. Skeptical downgrade from high to medium: (a) the one real-desk CFS² run (HANDOVER §4b, Main LR into Alto tops) showed master->PA causality holds on Jim's desk, and factory/common practice for bus->XLR wedges is post-fader, so this bites on house desks/recalled scenes/P16 feeds rather than the default case; (b) the dominant consequence is a silently meaningless ring_out report and a mis-stated back-off (tool reports wrong state), not a harmful write — the actual safety action (GEQ notch inserted PRE on the bus) stays in-path for PRE and POST taps and feedback_watch still works; (c) panic's POST-only reach is already conceded in its docstring and in research §11, and the desk's own bus-mute button has the same limitation (though GIG_CHECKLIST.md:10,79 overclaims 'mutes all outputs' and panic returns muted:[24] regardless). Not low: no operator-level mitigation exists (the gig checklist never mentions output taps), the research hands over the exact read the code omitted, the same blind spot means ring_out cannot even tell whether the bus feeds any physical output at all, and a bus that feeds a PRE wedge plus a POST/+M secondary destination would get that secondary blasted by the raise. Offline test as proposed is sound: declare /outputs/*/NN/{src,pos} in device.yaml, give FakeDesk per-output taps, couple SyntheticRta loop gain to the tapped level, and assert preflight refuses/warns when the target bus reaches outputs only via non-POST/non-+M taps (or none) and panic reports outputs it cannot silence — fails today. Minor citation nits: the panic test is tests/integration/test_desk.py:360-380 (not tests/test_desk.py) and the cfs helper is _write_master, not _set_master.

## E41. [medium] (routing-fx-provision, confirmed) A GEQ found in FX slots 1-4 and selected as a strip's insert is in that strip's signal path; /fx/N/source/l|r is irrelevant to validation.

**Encoded at:** src/x32mcp/fakedesk.py:534-535 (slots 1-4 default source MIX13..MIX16, i.e. send-fed) combined with :1117-1123 (_refresh_cuts treats ANY GEQ-typed slot named by insert/sel as in-circuit, never looks at /fx/N/source); tests/integration/test_desk.py:626-630 loads GEQ2 into FX1 and asserts source stays {'l':'MIX13','r':'MIX13'} without consequence.

**Code depends on it at:** src/x32mcp/provision.py:398-417 (validate_ringout_eqs: type check, on check, sharing check — no `fx['source']` check although desk.get_fx returns it, desk.py:695-698), :453-464 (plan_setup reuses such an insert as-is), :466-479 (partial reuse can hand FX1R..FX4R of such a slot to a second bus); module doc :17-18 admits 'FX 1-4 would also need /fx/N/source/l|r = INS (§3.4), which is not modelled' but only for allocation, not validation.

**Reality:** fx_routing_scenes.md §3.4: 'FX 1-4 used as inserts must also have /fx/N/source/l|r = 0 (INS)'; §1.1/§1.4: with source = MIXn the slot input is the bus-n send (send effect), the strip's insert send goes nowhere and the insert return injects the effect output of bus n. Real desks do use FX1-4 as inserts (transport.md §6.3 scene: `/ch/01/insert ON PRE FX4L`).

**On a real desk:** An engineer's GEQ2 in FX3 inserted on the wedge bus but with source/l still MIX13 validates ok; CFS² arms, notches par 1-31 of an EQ that is processing bus 13's send, VERIFY never sees decay, drives three bands to -9 dB on the wrong signal and aborts — while the wedge (now fed FX3's output of bus 13, or nothing) sounds wrong from the moment the insert was reused/switched on.

**Offline test:** FakeDesk: make _refresh_cuts (and audio) honour /fx/1-4/source (only INS puts the GEQ in the insert path); test committed as test_fx14_geq_insert_with_send_source_is_not_valid (GEQ2 in FX1, bus 1 sel FX1L ON, source MIX13 -> validate must return not ok with a 'source/INS' reason; today ok=True).

> **Verifier 1: CONFIRMED (medium)** — Both citations hold. Research: docs/research/fx_routing_scenes.md §3.4 line 305 states verbatim "FX 1-4 used as inserts must also have `/fx/N/source/l|r = 0 (INS)`; FX 5-8 are always inserts" (not marked UNCONFIRMED), and §1.1 line 65 says a slot 1-4 effect is send-based when source = MIXn and "is an insert when `source/l|r = INS (0)` and some strip's `insert/sel` points at FXnL/FXnR". transport.md §6.3 line 457 quotes a real-desk scene line `/ch/01/insert ON PRE FX4L`, so FX1-4 inserts occur in the field. Severity medium is appropriate: validate/preflight report a misrouted GEQ as ok and CFS would notch an EQ that is not in the bus's insert path (fresh allocation avoids slots 1-4, which keeps it from being the default path).

## E42. [medium] (routing-fx-provision, confirmed) A free GEQ2/TEQ2 slot is flat and can be inserted on a live bus as-is; loading a type is the only thing that changes a slot's curve, and the fake's 'all 64 pars default to raw 0.5' is what an idle slot looks like.

**Encoded at:** src/x32mcp/fakedesk.py:536-537 (every /fx/N/par defaults to raw 0.5 = 0.0 dB) and :675-684 (a /fx/N/type write flips the enum and REINTERPRETS the old raw pars — _FX_TYPE_RE at :105 is defined but never used, nothing resets to per-type defaults); tests/integration/test_cfs.py:151-154 asserts status.flat and bands_db == [0.0]*31 straight after setup.

**Code depends on it at:** src/x32mcp/provision.py:486-493 (`load = fx_type not in dual` -> an idle GEQ2/TEQ2 is used with load_type False, no flatten, its bands never enter the plan), :503-529 apply_setup then writes insert sel/on=True; only afterwards preflight (:656-659) downgrades the inherited curve to a *warning*, and cfs.py:886-888 adopts it as `existing` notches to deepen from.

**Reality:** HANDOVER §4a 'FX slot 5 already holds a GEQ2 (CFS² provisioning should reuse it)' — a real idle GEQ carries whatever the last show left (Jim's now carries M7's -9 dB notches). fx_routing_scenes.md §2.2: the desk's per-type defaults are X32CopyFX.c FXdef 'real default values' (GEQ2 = all 0.0), applied when a type is (re)loaded — so on the desk a type load IS a reset and 'reuse as-is' is NOT; the fake models the opposite (load preserves, idle is flat).

**On a real desk:** setup_ringout_eqs([3]) on a desk whose free slot 6 holds last week's GEQ2 inserts it on the wedge and switches it on: the wedge instantly acquires someone else's -12 dB holes (or +6 dB boosts -> instant feedback risk) with a Tier-2 prompt that only said 'insert FX6L on bus.3 PRE'; ring_out then treats those cuts as pre-existing notches, may refuse to notch a boosted band (BOOST_FORBIDDEN from policy.validate_notch via detector.py:568-570) and reports matched/‘already carries cuts’ noise. Conversely the fake hides that a GEQ2->GEQ2 'reload to flatten' would wipe the partner bus's side too.

**Offline test:** FakeDesk: reset pars to per-type defaults on /fx/N/type writes and seed idle GEQ slots with a non-flat curve in a fixture; test committed as test_free_geq_slot_with_old_cuts_is_not_inserted_live_as_is (slot 6 GEQ2 with par/08=/40=-12 dB, slot 5 busy -> plan must flatten or surface bands; today type_loads==[] and the plan is silent).

> **Verifier 1: CONFIRMED (medium)** — Core claim verified in code and reproduced. provision.py:486-493: for a free preferred slot `load = fx_type not in dual`, so an idle GEQ2/TEQ2 slot gets SlotAllocation(load_type=False), no type_loads entry, and nothing reads or plans its 64 pars; the module doc (provision.py:19-21) states this deliberately ('a free slot whose type is in geq.fx_types_dual is used as is'). apply_setup (:503-529) then writes insert sel/on=True/pos=PRE; validate_ringout_eqs runs only afterwards and `ok = not reasons` ignores non-flat bands, so the server (server.py:1592-1613) confirms with a Tier-2 summary built by _plan_summary (:1564-1575) that mentions only 'insert FX6L on bus.N PRE' and reports 'all validate'. The only handling of the inherited curve is downstream: preflight (:656-659) emits a warning and cfs._open_session (cfs.py:886-888) seeds NotchController/_DeskGeqWriter with the bands as `existing`; a boosted band then makes _apply (detector.py:568-570) compute current+step > 0 and policy.validate_notch (policy.py:410-416) raise BOOST_FORBIDDEN, which cfs._notch (cfs.py:1073-1076) logs and swallows -> no cut on that band. No flatten path exists anywhere (desk.set_fx_type only drops the par cache, desk.py:1400; no par writes in provision). The fake encodes the blind spot: fakedesk.py:536-537 defaults every /fx/N/par to raw 0.5 (0 dB), _store (:675-684) keeps old raw pars across a /fx/N/type write, _FX_TYPE_RE (:105) is defined and never referenced, and no fixture seeds a non-flat idle GEQ; test_cfs.py:151-154 asserts flat/[0.0]*31 right after setup. The claimant's committed test (worktree assumptions-routing-fx-provision, tests/integration/test_assumptions_routing_fx.py:136-151) fails against HEAD exactly as described (type_loads==[], plan dict carries no band info). Reality citations: HANDOVER §4a line 137-138 verbatim 'FX slot 5 already holds a GEQ2 (CFS² provisioning should reuse it)' — correct; after M7 (§4b, budget of 4 notches spent on Main LR via slot 5) that GEQ2 is non-flat, so un-inserting it and later provisioning buses would hit this path. Caveat: fx_routing_scenes.md §2.2 does say X32CopyFX.c FXdef are 'real default values' with GEQ2 = all 0.0, but it does NOT state they are applied on a type (re)load — that is the claimant's inference (plausible engineering common sense, and desk.py:1400 already assumes par semantics change on load), and the 'GEQ2->GEQ2 reload would wipe the partner side' remark is speculative. Neither caveat affects the main finding. Partial mitigations the claimant already acknowledged (post-hoc warning, CFS adopting cuts as existing) do not prevent the live insert of an unknown curve. Severity medium is appropriate: an operator-confirmed but under-described Tier-2 write puts someone else's cuts/boosts on a live wedge/main, and ring_out then reports/acts on inherited notches (refusing boosted bands).

> **Verifier 2: CONFIRMED (medium)** — Core claim reproduces exactly. plan_setup (src/x32mcp/provision.py:480-496) treats a preferred slot whose type is already GEQ2/TEQ2 and that no strip inserts as usable "as is" (load = fx_type not in dual -> False, no type_load, no band read), and the partial-reuse branch (:466-479) hands a requested bus the free side of a dual slot one of our buses already sits on, also as-is. apply_setup (:503-529) then writes insert sel + on=True PRE on the live bus. Nothing in the SetupPlan / Tier-2 payload (server.py _plan_summary 1563-1575: "insert FX6L on bus.1 PRE") mentions the slot's current curve, so the operator confirms a live insert blind. This is a documented design choice (provision.py module doc "Type loads: a free slot whose type is in geq.fx_types_dual is used as is"; DESIGN.md §14), but it rests on the belief that an idle GEQ side is flat, and every fixture honours that belief: FakeDesk defaults every /fx/N/par to raw 0.5 (fakedesk.py:536-537) and no test ever seeds a used slot; tests/integration/test_cfs.py:167-170 even exercises the exact partner-side topology (bus 2 un-inserted, bus 4 takes FX5R with type_loads==[]) with a pristine B side. Reality: HANDOVER §4a/§4b — Jim's own FX5 GEQ2 now carries M7's ring-out notches; any house X32's slots 5-8 carry last show's wedge curves; CFS never removes or flattens its own cuts, so after an operator un-inserts a rung-out bus the side keeps its curve and the next setup_ringout_eqs silently gives it to another wedge.

Verified consequences on the fake (worktree test, both scenarios): plan has type_loads==[] and load_type False; apply returns ok=True with flat:false and the inherited bands in geq.bands_db; validate/preflight report the cuts as a *warning* ("GEQ already carries cuts (100 Hz -12.0 dB)") but never name an inherited boost when any cut exists (provision.py:656-659 only lists notches = negative bands); cfs._open_session (cfs.py:886-888) adopts the curve as `existing`; a ring on an inherited +6 dB band makes NotchController._apply compute +3 dB -> policy.validate_notch raises BOOST_FORBIDDEN (policy.py:410-411) -> cfs._notch returns None (cfs.py:1073-1076) -> _notch_and_verify False -> ring_out aborts with back-off. So: cuts-only inheritance = wedge tone silently wrong + confusing 'already carries cuts' with matched_session None (low-ish); boost inheritance = a boost switched in live on a wedge with open mics (feedback risk at the moment of the confirmed write) and a ring-out that cannot tame the very band most likely to ring (fails spuriously, safe direction). 

Skeptical caveats that keep this at medium, not high: (1) the fake's idle default (0.5 = 0.0 dB) is what fx_routing_scenes.md §2.2 says a factory GEQ2 looks like (FXdef[27] all 0.0), so this is a fixture/coverage gap plus a design decision, not an emulator protocol infidelity — the FakeDesk is already capable of the real behaviour; (2) the state is not hidden: apply_setup's result and validate_ringout_eqs expose bands_db/flat/notches immediately after the write, and preflight warns before any ring-out; (3) the boost case needs someone to have left boosts on an un-inserted or partner GEQ side — plausible (monitor engineers do it) but less common than cuts; (4) the finding's secondary claim that a real type load resets pars to FXdef (and that the fake 'models the opposite' by reinterpreting raw pars, fakedesk.py _store; _FX_TYPE_RE at :105 is indeed unused) is a reasonable inference from X32 behaviour but is NOT stated in docs/research — it does not change the verdict because the code never relies on load-preserves. Net: a real, reproducible under-informed Tier-2 write with a gig-plausible trigger (CFS's own multi-act workflow on one desk), partially mitigated after the fact; medium is right, on its lower edge for the cuts-only case.

## E43. [medium] (routing-fx-provision, confirmed) An existing GEQ insert can be 'reused as-is' regardless of insert/pos; PRE only matters for inserts the code creates itself.

**Encoded at:** src/x32mcp/fakedesk.py:1103-1135 (_refresh_cuts ignores <strip>/insert/pos and /-prefs/rta/pos: a POST insert attenuates the synthetic RTA exactly like a PRE one, so no test can tell them apart); tests/integration/test_cfs.py:205-207 inserts FX5R at POST and the only complaint asserted is stereo sharing; provision.py:25 docstring 'An insert at PRE is accepted' (i.e. POST is the assumed norm).

**Code depends on it at:** src/x32mcp/provision.py:460-464 (reuse path appends at most {'on': True}; never {'pos': 'PRE'}), :398-417 (validate_ringout_eqs has no pos reason) versus its own invariant :292-297 `_RINGOUT_INSERT_POS = 'PRE'` (commit ddcfeb1) which is applied only at :475/:496 for new inserts; cfs.py:911 always selects the post-EQ RTA tap (meters.py:865/889).

**Reality:** HANDOVER §4b defect 4 (measured on the real X32): with the GEQ inserted POST the bus's post-EQ RTA tap is upstream of it — a -15 dB cut moved the RTA -0.2/+0.4/+1.2 dB; PRE showed the cut. Jim's own desk (GEQ2 in FX5 on Main LR) and any engineer's pre-existing wedge GEQ arrive through the reuse path, so the fix never reaches the common case. meters.md §5.3: /-prefs/rta/pos selects pre/post-EQ only; there is no post-insert tap.

**On a real desk:** On every desk where the GEQ was already inserted (the normal case) CFS² runs exactly the M7-defective configuration while setup_ringout_eqs reports 'already set up; all validate': VERIFY cannot see its own cuts, only eventual acoustic decay, so marginal rings get deepened to -6/-9 dB unnecessarily and validate/preflight 'flat'/'notches' claims describe an EQ the analyser never observes.

**Offline test:** FakeDesk: apply GEQ cuts to the SyntheticRta only when insert/pos == PRE (post-EQ RTA tap) — mirror the M7 measurement; test committed as test_reused_geq_insert_is_moved_pre (bus 1 already on FX5L GEQ2 at POST -> plan must emit {'pos':'PRE'} or validate must flag POST; today neither).

## E44. [medium] (routing-fx-provision, confirmed) Writing /fx/N/type takes effect instantly and atomically: the very next datagrams may set insert/sel+on onto that slot and read /fx/N + /fx/N/par back to validate, and the par line read back is already the new effect's.

**Encoded at:** src/x32mcp/fakedesk.py:675-684 + :594-601 (type write is a synchronous dict update; the next /node fx/N/par is rendered from the same raw floats under the new type — no load latency, no pushed par burst, no transitional state); tests/integration/test_cfs.py:141-154 (apply_setup -> res['ok'] True and validate flat in the same breath), test_desk.py:601-605 (set_fx_type then set_geq_band immediately).

**Code depends on it at:** src/x32mcp/provision.py:512-530 (apply_setup: set_fx_type -> get_inserts -> set_insert(on=True) -> validate_ringout_eqs with no settle/poll), src/x32mcp/desk.py:1399-1401 (only drops the par cache), :669-699 get_fx parses whatever par line comes back as GEQ dB; provision.py:336 maps unparseable/None tokens to 0.0 dB ('flat'); server.py:1599-1608 turns a not-ok read-back into GEQ_VALIDATION_FAILED.

**Reality:** HANDOVER §4b: 'setup_ringout_eqs reports a false failure: it validates immediately after writing, before the desk has applied insert/on' — the desk applies writes asynchronously; an FX type change additionally instantiates a DSP module and resets/pushes 64 parameters (fx_routing_scenes.md §2.2 FXdef defaults; §6.4 'load … not necessarily fully completed when the status is returned' for the analogous /load). Load duration over OSC is not documented anywhere in docs/research (UNCONFIRMED) and the code has no fallback (poll until `/fx/N` reads the new token).

**On a real desk:** A correct setup returns GEQ_VALIDATION_FAILED ('FX slot 5 holds DES2, not a GEQ/TEQ' or bands parsed from the old effect's display tokens, e.g. a de-esser threshold read as a +20 dB 'boost'), the operator re-runs it, and the bus insert is switched on while the slot is still (re)loading — an audible dropout/tick in a live wedge or the PA. REVIEW_BRIEF §5 names the class; this is the FX-load-specific instance the fake cannot reproduce.

**Offline test:** Give FakeDesk an `fx_load_ms` (e.g. 300 ms) during which /node fx/N still answers the old type and old par line, then resets pars to the type defaults and pushes them; assert apply_setup polls until `/fx/N` reads the requested token (bounded) and returns ok, and that insert/on is written only after the load. Fails today (ok=False / stale type).

> **Verifier 1: CONFIRMED (medium)** — All cited code and doc locations say what the finding claims, the code has no fallback, and an offline repro fails today exactly as predicted.

Code path verified: provision.apply_setup (src/x32mcp/provision.py:512-530) does set_fx_type -> get_inserts -> set_insert(sel,pos,on) -> validate_ringout_eqs back-to-back with no settle, poll or read-your-writes barrier. Desk.set_fx_type (desk.py:1390-1401) is a fire-and-forget conn.set (connection.py:520-530: 'Fire-and-forget write (no ack exists)') followed only by cache invalidation of /fx/N and _drop('/fx/N/par'); validate then re-reads /fx/N + /fx/N/par fresh (get_fx, desk.py:669-699) and, if the type token is not GEQ/TEQ, emits "FX slot N holds 'X', not a GEQ/TEQ" (provision.py:400-401); server.py:1599-1608 turns ok:false into DeskError GEQ_VALIDATION_FAILED. No retry/settle anywhere in server.py or provision.py (grep: none). Rate limiter is a 50-token bucket (device.yaml:733) so the first burst adds no delay; the type write and the /node fx/N read-back are separated only by a few LAN round trips.

Fake verified: FakeDesk SET handling (fakedesk.py:1038-1045 -> _store 675-684) is a synchronous dict update; _value_from_raw (594-601) renders /fx/N/par under whatever type is stored at that instant, and every FX par defaults to raw 0.5 regardless of effect (fakedesk.py:531-535 '_default_value ... par/ -> 0.5'), so a DES2->GEQ2 switch instantly reads back as a flat GEQ — no load latency, no transitional state, no par reset burst. tests/integration/test_cfs.py:141-146 asserts apply_setup ok True in the same breath; tests/integration/test_desk.py:601-605 (finding wrote 'test_desk.py', the file is under tests/integration/) does set_fx_type then set_geq_band after only a loopback round trip.

Ground truth verified: HANDOVER §4b (docs/HANDOVER.md:181-183) verbatim: 'setup_ringout_eqs reports a false failure: it validates immediately after writing, before the desk has applied insert/on ... Same read-after-write race as elsewhere; needs a settle before the read-back.' REVIEW_BRIEF §5 names the same systemic class. fx_routing_scenes.md §6.4 (line 564) carries the DOC fn.39-41 quote for /load|/save|/copy (claimant correctly labels it analogous, not direct); nothing in docs/research documents /fx/N/type application latency or the par reset on type change (grep confirms) — genuinely UNCONFIRMED, and the code depends on instant application with no fallback. Importantly, HANDOVER §4b records that the M7 live run had 'GEQ2 already in FX slot 5', so the type-load branch of apply_setup has never been exercised on real hardware; the observed live false failure came from insert/on alone, and a short fixed settle tuned for that would not obviously cover a DSP effect load. That makes this a distinct, actionable instance rather than a pure restatement of the known example, though it sits squarely inside the known read-after-write class (calibration list / REVIEW_BRIEF §5) — novelty is moderate.

Repro (worktree $SP/worktrees/verify-fx-type-load-latency, commit 5e676bf, tests/integration/test_cfs.py::test_apply_setup_survives_fx_type_load_latency): deferring the fake's /fx/N/type store by 300 ms makes apply_setup return ok=False with reasons {'1': ["FX slot 5 holds 'DES2', not a GEQ/TEQ"], '2': [same]} and records /bus/01/insert/on and /bus/02/insert/on written while the slot is still 'loading' — both predicted behaviours.

Caveats (do not change the verdict): the 'audible dropout/tick' when an insert is engaged mid-load is physics-plausible but unverified; the 'de-esser threshold read as +20 dB boost' example requires the /fx/N and /fx/N/par reads to straddle the switch (possible since _read_sections issues them concurrently, but an edge case — the GEQ printer itself clamps to +-15); §2.2's FXdef reference establishes GEQ2's default par table, not that a type change applies it. Severity medium is right: a correct Tier-2 setup reports GEQ_VALIDATION_FAILED at a gig (spurious failure / wrong state), no wrong write, re-run is idempotent.

> **Verifier 2: PARTIAL (medium)** — Core claim holds; the embellishments do not, and the core is largely the already-known HANDOVER §4b / REVIEW_BRIEF §5 defect seen through the FX-type-load path.

CONFIRMED parts:
1. apply_setup (src/x32mcp/provision.py:512-531) does set_fx_type -> get_inserts -> set_insert(sel,pos,on) -> validate_ringout_eqs with no settle, ack or poll. Desk._write (desk.py:871-884) is fire-and-forget via X32Connection.set (connection.py:520-530, 'no ack exists'); set_fx_type (desk.py:1389-1401) only invalidates /fx/N and drops /fx/N/par from the cache, so validate's get_fx re-reads /fx/N and /fx/N/par from the desk milliseconds after the type write (writes are back-to-back; policy token bucket does not space them). If /fx/N still answers the old token, validate_ringout_eqs (provision.py:396-401) appends "FX slot 5 holds 'DES2', not a GEQ/TEQ" and server.py:1599-1607 raises GEQ_VALIDATION_FAILED for a setup that actually succeeded. No settle has been added since M7 (git log: nothing after e9b78bb touches provision; grep finds no sleep/settle in provision.py/server.py).
2. Real-desk evidence that immediate read-after-write is stale exists for a plain int leaf (insert/on, HANDOVER §4b: 'validates immediately after writing, before the desk has applied insert/on'). A /fx/N/type write does strictly more work on the desk (parameter block reset to the effect defaults, fx_routing_scenes.md §2.2 verifier note on FXdef 'real default values'; DSP algorithm swap), so it is at least as exposed. The type-load path was never exercised on hardware: Jim's desk already had GEQ2 in slot 5 (HANDOVER §4a 'FX slot 5 already holds a GEQ2'), so M7 only hit the insert/on variant. At a fresh venue the preferred slots 5-8 will typically hold something else, making the type-load variant the common first-run case.
3. The FakeDesk cannot reproduce any of this: _store (fakedesk.py:675-684) applies every write synchronously on datagram receipt and _on_datagram processes in order, so a following /node always sees the write; latency_ms (fakedesk.py:772-779) only delays outbound replies uniformly and preserves ordering. It also does not reset par/01-64 to the new type's defaults on a type change (the old raw floats are simply re-rendered under the new type, fakedesk.py:594-601; test_desk.py:601-613 relies on par/64 staying at the generic 0.5 default) — a genuine divergence from the real desk, though benign for validation (real desk resets a fresh GEQ2 to flat). docs/research is silent on FX-type apply latency (transport.md §5.4/line 696: absolute latency UNCONFIRMED; fx_routing_scenes.md §13 has no item for it), so REFUTE-because-fake-matches-research does not apply.

REFUTED / speculative parts:
- 'operator re-runs it, and the bus insert is switched on while the slot is still (re)loading': wrong. apply_setup is idempotent (provision.py:514-528 skip when current==fx_type / insert fields match); by the time a Tier-2 re-confirmation round trip completes (>2 s cache TTL, desk.py:212) the re-run reads fresh state and writes nothing. insert/on is written once, in the first run, tens of ms after the type write.
- 'audible dropout/tick in a live wedge or the PA': speculative and low-impact. Engaging an insert on a slot that is mid-load is what every engineer does when changing an FX type in X32-Edit with the insert engaged; at worst a momentary gap on that bus during pre-show setup, not during performance. No wrong write, no safety issue, CFS does not act on it.
- 'de-esser threshold read as a +20 dB boost': /fx/N and /fx/N/par are fetched in the same pipelined node_many sweep ~1 ms apart, so a torn head/par read is unlikely; even if it happened it only pollutes flat/notches in the returned status (ok is driven by reasons, provision.py:422), and ring_out re-validates much later against settled state.
- The §6.4 '/load ... not necessarily fully completed' citation is about scene/library loads, an analogy, not evidence about /fx/N/type.

Net: this is the known read-after-write race (listed as a calibration example) with one useful refinement — a fixed settle tuned on insert/on may still be too short for a type load, so the robust barrier is to poll /node fx/N until it reads the requested token (bounded) before writing insert/on and validating — and one useful test-infrastructure point: give FakeDesk a write-apply delay (and par reset to type defaults on /fx/N/type) so both the known insert/on race and this variant fail offline today. Severity stays medium only because the confirmed consequence is an unmitigated spurious GEQ_VALIDATION_FAILED on the first setup at a gig; the distinct FX-load-latency magnitude is unverified and the safety angle does not hold, so it must not be counted as a finding independent of REVIEW_BRIEF §5.

## E45. [medium] (routing-fx-provision, confirmed) 'Can feed back' == 'an X32 or AES50 head amp sits behind the channel source': aux-jack, card and USB sources are never mics, every local/AES50 index is a real connected preamp, and only /ch strips (not /auxin strips) can be stage mics.

**Encoded at:** tests/integration/test_cfs.py:214-215,227,229 (USBL and CARD9-16 asserted not physical -> excluded; nothing tests AUX jacks, auxin strips or an AES50 block with no stage box); src/x32mcp/fakedesk.py:526 (auxin sources default AUX1..6/USB) and no /-stat/aes50/A|B or /-stat/xcardtype content modelled.

**Code depends on it at:** src/x32mcp/provision.py:562 (`channels = d.strip_targets('ch')` — auxin 1-8 strips never scanned), :582 `physical = headamp_index_for(c) is not None`, :591 include requires physical, :596-597 note; src/x32mcp/desk.py:772-779 (source AUX1-6 with routing IN/AUX = 'AUX1-4', the rear TRS jacks, -> None), :746-750 (CARD -> None; A/B blocks -> 32+/80+ unconditionally), :766-767 (userrout 129-166 card/aux-in -> None).

**Reality:** Physics: feedback needs an electro-acoustic loop (mic -> desk -> speaker -> air -> mic); a preamp is irrelevant. A wireless receiver on the X32 Rack's six Aux In TRS jacks (routing IN/AUX token 0 'AUX1-4 (really the 6 local AUX inputs)', fx_routing_scenes.md §4.4) or a Dante/MADI stage rack on the card (/-stat/xcardtype 3 X-DANTE, 7 DN32-DANTE, 5/9 MADI, §7.1) is a live mic; USB/X-Live playback is not. Conversely scales_params.md §12.2: AES50 indices 032-127 are 'AES50 port A/B connected devices' — with no stage box (/-stat/aes50/A|B chain empty, §7.1) there is no preamp there. HANDOVER §4b: discover_mics already 'cannot tell a connected mic from an empty channel' (7 candidates, 1 mic).

**On a real desk:** The roaming handheld radio mic on Aux In 1 — the single most feedback-prone source on a small stage — is excluded ('source AUX1 has no preamp'), so preflight can block with 'no candidate mics' on a bus that is one fader push from howling, or ring_out proceeds believing only the wired mics matter; a Dante stage box install gets 'no candidate mics' on every bus; an unpopulated AES50 block yields 8 phantom 'physical' candidates and set_phantom happily writes /headamp/032..079 into the void.

**Offline test:** Committed as test_radio_mic_on_an_aux_jack_is_a_feedback_source (ch 7 source AUX1, send -10 dB to bus 1 -> must be included; today include=False). Extend FakeDesk with /-stat/aes50/A|B and /-stat/xcardtype so 'physical' can mean 'a transducer can be connected here', scan auxin strips, and add the meter-activity cross-check HANDOVER §4b asks for (needs the fake's channel meters to read floor for unplugged inputs instead of following the fader).

> **Verifier 1: CONFIRMED (medium)** — Every citation checks out and the code has no fallback. provision.py:562 scans only d.strip_targets("ch") (auxin strips never considered); :582 `physical = (await desk.headamp_index_for(c)) is not None`; :591 `include = (not muted) and sending and physical`; :596-597 emits the note "source X has no preamp (not a physical input)". The module doc (provision.py:28-30) states the belief verbatim: "a physical preamp behind the channel source (headamp_index_for is not None: local XLR or AES50; USB/card/FX/bus sources are not mics)". desk.py:743-750 block_base returns None for CARD blocks and 32+/80+ for A/B blocks unconditionally; :764-768 userrout values >128 (129-160 Card In, 161-166 Aux In per fx_routing_scenes.md §4.8) -> None; :772-779 handles routing IN/AUX tokens only for r in 1..9, so token 0 "AUX1-4" (the six local Aux In jacks, §4.4 verified incl. DOC fn.15) -> None. The research the code follows (scales_params.md §12.4, itself UNCONFIRMED) is correct that aux jacks/card have no *head amp* ("0 = rear-panel AUX line inputs (no head amp)", "-1 ... card"), but nothing in research says such sources cannot be microphones; the leap from "no headamp" to "not a mic / cannot feed back" is purely the code's. Tests encode it: test_cfs.py:214-215 set ch4=USBL and IN/9-16=CARD9-16, :227/:229 assert both `not physical_input` and excluded; no test covers an AUX-sourced channel, an auxin strip, or xcardtype. FakeDesk models neither /-stat/aes50/A|B nor /-stat/xcardtype (grep: only /-stat/rtasource and selidx), so 'physical' can never mean 'a transducer can be here'. §7.1 confirms xcardtype 3 X-DANTE / 7 DN32-DANTE / 5,9 MADI and aes50/A|B chain strings exist on the real desk. HANDOVER §4b quote ("cannot tell a connected mic from an empty channel", 7 candidates, 1 mic) is accurate. No mitigation: a patch row with mic=True or ring_out's expected_mics only add notes/warnings (provision.py:593-611, cfs.py:688-692), never flip include; preflight (provision.py:643-645) hard-blocks with "no candidate mics" when nothing is included, and feedback_watch/ring_out (cfs.py:574-576, 669-673; server.py:1754-1756) raise PREFLIGHT_FAILED with no force/skip option; device.yaml mics: has only send_floor_db and mute_group_convention. I ran the claimant's committed test (worktree assumptions-routing-fx-provision, commit 25babfb, test_assumptions_routing_fx.py:157-168): it fails today exactly as described — ch 7 source AUX1, send -10 dB to bus 1 -> include=False, notes=['source AUX1 has no preamp (not a physical input)']. Concrete gig failures are real: a bus whose only open mic is a radio receiver on an Aux In jack, or any Dante/MADI-card stage-box install (all channels via CARD blocks), gets PREFLIGHT_FAILED 'no candidate mics' on every arm attempt, and discover_mics tells the operator the loudest mic in the wedge is 'not a physical input'. Caveats that do not change the verdict: the 'unpopulated AES50 block -> phantom physical candidates' sub-claim is a restatement of the already-known HANDOVER §4b lead and set_phantom writing /headamp/032+ with no stage box is harmless; and when other wired mics are included, ring_out/watch still catch a ring from the excluded source because the RTA taps the bus, not the mics — so the damage is spurious blocking/misreporting (medium), not a wrong write (high). Severity medium as claimed.

> **Verifier 2: CONFIRMED (medium)** — The core claim holds and is not mitigated. provision.py:562 scans only d.strip_targets("ch") (the eight /auxin strips, which carry the Aux In TRS jacks by default and have 16 bus sends per device.yaml:151, are never examined), and provision.py:582/591 sets include = unmuted AND sending AND (headamp_index_for is not None). desk.py:772-779 correctly (per scales_params.md §12.4: 'r=0 AUX1-4 = rear-panel AUX line inputs (no head amp)' and PDF /-ha = -1 for card) returns None for a channel sourced from AUX1-6 under the default IN/AUX=AUX1-4 routing and for CARD blocks — so the head-amp resolver matches the research; the defect is provision.py's design equation 'no head amp => not a mic', stated in the module doc (provision.py:37-40) which lists USB/card/FX/bus but never considers the aux jacks. Physics: feedback needs a transducer->bus->speaker->air loop; a preamp is irrelevant. A wireless receiver's line output on an X32 Rack Aux In (the exact desk in HANDOVER §4a, 16 local pres + 6 aux TRS — parking radio receivers on aux ins to save XLR channels is standard practice) or a Dante/MADI stage box on the card (fx_routing_scenes §7.1 xcardtype 3/5/7/9) is a live mic and is hard-excluded. Crucially there is no escape hatch: patch_mic=True from the operator's patch file only adds a note (provision.py:593-599), never flips include; preflight (provision.py:641-643) turns zero included mics into a blocker; cfs.feedback_watch/ring_out raise PREFLIGHT_FAILED with no force/skip parameter (cfs.py:670-673, grep shows no override). So a speech PA with two radio mics on Aux In 1-2, or any Dante-sourced install, cannot be rung out at all without physically re-patching — 'fails spuriously at a gig' = medium per the rubric. I ran the slice's committed test (worktree assumptions-routing-fx-provision, tests/integration/test_assumptions_routing_fx.py:157) and it fails today exactly as described: ch 7 source AUX1, send -10 dB to bus 1 -> include=False, note 'source AUX1 has no preamp (not a physical input)'. Parts I discount: (a) 'ring_out proceeds believing only the wired mics matter' has no algorithmic consequence — the detector works on the bus RTA, the mic list is informational (server.py:1642 summary, cfs.py:690 expected_mics warning), so a radio mic ringing alongside wired mics is still caught; (b) the 'unpopulated AES50 block yields phantom physical candidates' sub-claim is the already-documented HANDOVER §4b limitation (open socket vs connected mic), not new; (c) the set_phantom-into-the-void aside is an operator-requested write, out of scope for discover_mics. Not high: no wrong write, no safety exposure — it errs toward refusing. Not low: the refusal is un-overridable in software and the auxin strips are entirely invisible to the tool, on the product's own reference hardware.

## E46. [medium] (routing-fx-provision, partial) A channel contributes to the bus/PA iff its own mix/on is on and its send (or fader+LR assign) is above the floor; DCA state, send tap type and subgroup paths do not exist.

**Encoded at:** src/x32mcp/fakedesk.py:45-51/‘meters follow each strip's fader and mute’ and no DCA->member, send-tap or bus->main audio model; tests/integration/test_cfs.py:210-234 build candidates purely from mix/NN/level, mix/on, source and grp/mute.

**Code depends on it at:** src/x32mcp/provision.py:569-591 (muted = strip mix/on; send_db/send_on from get_sends level/on; main: fader_db + lr_assigned; include = not muted and sending and physical) — `s['type']` (desk.py:502) is read by get_sends but ignored here; grp/dca, /dca/N/on|fader, /config/mute and bus->LR (subgroup) assignments never consulted; preflight :643-645 turns the result into the 'no candidate mics' blocker and the mics list CFS² reports.

**Reality:** scales_params.md §11.2 send types {IN/LC, <-EQ, EQ->, PRE, POST, GRP}: a POST/GRP send is scaled by the channel fader (fader -oo => silent at any send level); fx_routing_scenes.md §5.2/§5.1: a DCA at -oo or /dca/N/on 0 silences its members' main (and, with /-prefs/dcamute, bus) contribution without touching /ch/NN/mix/on; vocal mics commonly reach Main LR through a subgroup bus (ch mix/st OFF, bus N -> LR), fx_routing_scenes.md §4.7 src 4-19. Real scene (transport.md §6.3): `/bus/01/mix/01 ON -oo +0 POST`, `/dca/1 OFF -8.3` — DCAs muted and POST taps in ordinary use.

**On a real desk:** ring_out(bus) runs 'with 4 mics' whose vocal DCA is down/muted for the changeover: the master goes to the ceiling, nothing rings, report says N dB of headroom — then the DCA comes up at showtime and the wedge howls at a level CFS² certified. ring_out('main') on a desk mixing vocals through a group bus blocks with 'no candidate mics' although every mic reaches the PA. POST-tapped sends with faders down produce the same false all-clear.

**Offline test:** Model DCA membership/mute, send tap and ch->bus->LR in FakeDesk's level engine and couple SyntheticRta ring growth to 'some included mic is actually audible'; tests: (a) ch 1 sends -20 dB to bus 1 but grp/dca bit 0 set and /dca/1/on 0 -> discover_mics must not include it (or must note 'DCA 1 muted'); (b) ch 5 mix/st OFF, mix/09 GRP, bus 9 -> LR on -> discover_mics('main') must include it. Both fail today.

> **Verifier 1: PARTIAL (medium)** — Core claim verified: discover_mics (src/x32mcp/provision.py:562-591) computes `include = (not muted) and sending and physical` from /ch/NN/mix/on, the send's level/on (or fader_db + lr_assigned for main) and headamp_index_for; it never reads mix/NN/type (get_sends returns it at desk.py:502 but provision ignores it), the channel fader for POST/GRP-tapped sends, grp/dca or /dca/N/on|fader, or /bus/NN/mix/st (subgroup-to-LR). preflight (provision.py:643-645) turns 'no included mic' into a hard blocker and otherwise passes the list to ring_out, whose Tier-2 confirmation text (server.py:1765-1769) presents them as 'open mics' and whose DONE path leaves the master at highest-reached − safety_margin with 'no feedback detected' (cfs.py:1373-1376). The FakeDesk has no audio model that could contradict this (fakedesk.py:50-51 doc, _strip_level :930-941 uses only mix/on+mix/fader; default send type is POST at :120; SyntheticRta ring growth is not coupled to any mic), and test_discover_mics (tests/integration/test_cfs.py:210-234) builds candidates only from mix/NN/level, mix/on, config/source, routing and grp/mute. Research supports the physics: scales_params.md §4.9 (l.497-498) 'type … 4 post-fader, 5 subgroup (level follows fader, send level fixed at 0 dB)' (enum also listed §11.2 l.698); fx_routing_scenes.md §5.1 (l.482) DCA-mute semantics (main-mix only by default, everywhere with /-prefs/dcamute — UNCONFIRMED beyond three corroborating secondary sources); transport.md §6.3 (l.457) real scene has `/dca/1 OFF -8.3` and POST-typed sends, and scales_params §4.9 quotes a real `/ch/01/mix/09 ON +0.5 +0 POST`. I reproduced offline in worktree wt/verify-assume-mics-audibility-repro (commit 1b8f44d, tests appended to tests/integration/test_cfs.py): (1) ch1 send −20 dB POST to bus 1 with fader −∞ → include=True; (2) ch1 LR on, fader 0, grp/dca=1, /dca/1/on 0 → discover_mics('main') include=True with no note; (3) all ch mix/st OFF, ch5 mix/09 GRP 0 dB, bus 9 mix/st ON → discover_mics('main') returns [] (preflight would block 'no candidate mics'). All three fail today; existing test_discover_mics still passes.

Why PARTIAL not CONFIRMED: (a) the headline bus scenario is overstated — with the default /-prefs/dcamute=0 a DCA mute does not touch bus sends at all (§5.1), and a DCA fader never affects PRE-tapped sends (the normal monitor tap), so 'vocal DCA down for the changeover → wedge certified then howls' only holds for POST/GRP-tapped sends via the DCA fader, or with dcamute=1; the claimant's proposed offline test (a) (bus send + /dca/1/on 0 ⇒ must not include) itself encodes a wrong belief at default prefs — the correct DCA repro is on Main LR (or with dcamute=1). (b) The 'fx_routing_scenes.md §4.7 src 4-19' citation is mis-aimed (that enum is physical-output sources, not bus→Main LR; the subgroup path is /bus/NN/mix/st, scales_params bus table) though the subgroup fact itself is established by §4.9. (c) Partial mitigations exist that the finding does not mention: DESIGN.md §14 states '`include` is a suggestion the model must confirm with the user', the ring_out confirmation summary shows the mic list to the operator, and HANDOVER §4b already records that discover_mics cannot establish audibility (unplugged-mic case) and proposes a meter cross-check — but none of these is a code fallback: preflight still auto-blocks the subgroup case and auto-passes the POST-fader-down / DCA-on-main cases, and ring_out then raises the master to ceiling−margin on a path with no live mic. Severity medium as claimed: tool reports wrong state (false 'open mics', false 'no candidate mics' blocker at a gig); the leave-master-hot-after-empty-ring-out consequence borders on high but requires the operator to confirm a visibly wrong mic list first.

> **Verifier 2: PARTIAL (medium)** — Code facts verified: provision.discover_mics (src/x32mcp/provision.py:569-591) decides `include` purely from strip mix/on, the bus send's level/on (or fader_db + mix/st for Main LR) and headamp presence; it never reads /ch/NN/grp/dca, /dca/N/on|fader, /-prefs/dcamute, the send tap `type` (which desk.get_sends already returns, desk.py:502, and which FakeDesk defaults to "POST" for every send, fakedesk.py:120), nor any ch->bus->LR subgroup path. preflight (:643-645) turns an empty include-set into a hard, non-overridable PREFLIGHT_FAILED (cfs.py:669-673; `_expected_mics` only adds a warning at :688-692). FakeDesk has no audio-path model at all ("bus fader/mute deliberately not coupled to ring growth", fakedesk.py:45-51) and tests/integration/test_cfs.py:210-234 exercise only mix/on, level, source and grp/mute, so nothing offline can contradict the heuristic.

Research supports the unmodelled paths: scales_params.md §4.9/§11.2 (VERIFIED) — send type 4 POST is post-fader, 5 GRP 'level follows fader, send level fixed at 0 dB' (so the stored mix/NN/level the code reads is not the effective send for GRP, and a POST/GRP send is silent with the fader at -oo); fx_routing_scenes.md §5.1/§5.2/§11 item 5 — /dca/N/on 0 or DCA fader down silences members' MAIN contribution (bus sends too only with /-prefs/dcamute=1); §4.7 src 4..19 bus->output. The captured real scene in transport.md §6.3 literally contains the Main-LR failure state: `/ch/01/mix ON +2.1 ON ...` (unmuted, fader up, LR on), `/ch/01/grp %00000001` (member of DCA 1), `/dca/1 OFF -8.3` (DCA 1 muted) — discover_mics('main') would report ch 1 include=True while it is silent in the PA. It also shows a real POST ch->bus send (`/ch/01/mix/09 ON +0.5 +0 POST`, scales_params §4.9).

Where the finding overreaches: its headline wedge scenario ('vocal DCA down for the changeover ... the wedge howls') is contradicted by the same research — with the default /-prefs/dcamute=0 and PRE-tapped monitor sends (the norm for wedges, and what the real scene shows for mix/01: `PRE`), DCA mute/fader does NOT remove a mic from a monitor bus, so ring_out(bus) on wedges is unaffected by DCA state. The `/bus/01/mix/01 ... POST` line it cites is a bus->matrix send, not evidence about ch->bus taps. So the real bite is narrower: (a) ring_out('main')/ring_out_system's final Main LR stage with DCA-muted or DCA-down vocal channels -> false include, ring-out climbs to ceiling against silence, reports 'no feedback detected' and leaves Main at ceiling-3 dB, untested with live mics; (b) POST/GRP-tapped bus sends with channel fader (or DCA, if dcamute=1) down -> same false all-clear on that bus (IEM/FX/subgroup buses rather than wedges); (c) vocals routed to LR via a subgroup bus (ch mix/st OFF) -> spurious hard 'no candidate mics' blocker on Main, not overridable; (d) GRP-type sends judged by a stored level the desk ignores.

Mitigation status: DESIGN §14/BRIEF §5 already frame discover_mics as an open-loop heuristic whose `include` the operator must confirm, and HANDOVER §4b flags the sibling 'unplugged mic' blindness — but the fix proposed there (cross-check input meter activity) would NOT catch these cases, because channel input meters are pre-fader/pre-DCA: a DCA-muted or fader-down POST mic still shows activity. So this is a distinct, real gap, not a duplicate. Severity stays medium (tool reports wrong state / fails spuriously; the Main-LR case leaves a raised master certified against silence), but at the lower end given operator confirmation, T2 confirmation on Main, and that the primary wedge/PRE use case is unaffected.

## E47. [medium] (scales-nodes, confirmed) The order in which a restore streams its `/` lines is acoustically irrelevant (a restore behaves like the desk's atomic scene recall).

**Encoded at:** src/x32mcp/nodes.py:112 `_SECTION_RANK` (config 0, delay 1, preamp 2, mix 3, send 4, eq 5, dyn 6, gate 7, insert 8, grp 9) + nodes.py:1174-1187 `_restore_sort_key` (families in params order: ch..main, dca, THEN headamp, THEN fx, THEN config); tests/test_nodes.py:805-807 asserts exactly this order ('/ch/01/mix' before '/ch/01/eq/2', '/ch/01/insert'; '/headamp/005' and '/fx/3' after every strip); FakeDesk has no coupling between levels/phantom and audio, and its SyntheticRta loop is never run during a restore.

**Code depends on it at:** src/x32mcp/nodes.py:1201-1227 restore_plan; src/x32mcp/desk.py:1312-1333 Desk.restore streams the lines one per rate-limiter slot (policy.writes_per_second 50, device.yaml:747) with no mute/duck around the sequence; server.py:1242 documents 'a full restore … can take a minute'; server.py:1250 previews only the first 15 changes in the same sweep order, so master/headamp/routing changes (which sort last) are the ones elided from the confirmation text.

**Reality:** A real console recalls a scene inside one DSP frame; this restore exposes every intermediate state for 20 ms..tens of seconds. Physics: raising a bus/main master or channel fader (rank 3) before that strip's EQ notches (rank 5), dynamics (6), gate (7) and insert-on (8) are back, and long before the GEQ feedback notches (`/fx/N/par`, family fx, written after ALL strips, DCAs and head amps) re-creates exactly the loop gain the notches were cut for — HANDOVER §4b measured rings growing to a howl within seconds at that gain. Head-amp gain/phantom (family headamp) is written after every channel fader is open: a +24 dB preamp step and 48 V engage into a live channel is a thump/howl (engineers mute before touching phantom). Probe of the actual plan for a post-ring-out snapshot restored onto a reset desk: `0 /ch/04/mix ON +2.0…`, 1-16 sends up, `17 /ch/04/eq/3 … -6.00`, `18 /bus/01/mix ON 0.0…`, `19 /bus/01/eq/2`, `20 /bus/01/insert ON PRE FX5L`, `21 /headamp/032 +44.5 ON`, `22 /fx/5/par …-9.0…` (GEQ notches dead last).

**On a real desk:** restore_snapshot (the documented undo, allowed in show mode) of a snapshot taken after a ring-out, onto a desk that was since flattened/pulled down: the wedge master returns to show level with a flat GEQ and no PEQ notches for (lines between)/50 s — on a whole-desk restore the `/fx/5/par` line can land 10-40 s after `/bus/01/mix` — the monitors howl at the musicians; then head amp 032 jumps +24.5 dB with phantom into the open SM58 channel (bang through PA). The operator confirmed a preview that showed channel names/faders and '… 212 more'.

**Offline test:** Committed failing test: $SP/worktrees/assumptions-scales-nodes (branch wt/assumptions-scales-nodes, commit cf11e8b) tests/test_assumptions_nodes.py::test_restore_plan_raises_levels_only_after_processing_inserts_geq_and_headamps — asserts eq/insert/fx-par/headamp lines precede the mix/master lines of the strips they protect (fails: `assert 1 < 0`). Stronger integration version: arm FakeDesk's SyntheticRta ring on bus 1 with growth gated on (insert off or GEQ flat) AND master ≥ −10 dB, run Desk.restore of a notched snapshot onto a flat/low live state, assert the ring band never exceeds the detector threshold during the restore. Fix direction: write levels last (or duck masters/mute strips first and release at the end), headamp+phantom before the strip's mix line, fx type/par before insert-on before bus master; or use `/load` of a saved scene for whole-desk undo.

Severity high: the documented undo, permitted in show mode, issues a write sequence that can put a wedge/PA into feedback and bang phantom through an open mic channel, with the hazardous lines elided from the confirmation preview, and the emulator is structurally incapable of revealing it. No mitigation exists in code.

> **Verifier 2: PARTIAL (medium)** — Core mechanism CONFIRMED, scope and severity overstated.

What holds: a `/`-line is applied by the desk the moment it lands (transport.md §6.6: value change is pushed to xremote clients immediately), so a streamed restore exposes every intermediate state, and nothing in Desk.restore (desk.py:1312-1333) ducks or mutes around the sequence; the rate limiter (device.yaml:733, 50/s, policy.py:375) makes the exposure lines/50 s long. The order is a deliberate design choice (DESIGN.md:418 'config, preamp, mix, sends, eq, dyn, gate, insert, grp, then bus/main/dca/headamp/fx/config'), pinned by tests/test_nodes.py:805-807, and it is acoustically WORSE than the real desk's own scene-file order, which within a strip is config, delay, preamp, gate, dyn, insert, eq, THEN mix/sends (research: .scn files are verbatim node dumps re-parsed by SetSceneParse.c, fx_routing_scenes.md §4.6) — i.e. the desk (and X32-Edit sync / Maillot's X32SetScene, which stream exactly these lines to live desks) put processing before level; nodes.py:112 `_SECTION_RANK` puts mix(3)/send(4) before eq(5)/dyn(6)/gate(7)/insert(8). Across families both the desk file and this code put /fx after the bus masters, so the GEQ-notches-last window exists either way, but here headamp gain precedes fx (desk file: headamp after fx) and config/routing/mute-groups come dead last (desk file: first). My probe of restore_plan between two fully different states: 1995 lines = 40 s; /bus/01/mix at idx 1385, /bus/01/insert 1401, /headamp/* 1826-1953, /fx/5 1958, /fx/5/par 1970 → 585 lines = 11.7 s of wedge master at snapshot level before its GEQ notches return, ~2.3 s of that at full restored preamp gain; within-strip mix→insert gap 16-26 lines = 0.3-0.5 s. CFS DONE leaves the master at peak−3 dB (cfs.py:1274-1285), a level that by construction rang without the notches, so re-applying a post-ring-out snapshot onto a flattened/other-band desk with outputs open would ring audibly for seconds. The GIG_CHECKLIST 'snapshot_desk("pre-<band>") — the undo for the whole changeover' + recall_scene flow makes the large-diff, notched-target case a documented use, and the restore itself re-raises desk-side pull-downs/unmutes buses (bus family) ~11 s before /fx/5/par; the 15-change preview (server.py:1250) is in sweep order so masters/fx/headamp are the elided tail. FakeDesk has no level→audio coupling, so no test can see it; the committed test (wt/assumptions-scales-nodes cf11e8b, test_restore_plan_raises_levels_only_after_processing_inserts_geq_and_headamps) fails today with `assert 1 < 0` (verified).

What does not hold / mitigations: (1) Direction. The primary documented undo — restore of the auto-pre-write snapshot after this tool's own ring-out — LOWERS the master first and removes notches after, which the current order handles safely; the proposed 'write levels last' fix would make that common direction the hazardous one (notches removed while the raised master is still up). The correct fix is direction-aware (attenuating writes first, gain-raising writes last) or duck/mute the affected masters for the duration — not a simple re-rank. (2) Small diffs (HANDOVER §4a: 3 sections in 9 ms; mid-set show-mode undo) give 20-60 ms windows — a few loop round-trips, no howl. (3) The headamp '+24.5 dB and 48 V into an open SM58 = bang' sub-claim is not an ordering defect: the intermediate state (fader up, gain low, phantom off) is quieter than the endpoint, and an atomic desk recall or X32-Edit sync engages phantom into an equally open channel; only a mute-around-restore would help, no re-ordering can. (4) Real-desk tooling (X32-Edit PC→desk sync, X32SetScene) also streams whole scenes unmuted with fx after bus masters; engineers mute outputs for that, and the checklist says outputs down during changeover. Net: a genuine untested physical assumption that can make wedges ring for seconds during a large raising-direction restore, but final state is correct, the default undo direction is safe, and it needs open outputs during a whole-desk restore — medium, not high.

## E48. [medium] (scales-nodes, confirmed) The channel→head-amp mapping can be computed client-side from routing enums (research §12.4) and the user-in slot for source InNN is `/config/userrout/in/NN`; the desk offers nothing better.

**Encoded at:** device.yaml:53-60 meta.roots has no `-ha` family and params has no `/-ha/NN/index` leaf (so neither Descriptor nor FakeDesk can express it); src/x32mcp/fakedesk.py builds no /-ha state; tests/integration/test_desk.py:725-733 exercises user routing only with `IN/1-8 = UIN1-8` (block b selects UIN block b, so slot == source number) and classic AN1-8; no test permutes UIN blocks or checks against a desk-reported index.

**Code depends on it at:** src/x32mcp/desk.py:722-779 headamp_index_for (docstring itself says 'scales_params.md §12.4 (UNCONFIRMED)'); desk.py:765 `patch = await self._leaf(f"/config/userrout/in/{src:02d}")` indexes the user-in table by SOURCE NUMBER; used by set_phantom (desk.py:1350+), set_gain, provision.discover_mics (provision.py:566 `physical = headamp_index_for(c) is not None`) and CFS preflight.

**Reality:** scales_params.md §12.3 (VERIFIED, PDF p.43): the console exposes read-only `/-ha/[00..39]/index` = 'the actual headamp used as source for a given input … −1 when the routing changes to an internal source such as the card slot' and the research says 'Prefer querying /-ha/NN/index over computing (subscribe it with /xremote)'. §12.4 is explicitly 'inferred, not stated in the PDF — mark UNCONFIRMED and validate against /-ha/NN/index on a real desk', and its own formula for UIN blocks is `userrout_in[(r-20)*8 + off]` (slot chosen by WHICH UIN block the routing block selects), not `userrout_in[source-1]`: with `/config/routing/IN/1-8 = UIN9-16`, ch 1 is fed by user-in slot 9. The code and the research disagree; the M5 desk happened to use UIN1-8/9-16/… in order so both gave the same answer.

**On a real desk:** On any desk whose input blocks select a non-identity UIN block (or PLAY routing with UIN, or aux-in via UIN1-6), set_phantom('ch.1', on) resolves head amp 000 instead of 032 and puts 48 V on local XLR 1 (a ribbon mic, a DI'd keyboard, a wireless receiver) while reporting success for ch 1; set_gain moves the wrong preamp (level jump on an unrelated channel through FOH); discover_mics/CFS classify card returns as physical mics and vice versa. All silently — there is no cross-check against the desk's own answer.

**Offline test:** Committed failing test (commit e0c294d): tests/integration/test_assumptions_restore.py::test_user_in_block_offset_not_source_number_selects_the_userrout_slot — FakeDesk with `IN/1-8=UIN9-16`, `userrout/in/09=33` → expects head amp 32, gets 0. Proper fix + test: declare `/-ha/{n:02d}/index` (n 0..39, osc i, tier 0) in device.yaml, have FakeDesk compute it from its routing state (so the emulator finally models §12.3), make headamp_index_for read `/-ha/NN/index` first and use the algorithm only as a fallback/cross-check that logs a WARNING on disagreement; test both permuted-UIN and `-1` (card) cases.

2.
