So the '48 V on a ribbon mic while reporting success' outcome cannot be triggered by the LLM/operator at a gig today — it is latent library behaviour (one wiring step away; BRIEF.md:64 does list phantom as a planned Tier-2 tool, and README:102 names wrong-mic phantom as a physical harm).
- discover_mics consumes only `is not None`. A wrong index misclassifies a channel only when the wrongly-read slot's class (physical vs OFF/card/aux) differs from the true slot's; with FW-4 default user-in slots (Local N) most cross-block channels come out 'physical' by luck. When it does differ the effect is: a card/USB feed listed as a mic (report noise) or real mics dropped → spurious PREFLIGHT_FAILED 'no candidate mics' / misleading notes at the gig. The mic list drives no writes (nothing is unmuted; notches go to the bus GEQ), so CFS does not 'act on garbage' in the write sense.
Net: real, reproducible wrong belief about the desk with a medium-class gig consequence today (tool reports wrong state / blocks spuriously on a cross-block-UIN desk) and a high-class consequence held back only by the fact that set_phantom-by-target is not exposed. **Encoded at:** src/x32mcp/nodes.py:266-291 tokenize takes the FIRST closing quote (`text.find('"', i+1)`, :280); tests/test_nodes.py:58 and :322 synth/name fixtures ('Vox Tony', '', '1 Diazno', 'Kick', "Tony's Vox", '  padded  ') never include `"`; tests/integration/test_desk.py:352-357 only proves OUR label() downgrades a quote; src/x32mcp/fakedesk.py:666 stores any string but no test sets a quoted name desk-side; desk.py:1163-1167 comment asserts 'the desk cannot store' a quote — unverified.

Dependents verified: desk.py:728-730 headamp_index_for reads config/source via _leaf (node-text path, not an OSC ,i GET) and returns None when it is not a str; provision.py:582/591 then sets physical=False -> include=False (the channel is not literally dropped if it is sending — it stays listed with a false "source OFF has no preamp" note — but it is excluded from the CFS mic set, and if it is the only mic preflight blocks with "no candidate mics"); desk.py:1363-1365 set_phantom by channel raises NOT_SUPPORTED; nodes.py:1191-1198/_leading_run + restore_plan:1220-1227 writes only `/ch/NN/config "12"` when the section differs, renaming the strip. Fixtures indeed never carry a quote (tests/test_nodes.py:58 synth names, :322 name loop; tests/integration/test_desk.py:352-357 only proves OUR label() downgrades a quote), while FakeDesk stores any string (fakedesk.py:666 `return str(arg)`) and format_token (nodes.py:367-370) emits it naively as `"12" Tom"`, so the fake is already capable of the behaviour — just never exercised. The committed tests in worktree wt/assumptions-scales-nodes (cf11e8b) both fail today as described (ran them: source None in both). Minor slips that do not change the verdict: the "which the desk cannot store" wording is at patches.py:375, not desk.py:1163-1167 (that comment says a quoted name "truncates the rest of the line on the desk"); the restore rename only fires when snapshot and live differ for that section. Reality: a `"` reaches a desk-side name trivially via any OSC leaf write (/ch/NN/config/name ,s — how X32-Edit/Mixing Station write names) and inch-mark names (12" Tom, 15" wedge, 18" sub) are a plausible live-sound habit; the code relies on an explicitly UNCONFIRMED emission format with no fallback. Severity medium is appropriate: wrong reported state (source None, colour '8'), spurious preflight exclusion/blocker and a cosmetic wrong write on restore; set_phantom fails safe, so not high.

> **Verifier 2: CONFIRMED (medium)** — The mechanism is real and reproduced: nodes.tokenize (src/x32mcp/nodes.py:266-291, first-closing-quote at :280) mis-splits a name whose embedded `"` is followed by whitespace. `/ch/05/config "12" Tom" 8 RD 5` → tokens ['"12"','Tom"','8','RD','5'] → parse_node_line gives {name:'12', icon:None, color:'8', source:None}. Every consumer reads config through node text (Desk._leaf → _section, desk.py:371-377), so headamp_index_for (desk.py:722-733) sees source None → returns None → set_phantom/set_gain by channel raise NOT_SUPPORTED 'no head amp behind its source' (desk.py:1363-1365); get_channel/get_strip report name '12', colour '8', no icon/source; discover_mics computes physical=False → include=False with the note 'source OFF has no preamp' (provision.py:582-597) and CFS start warns 'plan expects mics [9] … not routed/unmuted' (cfs.py:690-692); restore_plan's _leading_run (nodes.py:1191-1198,1220-1224) would emit `/ch/NN/config "12"` (rename) if that section ever differs between snapshot and live. The committed tests in worktree assumptions-scales-nodes (cf11e8b) fail today exactly as described (ran them: 2 failed). Research status: transport.md §6.3 (line 461) and §9.2 item 2 mark quote emission UNCONFIRMED/'avoid'; the only mitigation in the code is write-side (label() downgrades `"` to `'`, desk.py:1163-1167) — there is no read-side fallback, and the operator/X32-Edit/Mixing Station set names far more often than this tool. The FakeDesk is actually faithful here (format_token renders f'"{value}"' = the emulator's naive "%s", nodes.py:367-370); the assumption lives in the fixtures (no desk-side quoted name anywhere) and the parser.

Skeptical caveats that narrow (but do not refute) it: (1) the trigger is narrower than 'any quote' — because tokenize glues non-space text after the closing quote, `Tom 12"`, `10"`, `Vox "Tony"`, `Say "Hi"` all parse correctly; only a quote followed by whitespace inside the name (`12" Tom`, `"Tony" Vox`, `7" `) breaks. (2) Real-desk emission is unverified; naive printf is the most likely behaviour (emulator does it, no escape mechanism exists), but the desk could conceivably refuse/strip `"` on entry. (3) Consequences are per-strip and fail-safe: refusals and wrong read-back, nothing audible; discover_mics does not silently drop a sending channel — it lists it as excluded with a (wrong) note, and ring-out does not mute/unmute mics, so CFS does not act on garbage. (4) The 'crashes on colour 8' part depends on a separate finding; the restore rename needs the config section to differ (e.g. our label() recoloured that strip during the session, then undo). Likelihood at a gig is low (size-labelled toms typed in X32-Edit as `12" Tom`, quoted nicknames), but when it hits, preamp tools refuse with a misleading reason and state reads lie for that channel — that is the rubric's 'medium' (wrong state / spurious failure), at the low end. Fix is cheap and safe: for sections whose only string is the leading field, anchor the closing quote from the right using the known trailing token count; confirm the real emission once on the FW 4.13 desk.

## E50. [medium] (transport-connection, confirmed) Every datagram we SEND reaches the desk: the fault model only ever loses REPLIES (or everything at once), so all fire-and-forget writes — panic()'s 24 mutes, CFS notches, mutes, ramps — are certified as delivered.

**Encoded at:** src/x32mcp/fakedesk.py:451-453 + :792-799 (drop_next decrements only in _reply(), i.e. after the request was applied — docstring :57-58 says so explicitly); tests/test_connection.py:79-83 (Responder: 'drop means lose the reply… only answerable datagrams use the budget') and :74-75 (silent = all-or-nothing); tests/conftest.py:1-8,79-90 (in-memory shim: lossless, in-order); tests/integration/test_fakedesk.py:546-563 (drop test asserts 'a dropped echo still leaves the write applied'); HANDOVER §4a 'panic 24/24 verified' was on wired Ethernet.

**Code depends on it at:** src/x32mcp/desk.py:1184-1220 (panic: one burst of 24 conn.set() in ~0.4 ms, no read-back, reports count=24 delivered='sent'); src/x32mcp/connection.py:520-530 (set() is fire-and-forget by design, no verify option); every Desk._write / ramp step; CFS notch writes.

**Reality:** transport.md §2: 'Plain UDP, no ACK, no error report. DOC warns that burst … traffic over 54 Mb/s Wi-Fi loses datagrams silently' (DOC 269-274); §5.2: 'No ack. If you need confirmation, GET it back'; §10/§12.6: pace bulk writes 1-10 ms apart. Loss on a venue 2.4 GHz network is bidirectional and bursty; a 24-datagram burst in 0.4 ms is the worst case for an AP queue. At 5 % loss P(all 24 land)=0.29.

**On a real desk:** Operator on Wi-Fi says 'kill it'; panic() returns 'PANIC: 24 outputs muted (sent)' while Main LR (or a wedge bus) is still live and howling — the tool affirmatively lies in the one path that protects hearing. Same class: a CFS −3 dB notch that never arrived is recorded as applied; a mute reports muted. Probe test (worktree) with ONE lost inbound datagram: panic reported 24 muted, '/main/st/mix/on' still 1.

**Offline test:** Give FakeDesk an inbound-loss fault (done in worktree wt/assumptions-transport-connection: FakeDesk.drop_next_inbound(n), fakedesk.py) and a random loss_rate; tests/integration/test_transport_assumptions.py::test_panic_with_one_lost_datagram_still_silences_every_output FAILS today. Fix direction: panic repeats the (idempotent) burst 2-3× spaced ~20 ms and/or reads back /node main/st/mix, bus/NN/mix and re-sends the ones still ON, reporting 'verified'/'unverified' per output; CFS notch = write + read-back.

> **Verifier 1: CONFIRMED (high)** — All cited code and test lines say what the finding claims. FakeDesk's only loss fault is reply-side: drop_next (src/x32mcp/fakedesk.py:451-453) is decremented exclusively in _reply() (:792-799) after _on_datagram (:750-769) has already applied the request; the module docstring (:57-58) states "loses the next n replies (the requests are still processed)"; `silent` is all-or-nothing (:761, :773, :785). The unit-test Responder mirrors this (tests/test_connection.py:74-75 silent, :79-83 "drop means lose the reply … only answerable datagrams use the budget"), and tests/integration/test_fakedesk.py:560-563 explicitly asserts "a dropped echo still leaves the write applied". No fixture anywhere can lose an inbound SET, so no test can observe a fire-and-forget write that never landed. Code that depends on it: Desk.panic (src/x32mcp/desk.py:1184-1220) fires 24 conn.set() back-to-back, appends every target to `done` on send success, never reads back or repeats, and returns count=24/delivered="sent"; server.py:1064-1072 renders that as "PANIC: 24 outputs muted in … ms (sent)". X32Connection.set (connection.py:520-530) is fire-and-forget by design; Desk._write (desk.py:871-884) likewise. I ran the claimant's probe (worktree wt/assumptions-transport-connection, FakeDesk.drop_next_inbound(1)): test_panic_with_one_lost_datagram_still_silences_every_output FAILS today — panic logged "24 outputs muted in 0.2 ms" while /main/st/mix/on was still 1. Research check: transport.md §5.2 (line 340) "No ack. If you need confirmation, GET it back"; §12.6 (line 669) "pace bulk writes ~1–10 ms apart"; §10 (line 648) X32SetScene default 1 ms between commands and DOC recommends the `/` echo as flow control. Caveat on the §2 quote: the DOC Wi-Fi warning (line 149, and §10 line 649 "Overrun risk is on the receive side") is specifically about /node and /showdump reply bursts, which the claimant's ellipsis hid — outbound loss rests on UDP-over-Wi-Fi physics rather than a documented desk observation, but that is squarely within the brief's "engineering common sense" source, and README.md:807-811 explicitly contemplates a Wi-Fi tablet host relying on "DEGRADED handling to cover Wi-Fi hiccups" (the all-or-nothing model). HANDOVER §4a's 24/24 panic verification was on a link whose degraded test was "after the cable came out", i.e. wired. No fallback was missed for panic or plain mutes/faders (cache invalidation at desk.py:883/1208 means a later read is truthful, but the write's own result asserts success without verification). One sub-claim is partially mitigated: in ring-out mode a lost CFS notch fails _verify_decay (cfs.py:1200-1225) and is re-written deeper, so it is not silently "recorded as applied" forever — though the controller's depth bookkeeping still diverges from the desk. Severity high is warranted: panic is the hearing-protection path and the tool affirmatively reports an output muted that may still be live, with a cheap fix (repeat the idempotent burst and/or read back /main|bus|mtx mix/on).

> **Verifier 2: CONFIRMED (medium)** — Core claim holds. (1) The fault model genuinely cannot lose a request: FakeDesk.drop_next decrements only inside _reply() (src/x32mcp/fakedesk.py:451-453, 792-799; docstring :57-58 'loses the next n replies (the requests are still processed)'); `silent` is all-or-nothing; the unit-test Responder says so explicitly (tests/test_connection.py:79-83: 'a lost /xremote or SET is invisible to the client … so only answerable datagrams use the budget'); loopback/shim delivery is lossless. So tests/integration/test_desk.py:360-370 certifies `res['muted']` == desk state only because no datagram can go missing. (2) Desk.panic (desk.py:1184-1220) counts conn.set() calls that did not raise locally and returns count/muted/delivered='sent'; server.py:1070-1071 turns that into 'PANIC: 24 outputs muted in X ms (sent)'. No read-back, no repeat. (3) Research agrees with the finder, not the fake's network model: transport.md §2 'Plain UDP, no ACK … burst traffic over 54 Mb/s Wi-Fi loses datagrams silently'; §5.2 'No ack. If you need confirmation, GET it back'; §12.6 'pace bulk writes ~1-10 ms apart' (panic bursts 24 in ~0.4 ms). (4) Reproduced: the worktree probe (wt/assumptions-transport-connection, FakeDesk.drop_next_inbound(1)) fails on HEAD — panic logged 'PANIC: 24 outputs muted in 0.2 ms' while /main/st/mix/on was still 1. (5) Supporting evidence of an unrealised intent: docs/GIG_CHECKLIST.md:171-172 expects `delivered: "confirmed"`, a value the code can never produce; and cfs.py:45-48/1326 already implements the correct emergency pattern (raw re-send every 0.5 s + read-back until confirmed) for its master restore, so panic's omission is a real gap, not a protocol inevitability.

Severity downgraded high→medium on real-world consequence: the primary, live-tested topology is a PC at the desk on wired LAN (HANDOVER §4a: 24/24 verified muted on the real X32; cable-pull tests), where loss of 24 tiny datagrams is negligible; a failed panic is instantly audible (the howl continues) rather than a silent wrong write; README/GIG_CHECKLIST repeatedly position panic as a backstop behind the physical mute/X32-Edit reflex; and the summary does carry '(sent)' rather than 'confirmed'. It is not low because README:806-811 documents a Wi-Fi tablet host as a supported deployment ('expect … DEGRADED handling to cover Wi-Fi hiccups' — it does not cover single-datagram loss), venue 2.4 GHz loss is bursty and bidirectional, and the one tool whose job is hearing safety affirmatively reports 'N outputs muted' from a local send count. Peripheral sub-claims are weaker: a lost CFS notch is caught by the acoustic VERIFY stage (cfs.py:1200-1219) and deepened, so it self-heals at the cost of an over-deep cut (low); ordinary mutes/faders are fire-and-forget by protocol design and the cache is invalidated so the next read shows truth (low-medium). Fix is cheap and idempotent: repeat the 24-mute burst 2-3x ~20 ms apart and/or /node-read main/st, main/m, bus/NN, mtx/NN mix and re-send any still ON, reporting verified/unverified per output.

## E51. [medium] (transport-connection, confirmed) Any '/' echo acknowledges the oldest pending slash() — the echo's content is never compared with the line that was sent (DESIGN §8 chose 'reply address "/", FIFO').

**Encoded at:** docs/DESIGN.md §8 slash(): '(reply address "/", FIFO)'; tests/test_connection.py:417-433 and tests/integration/test_fakedesk.py:179-213 (one slash at a time, echo immediate); src/x32mcp/fakedesk.py:1012-1021 echoes verbatim (correct) but no test sends two lines whose echoes can cross.

**Code depends on it at:** src/x32mcp/connection.py:542-554 (slash → _request_bytes(key='/') with retries) and :139-143 (_reply_key ignores args for '/'); src/x32mcp/desk.py:1318-1333 (restore(): a line counts as 'written' when slash() returns; 'failed' only on RequestTimeout).

**Reality:** transport.md §6.6 (DOC 4591-4593): the desk echoes the '/' command back VERBATIM precisely so the client can do flow control per command; the emulator memcpy's the received datagram (X32.c 3769-3771). The echo therefore identifies the line; matching on address alone throws that away. With latency > timeout (previous finding) line N's second echo acknowledges line N+1 even if line N+1 was lost in transit.

**On a real desk:** restore_snapshot over a lossy link returns written=N failed=[] while one or more sections (a wedge send level, a mute) never reached the desk; the operator trusts the 'clean' restore; diff_snapshot afterwards would show it but nobody runs it mid-show. Probe: latency 300 ms + both datagrams of line 2 dropped inbound → slash(line 2) returned success, desk value unchanged.

**Offline test:** Worktree test test_slash_echo_of_previous_line_must_not_ack_a_lost_line FAILS today. Fix: key '/' waiters on the exact string ('/:'+text) — _reply_key(msg) for address '/' returns '/:'+msg.args[0].strip(); unmatched echoes are dropped. Zero cost, uses the CONFIRMED verbatim-echo property.

> **Verifier 1: CONFIRMED (medium)** — Both citations check out and the code has no fallback. (1) Research: docs/research/transport.md §6.6 (lines 524-540) says exactly what is claimed — the desk "echoes the `/` command back" to the sender (DOC 4591-4593, for flow control) and the emulator `memcpy(s_buf, w_buf, w_len); return(S_SND)` (X32.c 3769-3771, VERIFIED) echoes the whole received datagram verbatim, i.e. the echo identifies the line. (2) Design/code: docs/DESIGN.md:357 specifies 'await that echo (reply address "/", FIFO)'; src/x32mcp/connection.py:139-143 `_reply_key` returns `msg.address` for anything that is not a `node` reply, so every '/' echo maps to key "/" regardless of its string arg; connection.py:542-554 `slash()` calls `_request_bytes(encode("/", text), "/", per_attempt, self._retries)` and `_request_bytes`/`_pop_waiter` (747-795, 820) resolve the OLDEST non-done future in the "/" deque on any '/' datagram. Nothing compares the echoed text with the sent text. Notably DESIGN §8 already does payload-prefix matching for `/node` replies (key "node:/ch/01/config"), so the omission for '/' is an inconsistency, not a deliberate trade-off with a mitigation. (3) Dependence: src/x32mcp/desk.py:1312-1340 `restore()` is the sole caller of slash() (grep confirms only desk.py:1326); it counts a line as `written` when slash() returns and lists it in `failed` only on RequestTimeout; there is no read-back/verify step (only `self.invalidate()`). (4) Tests: tests/test_connection.py:417-433 and tests/integration/test_fakedesk.py:179-213 only ever have one slash in flight with an immediate echo; fakedesk.py:1012-1021 `_h_slash` echoes verbatim (faithful) but HEAD's FakeDesk cannot lose an inbound datagram, so echo crossing was never exercised. (5) Repro: I ran the claimant's worktree test (worktrees/assumptions-transport-connection, commit b32dd66, which adds `FakeDesk.drop_next_inbound` and uses the existing `/-fake/latency`): with 300 ms reply latency vs 250 ms per-attempt timeout, slash(line 1) is resolved by attempt-1's late echo, attempt-2's echo is left on the wire, then both datagrams of slash(line 2) are dropped before the desk — slash(line 2) returns normally: `Failed: DID NOT RAISE Exception` (1 failed in 0.71 s). So restore() would report written=N, failed=[] while /ch/03/mix/fader never changed on the desk. Once one line double-echoes, every subsequent line in the restore is acked by its predecessor's echo (off-by-one cascade), so flow control is defeated for the rest of the run and any outbound loss is silent; the final orphan echo is dropped via `_NOT_PARAMS` ('/' at connection.py:71/828). Precondition is a compound network event (an echo later than timeout_s=0.5 s default, e.g. Wi-Fi stall or desk busy, plus a lost datagram), and the consequence is a tool reporting a write that never landed rather than a wrong value written — medium, as claimed. Proposed fix (key '/' waiters on '/:'+text, derive the same from msg.args[0] in _reply_key, drop unmatched echoes) is sound and relies only on the CONFIRMED verbatim-echo property.

> **Verifier 2: CONFIRMED (medium)** — Mechanism verified in code and by running the finder's probe. connection.py:139-143 `_reply_key` returns the bare address "/" for a node-write echo (args ignored); connection.py:747-769 `_request_bytes` appends a fresh future per attempt under key "/" and `_discard`s the timed-out one; connection.py:781-794 `_pop_waiter` hands ANY "/" echo to the oldest live waiter. So when attempt 1's echo arrives after the per-attempt timeout (default 0.5 s, connection.py:245-246, retries=2), it resolves attempt 2's future and slash() returns while attempt 2's echo is still in flight; that stray echo then satisfies the NEXT slash() — desk.py:1324-1329 counts the line as `written` purely on slash() returning, and server.py:1260-1266 reports "N/N section(s) written" with no read-back. Once off-by-one, every later line in the restore is 'acked' by its predecessor's echo (persisting as long as RTT > the 20 ms write slot, device.yaml:733 writes_per_second 50), i.e. retry protection silently disappears while the tool still claims echo-verified delivery; the first outbound loss is then reported as written. Ran $SP/worktrees/assumptions-transport-connection tests/integration/test_transport_assumptions.py::test_slash_echo_of_previous_line_must_not_ack_a_lost_line on HEAD a408a2a code: FAILS ('DID NOT RAISE') and /ch/03 fader unchanged on the FakeDesk — slash() returned success for a line the desk never received.

Assumption class fits the brief: the FakeDesk fault model (fakedesk.py:451-453 drop_next = replies only; latency constant and, in the only latency test tests/integration/test_fakedesk.py:581-586, 120 ms < the 250 ms per-attempt timeout) encodes 'requests are never lost and replies never arrive after a retry fired' — a network property Wi-Fi does not honour. Existing slash tests (tests/test_connection.py:415-431, tests/integration/test_fakedesk.py:179-213) are one-line-at-a-time with an immediate echo. Research does not rescue the design: transport.md §6.6 (line 536) CONFIRMS the desk echoes the '/' line back verbatim (DOC 4591-4593; X32.c 3769-3771 memcpy) and DESIGN.md:747 itself records 'echoed back verbatim', yet DESIGN.md:357 chose 'reply address "/", FIFO' — the identifying content is discarded by choice, so the proposed fix (key '/' waiters on the echoed text) rests on a CONFIRMED property and costs nothing.

Skeptical weighting: on the primary documented deployment (wired PC on the desk LAN, README:289) an echo delayed >500 ms essentially never happens, so there it is theoretical. But README:806-811 explicitly supports hosting the server on a Wi-Fi tablet and promises 'the watchdog/DEGRADED handling covers Wi-Fi hiccups'; on congested 2.4 GHz venue Wi-Fi, RTT excursions >500 ms (or an L2-duplicated datagram, which desyncs with no latency requirement) plus a few % datagram loss within a long restore ('can take a minute', server.py:1242) are realistic, and the outcome is a false-clean undo (a wedge send / mute / EQ section not restored, reported written) that nothing re-checks mid-show. Not a harmful write and needs two coinciding network faults, so not high; not mitigated and not cosmetic, so not low. Medium (low end) stands.

Both fail today (no such fields exist).
