Code: desk.py:92 _PANIC_FAMILIES=("main","bus","mtx") citing §11 option 1; desk.py:1184-1220 panic() writes only {prefix}/mix/on 0 and returns muted/count with no tap read, no not_silenced list, no clearsolo (grep: no 'clearsolo' and no '/outputs' anywhere in src/); server.py:128-129 system instructions "panic() mutes every mix bus ... use it whenever the user says stop / kill it / mute everything"; server.py:1065-1071 summary "PANIC: N outputs muted"; README:204 "It mutes all 24 outputs"; GIG_CHECKLIST:11 "mutes all outputs in one go". device.yaml (835 lines) has no /outputs/{main,aux,p16,aes,rec} tree at all, so FakeDesk cannot represent a PRE/DirectOut/Monitor-tapped output; fakedesk.py:930-941 _strip_level follows only mix/on+fader; tests/integration/test_desk.py:360-370 'test_panic_mutes_24_outputs_fast' asserts count==24 and the 24 mix/on==0 — it certifies the writes, conflating strips with physical outputs. provision.py:627-663 preflight checks GEQ/mics/muted/master only — no check that the bus actually controls a speaker (no tap/src read), and cfs.py's RAISE loop treats the bus master as the loop-gain variable. REVIEW_BRIEF:121 explicitly asks whether there is any state in which panic fails to silence the outputs — this is one, and no test can express it today. No code fallback was missed by the claimant. Tempering factors (why medium, not high): the limitation is a deliberate, documented design choice (desk.py:1187 docstring "Silences every POST-tapped output (§11 option 1)"; HANDOVER §4a "Input channels are deliberately untouched"); README:621-626 and GIG_CHECKLIST frame panic as a backstop with the physical mute/X32-Edit as the reflex; on factory-default routing (bus/main POST taps) panic does silence the PA and wedges, and in a feedback event breaking the PA/wedge loop also stops what DirectOut/P16/record/monitor feeds carry. The realistic uncovered paths are P16/IEM direct-outs, monitor/phones (src 74/75), PRE record/broadcast splits and input-routed AES50/card blocks — real (common on church X32 rigs) but narrower than 'speakers keep howling'; the ring_out-on-PRE-tapped-wedge scenario is physically correct but an unusual configuration in which the engineer's own master is equally meaningless. 'M5 was on one rack with default taps' is the claimant's inference — HANDOVER only says 24/24 verified muted and confirmed visually. Net: the overclaim ('24 outputs muted' / 'mute everything') with no tap awareness or not_silenced reporting is a confirmed assumption the fake and tests cannot falsify; the proposed offline test (add /outputs/*/NN/{src,pos} to device.yaml+FakeDesk, model §4.7 mute semantics on output meters, assert panic reports not_silenced / preflight warns) is sound and would fail today.

> **Verifier 2: PARTIAL (medium)** — The factual core holds: device.yaml declares no /outputs/{main,aux,p16,aes,rec}/NN/{src,pos} nodes (grep: zero hits), so the FakeDesk cannot represent a PRE/IN/EQ-tapped XLR or a DirectOut-fed output, and nothing in src/ (desk.py, provision.py, cfs.py, server.py) ever reads an output tap or sends /-action/clearsolo. FakeDesk output levels are derived purely from mix/on+fader (fakedesk.py:929-941), i.e. it models an all-POST world. fx_routing_scenes.md §11 option 1 states verbatim that the 24-mute approach 'does not silence outputs whose pos is IN/LC, <-EQ, EQ-> or PRE (no +M), nor DirectOut taps ... nor AES50/Card blocks routed from inputs', §13 item 13 marks factory pos=POST as UNCONFIRMED, and option 3 recommends clearsolo + input-strip mutes as belt-and-braces. The panic test (tests/integration/test_desk.py:359-370) only asserts 24 mix/on==0 writes; the server instructions (server.py:128-129) tell the LLM to use panic for 'mute everything' and the result says 'PANIC: 24 outputs muted' with no not_silenced list. So the code's claim to be the 'kill it' action does rest on every loudspeaker being POST/+M-tapped from a bus/main/matrix, and that is untestable offline today.

Why not CONFIRMED/high: (1) This is a deliberate, documented design choice, not a hidden belief — desk.py:1185-1187 docstring explicitly says 'Silences every POST-tapped output (§11 option 1)', and GIG_CHECKLIST.md:9-11,77-80 and README:621-626 state panic is a backstop and the reflex is the physical mute/X32-Edit. (2) Real-world likelihood is low: X32 factory taps are POST (general knowledge, and M5 verified 24/24 muted on the real rack, HANDOVER §4a:114-115); loudspeakers (mains, fills, subs, delays, wedges) are in practice fed from main/bus/matrix POST so the master controls them; PRE/DirectOut taps are overwhelmingly recording/broadcast/P16 feeds, not PA, and the solo/monitor bus feeds the engineer's own phones/nearfields, not the audience. (3) The failure is audible instantly (the wedge keeps howling) rather than a silent lie that propagates into later writes. (4) The ring_out half is essentially theoretical: an operator who PRE-taps a wedge has already decided the bus master does not control it, so asking to ring out that bus by raising its master is a self-contradictory setup; the RTA sourced on the bus would also show the master rise with no ring, ending at the ceiling with zero notches — misleading but requires operator error to reach. Net: a real, cheaply-fixable fidelity gap in an emergency tool (read /outputs/*/src,pos once and report not_silenced / add clearsolo; add the nodes to device.yaml+FakeDesk so a PRE-tap test can fail), but conditional on non-default routing and already flagged in docs — medium, not high.

## E53. [medium] (unconfirmed-hunter, confirmed) The head amp behind a channel can be computed from /config/routing + /config/userrout with user-input N always being /config/userrout/in/N (UIN block k only ever feeds input block k), so /-ha/NN/index need not be consulted before switching phantom power.

**Encoded at:** tests/integration/test_desk.py:711-737 (only IN/1-8 = UIN1-8 is exercised; FakeDesk has no /-ha model and cannot cross-check); device.yaml declares no /-ha/00..39/index leaves.

**Code depends on it at:** src/x32mcp/desk.py:722-785 headamp_index_for - UIN branch reads f'/config/userrout/in/{src:02d}' (764-768) instead of the research's userrout_in[(r-20)*8+off]; aux-in UIN1-2/1-4/1-6 blocks (routing_in_aux 13-15) fall through to None (777-783); result feeds set_phantom (desk.py:1352-1370, writes /headamp/NNN/phantom) and discover_mics 'physical' (provision.py:582).

**Reality:** scales_params.md §12.3: '/-ha/[00..39]/index (read-only) returns the actual headamp used as source for a given input ... Prefer querying /-ha/NN/index over computing'; §12.4 + §17: the algorithm's 'structure is inferred, not stated in the PDF - mark UNCONFIRMED and validate against /-ha/NN/index on a real desk'; §12.4 code indexes the user-in table by UIN block, not by channel number; §16 item 16 shows even bitfocus gets AES50-B wrong (064 vs 080). HANDOVER §4a defect 5 already proved one variant wrong on FW 4.13. No runtime cross-check exists although the FW 4.x desk answers /-ha.

**On a real desk:** On a desk with In 1-8 <- 'User In 9-16' (or aux-ins on UIN, or an AES50-B stage box), set_phantom('ch.3', on) puts 48 V on a different XLR - a ribbon mic or a line device on that input, plus a phantom thump through the PA if that channel is open - while the intended condenser stays dead; discover_mics marks card feeds as physical mics or real mics as non-physical.

**Offline test:** Add /-ha/00..39/index to device.yaml and have FakeDesk compute it from routing+userrout (research §12.4 algorithm, incl. UIN block cross-assignment and aux UIN); make Desk.headamp_index_for read /-ha first and only fall back to computing, refusing set_phantom-by-target when the two disagree. Tests: IN/1-8 = UIN9-16 with userrout/in/09 = 1 -> ch.1 must resolve to head amp 0 (today: reads userrout/in/01); IN/AUX = UIN1-2 -> auxin.1 resolves (today None).

> **Verifier 1: CONFIRMED (high)** — Both citations check out and the defect reproduces offline.

Research: scales_params.md §12.3 (lines 773-783) says verbatim "Prefer querying `/-ha/NN/index` over computing"; §12.4 (785-787) marks the compute-it-yourself algorithm "inferred, not stated in the PDF — mark UNCONFIRMED and validate against /-ha/NN/index on a real desk", and its code indexes the user-in table by UIN block: `userrout_in[(r - 20) * 8 + off]` (line 815) and, for aux-ins, `r in (13,14,15) → userrout_in[a]` (line 825); §17 (line 1049) repeats that /-ha is authoritative; §10 (651-653, VERIFIED from PDF p.21 and X32SetScene.h) confirms every /config/routing/IN block accepts any of UIN1-8/9-16/17-24/25-32, so cross-block assignment is a legal desk state. HANDOVER §4a defect 5 (lines 127-141) is as described.

Code: desk.py:721-785 headamp_index_for. The UIN branch (764-768) tests only `tok.upper().startswith("UIN")` and reads `/config/userrout/in/{src:02d}` — it discards which UIN block the token names, so it is correct only when routing block b carries UIN block b. The aux branch (777-783) loops over enum ranges 1-9 only; UIN1-2/1-4/1-6 (13-15) fall through to None. No `/-ha` read exists anywhere in src/ (grep: zero hits), device.yaml declares no /-ha leaves, FakeDesk has no /-ha model, and the only test (tests/integration/test_desk.py:710-740) exercises IN/1-8=UIN1-8, the one case where the two indexings coincide. Result feeds Desk.set_phantom(target) (desk.py:1352-1370, guarded write to /headamp/NNN/phantom, no cross-check) and discover_mics `physical` (provision.py:582). No fallback was missed.

Empirical repro (worktree wt/verify-uin-crossblock-repro, commits d79d305, ac0cafd; tests/integration/test_uin_crossblock_repro.py, all 4 fail on HEAD a408a2a): IN/1-8=UIN9-16, userrout/in/09=1, /in/01=5 → headamp_index_for('ch.1') returns 4 (research: 0) and set_phantom(Target('ch',1), True) returns {'headamp': 4, 'address': '/headamp/004/phantom'} with FakeDesk /headamp/004/phantom=1 and /000=0 — 48 V on the wrong preamp. The more plausible layout IN/9-16=UIN1-8 (local 1-8 + one user bank) also breaks: ch.9 → 16 instead of 32. IN/AUX=UIN1-2 → auxin.1 → None (research: 2), so set_phantom raises NOT_SUPPORTED and discover_mics drops a real mic as 'not a physical input'.

Caveats that do not change the verdict: set_phantom is in the DESIGN §13 Desk contract and tested but is not currently registered as an MCP tool in server.py (no 'phantom' in server.py/webui.py), so the wrong write is reachable through the Desk API rather than by the LLM today; discover_mics mislabelling is LLM-reachable now. The 'AES50-B stage box' example in failure_on_real_desk is not supported — the code's B mapping (80+) matches the PDF; §16 item 16 only shows third parties get it wrong. Severity kept high per the rubric (wrong guarded write to phantom power = hardware/safety) given the write path exists in product code with no /-ha validation despite the research flagging the algorithm UNCONFIRMED.

> **Verifier 2: PARTIAL (medium)** — The technical core is CONFIRMED, the severity/narrative is overstated.

Confirmed: desk.py:764-768 resolves a UIN block by reading /config/userrout/in/{src:02d} (src = channel input number), i.e. it assumes UIN block k only ever feeds input block k. scales_params.md §12.4 indexes userrout_in[(r-20)*8+off] (the UIN token picks WHICH eight user-in slots feed the block) — the only reading under which the four UIN tokens are not synonyms. desk.py:777-783 handles routing_in_aux 1..9 only, so UIN1-2/1-4/1-6 (13..15) fall through to None although §12.4 resolves them. Nothing in src/ ever reads /-ha/NN/index although §12.3 says to prefer it and §17 says the computed algorithm is UNCONFIRMED and must be validated against it; device.yaml declares no /-ha leaves and FakeDesk has no head-amp model, so tests/integration/test_desk.py:711-740 (diagonal IN/1-8=UIN1-8 only) cannot catch either gap. Repro in worktree (commit 1f84223): IN/1-8=UIN9-16, userrout/in/09=1, /in/01=129 -> headamp_index_for('ch.1') returns None (should be 0); with /in/01=5, Desk.set_phantom('ch.1', True) writes /headamp/004/phantom instead of /headamp/000; ch sourced AUX1 with IN/AUX=UIN1-2, /in/01=33 -> None (should be 32). All three tests fail today.

Why not 'high': the wrong 48 V write exists only in the Desk Python API. set_phantom is not an MCP tool (server.py has no phantom/headamp tool), not on the web UI, and patches.py/apply_patch_plan never touches phantom — at a gig driven through the shipped server nothing can put phantom on the wrong XLR. The only production consumer of headamp_index_for is discover_mics' physical flag (provision.py:582), which only tests None-vs-not-None: under cross-assigned UIN blocks it misclassifies only when the wrongly-read slot and the real slot differ in category (preamp vs card/OFF), giving a spurious 'no candidate mics' preflight blocker (provision.py:645, ring_out refused) or a USB feed counted as a mic — a heuristic HANDOVER §4b already calls weak. Trigger likelihood is low: FW-4 users almost always set the UIN blocks diagonally (the real X32 Rack in HANDOVER §4a/§139-141 was diagonal and resolved correctly), cross-assignment has little purpose because the slots themselves are patchable, and channels sourced from AUX1-6 routed via UIN are rare. The AES50-B/bitfocus aside is a non-issue: block_base() uses 080 for B, matching the PDF (§12.2). Net: a real, unmitigated UNCONFIRMED-dependency with no /-ha cross-check, latent wrong-write in a DESIGN §13-contract method, but reachable gig impact is 'tool reports wrong state / preflight fails spuriously' under uncommon routing -> medium.

## E54. [medium] (unconfirmed-hunter, partial) /meters/15 always carries the RTA-tab analysis of /-prefs/rta/source, whatever page the console or a remote editor is showing, for the whole session.

**Encoded at:** src/x32mcp/fakedesk.py:943-946 (frames independent of any screen state; /-stat/screen/* not modelled, not in device.yaml); all CFS integration tests inject SyntheticRta directly (tests/integration/test_cfs.py, test_server_tools.py::test_cfs_tools_with_injected_synthetic_rta).

**Code depends on it at:** src/x32mcp/meters.py:868-938 set_rta_source writes source/pos/options/autogain/det only - never /-stat/screen/screen or /-stat/screen/METER/page, never options bit 3 (Post GEQ); src/x32mcp/cfs.py:900-929 arms once and never re-reads /-stat/rtasource, /-stat/screen or /-stat/solo during RAISE/VERIFY.

**Reality:** meters.md §5.3 (l.446-461): 'Which of the three analyses /meters/15 carries when a PEQ or GEQ page is displayed on the console (or on a remote client) remains UNCONFIRMED (the DOC says the stream is "Used for RTA and some Effects, for example Dual GEQ, Stereo GEQ"). Safe practice: put the console on the METERS/RTA tab (/-stat/screen/screen ,i 1, then /-stat/screen/METER/page ,i 4) or at least do not leave an FX GEQ page showing'; 'The channel PEQ overlay always shows the selected channel'; the GEQ overlay 'by default analyses the bus the GEQ is inserted on' pre-GEQ unless bit 3. The safe practice is not implemented and there is no detection.

**On a real desk:** During a ring-out the engineer naturally opens FX5's GEQ page to watch the cuts appear (or taps a vocal channel's EQ): the stream flips to the GEQ overlay (pre-GEQ: the detector goes blind to its own notches and deepens every band to -9) or to the selected channel's pre-fader spectrum (a playback channel = music -> false notches; a dead channel -> deaf detector while the master keeps rising).

**Offline test:** Model /-stat/screen/screen + page and /-stat/selidx in FakeDesk: when screen=EFFECTS on a GEQ slot serve the insert-bus spectrum pre-GEQ unless options bit 3; when screen=CHANNEL/EQ serve the selected strip. Test: arm feedback_watch on bus 1, then fakedesk.set('/-stat/screen/screen', EQ page) with selidx = a channel without the ring -> expect CFS to force METER/RTA page at arm and to pause/abort (or re-assert) on the pushed screen change; today detection silently stops / cuts go unverified.

> **Verifier 1: PARTIAL (medium)** — Citations verified. docs/research/meters.md §5.3 l.451/453/461 say exactly what is quoted: the PEQ overlay always analyses the selected channel, the GEQ overlay analyses its insert bus (pre-GEQ unless options bit 3), and which of the three analyses /meters/15 carries while a PEQ/GEQ page is shown (console or remote client) is UNCONFIRMED, with an explicit 'safe practice' (force /-stat/screen/screen=1, METER/page=4). Code check: set_rta_source (src/x32mcp/meters.py:860-938) writes only source/pos/options-bit-5/autogain/det and reads /-stat/rtasource once; nothing in src/ references /-stat/screen at all (grep empty; device.yaml has only /-stat/selidx at l.541, no screen node); cfs._arm (cfs.py:901-929) calls set_rta_source once and nothing re-reads /-stat/rtasource or watches pushes during RAISE/VERIFY (no other rtasource reference in cfs.py/desk.py/server.py). FakeDesk._meter_values (fakedesk.py:946-948) serves SyntheticRta frames regardless of any screen state, and the CFS integration tests inject SyntheticRta directly (test_cfs.py:408,540; test_server_tools.py:571-572). So the dependency on an UNCONFIRMED item with neither the documented safe practice nor any detection/fallback is real, which the brief defines as a finding. Downgrades: (1) the adverse behaviour itself is unverified either way — the research's 'most reasonable reading' is that /meters/15 follows /-prefs/rta/source, and HANDOVER §4b's 600 s real-desk runs detected and notched successfully while the operator watched the panel/X32-Edit (pages unknown), so there is no evidence the stream actually flips; the remote-client variant is more speculative still. (2) The GEQ-overlay half of the failure narrative is overstated: HANDOVER §4b item 4 records that when a notch breaks an acoustic loop the ring stops in the room and the RTA sees it 'wherever it taps', so a pre-GEQ tap on the same bus would not deterministically 'deepen every band to -9' for real feedback — it only loses direct measurement of the cut (same as the already-observed POST-insert case). (3) RAISE is bounded by min(policy ceiling, master_ceiling_db, target) (cfs.py:22,674), limiting the deaf-detector case. The PEQ-overlay-on-a-playback-channel case (music spectrum -> spurious notches) remains a plausible garbage-in path but is doubly conditional (unconfirmed firmware behaviour + operator opening an EQ page mid-ring-out). Net: confirmed missing mitigation for a documented UNCONFIRMED risk; failure mode plausible but unproven and partly exaggerated -> medium, not high.

> **Verifier 2: PARTIAL (medium)** — The assumption is genuinely encoded and genuinely unverified, but the claimed failure is overstated and the severity should come down from high to medium.

What holds up: (1) src/x32mcp/fakedesk.py:943-946 serves SyntheticRta frames for /meters/15 unconditionally — no /-stat/screen/*, no METER/page, no coupling to /-stat/selidx or to the GEQ-overlay view; grep for "screen" over src/ and device.yaml returns nothing. (2) set_rta_source (src/x32mcp/meters.py:860-938) writes source/pos, clears options bit 5, forces autogain off and det=PEAK, verifies /-stat/rtasource ONCE, and never touches /-stat/screen/screen or /-stat/screen/METER/page; cfs._arm (src/x32mcp/cfs.py:901-929) calls it once and nothing in cfs.py ever re-reads /-stat/rtasource or listens for the /xremote push of it during RAISE/HOLD/VERIFY (grep '/-stat' in cfs.py: no hits). (3) docs/research/meters.md:453 and :461 explicitly mark 'which analysis /meters/15 carries while a PEQ/GEQ page is displayed (console or remote client)' as UNCONFIRMED and prescribe a safe practice (force METER screen, RTA page) that the code does not implement — by REVIEW_BRIEF's own rule, depending on an UNCONFIRMED item without a fallback is a finding. (4) docs/GIG_CHECKLIST.md:231 actually tells the operator to watch the GEQ band in X32-Edit during feedback_watch, so 'someone opens an EQ/GEQ view mid-session' is the prescribed workflow, not a corner case. (5) A confirmed sibling path — another client (X32-Edit's own RTA page) writing /-prefs/rta/source or /-action/setrtasrc mid-session — is equally undetected, which independently justifies a runtime /-stat/rtasource watch.

Why not CONFIRMED/high: (a) The research does not say the real desk re-points the stream; it says nobody knows. The FakeDesk's behaviour (stream follows /-prefs/rta/source regardless of page) is one of the two candidate real behaviours, so this is an untested exposure, not a demonstrated defect like the nine M5/M7 ones. (b) The most likely operator action — opening the ring-out slot's own GEQ page — would, per meters.md:451/461 and the manual quote, analyse 'the bus the GEQ is inserted on', i.e. the SAME bus CFS is watching; only the tap point could differ (pre-GEQ). HANDOVER §4b defect 4 (docs/HANDOVER.md:165-169) already established that tap point does not break verification of a real notch: 'when a notch breaks the loop the ring stops acoustically and the RTA sees it wherever it taps'. _verify_decay (cfs.py:1225-1255) only needs the band to fall decay_verify_db, which acoustic decay delivers at any tap; if the ring genuinely persists after -3 dB, deepening is the correct action. So 'goes blind to its own notches and deepens every band to -9' is wrong for real feedback (it is only true for a sustained test tone or the synthetic ring). (c) The solo hijack, the one re-pointing mechanism the manual CONFIRMS affects the RTA tab, is already mitigated (SOLO_PRIORITY_BIT cleared, meters.py:90, :901-904). (d) The residual real risk is the channel-PEQ-overlay case (engineer selects a channel / X32-Edit EQ view re-points the single analyser to the selected strip): a dead strip makes the detector deaf while ring_out keeps raising 1 dB/1.5 s to the operator-confirmed target; a playback strip could yield a bounded number of false -3..-9 dB cuts via the 25 dB prominence override. That is plausible but unconfirmed, operator-present, bounded by target_gain_db, notch budget and cuts-only GEQ — 'tool silently blind / acting on the wrong signal at a gig' = medium, not a demonstrated wrong-write/safety high.

Cheap offline test/mitigation (agree with the finding's direction): give FakeDesk /-stat/screen/screen + METER/page + a 'PEQ page shows selidx strip' mode, assert set_rta_source/_arm write screen=1,page=4 (meters.md:453 safe practice), and have CFS watch pushed /-stat/rtasource (already delivered via /xremote) and pause RAISE / re-assert / warn when it deviates from stat_expected — that also covers the confirmed 'other client changed the RTA source' path.

## E55. [medium] (unconfirmed-hunter, confirmed) /meters/15 dB values are absolute (independent of the console's manual RTA gain), so fixed dB thresholds fitted on one desk transfer to any desk once auto-gain is off.

**Encoded at:** src/x32mcp/fakedesk.py:159 defaults 'rta/gain': 24.0 with autogain True (the DOC's own example prefs line) yet fakedesk.py:943-946 never applies gain to frames; SyntheticRta has no gain/clip-at-0 stage beyond the clamp; device.yaml:765-766 lists autogain_param/det_param but no gain_param.

**Code depends on it at:** src/x32mcp/meters.py:906-916 switches autogain OFF (making /-prefs/rta/gain the operative manual gain) but never writes gain; detector absolute gates device.yaml:799 min_level_db -45, 812-813 override 25 dB/6 frames, cfs.py:823-877 floor calibration (no cap), RTA hard ceiling 0 dB = clip (meters.py:88, meters.md §4.2).

**Reality:** meters.md §4.2 (l.307): 'UNCONFIRMED: whether the reported dB is affected by /-prefs/rta/gain / autogain ... Best inference: values are the analyser output as displayed, so gain/autogain probably do shift them'; HANDOVER §4b defect 1 confirmed the autogain half on the real desk, which makes the manual-gain half near certain; §5.1: gain is linf 0..60 dB in 6 dB steps and is whatever the operator last left it at.

**On a real desk:** A desk left at RTA gain +42..+60: every band reads tens of dB hot, the -45 gate passes room noise (budget burned on rumble again), and a real howl clips at 0 dB together with its neighbours so prominence collapses below 12/25 dB - the loud, established ring becomes undetectable exactly when ring_out is pushing the master. A desk at gain 0 vs Jim's (unknown) gain shifts every M7-fitted number.

**Offline test:** Make FakeDesk add rta/gain to every /meters/15 band when autogain is off and saturate at 0 dB. Tests: (1) after set_rta_source, /-prefs/rta/gain must read 0 (write it in the recipe; today untouched = 24); (2) with gain 60 a -20 dB ring at 2.5 kHz must still be detected within 300 ms (today, once the fake models gain, prominence is ~0 and nothing is emitted).

> **Verifier 1: CONFIRMED (medium)** — Both halves of the claim check out. Research: docs/research/meters.md l.307 says verbatim "UNCONFIRMED: whether the reported dB is affected by /-prefs/rta/gain / autogain ... Best inference: values are the analyser output as displayed ... so gain/autogain probably *do* shift them — test with a known tone"; l.526 repeats it as still-UNCONFIRMED; §5.1 l.395 confirms /-prefs/rta/gain is linf 0..60 dB in 6 dB steps; l.446 (manual) says with auto-gain disabled "the gain can be manually adjusted". HANDOVER §4b defect 1 (l.154-156) confirms on the real desk that auto-gain DID move every /meters/15 band, which makes the manual-gain half of the same UNCONFIRMED item near-certain. Code: meters.py:906-916 reads/clears /-prefs/rta/autogain and 918-923 forces det=PEAK, but nothing anywhere in src/ writes /-prefs/rta/gain (grep: the only occurrence is the FakeDesk default); device.yaml:765-766 defines autogain_param/det_param and no gain_param. So after set_rta_source the operative analyser gain is whatever the operator last left on encoder 4 (0..60 dB), and every absolute number fitted at M7 (device.yaml:797 min_level_db -45, the SyntheticRta/encoder clamp to 0 dB at meters.py:712/244) silently shifts by that unknown offset. Fake: fakedesk.py:159 seeds 'rta/gain': 24.0 / 'rta/autogain': True (the DOC example line) and fakedesk.py:944-946 returns SyntheticRta frame values untouched — neither gain nor autogain is applied — so no test can observe the dependence. Fallbacks I looked for: (1) prominence and growth are relative, so a constant offset cancels — true, which is why the realistic failures are the absolute min_level gate (desk gain lower than Jim's -> real rings gated out below -45; higher -> noise clears the gate) and 0 dB saturation flattening prominence at very high gain; the saturation/prominence-collapse scenario is physically plausible but depends on the X32 RTA filter skirts, so treat that part as plausible rather than proven. (2) cfs._calibrate_floor (cfs.py:824-877) would adapt the gate upward, but it is invoked at cfs.py:890 inside _open_session, before self._frames.start() at cfs.py:923, so on a real arm it times out after _FLOOR_FIRST_FRAME_S=0.3 s with no frames and returns cfg unchanged — exactly what HANDOVER §4b 'Also outstanding' says (attempted, effectively inert) — and it can only raise the gate, never lower it. No effective fallback exists. Minor citation nits that do not change the verdict: min_level_db is device.yaml:797 (not 799); meters.py:88 is RTA_FLOOR_DB, the 0 dB ceiling lives in the clamp at meters.py:244/712 and meters.md §4.2 ("0x0000 = clipping"). Severity medium is right: the consequence is missed or spurious detections / budget burned (bounded -3..-9 dB GEQ cuts), and the fix is a one-line write of /-prefs/rta/gain to a pinned value in set_rta_source plus a FakeDesk that adds rta/gain to /meters/15 when autogain is off.

> **Verifier 2: CONFIRMED (medium)** — The finding holds up under skeptical review; I could not refute it on either available ground.

(1) Does the real desk do this? docs/research/meters.md §4.2 l.307 marks it UNCONFIRMED but infers "gain/autogain probably do shift them". The autogain half of that same sentence was then confirmed empirically on X32RACK-Jim (HANDOVER §4b defect 1 / commit f43f10c: with autogain ON "every band's reported level drifts together" in /meters/15, 337 false detections). Autogain is automatic control of the same display-gain stage that /-prefs/rta/gain sets manually (X32 manual §7.3 encoder 4, meters.md l.446: "when disabled, the gain can be manually adjusted"), so the stream is demonstrably post-gain-stage; it would be bizarre firmware that applies the auto value but not the manual one. So the FakeDesk (which applies neither gain nor autogain to frames: fakedesk.py:943-946 returns SyntheticRta values verbatim; the prefs at fakedesk.py:159-160 are inert node fields) does NOT match what research+handover say the real desk does. Cannot refute on "fake matches reality".

(2) Does code depend on it without a fallback? Yes. meters.py:906-916 forces autogain OFF — which makes /-prefs/rta/gain (linf 0..60 dB, persisted console pref, whatever the operator last left, meters.md §5.1 l.395) the operative offset on every band — and never writes, reads or reports gain; device.yaml:765-766 has autogain_param/det_param but no gain_param; RtaSourceResult has no gain field; GIG_CHECKLIST never mentions RTA gain. Every absolute number fitted at M7 (min_level_db -45 device.yaml:~799; the -51.7 floor; the "-25 dB howl") is in units of "Jim's desk at Jim's unknown manual gain". Additionally it is unknown (and untested) whether switching autogain OFF over OSC reverts to the stored manual value or freezes the last auto-chosen value — if the latter, the offset depends on the room level at arm time even on Jim's own desk. Per the brief, depending on an UNCONFIRMED item with no fallback is itself a finding; here the fallback is one OSC write.

(3) Would it actually bite at a gig? I ran the real FeedbackDetector with device.yaml's config over synthetic frames with a uniform offset delta and the documented 0 dB clip (script: $SP/reports/verifier-rta-gain/gain_exp.py). Results: growing 2.5 kHz ring (-70 -> -15 true, bg -70): detected at delta -24..+36 (later as delta falls: 2.6 s at -24 vs 1.35 s at 0), NOT detected at delta -36 (never clears the -45 gate) nor at +60 (background saturates near 0, prominence gone). Early-onset ring capped at -40 true over a -85 bg: detected at delta >= 0, missed entirely at delta -12 and -24 (level gate). Established -10 dB howl with music neighbours at -50 true (Jim's 'music playing' test): override fires at delta <= +24, fails at +36/+48/+60 because neighbours clip toward 0 and prominence drops below 25 — i.e. HANDOVER defect 2 ('established feedback unreachable') returns. So within the pref's real 0..60 dB range, an offset of roughly |24-36| dB from Jim's setting flips outcomes: negative -> detector deaf to onset rings while ring_out keeps stepping the master up (operator/PA hears sustained ringing, tool reports nothing); positive -> level gate passes programme/rumble (more wasted 40/80 Hz notches = wrong GEQ writes, bounded at -9 dB) and loud howls become unprovable.

Mitigations considered and rejected: cfs._calibrate_floor (cfs.py:824-877) is relative and would partly absorb a positive offset on the level gate, but (a) it runs in _open_session before _arm starts the frame source, so on the real path it times out after 0.3 s and does nothing (HANDOVER §4b says exactly this, 'backed out unfinished'), (b) it only raises the gate, so it cannot help the negative-offset (deaf) case, and (c) it does nothing about 0 dB saturation collapsing prominence. Prominence/growth/decay-verify are relative and survive a uniform offset except through clipping. No other mitigation exists.

Why medium and not high/low: likelihood is conditional — most desks ship autogain ON with the manual gain at factory default, so many desks will land at the same offset as Jim's; it bites on a house desk where someone has used manual RTA gain (the manual's own suggested use), or if the firmware freezes the auto value at switch-off. When it bites the consequence is in the CFS signal path (deaf detector during ring_out, or budget burned on garbage), it is completely unmitigated and invisible in every report, and the fix is trivial (add gain_param, write a fixed gain in set_rta_source, report it; make FakeDesk add gain and model autogain so a test can fail today). Not low: nothing cosmetic about the detector's only absolute gate floating by up to +/-60 dB. Not high: requires a non-default desk state plus an UNCONFIRMED-but-likely protocol fact.

Minor corrections to the finding text: meters.py:88 is RTA_FLOOR_DB (-128), the 0 dB = clip ceiling comes from meters.md §4.2 and the SyntheticRta clamp, not that line; the floor calibration is relative rather than another absolute gate (but is inert at arm time as explained); the '+42..+60' scenario is illustrative — my runs put the break points at roughly |delta| >= 24-36 dB depending on programme level.

## E56. [medium] (unconfirmed-hunter, confirmed) The RTA's display ballistics (decay time, peak hold) do not affect the /meters/15 data, so a notched ring drops in the stream as fast as it dies acoustically.

**Encoded at:** src/x32mcp/fakedesk.py:160 stores 'rta/decay': 1.0, 'rta/peakhold': 'OFF' but frames ignore both (943-946); SyntheticRta cut model drops a ring by the full cut every frame (meters.py SyntheticRta docstring 'level -= c per frame'; tests/test_meters.py:436-448, tests/integration/test_fakedesk.py:427).

**Code depends on it at:** src/x32mcp/meters.py:868-938 (set_rta_source forces autogain/det, never decay or peakhold); src/x32mcp/cfs.py VERIFY: device.yaml:820-822 decay_verify_db 6 within decay_verify_s 1.5 on 2 consecutive frames, else deepen -3 -> -9 then ABORT with abort_backoff_db 6 (cfs.py module doc l.23-28).

**Reality:** meters.md §5.1: /-prefs/rta/decay logf 0.25..16 ('adjustable decay time', unit UNCONFIRMED, presumably s) and /-prefs/rta/peakhold enum OFF,1..8; §4.2 best inference: the stream is 'the analyser output as displayed'; lead reviewer's note that set_rta_source never sets them. With det=PEAK (which the code forces) decay/peak-hold are precisely the parameters that shape a falling band.

**On a real desk:** Operator's RTA left at decay 16 (s) or peak hold on: the notch kills the ring in the room but the band falls <6 dB in 1.5 s in the data, VERIFY fails, CFS deepens a working -3 dB cut to -6, -9 (audible tonal damage to the wedge/PA), spends the budget, ABORTs and backs the master off 6 dB - reporting failure for a ring-out that had succeeded.

**Offline test:** Give SyntheticRta/FakeDesk display ballistics: per-band fall limited to (128 dB / decay_s) per second and a peak-hold latch when peakhold != OFF, driven by the /-prefs/rta values. Tests: with fakedesk rta/decay = 16 and peakhold = '2', a -3 dB notch that kills a 15 dB/s ring must VERIFY ok (requires set_rta_source to write decay 0.25 and peakhold OFF, and/or VERIFY to scale its window by decay); fails today once the fake honours the prefs.

> **Verifier 1: CONFIRMED (medium)** — Both citations hold and there is no fallback. (1) Research: docs/research/meters.md §5.1 (l.402-403) documents /-prefs/rta/decay as logf 0.25..16 in 19 steps, 'unit not stated (UNCONFIRMED; presumably seconds)', and /-prefs/rta/peakhold enum OFF,1..8; §4.2 (l.307) says whether /meters/15 is raw or display-processed is UNCONFIRMED with 'Best inference: values are the analyser output as displayed'. HANDOVER §4b defect 1 (l.154-156) then empirically settled that inference for auto-gain: a display pref DID reshape the /meters/15 stream on the real desk (337 false detections), and the fix made set_rta_source force autogain OFF and det PEAK — i.e. the code itself already treats -prefs/rta ballistics as stream-shaping, yet leaves the other two ballistics params (decay, peakhold, added in the same later firmware per §5.3 l.446) at whatever the operator left them. (2) Code: set_rta_source (meters.py:860-945) writes source, pos, options bit 5, autogain, det — never decay or peakhold; a repo-wide grep finds no write of /-prefs/rta/decay or /-prefs/rta/peakhold anywhere in src/. cfs._verify_decay (cfs.py:1221-1252) requires the notched band to sit decay_verify_db=6 below level0 on decay_verify_frames=2 consecutive frames within decay_verify_s=1.5 (device.yaml:820-822), with no scaling by the desk's decay setting; on failure _notch_and_verify (cfs.py:1200-1219) deepens by notch_step_db -3 to notch_max_db -9 and, when it cannot deepen, returns False -> ABORT with abort_backoff_db 6 (device.yaml:829; module doc cfs.py:22-28). (3) Fake/tests: fakedesk.py:159-160 stores rta/decay 1.0 and rta/peakhold 'OFF' as inert state; _meter_values (fakedesk.py:944-946) returns SyntheticRta frames that consult neither (nor autogain/det, so the suite cannot distinguish any ballistics setting); SyntheticRta's cut model (meters.py:572-578) drops a ring by the full cut per frame (2.25 dB/frame = 45 dB/s for a -3 cut on a 15 dB/s ring), and tests/test_meters.py:436-449 and tests/integration/test_fakedesk.py:425-427 certify exactly that instantaneous fall. So VERIFY's 6 dB/1.5 s window was tuned against a fake with zero display ballistics. Caveat that keeps this at medium rather than high: the exact semantics of decay (dB range per decay-time) and whether peak-hold latches the streamed bars or only a display overlay are unverified, so the magnitude of the real-desk effect is inferred; but the direction is supported by the autogain precedent, the dependency has no fallback, and the consequence (needless deepening to -9 dB, ABORT, 6 dB master back-off, false failure report for a ring-out that acoustically succeeded) is a wrong-but-bounded, cuts-only write. The proposed offline test (make SyntheticRta/FakeDesk honour rta/decay and rta/peakhold, then require set_rta_source to normalise them or VERIFY to scale its window) is sound and would fail today.

> **Verifier 2: CONFIRMED (medium)** — All factual claims check out. (1) The fake: src/x32mcp/fakedesk.py:159-160 seeds 'rta/decay': 1.0 and 'rta/peakhold': 'OFF' into state, but the /meters/15 path (_meter_values, fakedesk.py:944-946) returns self.rta.last_frame verbatim — no /-prefs/rta display pref (gain, autogain, det, decay, peakhold) touches the frame; only source/pos/inserts feed SyntheticRta via _refresh_cuts (1103-1135). SyntheticRta's cut model (meters.py:572-578) makes a -3 dB cut drop a 15 dB/s ring 2.25 dB per frame = 45 dB/s, asserted by tests/test_meters.py:436-449 and tests/integration/test_fakedesk.py:427; test_cfs.py:407/539 even shrink decay_verify_s to 0.3 s on the strength of that instant fall. (2) The code: set_rta_source (meters.py:860-940) writes source, pos, options bit 5, autogain=0, det=PEAK and nothing else; grep of src/ and device.yaml finds no writer of /-prefs/rta/decay or /peakhold anywhere (they exist only as descriptor params, device.yaml:566-567). CFS VERIFY (cfs.py:1221-1253, device.yaml:820-822) needs the notched band >= 6 dB below level0 on 2 consecutive frames within 1.5 s, else _notch_and_verify (1200-1219) deepens and re-verifies, ABORT + abort_backoff_db 6 (device.yaml:829) when it cannot. GIG_CHECKLIST.md has no operator step to set decay/peak-hold. (3) Reality: meters.md §5.1 documents decay as logf 0.25..16 'adjustable decay time' (unit UNCONFIRMED) and peakhold OFF/1..8; §4.2 marks whether the stream is display-processed as UNCONFIRMED with best inference 'the analyser output as displayed'. The one display pref that WAS tested on hardware — autogain, in the same /-prefs/rta node — turned out to be in the stream and cost the whole notch budget (HANDOVER §4b defect 1); the project's own det=PEAK fix assumes the detector pref shapes the stream too. So the code relies on the favourable reading of an UNCONFIRMED item with no fallback, which the brief defines as a finding, and the fake cannot express the unfavourable reading. Skeptical caveats that keep this at medium rather than high, and slightly soften the stated failure: (a) decay-in-stream is probable but unproven; peak-hold is plausibly a separate overlay trace not carried in the 100 shorts, so that half is weaker; (b) it needs a non-default operator setting — M7 on the real desk passed VERIFY on two genuine rings at whatever decay that desk had, so factory-ish settings evidently work; (c) level0 is sticky (max(det.level_db, current) at cfs.py:1204-1205), so the deepen rounds accumulate ~4.5 s of fall time: under a τ-like 16 s decay a 30 dB-prominent ring passes on the third try at -9 dB (two unnecessary deepens), a 15 dB ring ABORTs; mid settings typically cost one unnecessary -3 dB step rather than a full ABORT; (d) every wrong write is in the safe direction (deeper cut, lower master). Net effect at a gig on a house desk left with long decay: unnecessary -6/-9 dB 1/3-octave notches (audible tonal damage), possible spurious ABORT with master -6 dB, and a ring_out report claiming failure for a ring that was actually killed — 'tool reports wrong state / fails spuriously' = medium. Not mitigated anywhere; fix is two more writes (decay -> 0.25, peakhold -> 0) plus read-back in set_rta_source and restore at disarm, and giving SyntheticRta/FakeDesk pref-driven ballistics so a test can fail today.

## E57. [medium] (unconfirmed-hunter, confirmed) An input channel is an open stage mic feeding the bus iff its own MUTE is off, its send level is >= -40 dB and a preamp sits behind its source - DCA mutes/faders, mute-group semantics, the send tap and the channel fader do not matter.

**Encoded at:** FakeDesk has no acoustic coupling between channels and the SyntheticRta at all (fakedesk.py module doc: 'The bus fader/mute is deliberately not coupled to ring growth'), so every discover_mics/preflight test (tests/integration/test_cfs.py preflight tests) certifies bookkeeping, never audibility.

**Code depends on it at:** src/x32mcp/provision.py:569-590 (include = not strip['muted'] and send>=floor and physical; strip['muted'] is /ch/NN/mix/on only, desk.py:452); send 'type' (PRE/POST/GRP, available from get_sends desk.py:478-479) and the channel fader are ignored for POST sends; /dca/N/on|fader, /config/mute + /-prefs/hardmute|dcamute never read; preflight blocks only on 'no candidate mics' (provision.py:645-647).

**Reality:** fx_routing_scenes.md §5.1 + §13 item 14: hardmute/dcamute semantics UNCONFIRMED ('with DCA groups on, a DCA mute mutes member channels everywhere (including bus sends), otherwise ...'); scales_params.md §4.9: send type POST follows the channel fader, GRP ignores the send level; HANDOVER §4b: 'discover_mics cannot tell a connected mic from an empty channel ... reported 7 candidates when only ch 4 had a microphone'. Muting the vocal DCA during changeover is standard practice.

**On a real desk:** Band DCA muted (or vocal faders down on POST-fed IEM sends) during the ring-out: preflight lists 6 'included' mics, ring_out climbs to the ceiling with no live loop, writes a report 'gain before feedback 0.0 dB, 0 notches', and the engineer unmutes the DCA at downbeat into an un-rung system at a level the tool certified as safe.

**Offline test:** Couple FakeDesk's ring growth to an actual loop gain: ring grows only if some channel with a live preamp reaches the RTA-source bus through mix/on, DCA on+fader (per dcamute), mute groups (per hardmute), send on/level/type and (for POST) the channel fader, and the bus master/mute. Tests: DCA 1 (containing every candidate) off -> preflight must block or warn 'all candidates DCA-muted'; POST send with channel fader -oo -> not included. Today both pass as included and ring_out completes 'DONE'.

> **Verifier 1: CONFIRMED (medium)** — Citations check out and the code has no fallback. (1) Code: src/x32mcp/provision.py:569-591 computes `muted = strip['muted']`, `sending = send_on and send_db >= floor`, `physical = headamp_index_for() is not None`, `include = (not muted) and sending and physical` (line 591; claimant said 569-590, off by one). desk.py:452 derives `muted` solely from `mix/on` (or `on` for DCA strips). For bus targets discover_mics reads only `sends[i]['level_db']` and `['muted']` (provision.py:575-579); the send `type` that get_sends returns (desk.py:502, docstring 476-479) and the channel fader are never consulted, so a POST-tapped send with the channel fader at -oo is 'included' and a GRP-tapped send (level fixed at 0 dB per scales_params.md §4.9) with its level param at -oo is excluded. For Main LR it uses fader_db + mix/st only. grep confirms nothing in provision.py/cfs.py/desk.py reads /dca/N/on, /dca/N/fader, grp/dca, /config/mute, /-prefs/hardmute or /-prefs/dcamute. preflight (provision.py:643-645) blocks only when `included` is empty; cfs.py expected_mics (688-690) only warns about expected mics that are MISSING, never about spurious inclusions; there is no meter-activity cross-check anywhere. (2) Fake/tests: fakedesk.py:36-44 module doc states the closed loop is only 'RTA sees spectrum through the RTA-source strip's GEQ insert' and 'The bus fader/mute is deliberately not coupled to ring growth'; SyntheticRta (meters.py:558-578) grows an injected ring independent of any channel path; tests/integration/test_cfs.py:210-234 test_discover_mics asserts pure bookkeeping (mix/on, send level, source, grp/mute bit) — no test can distinguish 'included' from 'audible'. (3) Research: fx_routing_scenes.md §5.1 and §13 item 14 do mark hardmute/dcamute semantics UNCONFIRMED with exactly the quoted wording; both readings agree a DCA mute removes members from the MAIN mix, so on ring_out_system's Main LR stage a muted vocal DCA yields false 'included' mics without depending on the UNCONFIRMED item; on a monitor bus the error depends on dcamute (ON -> sends muted too) or on POST taps. scales_params.md §4.9 confirms type 4 = post-fader, 5 = GRP 'level follows fader, send level fixed at 0 dB'. HANDOVER §4b line 184 confirms the 7-candidates/1-mic observation. (4) Consequence verified in cfs.py:1168-1170 and 1254-1290: with no detections the loop ends 'target reached', final_stage DONE, master left at ceiling (device.yaml master_ceiling_db 0 / bus_fader_max_db 0) minus safety_margin_db 3, and a gain-before-feedback figure is reported — i.e. the tool raises and leaves a bus/main master near 0 dB on a premise (open mics) it never verified. Caveats that do not refute: whether /config/mute needs reading is moot if X32 mute groups flip ch mix/on (research silent); DCA-fader-down only matters for POST sends/main. The finding is a genuine extension of the known HANDOVER §4b lead (that one is about state the desk cannot reveal; this one is about readable desk state — DCA on/fader, grp/dca, send tap, channel fader — that the code ignores). Medium is appropriate: tool reports wrong state and completes a meaningless ring-out; the resulting master write is operator-requested and policy-clamped, so not 'high'.

> **Verifier 2: PARTIAL (medium)** — Core claim holds, one sub-claim does not, and the headline wedge scenario is conditional on an UNCONFIRMED pref.

CONFIRMED parts. (1) discover_mics' verdict is exactly `include = (not muted) and sending and physical` (provision.py:590-591) where `muted` is only /ch/NN/mix/on (desk.py:452), the bus 'send' is only mix/NN/on+level (provision.py:578-581) and for Main LR only fader+mix/st (575-576). /dca/N/on, /dca/N/fader, /ch/NN/grp/dca and mix/NN/type are never read anywhere in provision.py or cfs.py (grep: zero hits). (2) The fixtures make this invisible: FakeDesk defaults EVERY send to type POST with the channel fader at 0 dB (fakedesk.py:117-120) whereas a real desk ships 1-8 PRE / 9-16 POST (scales_params.md §4.9, real scene1.scn:47/55), DCA on/fader and grp/dca exist in fake state but gate nothing, and ring growth is injected by the test on RAISE>=-18 dB (test_cfs.py:331-333) with 'the bus fader/mute deliberately not coupled' (fakedesk.py:44) - so no test can distinguish an audible mic from a bookkeeping one. (3) The prior-attempt worktree $SP/worktrees/verify-assume-mics-audibility-repro (commit 1b8f44d) holds three repro tests; all three FAIL today: POST send + ch fader -oo -> include=True; ch in DCA1 with /dca/1/on=0, LR ring-out -> include=True, notes=[]; vocal routed to LR only via a GRP send to bus 9 -> discover_mics('main') returns [] (preflight would block 'no candidate mics' spuriously). (4) Consequence path is real in cfs.py: with no acoustic loop the raise loop runs to `reason='target reached'` (1169), backs off safety_margin_db 3 dB (1278) and reports '... no feedback detected; DONE' (1375) leaving the master at ceiling-3 dB - an un-rung system with a DONE report. The research's own real-desk scene has `/dca/1 OFF -8.3` (Vocals) and `/dca/6 ON -oo` (scales_params.md §4.8 excerpt), i.e. real desks do sit with vocal DCAs muted / at -oo, and DCA mute does not flip /ch/NN/mix/on (flashing LED only), so preflight - which blocks on channel mute and bus mute and whose stated job (BRIEF §5) is 'intended mics unmuted and routed' - silently misses the most common changeover mute.

REFUTED / downgraded parts. (a) Mute groups: on a real X32 engaging /config/mute/N drives the members' own mix/on to OFF (that is what 'Hard Mutes' modifies on release), so strip['muted'] already captures group mutes; not reading /config/mute or /-prefs/hardmute is not a real-desk defect. (b) The headline 'band DCA muted during a WEDGE ring-out' only bites when Setup->Mute System 'DCA groups' is on; per fx_routing_scenes.md §5.1/§13 item 14 (UNCONFIRMED, 4 secondary sources) the default is main-mix-only, in which case wedge sends still pass and the ring-out is genuine. The Main LR stage (ring_out('main') / last stage of ring_out_system) is affected unconditionally by DCA mute and DCA fader -oo. (c) POST+fader-down is low for ring-out targets (wedges are PRE; matters only for buses 9-16 left at factory POST); GRP-via-subgroup on Main LR fails safe (spurious blocker) or merely under-lists. (d) Mitigations exist: DESIGN §14 'include is a suggestion the model must confirm with the user', ring_out is Tier-2 confirmed, and HANDOVER §4b already records that the candidate list cannot prove audibility. But unlike the unplugged-mic case, DCA state IS readable over OSC and the tool gives the model nothing to ask about, so the mitigation does not cover it.

Net: a genuine baked-in assumption (fake: all sends POST, faders 0 dB, DCAs inert, loop always present) with a plausible gig failure (DCA-muted vocals -> Main LR or 'DCA groups'-mode wedge ring-out completes DONE with 0 notches and a raised master; engineer unmutes DCA into an un-rung system). Medium, not high: operator-in-the-loop, bounded writes (ceiling), requires ringing out with the DCA down; not low: common practice, desk-readable, and the tool actively certifies DONE. Cheapest fix needs no resolution of the UNCONFIRMED semantics: read /dca/[1-8]/on|fader + /ch/NN/grp/dca and emit a preflight warning/blocker 'ch.N is in DCA k which is muted/-oo' (and for Main LR exclude), use send type (POST->also require ch fader > floor; GRP->ignore send level), and warn when ring_out reaches target with zero detections.

## E58. [low] (cfs-detector-fixtures, confirmed) After a +1 dB step a ring 'declares itself' within the 1.5 s dwell: fixtures inject the ring already 11 dB above the local background (-34 vs a -45.7 base at 2.4 kHz) at 20 dB/s, and the integration tests run dwell_ms=60.

**Encoded at:** tests/integration/test_cfs.py:333 (inject_ring(2400, 20.0, start_db=-34) on the RAISE >= -18), :338 (dwell_ms=60), src/x32mcp/meters.py:598-599,617-618 (base -25@100 Hz .. -55@10 kHz => -45.7 at 2.4 kHz), :633 (default start_db=-45).

**Code depends on it at:** src/x32mcp/cfs.py:663 + device.yaml:826-827 (step 1 dB, dwell 1500 ms), :1168-1197 (next step as soon as the dwell passes with no pending detection), src/x32mcp/detector.py:382 (must first clear min_level_db -45), :100 (3 frames), :341 (growth_min 6 dB/s).

**Reality:** A real ring builds from the band's ambient level (-70..-90 on an idle bus, meters.md §2.2/-128 floor) at excess/tau dB/s: near threshold (0.2-0.5 dB excess) on an 8 m loop that is 8-20 dB/s, so climbing 30-45 dB to the -45 gate takes 1.5-5 s > dwell; below 0.15 dB excess the slope is under growth_min and scores 0. The machine therefore steps again, meeting the ring at 1.2-1.5 dB excess = 48-60 dB/s (the onset-guard edge). LF bands (1/10-oct filters, ~0.3 s response at 40 Hz) are slower still.

**On a real desk:** gain_before_feedback is reported one step (or more) too high, the safety margin is taken from an overshot level, and the ring is met steep and loud instead of nascent. Offline (LoopCoupledRing, tau=25 ms, onset -16.5): feedback physically present at -16 but first detected at -15 with slope 58.5 dB/s at -24 dBFS; test asserts gain_before_feedback <= -16 and FAILS.

**Offline test:** …/test_assumptions_cfs.py::test_ring_out_against_a_loop_whose_growth_follows_the_fader[0.025-FOH 8 m] (FAILS today) with DEFAULT step/dwell. Fix direction: make the dwell adaptive - do not step while any candidate streak is alive/rising (detector.candidates), gate relative to the measured per-band ambient rather than a fixed -45, and treat 'ring appeared within N s of a step' as onset = previous level.

> **Verifier 1: CONFIRMED (medium)** — All code/fixture citations check out and the ring-out RAISE loop has no fallback for a ring that is still building when the dwell expires.

Encoded: tests/integration/test_cfs.py:333 injects the ring by fiat at start_db=-34, 20 dB/s once master >= -18, and :338 runs dwell_ms=60; SyntheticRta base (meters.py:598-599 defaults -25@100 Hz/-55@10 kHz, :617-618 log slope) is -45.70 dB at 2.4 kHz (computed), inject_ring default start_db=-45 (meters.py:633). Every other ring in tests/ is injected at -30..-45 with a fixed 15-20 dB/s and dwell 10-400 ms (test_cfs.py:262,409,541; test_server_tools.py:617; test_meters.py:394-468) — none couples growth to the fader, none uses the default dwell. The stock FakeDesk has no loop model at all (fakedesk.py only recomputes cuts). Worse, the closed-loop test's own assertion `-18.0 <= gain_before_feedback_db <= -7.0` (test_cfs.py:343) tolerates an 11-step-late detection: I re-ran that exact scenario and the ring injected at master -18 is first detected at master -13 (GBF reported -13, 5 steps late) — the assertion encodes 'GBF timing does not matter'.

Depends: cfs.py:663 / device.yaml:826-827 default step 1 dB, dwell 1500 ms; _run_ringout (cfs.py:1147-1197) pops pending, and if none writes the next +step immediately; _dwell (cfs.py:1126-1133) only wakes on an emitted Detection (ses.wake set at :1044) — it never consults ses.det.candidates / ses.candidate, so a live, rising-but-not-yet-confident streak does not hold the fader. first_feedback_master_db is simply ses.master_db at emission (cfs.py:1038-1039) with no back-dating. Detector gates: min_level_db -45 (device.yaml:797, applied detector.py:382), persistence 3 frames (detector.py:100/device.yaml:801), growth_min 6 dB/s (detector.py:341), onset guard 60 dB/s (detector.py:335-338).

Reality: growth rate of a regenerative loop = excess loop gain / loop delay is standard acoustics; 8 m + desk latency ≈ 25 ms gives 40 dB/s per dB of excess, so a crossing step landing 0.2-0.5 dB past onset grows 8-20 dB/s and cannot climb tens of dB to the -45 gate (+12 dB prominence, +3 frames) inside 1.5 s; the next +1 dB step then meets it at 48-60 dB/s, at the onset-guard edge. HANDOVER §4b is consistent: the only real-desk CFS run was a manual-push feedback_watch, the real 8 kHz ring had already plateaued before growth could be scored (defect 2), so the stepping loop's dwell has never met a real loop. Caveats (magnitude, not direction): meters.md §2.2 documents a -100 dB idle pre-fade / -128 floor on a level meter, not RTA band ambients, so '-70..-90' is the claimant's estimate; and the LoopCoupledRing ignores sub-threshold regenerative build-up (band already elevated ~5-10 dB just below onset), which would shorten the climb somewhat. Neither gives the code a mechanism to wait for a nascent ring.

Reproduction: the claimant's worktree test (worktrees/assumptions-cfs-detector-fixtures/tests/integration/test_assumptions_cfs.py:167-186) fails today exactly as stated with DEFAULT step/dwell: FOH 8 m (tau 25 ms, onset -16.5) -> 'feedback first at -15.0 dB', first detection slope 58.4 dB/s at -23.9 dBFS, assert gbf <= -16 fails; wedge 1.5 m -> growth 97.8 dB/s trips the onset guard, caught only by the 25 dB/6-frame override at -10 dBFS, notch at -10 (assert <= -25 fails).

Severity medium is right: the tool reports gain-before-feedback at least one step optimistic and meets the ring steeper/louder than necessary (audible squeal through PA/wedge at soundcheck), but the notch is still written to the correct band within limits; no unsafe write.

> **Verifier 2: PARTIAL (low)** — The modelling gap is real and the physics is right, but the gig consequence is bounded and mostly a report-metric bias, so I keep the finding and downgrade it to low.

What holds up:
- The fake never couples ring growth to the bus master: src/x32mcp/fakedesk.py:43-44 says so explicitly ("The bus fader/mute is deliberately not coupled to ring growth"), SyntheticRta rings grow at a fixed injected rate (meters.py:633-637), and the only ring-out integration test injects the ring by fiat at -34 dB / 20 dB/s the moment the master passes -18 (tests/integration/test_cfs.py:331-333) with dwell_ms=60 (:338). Nothing in tests/ relates ring build-up time to step/dwell. The raise loop (cfs.py:1147-1197) sleeps dwell_ms and steps again unless a *completed* Detection is pending; it never consults ses.det.candidates / ses.candidate (published at cfs.py:1050-1060 but unused by the loop), so there is no adaptive dwell.
- Physics: regenerative growth ≈ excess_dB per loop round-trip = excess/T dB/s (T≈23-25 ms for an 8 m FOH path). A step that lands 0.2-0.5 dB past onset grows 8-20 dB/s; from a realistic per-1/10-octave-band ambient of -75..-90 dBFS (50-60 dBA room through an SM58 at +44 dB; RTA taps the bus pre-fader) it needs 30-45 dB to clear the fixed -45 gate (device.yaml min_level_db, detector.py:381) plus 3 frames (detector.py:100) — 1.5-5 s, i.e. >= the 1500 ms default dwell (cfs.py:663, device.yaml ringout.dwell_ms). So the machine typically takes one more 1 dB step and meets the ring at ~1.2-1.6 dB excess (48-64 dB/s), which also happens to sit on the 60 dB/s onset-guard edge (detector.py growth_max_db_per_s). I reproduced the slice's probe in its worktree: tests/integration/test_assumptions_cfs.py::test_ring_out_against_a_loop_whose_growth_follows_the_fader[0.025-FOH 8 m] fails with gain_before_feedback_db = -15.0 for an onset of -16.5 (first detection: band 70, level -23.9 dBFS, slope 58.4 dB/s, master -15.0).
- ring_out's step/dwell has never run on hardware (HANDOVER §4b's live catch was operator-driven gain), so 1 dB / 1500 ms are unvalidated design numbers.

Why it is not medium:
- gain_before_feedback is report-only: it is set from ses.master_db at detection (cfs.py:1038-1039), rendered at :349-350/:1366-1385, and consumed nowhere else in src/ (grep: the only other reference is the test assertion at test_cfs.py:343, which already tolerates an 11 dB window, -18..-7 — the stock test itself steps ~10 times past the injection before detecting, so the suite never claimed 'declares itself within the dwell'). The bias is ~one step, i.e. the procedure's own advertised 1 dB resolution; 'or more' needs arena-length loops or the separate onset-guard failure.
- The finding's 'safety margin is taken from an overshot level' is wrong about the mechanism: BACKOFF is taken from the final master (target reached / budget spent, cfs.py:1274-1281), never from GBF. A ring that has not declared itself within the last dwell has < ~0.75 dB excess and the 3 dB safety_margin_db absorbs it; a late catch at 1.5 dB excess is still tamed by the first -3 dB cut (net -1.5 dB, VERIFY passes at ~60 dB/s decay), on the correct band, within policy. No wrong write, no boost, no wrong strip, no spurious ABORT attributable to this.
- 'Met steep and loud at -24 dBFS' is partly an artefact of the fake, not physics: SyntheticRta's pink base is -45.7 dB at 2.4 kHz (meters.py:598-599,617-618), so the 12 dB prominence test cannot pass below about -34 there; in a real quiet room prominence is satisfied long before the -45 gate and a 60 dB/s ring is emitted ~3 frames after the gate (about -36 dBFS pre-fader). A sub-second ring at roughly programme level during a soundcheck ring-out — a procedure whose purpose is to provoke rings, with no audience — is what ringing out by hand sounds like too.
- The genuinely nasty variant (second-step excess or a short wedge loop pushing growth past 60 dB/s so growth scores 0 and only the 25 dB/6-frame override fires near full scale — the [0.005-wedge] case notched at -10 dBFS) is the separate onset-guard finding, not this one.

Net: a valid instance of the brief's class (fixture encodes 'ring is born loud and grows at a rate unrelated to the fader'), worth fixing cheaply (hold the step while any candidate streak within band_tolerance is alive and rising; gate relative to the arm-time per-band floor; optionally attribute a ring that appears within N s of a step to the previous level), but on a real desk it costs ~1 dB of optimism in a report line and a somewhat louder catch, not a wrong write or a failed run.
