## E76. [low] (meters-rta, confirmed) Averaging RTA frames arithmetically in dB gives 'the level' of a band — frame-to-frame values are assumed to hover within a few dB of a stable mean (SyntheticRta: ±3 dB noise), never alternating between signal and the −128 floor.

**Encoded at:** src/x32mcp/meters.py:766-792 (average_frames: element-wise mean in the native domain, i.e. mean of dB for type 15); tests/test_meters.py:329-346 averages −40,−41,−42; SyntheticRta never emits −128 (see previous finding).

**Code depends on it at:** src/x32mcp/server.py:1517-1530 (get_rta: `frame = await average_frames(src, n …)`, peaks and db[] reported straight from the dB mean, default 10 frames); webui shows single frames so it is unaffected; cfs._calibrate_floor uses max-of-max (opposite bias).

**Reality:** meters.md §4.2: floor is exactly −128 and 0.0 = clip; with det=PEAK (forced by set_rta_source) speech/music bands drop to the floor between transients. Mean of dB ≠ dB of mean power: a band at −30 dB in half the frames and −128 in the rest averages to −79 dB (power mean −33 dB). Repro test prints −79.0.

**On a real desk:** get_rta tells the LLM/engineer 'peaks: 1 kHz −79 dB' for a talker at −30 dBFS, or ranks a steady −60 dB hum above intermittent −30 dB programme; any reasoning built on get_rta ('is there signal on this bus?', 'which band is hot?') is wrong whenever the source is not stationary.

**Offline test:** Committed (fails today): test_average_of_intermittent_band_is_not_the_floor. Fix: average RTA frames in the power domain (10·log10 mean 10^(dB/10)), or report max/percentile per band alongside the mean, and treat −128 as 'no data'.

> **Verifier 1: CONFIRMED (medium)** — All citations check out. src/x32mcp/meters.py:766-792 average_frames takes an element-wise arithmetic mean of frame.values in the native domain, which for meter_type 15 is dB (docstring l.767-769 says so explicitly); there is no floor/no-data handling and no power-domain conversion. src/x32mcp/server.py:1489-1527 get_rta calls average_frames (l.1517, default frames=10) and reports db[] and the top-5 peaks straight from that dB mean (l.1524-1525) with no max/percentile alongside. tests/test_meters.py:329-346 only exercises tightly clustered values (−40/−41/−42 → −41.0; −40/−41 → −40.5). SyntheticRta (meters.py:558-579, defaults noise_db=3.0, base −25..−55 dB) clamps to RTA_FLOOR_DB but with default parameters never reaches it, and FakeDesk serves SyntheticRta frames for /meters/15 (fakedesk.py:301, 944-945), so no fixture ever presents a −128 band to average_frames. Reality per the cited sources: meters.md §4.2 l.284-286/304 and pitfall l.469 — 0x8000 = −128.0 exactly is the floor/'no signal', 0.0 = clip; HANDOVER.md l.98 — on the real desk 'values were all floor/zero because the desk was silent'; set_rta_source does force det=PEAK (meters.py:919-924, HANDOVER §4a item 1). The claimant's repro test exists and fails today exactly as stated (worktree assumptions-meters-rta, tests/integration/test_assumptions_meters_rta.py:134-144 → 'reports -79.0 dB'). No fallback was missed: cfs does not use average_frames (only server.py:1435 get_meters, which averages linear floats, and get_rta). One mitigation the claimant did not weigh: the console's /-prefs/rta/decay (meters.md §5.1 l.402, 0.25–16, FakeDesk default 1.0) is never written by set_rta_source and, if it shapes the /meters/15 stream the way autogain demonstrably did, bands fall gradually rather than snapping to −128 inside a 500 ms window — so the −30/−128 alternation is a worst case and typical speech error is smaller (several dB to low tens of dB, not 49 dB). But decay's unit and its effect on the stream are both UNCONFIRMED (meters.md l.402, l.526), so the code cannot rely on it, and the Jensen bias (mean of dB ≤ dB of mean power) plus treating the −128 sentinel as a number remain real for any non-stationary source, gated/muted strip, or partially silent measurement. get_rta is read-only (no wrong write, CFS unaffected), so this is 'tool reports wrong state' = medium, at the lower end given the decay smoothing.

> **Verifier 2: PARTIAL (low)** — Mechanically true, consequence overstated. average_frames (src/x32mcp/meters.py:766-792) does take the element-wise mean of dB values for type-15 frames, get_rta (src/x32mcp/server.py:1517-1530) reports db[] and peaks straight from that mean, tests/test_meters.py:329-346 only averages −40/−41/−42, and SyntheticRta (meters.py:558-623, ±3 dB noise, clamped but never resting at −128) never produces floor frames or large frame-to-frame swings — so the stationarity assumption is real and unexercised, and the committed repro (worktree assumptions-meters-rta tests/integration/test_assumptions_meters_rta.py:134-144) does print −79.0. But the headline failure ('talker at −30 dBFS reported as −79', 'steady −60 hum ranked above −30 programme') requires BOTH (a) zero fall ballistics — frames alternating signal/floor every 50 ms — and (b) the inter-transient floor being exactly −128. Neither is supported by the sources of truth: meters.md §5.1 documents /-prefs/rta/decay as a 0.25…16 release setting (unit UNCONFIRMED, and §4.2 leaves UNCONFIRMED whether /meters/15 is pre- or post-display — best inference 'as displayed'), i.e. the analyser has fall ballistics; §4.2 defines 0x8000 = −128 as 'no signal', which an open mic or a bus carrying programme never reaches between syllables (HANDOVER §4b measured a −51.7 dB floor with quiet music; an open SM58 at +44.5 dB has room/preamp noise far above −128); and the test's citation of HANDOVER §4a 'all floor' is a silent desk ('values were all floor/zero because the desk was silent', HANDOVER.md:98), not inter-transient behaviour. Simulating a PEAK detector with linear-dB release over the default 10 frames: stationary sources (music bed, hum, pink noise, a feedback ring — what get_rta is actually used for) bias <1–3 dB; speech with a −80 dB room floor biases ~2.6 dB at 128 dB/s release, ~13 dB at 512 dB/s, and only reaches the claimed −37 dB error with instant fall AND a −128 floor. Misranking a −60 dB hum above −30 dB speech needs the −128 floor case. Impact is also contained: average_frames is consumed only by get_rta and get_meters (server.py:1435, 1517); CFS feeds raw frames to the detector (cfs.py:1034), _calibrate_floor uses max-of-max, the webui shows single frames; get_rta is a Tier-0 'look' tool (GIG_CHECKLIST.md:74, 192) and nothing writes or gates on its numbers. Note the lead's own fix (worktree lead-rta-ballistics 7b0c07d) forces decay to its minimum at set_rta_source, which makes get_rta(target=…) frames maximally transient-following and slightly strengthens the case for power-domain averaging or reporting per-band max alongside the mean — a worthwhile robustness improvement, but an advisory under-read of a few dB on non-stationary sources, not a wrong write, safety issue, or a tool lying about desk state at a gig. Downgraded medium → low.

## E77. [low] (meters-rta, partial) A GEQ band is a brick-wall ±1/6-octave filter: every RTA band maps to exactly one nearest ISO band and receives 100 % of that band's gain (plus master), cuts on adjacent GEQ bands never overlap, and a ring always sits on an ISO centre (every ring in the repo is 2400 Hz → GEQ 2500).

**Encoded at:** src/x32mcp/fakedesk.py:1129-1134 (nearest-GEQ-band, full gain) and src/x32mcp/meters.py:661-667 (set_geq_gain: ±1/6 oct, full depth) + :572-578 docstring ('one −3 dB GEQ step kills any ring slower than 60 dB/s'); rings only ever injected at 2400 Hz: tests/integration/test_cfs.py:262,333,409,541, test_server_tools.py:617, test_meters.py:394-468, webui.py:589.

**Code depends on it at:** src/x32mcp/detector.py NotchController (nearest GEQ band per detection, merge_adjacent_bands 1, notch_step −3, max −9, budget 6) and cfs.py:1200-1254 (deepen until a 6 dB drop) — the step size, max depth, budget and verify thresholds were all validated only against this coupling model.

**Reality:** HANDOVER §4b #4: on the real desk a −15 dB GEQ cut (PRE) read only −5.9/−6.0/−3.9 dB on the three nearest RTA bands (≈40 % of nominal on programme material); a 1/3-octave graphic band is a bell whose gain at ±1/6 octave (a ring midway between ISO centres, e.g. 2.8 kHz) is roughly half its centre gain in dB, and adjacent bands' skirts add. HANDOVER §4b: 'the next band up rang' — real rings hop to neighbouring frequencies.

**On a real desk:** A ring at 2.8–2.9 kHz gets −3 dB at 3.15 kHz ≈ −1.5 dB at the ring: VERIFY fails, deepen, fail, −9 dB (≈ −4.5 at the ring) then 'not tamed' ABORT with back-off, having spent a budget slot and carved 9 dB out of 3.15 kHz; two close rings produce overlapping −9 dB cuts ≈ −12…−15 dB across half an octave of the vocal range. None of this can occur in the emulator.

**Offline test:** Replace the nearest-band map in FakeDesk._refresh_cuts / SyntheticRta.set_geq_gain with a summed bell response per GEQ band (e.g. RBJ peaking biquad magnitude, Q≈4.3) evaluated at each RTA centre; inject rings at 2871 Hz and 5300 Hz; assert ring_out tames them within budget without exceeding −9 dB total at any RTA band (fails/aborts today) — likely needs the planner to split a cut across the two adjacent ISO bands.

> **Verifier 1: PARTIAL (low)** — Citations check out; the consequence does not. (1) ENCODING — confirmed exactly as cited: src/x32mcp/fakedesk.py:1129-1134 maps each RTA band to the single log-nearest of the 31 GEQ centres and applies 100 % of (band gain + master) as the cut; src/x32mcp/meters.py:661-667 set_geq_gain applies full depth to every RTA band within ±1/6 oct; meters.py:572-578 docstring states 'one −3 dB GEQ step kills any ring slower than 60 dB/s'. Every closed-loop ring in the repo is injected at 2400 Hz (tests/integration/test_cfs.py:262,333,409,541; test_server_tools.py:617; test_meters.py:394,438,457,468; webui.py:589; test_detector e2e add_ring(2400)) plus one at 1000 Hz (test_meters.py:416) — 2400 Hz lands on RTA band 69 (2332 Hz), 0.1 oct from ISO 2500, i.e. inside the fake's full-gain window; no test ever rings between ISO centres in closed loop. NotchController defaults (detector.py:109-117: step −3, max −9, budget 6, merge_adjacent 1, decay_verify 6 dB/1.5 s/2 frames) and cfs.py:1200-1250 (_notch_and_verify/_verify_decay) are as described. (2) REALITY — HANDOVER §4b #4 (docs/HANDOVER.md:165-166) does say a −15 dB PRE cut read −5.9/−6.0/−3.9 dB on the RTA, and line 146 says 'the next band up rang'. docs/research says nothing about GEQ filter shape, so the bell-shape claim rests on engineering common sense (reasonable: RBJ 1/3-oct peaking gives exactly G/2 dB at ±1/6 oct). (3) WHERE IT FALLS APART — the claimed failure ('−3 at 3.15k ≈ −1.5 at a 2.8–2.9 kHz ring: VERIFY fails, deepen, fail, −9, not-tamed ABORT') treats VERIFY as needing to see the static filter attenuation. It does not: _verify_decay (cfs.py:1221-1250) waits for the ring LEVEL to fall 6 dB, and a ring is regenerative — ring_out raises the master in 1 dB steps (device.yaml:826, cfs.py:1174) so excess loop gain at first ring is ≲1 dB and even a −1.5…−1.8 dB effective cut drives it below unity and it decays tens of dB/s acoustically. HANDOVER §4b itself records that on the real desk 'a notch killed it' and explains cuts 'audibly worked' because 'when a notch breaks the loop the ring stops acoustically and the RTA sees it wherever it taps'. I also ran the claimant's own proposed model: SyntheticRta ring at 2871 Hz (band 72) growing 20 dB/s, cut by the RBJ-bell value of a −3 dB band at 3150 Hz evaluated at 2871 Hz (−1.83 dB) — the ring decays 0.83 dB/frame (≈16.5 dB/s), 6 dB in ~0.36 s, so VERIFY passes on the FIRST −3 dB step; the synthetic kill threshold merely moves from 60 dB/s to ~36 dB/s. So the proposed offline test ('fails/aborts today') would in all likelihood pass today, and the ABORT cascade is not substantiated. (4) WHAT SURVIVES — a genuine, untested fidelity gap: off-centre rings get roughly half the nominal depth, so notch_max_db −9 is effectively ≈−4.5…−5.4 dB at the ring (only matters for hard/fast rings, e.g. assist mode mid-show, where the emulator always succeeds and the real desk could report 'not tamed' and back off 6 dB), and two adjacent −9 dB cuts (possible once the first is at max, detector.py:557-566) sum acoustically past the per-band −9 policy cap. Neither is demonstrated by handover evidence; the one real-desk data point shows the −3 dB step working. Hence PARTIAL, low severity: assumption and encoding confirmed, cited failure mode and 'fails today' test refuted.

> **Verifier 2: PARTIAL (low)** — The assumption is real but the claimed consequence is not.

CONFIRMED part: the emulator's GEQ->RTA coupling is an idealised brick wall — src/x32mcp/fakedesk.py:1129-1134 maps every RTA band to the single log-nearest ISO band and applies 100 % of that slider (+master); src/x32mcp/meters.py:661-667 (SyntheticRta.set_geq_gain) applies full gain to every RTA band within ±1/6 oct; tests/integration/test_fakedesk.py:424 asserts rta.cuts[band(2400 Hz)] == 6.0 exactly for a -6 dB slider at 2.5 kHz although that RTA band (2379 Hz) is 0.07 oct off-centre; and every end-to-end CFS ring in the repo is injected at 2400 Hz (test_cfs.py:262,333,409,541; test_server_tools.py:617; test_meters.py:394-468; webui.py:589), i.e. always adjacent to an ISO centre. docs/research/fx_routing_scenes.md §2 documents only the 31 ISO centres and the ±15 dB linf range — nothing about the filter bell/Q — so the brick wall is an unverified modelling choice, and HANDOVER §4b(4) (-15 dB PRE cut read -5.9/-6.0/-3.9 on the three nearest RTA bands) shows the real analyser does not see 'full slider value on the 3-4 nearest bands'. NotchController (detector.py:538-565) only ever cuts the one nearest band and has no 'bracket both flanking bands' move.

REFUTED part (the consequence): I built exactly the offline test the finding proposes. Worktree wt/verify-geq-bell replaces _refresh_cuts with a summed RBJ peaking-EQ magnitude per GEQ band (GEQ_MODEL=bell, Q=4.32 = true 1/3-oct constant-Q, the finding's worst case: -3 slider -> -1.5 dB at the ISO midpoint; also Q=2 proportional-Q style) and runs ring_out with rings at 2400, 2871, 3536 (exact ISO midpoint), 5300 Hz. Every case ends DONE, none ABORTs: 2871->band 23 -3 (effective 1.83 dB at the ring), 3536->band 23 -3 (effective 1.50), 5300->band 25 -3 (2.2); only a fast 40 dB/s midpoint ring needed -3 fail/-6 ok and ended at -9, still DONE. With Q=2 all six tame at -3. The whole product integration suite (test_cfs + test_server_tools + test_fakedesk, 83 tests) passes under the bell model; the single failure is the emulator self-test test_fakedesk.py:424 asserting its own brick wall. Reason: CFS never relies on the coupling fraction — VERIFY (cfs.py:1200-1254) watches the ring's own level for a >=6 dB decay and deepens otherwise, and a ring whose loop is broken decays acoustically by far more than the cut wherever it sits (HANDOVER §4b(4) itself notes cuts 'audibly worked' even POST). In ring_out the +1 dB step (cfs.py:441) bounds the excess loop gain at first ring to <=~1 dB, so even 1.5 dB effective from a -3 slider kills it; the finding's '-3 fail, -6 fail, -9 fail, ABORT' sequence requires >4.5 dB excess, which ring_out's own stepping never produces. So 'assert ring_out tames them within budget … (fails/aborts today)' is false: it passes today.

Residual, real but narrow: (a) in feedback_watch, where excess is uncontrolled, a ring within ~0.12-0.167 oct of an ISO midpoint with per-trip excess between ~4.5 and 9 dB exhausts the nearest band to -9 and is not killed while the equally-near flanking band is never tried (experiment: 3150 Hz @ e=5 dB killed at -9; identical ring at 3536 Hz left at cap with band 23 at -9, band 24 untouched; at e=3.5 dB the midpoint ring is killed) — on-centre the same planner gives up only above 9 dB, so the off-centre effect halves the give-up threshold rather than creating a new failure class, and in watch mode the human is on the fader by design; (b) off-centre rings buy roughly half the headroom per budget line and sometimes get -6/-9 on one band where two flanking -3s would be gentler (tonal cost in the 2-4 kHz range, cuts only, bounded); (c) on an interacting (non-TrueEQ) GEQ two adjacent -9 bands combine to about -11…-15 dB between centres, deeper than the per-band notch_max intent — again tonal, never a boost, bounded, and exactly what a human does on an analogue graphic. None of these is a wrong write, a safety issue, CFS acting on garbage, or a tool reporting false state; no spurious ABORT occurs for realistic ring_out excess. The HANDOVER '-5.9/-6.0/-3.9 for -15' numbers are three PEAK-detector readings on non-stationary programme and conflate analyser selectivity/programme variance with filter gain; they show the emulator is idealised, not that coupling is 40 %.

Net: a genuine untested modelling assumption worth fixing in the emulator (make SyntheticRta/FakeDesk use a measured bell, add midpoint-ring cases, consider a bracket-both-neighbours plan when the interpolated ring sits >0.1 oct from the chosen centre), but the product's closed-loop VERIFY->deepen design already mitigates it and the predicted gig failure does not materialise. Severity downgraded medium -> low.

## E78. [low] (meters-rta, partial) On /meters/0 (and /1, /13) an input channel's meter follows its fader and mute (post-fader), and every unmuted strip with its fader up carries programme at ≈ −12 dBFS; an idle strip reads 1e-5 (−100 dB).

**Encoded at:** src/x32mcp/fakedesk.py:930-941 (_strip_level: 0.25 × fader gain × wobble for every strip; SILENCE_LIN 1e-5 when muted/fader down) and tests/integration/test_fakedesk.py:284-286 ('/meters/0 … muted: silence level'), :313-318.

**Code depends on it at:** src/x32mcp/server.py:1420-1456 (get_meters('channels') = /meters/0[0:32] presented as 'signal levels … −90 = silence'); HANDOVER §4b's proposed discover_mics fix ('cross-check candidates against actual meter activity: an unplugged input reads near-silent, a live mic picks up room noise') would be developed against a fake where an unplugged channel reads −12 dBFS and a muted live mic reads silence.

**Reality:** meters.md §3 specifies only *which* strips /meters/0,1,13 carry, not the tap; the only documented taps are /meters/6 [0] 'post gain/trim (pre-fade)' and [3] 'post-fade' (§3, §2.2), and the §2.2 capture shows an idle input at −100.35 dB pre-fade and a muted post-fade path at exactly −128.00 (not −100). Whether the METERS-page channel meters are pre- or post-fader is UNCONFIRMED by the research (console channel meters are conventionally pre-fader).

**On a real desk:** get_meters('channels') on a real desk most likely shows a hot mic on a channel whose fader is down (LLM: 'ch 5 is loud, pull it down' — it already is) or, if post-fader, cannot be used to find connected mics; either way the fake certifies one answer the research does not give, and mic-presence logic tuned on it (every open channel 'has signal') inverts on hardware.

**Offline test:** Give FakeDesk strips an explicit `input_dbfs` (default −100 = nothing plugged; set per test) and make /meters/0,/1,/13 and /meters/6[0] pre-fader from it, /meters/6[3] and bus/main meters post-fader with a −128 floor when muted; flip test_fakedesk.py:284-286 accordingly and add a discover_mics meter cross-check test (unplugged channel must not be a mic). Confirm the tap on the desk once (fader down, talk, read /meters/0).

> **Verifier 1: PARTIAL (low)** — Citations check out. fakedesk.py:930-941 `_strip_level` returns SILENCE_LIN (1e-5) when `mix/on`==0 or fader<=0 and otherwise 0.25 x fader-gain x wobble (~-12 dBFS at 0 dB) for every strip, with no notion of whether anything is plugged in; :956-961 feed /meters/0, /13 and /meters/1[0:32] from that post-fader path; only /meters/6[0] uses pre_fade=True. tests/integration/test_fakedesk.py:284-286 positively asserts that muting ch 2 drops /meters/0[1] below 1e-4, citing 'meters.md §6.3' — but §6.3 only says silence is not 0.0; it says nothing about /meters/0 following the mute. :313-318 assert v[0]>0.1 on /meters/1 and /meters/2 (programme on every open strip) and the /meters/6 pre/post split (the latter IS documented). meters.md §3 (lines 241-256) indeed gives only the strip order for /meters/0,/1,/13 ('32 input channels …') with no tap; the only documented taps are /meters/6 [0] 'post gain/trim (pre-fade)' and [3] 'post-fade'; §2.2 (lines 193-198) shows idle pre-fade = 9.6e-6 (-100.35 dB) and muted post-fade = exactly -128.00 dB, so the fake's 1e-5 for a muted post-fade path also disagrees with the one real capture (cosmetic: lin_to_db floors both at -90). HANDOVER §4b (line ~185) verbatim proposes the meter-activity cross-check for discover_mics, and §4a additionally records that on the real, silent desk '/meters/1 … values were all floor/zero' — direct evidence against the fake's 'every unmuted fader-up strip reads -12 dBFS' model. X32 channel meters (surface, X32-Edit, METERS/channel page) are in practice pre-fader input meters, so the fake's post-fader/post-mute choice for /meters/0,/1,/13 is very likely the wrong one, and the test certifies it.

Where the finding overreaches: current product dependence is thin. The only consumer of /meters/0 channel words is get_meters (server.py:1418-1457), which relays averaged dBFS with no pre/post-fader claim and no logic keyed to the tap; its '-90 = silence' is just the lin_to_db floor (meters.py:125-130) and is correct for a real idle input (-100 -> -90). provision.discover_mics does not read meters today, so the 'inverted mic-presence logic' is a prospective trap for the planned §4b fix, not a shipped defect; the 'LLM says pull ch 5 down' scenario is an interpretation risk from an ambiguous docstring, not a tool reporting wrong state. No wrong write, no CFS decision, no spurious failure results on hardware today. Hence PARTIAL: the encoded assumption and the unsupported test assertion are real and of the requested class (and worth fixing in the fake before the discover_mics cross-check is written: per-strip input level defaulting to 'nothing plugged' ~-100 dB, /meters/0,/1,/13 and /6[0] pre-fader from it, /6[3] and bus/main post-fader with a -128 floor, flip test_fakedesk.py:284-286, document the tap in get_meters' docstring, confirm once on the desk), but severity is low rather than medium.

> **Verifier 2: PARTIAL (low)** — The fake behaviour is as described and very probably contradicts hardware, but no shipped code's correctness depends on it, so the gig consequence is interpretational, not a lying tool or a wrong write.

What is true: FakeDesk._strip_level (src/x32mcp/fakedesk.py:930-941) makes every /meters/0, /1[0-31], /13 strip post-fader AND post-mute (SILENCE_LIN when /mix/on=0 or fader<=0, else 0.25*fader-gain), and gives every open strip synthetic programme at ~-12 dBFS; tests/integration/test_fakedesk.py:284-286 ('muted: silence level') and :298/313-314 certify exactly that. docs/research/meters.md §3 gives only the strip order for ids 0/1/13, never the tap, so this is an undocumented belief the fake invented. The best real-hardware evidence the research itself cites points the other way: Maillot's X32Automix.c (a real client on a real console, cited in meters.md §1.1/§4.1) reads /meters/1 [0-31] 'to validate if data is incoming on a given channel' and raises a channel's fader from its pre-recorded LOW ('no sound') position when that meter crosses X32sensitivity (RunAutomix lines ~626-640) — that algorithm can only work if the channel meter is pre-fader. Console channel meters are conventionally post-preamp/pre-fader and unaffected by mute. So on a real X32 a muted or fader-down live mic will still read hot on get_meters('channels'), and an unplugged open channel reads ~-100 dB, the inverse of the fake on both counts.

Why it is not medium: the only product consumer of these meters is get_meters (src/x32mcp/server.py:1418-1457), a pure relay that floors at -90 dB (meters.py:162) and whose docstring/README/DESIGN say 'signal levels', claiming neither tap; its test (tests/integration/test_server_tools.py:550-559) asserts shape only. CFS (cfs.py:508) and the dashboard use /meters/15 only; discover_mics (provision.py:551) consults no meters at all — the HANDOVER §4b meter cross-check is a proposal, not code, so 'code_depends_at' for it is hypothetical. The -100 vs -128 floor difference is invisible behind the -90 display floor. Real-desk consequence today: an LLM may misread a pre-fader hot channel as contributing to the mix ('pull ch 5 down' when it is already down) — recoverable by reading the fader, no wrong write, no safety path. Worth fixing before the discover_mics meter cross-check is written (give FakeDesk strips an input level independent of fader/mute, make ch meters pre-fader, and document the tap in get_meters' docstring after one fader-down/talk check on the desk), but as it stands it is a latent fake-fidelity gap, severity low.

**Code depends on it at:** src/x32mcp/meters.py:442-447 (LiveMeters always appends time_factor as the last int, so a /meters/5 or /meters/6 subscription without extra_args puts tf where the desk reads chn_meter_id/channel_id). Caveats found while trying to refute: (a) meters.md §1.1's form table itself labels that same hex as '`,si /meters/N <tf>` subscribe with time factor', so the research doc is internally inconsistent on this one row — but §2.2, §3 and transport.md §8 (and the X32.c byte offsets) outnumber it and are the more specific statements; (b) LiveMeters does support the correct form via extra_args (test_live_extra_args_forms sends ,sii /meters/6 16 1) and the docstring at meters.py:373-374 documents it; (c) production never subscribes ids 5/6 (server.py:1432 via METER_GROUPS uses ids 0 and 2; server.py:1512 and cfs.py:508 use 15), so no shipped tool currently lies. Consequently every FakeDesk-backed assertion sees verified=True (tests/integration/test_fakedesk.py:391-397, test_cfs.py:252, test_server_tools.py:562/607) and the only unverified test (test_meters.py:683-691, mirror=False) models a permanently stale desk, never a late one — the retry/settle path with a real delay is never exercised. meters.py:926-937 does verify_attempts=2 with a 0.1 s sleep and a self-admitted unsourced comment 'the desk applies prefs asynchronously'; a mismatch is log.warning + verified=False, surfaced only as a reported field (cfs.py:207, 929; server.py:1511, 1645 'RTA NOT verified') — nothing refuses or retries further. REVIEW_BRIEF §5 and HANDOVER §4b do document stale read-after-write on the real desk (label, insert/on -> GEQ_VALIDATION_FAILED), meters.md line 427/481 (§6 item 15) does carry the '/-stat/rtasource may not reflect the METERS/RTA screen' warning (though that is about console reset, not async application), and GIG_CHECKLIST.md:228 does pre-emptively ask the operator to record stat_actual if verified is false.

Why PARTIAL rather than CONFIRMED: (1) the code is not fallback-free — besides the 2-attempt/100 ms retry, three intervening round-trips (options, autogain, det reads at meters.py:900-923) elapse between the pos write and the first /-stat read, and the outcome is non-fatal and honestly reported; (2) there is no real-desk observation that /-stat/rtasource lags by more than that bound — M7 (HANDOVER §4b) ran set_rta_source on Main LR live and no spurious 'NOT verified' was recorded among the defects, and ringout_reports/ is empty, so the claimed gig failure (operator habituates to a false flag) is plausible-by-analogy but undemonstrated; (3) the finding is a further site of the already-known read-after-write class rather than a new class. The untested-bound observation and the proposed offline test (a FakeDesk prefs_apply_delay_ms that defers the /-stat mirror and its push, asserting set_rta_source still verifies by waiting for the pushed update / polling ~1 s) are valid and worth doing when §5's general write-barrier fix lands. Severity low as claimed: reporting-only, no wrong write, CFS does not act on the flag.

> **Verifier 2: PARTIAL (low)** — The encoded assumption is real but the finding overstates it and the gig consequence is cosmetic.

What is true: FakeDesk mirrors /-stat/rtasource inside the same datagram handler (src/x32mcp/fakedesk.py:1082-1101, pushed immediately) and the unit-test FakeDeskConn mirrors inside set() (tests/test_meters.py:654-661), so every FakeDesk/CFS test sees verified=True trivially (test_fakedesk.py:391-397, test_cfs.py:252). No fixture can defer the mirror, so the retry branch of set_rta_source (meters.py:928-934, attempt 2 succeeding after the 0.1 s sleep) is never exercised; only the permanently-stale (mirror=False) and deaf cases are (test_meters.py:688-699). I probed the tolerance with a delayed-mirror conn: set_rta_source verifies for an apply delay of 0/50/100 ms and reports verified=False, stat_actual=<old value> from ~120 ms upward (scratchpad reports/verifier-rta-stat/delay_probe.py). docs/research/meters.md gives no bound on how fast the desk resolves prefs into /-stat/rtasource (§5.2/§5.3 only say 'read /-stat/rtasource back to confirm'; §6.15 is about staleness after a console reset, a different situation), and HANDOVER §4b / REVIEW_BRIEF §5 confirm zero-settle read-after-write is racy on the real desk (label, insert/on). So the 110 ms budget is an unmeasured guess.

Why it is not more than low, and why 'assumed synchronous' is overstated: (1) the code does NOT assume synchrony — the first /-stat read already comes after three GET round-trips (options, autogain, det) plus up to three SETs, and there is an explicit 100 ms settle-and-retry with the comment 'the desk applies prefs asynchronously'; the observed real-desk races were immediate read-backs with no settle at all, and nothing in research/handover says the settle exceeds ~100 ms. (2) verified gates nothing: cfs.py:911-929 only publishes rta_verified, _rta_dict (cfs.py:203-207) and server.py:1511/1645 only report it ('RTA NOT verified'); no write, no preflight decision, no detector behaviour depends on it. A false negative is a log.warning plus a misleading status string — nobody hears anything different and no wrong parameter is written. (3) No real-desk evidence it actually misfires: CFS was armed live several times at M7 on FW 4.13 (HANDOVER §4b lists its defects in detail, including the analogous setup_ringout_eqs GEQ_VALIDATION_FAILED race) and an unverified RTA is not among them; GIG_CHECKLIST.md:228 'if not, record stat_actual' is generic diligence, not an observed failure. (4) The 'operator learns to ignore the only flag that would reveal a genuinely wrong source' argument is a second-order human-factors concern; the first-order gap (an unverified/wrong RTA source does not block arming, so a dropped UDP prefs write would let the detector notch Bus N from another strip's spectrum) is a separate design question about gating, not about the FakeDesk's mirror timing.

Net: a genuine untested-timing assumption with an unmeasured 110 ms bound, worth a FakeDesk prefs_apply_delay knob and either waiting for the pushed /-stat/rtasource update or polling up to ~1 s — but on a real desk the worst outcome is a spurious 'NOT verified' line. PARTIAL, low.

## E81. [low] (meters-rta, confirmed) get_rta(target) may rewrite the console's RTA preferences (autogain OFF, detector PEAK, Solo-Priority cleared, source, pos) and leave them that way; nobody is looking at the console's own RTA.

**Encoded at:** No test restores or even reads back the prefs after get_rta/feedback_watch; FakeDesk has no notion of an operator-visible RTA screen (fakedesk.py:159-160 are plain state).

**Code depends on it at:** src/x32mcp/server.py:1508-1511 (_RtaPrefsWriter → set_rta_source on a Tier-0-looking read tool) and meters.py:900-924; cfs._disarm does not restore /-prefs/rta/* either.

**Reality:** meters.md §5.3 (X32 manual): Auto Gain is 'recommended for most situations to ensure meaningful readings'; these are the engineer's global analyser settings shared by the RTA tab and both EQ overlays, not per-client state.

**On a real desk:** After one get_rta('ch.5') the FOH engineer's RTA overlay goes dark/unscaled (autogain off, manual gain wherever it was) and stops following solo; they 'fix' it on the console mid-show — which is precisely the retargeting that finding #3 cannot detect.

**Offline test:** Snapshot /-prefs/rta before set_rta_source and assert get_rta (no CFS session) restores it on completion and cfs.stop() restores it on disarm; FakeDesk already supports the reads.

> **Verifier 1: CONFIRMED (low)** — Every citation checks out and there is no fallback the claimant missed — in fact the one plausible fallback (the advertised snapshot undo) explicitly excludes /-prefs, which strengthens the finding.

(1) Code path: server.py:1508-1511 — get_rta(target) with no CFS session resolves the target and calls set_rta_source(_RtaPrefsWriter(a,t), ...). meters.py:888-889 writes /-prefs/rta/source and /-prefs/rta/pos; 900-904 clears Solo-Priority bit 5 of /-prefs/rta/options; 911-916 forces /-prefs/rta/autogain=0; 919-924 forces /-prefs/rta/det=1 (PEAK). Nothing records the prior values and nothing writes them back: grep for autogain / '/-prefs/rta' across src/ hits only meters.py (the writes), fakedesk.py, nodes.py docstrings, server.py:1463 docstring and cfs.py:916 (a cache invalidate). cfs._arm (cfs.py:911) does the same writes via the raw conn; cfs._disarm (cfs.py:931-949) only unsubscribes frames and cancels the consumer; _finish/_unwind never touch prefs.

(2) The 'fallback' angle: get_rta's docstring (server.py:1492-1493) says the writes are 'Tier 1, snapshotted ... like any mix move', implying restore_snapshot is the undo. But nodes.py:111 _RESTORE_EXCLUDED_FAMILIES = {show, stat, prefs, action} and restore_plan (nodes.py:1204,1212) 'never restores' -prefs sections. So even the operator/agent running restore_snapshot('latest') leaves autogain OFF, det PEAK, Solo Priority cleared and the source repointed. The docstring also under-discloses: it names source/pre-post/solo-priority but not autogain or detector.

(3) Research: docs/research/meters.md §5.3 (line 432 header; line 446) quotes the X32 manual verbatim: Auto Gain is 'recommended for most situations to ensure meaningful readings', and the same section (bit-5 row) says Solo Priority 'affects both the GEQ RTA view and the dedicated RTA tab view' — i.e. these are the console's single global RTA-settings screen, shared by the RTA tab and both EQ overlays, not per-client state. HANDOVER §4a item 1 (HANDOVER.md:154-156) confirms the design choice to force autogain off for the detector but says nothing about putting it back.

(4) Tests/fake: fakedesk.py:159-160 hold rta/autogain True, rta/det RMS etc. as plain state with no model of an operator-visible screen; tests/integration/test_server_tools.py:520-534 (test_get_rta_target_writes_the_prefs_through_the_policy) asserts only that the writes went through the policy path — no test reads /-prefs/rta back after get_rta or after cfs stop, and tests/integration/test_cfs.py has zero references to autogain/det/prefs/rta.

Severity low is right: no audio-path write, no safety issue, CFS does not act on garbage; it is a persistent, partly undisclosed, un-undoable change to the FOH engineer's global analyser settings (auto-scaling off, RMS->PEAK, solo no longer hijacks the RTA, source moved) that they will notice and 'fix' on the console — which is exactly the retarget the tool cannot detect. 'Goes dark' is slightly overstated (manual gain still applies), but 'stops auto-scaling and stops following solo' is accurate.

> **Verifier 2: PARTIAL (low)** — The behaviour described is real but it is a documented, tested, policy-routed design decision rather than a hidden belief the emulator papered over, and its gig consequence is operator annoyance, not a wrong audio write or a lying tool.

Confirmed facts: get_rta(target) outside a CFS session calls set_rta_source through _RtaPrefsWriter (server.py:1508-1511, 1459-1484), which writes /-prefs/rta/source, /pos, clears options bit 5, forces /autogain=0 and /det=1 (meters.py:889-916) and nothing ever writes them back; Cfs._disarm (cfs.py:931-948) only stops frames/consumer. FakeDesk defaults autogain ON / det RMS (fakedesk.py:159-160) exactly like a factory desk, so the fake is faithful here — writes persist as global console prefs on both. The get_rta docstring (server.py:1490-1495) is stale after the M7 fix: it names 'source, pre/post, solo priority' but not auto-gain/detector, and rta_info (server.py:1511) drops autogain_cleared/detector_set_peak, so neither the model nor the operator is told the analyser gain mode changed.

Why it is not more than low / why PARTIAL rather than CONFIRMED: (1) the write is deliberate and disclosed — the tool docstring says passing target 'WRITES the console's RTA prefs … Tier 1, snapshotted and rate-limited like any mix move', device.yaml:557-566 classifies every rta/* pref Tier 1, and tests/integration/test_server_tools.py:520-534 asserts the writes go through the policy with a pre-write snapshot; (2) it is already undoable — /-prefs/rta is in the snapshot sweep (device.yaml:704), ensure_pre_write_snapshot runs before the first pref write (server.py:1478, cfs.py:906), so diff_snapshot shows 'Prefs RTA source MAIN -> BUS03' etc. (tests/test_nodes.py:751) and restore_snapshot writes the /-prefs/rta line back; every write also publishes desk.write to the event log/dashboard; (3) no audio path is touched and no tool reports wrong state — the harm is that the engineer's shared analyser settings (meters.md §5.3: one RTA settings screen, autogain 'recommended for most situations') silently change: fixed source instead of selected/monitor, solo-follow off, auto-gain off with whatever manual gain was last set. 'Goes dark' is overstated — manual gain still applies and bars remain, just unnormalised; (4) auto-restoring autogain on completion is a reasonable nicety but restoring it mid-show is exactly what would poison a subsequent feedback_watch if set_rta_source did not re-force it (it does, every arm), so the current 'leave it off' is defensible for this tool's purpose. The residual, genuinely un-mitigated part is the undisclosed autogain/det change in the docstring/result and the absence of a restore on cfs.stop()/get_rta completion — cosmetic/operator-workflow, hence low.

## E82. [low] (routing-fx-provision, confirmed) GEQ band gains are independent: a -9 dB slider is a -9 dB acoustic cut, so policy's notch_max_db bounds what the audience loses, and cutting the nearest 1/3-octave band removes exactly that much at the ring frequency.

**Encoded at:** src/x32mcp/fakedesk.py:1129-1134 (_refresh_cuts: each RTA band attenuated by exactly the NEAREST GEQ band's slider value — brick-wall 1/3-octave, no skirts, no neighbour interaction); src/x32mcp/meters.py:661-667 set_geq_gain same model; tests/integration/test_cfs.py:270-275 (-3 dB slider => ring level drops >3 dB within 0.4 s).

**Code depends on it at:** src/x32mcp/provision.py:437/490-493 (always loads GEQ2, the classic graphic, never TEQ2), detector.py:545-569 + policy.py:405-422 (max -9 dB per band, merge_adjacent_bands=1 lets adjacent bands each reach -9), device.yaml geq.fx_types_dual [GEQ2, TEQ2].

**Reality:** fx_routing_scenes.md §1.2/§2.1: the desk offers GEQ2/GEQ ('Dual/Stereo Graphic EQ') and TEQ2/TEQ ('True' graphic EQ). A classic constant-Q graphic's bell filters overlap: three adjacent -9 dB sliders sum to roughly -14..-16 dB at the middle band and a single band's -9 dB reaches only ~-4 dB a 1/3-octave away; 'TrueEQ' exists precisely to make the response equal the sliders. A ring sitting between two ISO centres (RTA 1/10-oct band vs GEQ 1/3-oct, band_for_freq nearest-centre) gets ~half the slider depth.

**On a real desk:** With GEQ2, CFS²'s '-9 dB max, cuts only' promise understates the hole it can dig (adjacent merged notches -> ~-15 dB, clearly audible tonal damage on a vocal wedge), while an off-centre ring receives less cut than logged, fails VERIFY and gets deepened/neighbour-notched — spending budget and carving wider than the report shows. Loading TEQ2 instead would make the written numbers true.

**Offline test:** Replace the fake's nearest-band brick wall with summed RBJ peaking biquads (Q≈4.3 per 1/3-oct band) evaluated at each RTA centre; tests: (a) three adjacent -9 dB bands must not attenuate any RTA band beyond policy.notch_max_db - tolerance unless type is TEQ2 (fails -> motivates TEQ2 or an aggregate-depth guard); (b) a ring injected at 2240 Hz (between 2k and 2k5) must still verify after one step or the controller must split the cut.

> **Verifier 1: CONFIRMED (low)** — All code citations check out. fakedesk.py:1129-1134 (_refresh_cuts) attenuates each 1/10-oct RTA band by exactly the NEAREST 1/3-oct GEQ slider value (+master) — a brick-wall, no skirts, no neighbour summation; meters.py:661-667 set_geq_gain is the same idealisation (±1/6 oct, full slider depth); and the SyntheticRta ring model (meters.py:716-717) then subtracts that full cut from the ring every frame, which is what test_cfs.py:270-275 certifies (−3 dB slider ⇒ ring falls >3 dB in 0.4 s). provision.py:437 always loads fx_types_dual[0] = GEQ2 (device.yaml:770 lists [GEQ2, TEQ2]; TEQ2 is only reused if already present, never chosen); detector.py:545-569 + policy.py:405-422 bound the SLIDER at −9 dB per band and, with merge_adjacent_bands=1, a detection one band away from a maxed notch opens a new notch at the neighbour, so adjacent bands can each sit at −9. Research fx_routing_scenes.md §1.2/§2.1 confirms only what the claimant attributes to it: GEQ2 = 'Dual Graphic EQ', TEQ2 = 'Dual TrueEQ' / 'true dual graphic eq' both exist (and §1.3 shows TEQ2=2 is loadable in insert slots 5-8). The band-interaction physics is not in the research docs but is standard live-sound knowledge (TrueEQ's stated purpose is to make response match sliders), which the brief accepts as a source; moreover HANDOVER §4a item 4 (uncited by the claimant) gives direct real-desk evidence that slider ≠ RTA cut: a −15 dB GEQ cut PRE moved the RTA bands only −5.9/−6.0/−3.9 dB, where the fake would show exactly −15. Mitigations exist and cap the severity: the controller is closed-loop — VERIFY (cfs.py:1200-1250) measures the actual RTA drop, deepens, and at −9 aborts with back-off/restore (cfs.py:1160-1163, tested open-loop in test_cfs.py:403-420) — so the under-cut direction costs budget/aborts early rather than producing a wrong or unsafe write; the over-cut direction (adjacent −9 sliders summing deeper than −9 acoustically on GEQ2) is bounded, cuts-only, and a tonal-quality issue; README:238's '−9 dB maximum per band' is literally honoured as a slider limit. The claimant acknowledged the VERIFY/deepen path and rated it low, which is the right level. Quantitative figures (−14..−16 dB, ~−4 dB a third-octave away) are estimates, directionally correct.

> **Verifier 2: PARTIAL (low)** — The modelling gap is real but the claimed code dependence and gig consequence are overstated.

TRUE PART: fakedesk.py:1129-1134 (_refresh_cuts) and meters.py:661-667 (set_geq_gain) model a GEQ band as a brick-wall 1/3-octave cut applied in full to the nearest RTA bands, with no skirts and no neighbour summation. A real GEQ2 ("Dual Graphic EQ") has overlapping bells; TEQ2 ("TrueEQ", fx_routing_scenes.md §1.2/§2.1 list both) exists precisely to make response == sliders. My own RBJ check (BW 1/3 oct): three adjacent -9 dB sliders give about -13 dB at the middle centre (-16 dB at BW 0.5 oct); a single -3 dB slider gives -1.6 dB at a ring 1/6-octave off-centre. provision.py:437 always loads fx_types_dual[0] = GEQ2 (device.yaml:770) when it has to load a type. So the fake is optimistic about how precisely a slider maps to attenuation at the ring, and nothing in docs/research verifies a response shape either way (cannot REFUTE on research grounds).

WHY IT DOES NOT BITE: (1) No product code computes or relies on slider-depth == acoustic-depth. The controller is closed-loop: cfs.py:1200-1219 (_notch_and_verify) writes -3, then _verify_decay (cfs.py:1221-1253) requires the measured ring band (±band_tolerance) to fall >= decay_verify_db (6) on 2 consecutive frames within 1.5 s, else deepens, else aborts 'not tamed'. Less-than-slider attenuation at an off-centre ring simply produces another deepen step or, in ring_out, the ring returning 1-2 dB of master later — exactly how a human rings out with a graphic. HANDOVER §4b records this working on the real desk with a GEQ2 in slot 5: 'the ring started, a notch killed it; ... the next band up rang, and that was caught too'. Feedback onset has only fractions of a dB of excess loop gain per trip, so even -1.6 dB effective kills a nascent ring. (2) The -9 dB limit is specified as a per-slider limit (BRIEF.md:76 '−3 dB per action, deepening to −9 dB max; adjacent-bin detections merge'; policy.py:405-422 validates band gain), and the report/logs print slider values that are exactly what X32-Edit shows — the tool does not report a wrong state. Any engineer using the stock GEQ knows adjacent sliders sum; with GEQ2 the loop actually reaches the needed acoustic cut with shallower-looking sliders than TEQ2 would, and it only deepens while the ring persists, so the 'digs a deeper hole than promised' scenario requires nine failed-to-tame detections inside 2/3 octave. (3) The finding's 'fails VERIFY and gets deepened — spending budget' is wrong on budget: detector.py:548-549/601-602 count distinct touched bands; deepening is free, and merge_adjacent_bands=1 (detector.py:557-565) deepens the existing neighbour before opening a new band. (4) The proposed offline test (b) would not fail today even with summed biquads: ring at 2240 Hz, growth 20 dB/s = 1 dB/frame vs an effective 1.6-2.7 dB/frame cut in the SyntheticRta loop model (meters.py:714-718) still decays 12-34 dB/s and verifies in <0.5 s. Test (a) asserts an acoustic <= -9 dB requirement the product never states.

NET: a fidelity limitation of the emulator plus a defensible-but-undocumented product choice (GEQ2 rather than TEQ2 as load_type). Worth a one-line note or making TEQ2 the preferred load type so written numbers equal response, but no write is wrong, no safety property is violated, and no tool reports false state. Low severity, enhancement-class.

## E83. [low] (routing-fx-provision, partial) Two strips can hold the same insert point simultaneously and the desk will report it that way; an insert, once validated at preflight, stays in circuit for the whole session.

**Encoded at:** src/x32mcp/fakedesk.py:1052-1066/_store (insert/sel is a plain per-strip enum: bus 1 and bus 2 may both read FX5L; no /-insert/* ownership table, no eviction) — the validator branch provision.py:405-412 ('FX5L is also inserted on …') is only reachable on the fake; no test flips insert/on or sel during a WATCH/RINGOUT session.

**Code depends on it at:** src/x32mcp/provision.py:405-412 (duplicate-sel reasoning), :444-451 (`used` map trusts simultaneous duplicates), cfs.py:884-897 (fx_slot/side/sel captured once at _open_session; _DeskGeqWriter keeps writing that slot; no subscription to <bus>/insert/* pushes, no re-validation before each notch).

**Reality:** fx_routing_scenes.md §3.4 + §13 item 5: the console enforces one owner per insert point ('there will be a warning when you try to insert an effect slot that has already been used'); over OSC the outcome is UNCONFIRMED, best inference last-write-wins with the previous owner's sel reset to OFF, observable via `/-insert/fx[1-8]L|R` (DOC p.43) — which the descriptor does not declare. transport.md §4: the desk pushes such changes to /xremote clients, and Desk._on_push merely invalidates cache.

**On a real desk:** The state the validator describes never occurs; the real symptom — our bus's sel silently flipped to OFF because X32-Edit/another plan took FX5L, or the engineer bypassing the insert to A/B it mid-ring-out — is not noticed: CFS² keeps notching a GEQ that is no longer in the wedge path, VERIFY fails, it escalates to -9 dB and aborts with a misleading 'not tamed', leaving cuts that bite when the insert is re-enabled.

**Offline test:** FakeDesk: enforce single ownership (a second strip selecting FXnS resets the first to OFF and pushes both) and serve /-insert/*; tests: (a) apply_setup for bus 2 onto a point bus 1 owns must surface bus 1's eviction; (b) during feedback_watch, fakedesk.set('/bus/01/insert/on', 0) must abort/pause the session ('insert bypassed') before the next notch. Both fail today.

> **Verifier 1: PARTIAL (low)** — Citations check out, but half of the finding is overstated. ACCURATE: (1) FakeDesk stores insert/sel as a free per-strip value with no ownership/eviction model and serves no /-insert/* table (fakedesk.py:675-684 _store; generic SET path 1038-1066; grep for "-insert" in src/ and device.yaml finds nothing), whereas fx_routing_scenes.md §3.4 (line 303) states the VERIFIED constraint 'an insert point can be inserted in one strip only' and line 304/§13 item 5 mark the OSC outcome UNCONFIRMED (last-write-wins with previous owner reset to OFF, or simply overridden; 'verify by re-reading /-insert/*'). (2) CFS captures fx_slot/side/sel once in _open_session (cfs.py:879-897), _DeskGeqWriter is bound to that slot (cfs.py:397-417), the controller subscribes only to connection.state (cfs.py:522), and neither _notch (1070-1094) nor _notch_and_verify (1200-1219) nor _run_ringout re-reads insert/on|sel; Desk._on_push only invalidates cache (desk.py:282-284). Tests flip insert/on only before preflight (tests/integration/test_cfs.py:173-186), never mid-session. So an engineer bypassing the insert to A/B mid ring-out (or another client re-pointing sel) is not noticed: VERIFY fails, the band is deepened to -9 dB, ring_out aborts with the misleading 'not tamed' reason (cfs.py:1160-1162) leaving up to three stale cuts on a GEQ that is out of circuit; in WATCH mode it can burn the whole notch budget on inaudible cuts. OVERSTATED/REFUTED parts: (a) 'the state the validator describes never occurs' — the research explicitly leaves 'simply overridden' open, in which case two strips CAN both read FX5L and provision.py:405-412 is exactly the defensive fallback the brief asks for on an UNCONFIRMED item, not code that depends on the fake; (b) the `used` map (provision.py:444-451, 472, 484-485) only asks 'is (slot,side) taken by anyone' and refuses occupied points, which is correct under either ownership semantics — no wrong allocation results; (c) proposed offline test (a) is not reachable through plan_setup (it never plans onto an occupied point; server.py:1589 re-plans on the confirm call, so the plan→apply race is negligible) and there is no direct set_insert MCP tool, so 'we evict someone else' needs a hand-built plan. Net: the mid-session no-revalidation gap is real but already fails safe in ring_out (abort + 6 dB master back-off after one band), the eviction-by-others scenario rests on UNCONFIRMED behaviour, and the operator-bypass scenario is operator-induced; the FakeDesk is in fact already capable of the insert/on flip (its _refresh_cuts honours insert/on, fakedesk.py:1115) so only the test and the CFS check are missing. Severity low, as claimed.

> **Verifier 2: PARTIAL (low)** — Two claims, different fates.

(a) "Two strips can hold the same insert point and the desk reports it that way" — largely REFUTED as a defect. docs/research/fx_routing_scenes.md §3.4 and §13 item 5 mark the desk's over-OSC behaviour on a duplicate insert as UNCONFIRMED (last-write-wins is only 'best inference'); the FakeDesk's plain per-strip enum (fakedesk.py _store, no /-insert table) is one of the two plausible readings, not a contradiction of verified research. More importantly, no product write depends on the both-hold model: Desk.get_inserts (desk.py:711-720) reads insert/on|pos|sel on EVERY insert-capable family (ch, bus, mtx, main), plan_setup's `used` map (provision.py:444-451) is built from that live read, the fresh-slot loop skips any slot with either side used (provision.py:483-485) and partial reuse checks (slot, other) in used (:471-473) — so plan_setup never plans a sel onto an occupied point under either model. apply_setup then re-reads all */insert/sel through validate_ringout_eqs (provision.py:531) — exactly the 'write, then re-read and reconcile' the research prescribes. The duplicate-sel reason at provision.py:405-412 is defensive dead code on a last-write-wins desk, not a wrong write. The only way our own write evicts a third party is a plan -> Tier-2 confirm -> apply race with someone patching FX5-8 inserts in that window, and only if the real desk is LWW: theoretical. The proposed offline test (a) ('apply_setup for bus 2 onto a point bus 1 owns') cannot be produced by plan_setup at all.

(b) "An insert validated at preflight stays in circuit for the session" — CONFIRMED as an untested operator/second-client assumption. cfs.py:884-897 captures ins.fx_slot/side/sel once in _open_session; `grep insert cfs.py` has exactly that one hit; CFS registers no conn.on_update handler (only Desk._on_push, desk.py:282-284, which merely invalidates cache) and never re-runs validate_ringout_eqs before a notch. Tests bypass the insert only BEFORE preflight (tests/integration/test_cfs.py:179-192); none flips /bus/NN/insert/on or sel during ring_out/feedback_watch. The FakeDesk already models the physical consequence (fakedesk.py:1114-1118 clears the SyntheticRta cuts when the RTA-source strip's insert is off; tests/integration/test_fakedesk.py:435-438 proves it), so the offline test (b) is writable today and would fail: CFS would go NOTCH -3 -> VERIFY fail -> -6 -> -9 -> ABORT 'ring at N Hz not tamed: GEQ band cannot cut deeper than -9 dB…' (cfs.py:1160-1163, 1200-1219) instead of 'insert bypassed'. transport.md §4.2 confirms the desk pushes single-leaf changes like this to /xremote clients, so detection would be cheap.

Real-gig consequence is bounded, hence low: it needs a human (engineer A/B-ing the GEQ, or another X32-Edit user grabbing FX5L — the latter itself UNCONFIRMED behaviour) to act mid-session; in RINGOUT the generic not-tamed abort plus abort_backoff_db 6 dB (device.yaml:829) still kills the ring after at most 3 x decay_verify_s = 4.5 s of untamed ringing, leaving one bogus -9 dB cut and a misleading abort reason; in WATCH it burns the notch budget on a GEQ that is out of circuit while feedback_watch claims to be guarding, but the person who bypassed it is standing at the desk. No wrong-strip write, no safety escalation beyond what any untameable ring already causes. Agree with the submitter's 'low'.
