**On a real desk:** Connecting to an older-firmware X32 (plenty of FW 2.x/3.x desks in venues) succeeds with no warning; feedback_watch then runs with auto-gain on and floods notches exactly as in the first M7 run; on an XR18 mistakenly targeted, panic() writes /main/st/mix/on which does not exist → silence from the desk, tool says 'sent'.

**Offline test:** Parametrise FakeDesk(firmware='2.12', model='X32CORE'/'XR18') with the corresponding address set (drop /-prefs/rta/det etc. for 2.x); assert connect() returns a 'warnings' list / refuses XR18, and set_rta_source reports autogain_cleared=False → feedback_watch refuses to arm. Fails today (no check exists).

> **Verifier 1: PARTIAL (low)** — The core assumption is real and the code citations check out: connect() (src/x32mcp/connection.py:325-340) stores the four /info strings in ConsoleInfo and sets CONNECTED unconditionally; nothing anywhere in src/ compares ConsoleInfo.model/firmware against device.yaml meta (model: X32, firmware_tested: "4.x", device.yaml:46-50) — grep for .model/.firmware outside fakedesk finds only log/summary strings (server.py:188,661,716). The test mini-server (tests/test_connection.py:88-89) and FakeDesk defaults (fakedesk.py:288-290, /info handler at :830) always report X32RACK/4.06/V2.07, and FakeDesk serves the full FW-4.x address tree regardless of the firmware kwarg, so no test can exercise an older/other desk. transport.md §3.1 does list X32CORE/M32C and the XR18 ,ssss reply on port 10024, and transport.md §5.3 does say unknown addresses are silently ignored. CFS._arm (cfs.py:911-929) arms regardless of verified/autogain_cleared/detector_set_peak, and _rta_dict (cfs.py:203-207) does not even surface the latter two flags.

However the 'reality' and 'failure' narrative overstates what the research supports: (1) the cited meters.md text (line 446, actually in §5.3 not §5.1) says only decay/peakhold/det were added in later firmware — the same sentence says the fw-2.x-era manual documents encoder 4 = Auto Gain (/-prefs/rta/autogain), so the M7 defect-#1 fix (auto-gain off) is NOT silently lost on FW 2.x; only the PEAK-detector write would be. 'feedback_watch floods notches exactly as in the first M7 run' is therefore unsupported. (2) set_rta_source has a fallback the claimant missed: it reads /-prefs/rta/det first (meters.py:918-923 via _read, which returns None on timeout) and only writes if a value came back, reporting detector_set_peak=False — it degrades to the desk's native detector rather than writing blind. (3) The XR18 scenario requires the operator to override the default port 10023 (connection.py:288, server.py:626/645; discover broadcasts on 10023) with 10024 — an XR18 never answers the default probe. (4) '/lr instead of /main/st' is not in transport.md (true of X-Air generally, but not a cited research fact). Net: a genuine untested assumption (no model/firmware gate, FakeDesk cannot emulate a reduced address set), correctly self-rated low, with an exaggerated failure story.

> **Verifier 2: PARTIAL (low)** — The core assumption is real but the claimed consequences are overstated. TRUE: X32Connection.connect() (src/x32mcp/connection.py:325-345) stores model/firmware from /info and goes CONNECTED unconditionally; nothing compares them with device.yaml meta (model: X32, firmware_tested: "4.x", device.yaml:47-50); FakeDesk._reply_for hardcodes "X32RACK"/"4.06" (fakedesk.py:288-291) and even ignores its own model=/firmware= constructor params, so the test double literally cannot express an older-firmware or non-X32 responder, and tests/test_connection.py only ever sees 4.06. So "any ,ssss answer = supported desk" is baked in. OVERSTATED: (1) The FW 2.x 'back to HANDOVER §4b defect #1 (auto-gain floods notches)' narrative is wrong per the research: meters.md §5.3 (line 446) says the fw-2.x-era manual already documents Auto Gain on encoder 4 = /-prefs/rta/autogain; only decay/peakhold/det are 'added in later firmware (UNCONFIRMED which version)'. set_rta_source reads each pref before writing (meters.py:911-925, _read bounded by read_timeout_s and returning None on silence), so on a desk lacking /-prefs/rta/det the code degrades to detector_set_peak=False (RMS detector, less sensitive to a narrow tone) rather than writing blindly or feeding CFS garbage — i.e. there IS a fallback for the UNCONFIRMED item. (2) The XR18 scenario requires the operator to explicitly pass port 10024 (connect() and discover_consoles default to 10023, transport.md §2 table line 143); after that every /node snapshot read would time out loudly, so 'panic says sent into silence' is operator-error/theoretical. (3) It is not fully silent: the connect tool's summary returns model and FW to the model/operator (server.py:661, :716). (4) FW-dependent node token counts are already handled (device.yaml:43, nodes.py:48/918). Residual real-gig effect: an FW 2.x/3.x X32 or an X32CORE connects with no compatibility warning; individual features then fail as timeouts/False flags (e.g. /meters/16 absent below 3.04, det pref unanswered) rather than as wrong writes. That is defensive-hardening / cosmetic — low, matching the finding's own rating, but the specific failure story (auto-gain regression, XR18 panic) does not hold.

## E105. [low] (unconfirmed-hunter, confirmed) A GEQ that a bus already inserts is usable for ring-out whatever its insert position; the analyser sees GEQ cuts through a POST insert.

**Encoded at:** src/x32mcp/fakedesk.py:1103-1131 (_refresh_cuts couples the GEQ to the RTA whenever insert/on and sel match - it never reads {prefix}/insert/pos or /-prefs/rta/pos); tests/integration/test_fakedesk.py:411-427 inserts '/bus/03/insert ON POST FX5L' and asserts the RTA band drops - the exact belief HANDOVER §4b.4 falsified; tests/integration/test_cfs.py:151 only checks freshly allocated inserts are PRE.

**Code depends on it at:** src/x32mcp/provision.py:459-463 (plan_setup reuse path keeps an existing GEQ insert as-is, adding only on:True - pos never corrected to _RINGOUT_INSERT_POS), 400-411 + module doc l.25 (validate_ringout_eqs never flags POST), 292-297 (the comment that says PRE is mandatory).

**Reality:** HANDOVER §4b defect 4 (real X32, 2026-09-20): a -15 dB cut through a POST insert moved the post-EQ RTA by -0.2/+0.4/+1.2 dB, the same cut PRE by -5.9/-6.0/-3.9 dB; 'PRE only restores the ability to measure a cut directly'. Jim's own desk arrived with GEQ2 in FX5 inserted POST on Main LR - the reuse path is the common path.

**On a real desk:** setup_ringout_eqs on a desk whose house GEQ is inserted POST reports ok and changes nothing; CFS then cannot see its own cuts: an insufficient notch and a sufficient one look identical until the room decides, verify_decay's measured 'drop' is acoustic luck, and existing-cut depth checks (matched_session) compare against a graph the analyser never sees.

**Offline test:** Make _refresh_cuts honour position: couple cuts only when insert/pos == PRE and rta/pos == POST (or insert POST and an RTA tap after it - none exists). Then (1) flip test_fakedesk.py:411 to expect NO drop with POST, (2) plan_setup on a bus with an existing 'ON POST FX5L' GEQ must emit {pos: PRE} and validate_ringout_eqs must give reason 'insert is POST: detector cannot see cuts'. Both fail today.

> **Verifier 1: CONFIRMED (medium)** — Both halves of the finding check out. (1) Research/handover: docs/HANDOVER.md:165-169 (§4b defect 4) says exactly what is claimed — a −15 dB cut through a POST insert moved the post-EQ RTA by −0.2/+0.4/+1.2 dB, the same cut PRE by −5.9/−6.0/−3.9 dB, 'Provisioning now uses PRE', and 'PRE only restores the ability to measure a cut directly'; §4b:149 confirms the M7 desk had 'GEQ2 already in FX slot 5, inserted on Main LR', i.e. the reuse path. docs/research/meters.md:398/449 documents only a PRE-EQ/POST-EQ RTA tap (/-prefs/rta/pos), nothing downstream of the insert. (2) Code: src/x32mcp/fakedesk.py:1103-1135 _refresh_cuts couples the GEQ to the SyntheticRta on insert/on + insert/sel + GEQ type only — it never reads {prefix}/insert/pos or /-prefs/rta/pos, so the fake models a POST insert as fully visible to the analyser; tests/integration/test_fakedesk.py:410 slashes '/bus/03/insert ON POST FX5L' and :424-427 assert the cut appears in rta.cuts and the ring decays — the belief M7 falsified. src/x32mcp/provision.py:459-464 reuse path records the existing InsertInfo (pos carried through as-is) and appends only {on: True} when bypassed — no pos correction; _RINGOUT_INSERT_POS (l.297) is applied only on the partial-reuse (l.475) and fresh-slot (l.496) paths, which is all commit ddcfeb1 changed. validate_ringout_eqs (l.390-420) has reasons for no insert / wrong FX type / bypassed / shared slot / stereo, never for pos; module doc l.24-25 'An insert at PRE is accepted' (i.e. position is not a blocker either way). preflight (l.640-662) and CfsManager._open_session (cfs.py:879-897) add no pos check either. No fallback exists anywhere in src (grep for POST/insert/pos/_RINGOUT_INSERT_POS). (3) Empirical repro in worktree $SP/worktrees/verify-unconfirmed-post-reuse-repro (commit 0ee9393, tests/integration/test_cfs.py::test_verify_post_insert_reuse_is_not_corrected): with '/fx/5 GEQ2' + '/bus/01/insert ON POST FX5L', plan_setup(desk,[1]) returns reuse pos='POST', inserts=[], empty=True; validate_ringout_eqs ok=True reasons=[]; insert/pos stays POST. So setup_ringout_eqs on a desk whose house GEQ is inserted POST reports success and changes nothing, and CFS then runs blind to its own notches (provision.py:295-296's own comment: 'can never verify decay and drives every ring to the -9 dB maximum'). Minor nit: cited test lines are off by one (insert slash is test_fakedesk.py:410, PRE assertion is test_cfs.py:150) — immaterial. Severity medium is right: not a wrong/unsafe write, but the tool reports a usable GEQ when the detector cannot measure its cuts, and the handover itself narrows the acoustic impact (loop-breaking notches still show wherever the RTA taps).

> **Verifier 2: PARTIAL (low)** — Code facts CONFIRMED, consequence OVERSTATED.

Confirmed (read + reproduced): (a) src/x32mcp/fakedesk.py:1103-1131 `_refresh_cuts` couples the inserted GEQ to the SyntheticRta whenever `{prefix}/insert/on` is set and `insert/sel` names a GEQ slot; it never reads `{prefix}/insert/pos` (nor `/-prefs/rta/pos`), so the emulator cannot distinguish PRE from POST and no test can catch a POST-dependent bug. (b) src/x32mcp/provision.py:459-463 (plan_setup reuse path) records an existing GEQ insert in `plan.reuse` and only ever appends `{on: True}`; `pos` is never corrected to `_RINGOUT_INSERT_POS` — commit ddcfeb1 changed only the partial-reuse and fresh-slot paths (l.475, l.496). (c) validate_ringout_eqs (provision.py:400-411) has no POST reason; module doc l.25 'An insert at PRE is accepted' predates M7; preflight (l.639-660) does not warn either. (d) Repro in worktree verify-unconfirmed-post-reuse-repro (tests/integration/test_cfs.py::test_verify_post_insert_reuse_is_not_corrected): `/fx/5 GEQ2` + `/bus/01/insert ON POST FX5L` → plan_setup reuse={1: pos:'POST'}, inserts=[], empty=True; validate ok=True reasons=[]; pos after = POST. So on the exact configuration that exposed HANDOVER §4b defect 4 (house GEQ2 in FX5 already inserted POST — the reuse path), setup_ringout_eqs returns ok:true, changed:0 and the documented fix ('Provisioning now uses PRE') is silently not applied. That is a genuine incomplete fix of a known real-desk defect, invisible to the emulator.

Why PARTIAL / downgraded to low: the claimed gig failure does not follow. HANDOVER §4b.4 itself narrows the POST cost: 'when a notch breaks the loop the ring stops acoustically and the RTA sees it wherever it taps, which is why cuts audibly worked; PRE only restores the ability to *measure* a cut directly' — M7's two successful catches ran through this very POST house insert. CFS VERIFY (cfs.py:1221-1253, device.yaml decay_verify_db=6 within 1.5 s) is acoustics-driven at either position: even PRE showed a −15 dB cut as only −5.9/−6.0/−3.9 dB, so a −3/−6 dB step never passes VERIFY electrically; an effective notch decays the ring acoustically in tens of ms (per-round-trip loss) and an ineffective one keeps growing and is deepened — identical logic PRE or POST, no over-cutting, nothing the audience hears differently, CFS does not act on garbage. 'verify_decay's drop is acoustic luck' is wrong — acoustic decay is the real signal. 'matched_session compares against a graph the analyser never sees' is wrong — _matched_session compares GEQ par read-backs to the report, not RTA data. The FakeDesk claim is also only half right: SyntheticRta does NOT display-attenuate rings (meters.py:708 `_spread(contrib, r.band, r.level)` — no cut), a cut acts on the ring only through the loop-gain term (meters.py:716-717), i.e. the fake's ring response is already an acoustic-loop model valid for POST; only the base-spectrum/notes attenuation (meters.py:707,711) and the `rta.cuts` coupling are PRE-only behaviour. Hence tests/integration/test_fakedesk.py:411-427's `l2 < l1 − 3` decay assertion is not the belief §4b.4 falsified, and proposed offline test (1) ('expect NO drop with POST') would encode wrong physics; test (2) (plan_setup emits pos:PRE or validate/preflight flags POST on reuse) is the right one and fails today. Also note auto-forcing PRE on an engineer's deliberately-POST house GEQ is itself a guarded, audible-path write; a validation reason/warning is the safer fix. Net: real, trivially fixable gap in enforcing the project's own post-M7 invariant (and provision.py:292-297's comment overstates that invariant vs HANDOVER), but functionally mitigated by physics — diagnostic/measurement loss, not a wrong write or a lying tool at a gig.

## E106. [low] (unconfirmed-hunter, partial) The desk answers /save ,siss scene ... within the 0.5 s parameter-read timeout, and re-sending /save on silence is harmless.

**Encoded at:** src/x32mcp/fakedesk.py _h_save (l.~1150-1175) replies ',si scene 1' synchronously in the datagram handler; the only latency knob (latency_ms) is global, so no test has a slow /save with fast parameter reads.

**Code depends on it at:** src/x32mcp/desk.py:1291-1310 save_scene -> self._conn.request('/save', ...) with defaults; src/x32mcp/connection.py:245-246 (timeout_s 0.5, retries 2) and 747-770 (_request_bytes RE-SENDS the datagram on every timeout); a late reply is dropped as unmatched (connection.py:34).

**Reality:** transport.md §5.3 (l.358): 'UNCONFIRMED numeric latency of a real desk ... Recommend a 50-100 ms per-request timeout with one retry' - stated for parameter GETs only; fx_routing_scenes.md §6.4 documents the /save reply form but no timing; a scene save serialises ~2000 node lines to flash and HANDOVER §4a lists Scenes as 'Still to do' (never exercised live). /save is not idempotent in effect (each one rewrites the slot and bumps the desk UI).

**On a real desk:** save_scene('pre-show') on a desk that takes ~1 s to write flash: three /save commands are fired 0.5 s apart, the tool returns TIMEOUT / 'desk refused to save' although the scene was saved (three times), the LLM tells the operator the backup failed and may retry or pick another slot.

**Offline test:** Add a per-command reply delay to FakeDesk (e.g. FakeDesk.command_latency['/save'] = 0.9 s) and count /save datagrams received. Test: save_scene(5, 'x') returns ok with exactly one /save on the wire -> requires request('/save', ..., timeout=~3 s, retries=0); today: 3 datagrams and DeskError TIMEOUT.

> **Verifier 1: REFUTED (low)** — The cited code lines are real (desk.py:1290-1310 save_scene -> conn.request('/save',...) with defaults; connection.py:245-246 timeout_s=0.5, retries=2; connection.py:747-770 _request_bytes re-sends each attempt), and HANDOVER.md:130-132 does list Scenes as untested live. But the finding's mechanism, failure scenario and research reading are wrong:

1. Missed fallback: reply matching is per ADDRESS key, not per datagram (connection.py:752 self._pending[key].append(fut); :820 _pop_waiter(_reply_key(msg))). A slow reply to the FIRST /save satisfies the 2nd or 3rd attempt's waiter, so the effective tolerance is timeout x attempts = 1.5 s, not 0.5 s. Empirically (worktree probe tests/integration/test_verify_save_latency.py, prod defaults 0.5 s x 3, FakeDesk /save reply delayed): 0.3 s -> ok/1 datagram; 0.9 s -> ok/2 datagrams; 1.2 s -> ok/3 datagrams; only 2.0 s -> TIMEOUT. The claimed failure ('desk takes ~1 s -> tool returns TIMEOUT / desk refused to save although saved') is false at the stated latency, and 'desk refused to save' (SCENE_FAILED, desk.py:1307) cannot arise from slowness at all. The proposed offline test's 'today: 3 datagrams and DeskError TIMEOUT' at 0.9 s is also wrong (today: 2 datagrams, ok:true).

2. Wrong research reading: the finding says fx_routing_scenes.md 6.4 gives 'no timing'. It does: line 564 quotes Behringer DOC fn.39-41, 'The load/save/copy operation is not necessarily fully completed when the status is returned' - i.e. the ,si scene 1 status is returned BEFORE the (slow) flash write, contradicting the premise that the reply is gated on serialising ~2000 lines. transport.md line 358 is quoted correctly but sits in 5.4 (not 5.3) and recommends 50-100 ms with one retry; the code's 1.5 s window is 15x that budget - a margin, not a dependency on an UNCONFIRMED number.

3. Wrong citation: 'a late reply is dropped as unmatched (connection.py:34)'. /save is not in _NOT_PARAMS (connection.py:71 = {/info,/xinfo,/status,/}), so an unmatched late /save reply is NOT dropped; it is cached as a pseudo-parameter '/save' and published as an 'update' event (connection.py:831-833) - observed in the probe. Cosmetic only.

4. Idempotence: duplicate /save to the same slot with the same name/notes from the same desk state yields the same end state; FakeDesk _h_save (fakedesk.py:1159-1184) models exactly that. 'Bumps the desk UI'/harm from re-send is speculation with no research or handover support. Maillot's X32GetLib.c:798-828 sends /save once and polls unboundedly - consistent with either fast or slow replies, no numeric evidence.

Net: what survives is 'scene save never exercised live; if a real desk took >1.5 s to return status the tool would report a spurious TIMEOUT, and between 0.5-1.5 s it sends 1-2 redundant /save and leaves a stray /save cache entry' - speculative, contradicted by the only documentary timing evidence, and already mitigated by the 3-attempt key-matched window. Not a confirmed instance of the defect class; at most low/cosmetic.

> **Verifier 2: PARTIAL (low)** — The structural observation is correct but the stated real-world failure is wrong and the premise is unsupported.

What holds: save_scene (src/x32mcp/desk.py:1290-1310) sends /save through X32Connection.request with the parameter-GET defaults (connection.py:245-246: 0.5 s per attempt, retries=2) and _request_bytes (connection.py:747-770) re-sends the command datagram on each timeout; FakeDesk._h_save (fakedesk.py:1159-1184) replies synchronously and the only latency knob is the global latency_ms (fakedesk.py:312, 772-779), so no test isolates a slow /save. /save latency on a real desk is UNCONFIRMED (transport.md §5.4, l.~358) and scenes were never exercised live (HANDOVER §4a l.130-132).

What does not hold: (1) The claimed gig failure ('desk takes ~1 s -> three /save, tool returns TIMEOUT') is false for the shipped defaults. Because every attempt registers a waiter on the same key '/save', the late reply to the FIRST datagram satisfies a LATER attempt's waiter. I verified against the FakeDesk with only the /save reply delayed and production timeouts (0.5 s x 3): delay 0.4 s -> 1 datagram, ok; 0.9 s -> 2 datagrams, ok=True; 1.3 s -> 3 datagrams, ok=True; only 1.7 s (>1.5 s window) -> DeskError TIMEOUT (scene still saved). So a ~1 s desk is reported correctly; a false TIMEOUT needs >1.5 s reply latency. (2) The only source on timing points the other way: fx_routing_scenes.md §6.4 l.564 quotes DOC fn.39-41 'The load/save/copy operation is not necessarily fully completed when the status is returned' - i.e. the desk acks BEFORE finishing the write, so the reply is not gated on the flash serialisation the finder hypothesises; §5.4 says replies are 'well under 10 ms' typically. Maillot's real-desk X32GetLib.c (l.801-830) waits for the /save reply without re-sending, but with no evidence it is slow. (3) The re-send is idempotent in effect: same slot, same name/notes, and save_scene holds the policy write lock so this tool cannot change desk state between duplicates; 'bumps the desk UI' is cosmetic. Worst realistic outcome if a desk were pathologically slow (>1.5 s): the LLM reports 'no reply to /save' while the scene is in fact saved - confusing, no audio/safety consequence, operator can see the slot on the Scenes screen. Minor side effect the finder missed: duplicate late '/save ,si scene 1' replies fall through to the pushed-update path and are cached under address '/save' (connection.py:828-833) and could pre-satisfy an immediately following /save request's waiter (stale ack) - edge case, low.

Net: a cheap hardening (request('/save'|'/load'|'/delete', timeout~2-3 s, retries<=1) plus a per-command reply-delay knob in FakeDesk) is reasonable because the latency is UNCONFIRMED and untested live, but the finding's concrete failure requires a latency 1.5x beyond what it posits and contrary to DOC fn.39-41, and the duplicate writes are harmless. Downgraded to low.

## E107. [low] (unconfirmed-hunter, partial) We are always one of the desk's (at most four) /xremote clients, so pushed updates keep the caches honest and silence means nothing changed.

**Encoded at:** src/x32mcp/fakedesk.py:96-98,845-853 models the 4-client cap but every test connects one or two clients; no test runs X32Connection as client #5.

**Code depends on it at:** src/x32mcp/connection.py:892-925 (heartbeat sends /xremote, never learns whether it registered - /xremote is unacked; watchdog only probes /info); Desk/connection read caches device.yaml:739 read_cache_ttl_s 2.0 (desk.py:212-232,313) rely on pushes for sub-TTL freshness; dashboard/live mapper rely on pushes entirely.

**Reality:** transport.md §2/§4.1 (DOC-confirmed): 'Triggers X32 to send all parameter changes to maximum four active clients'; what a fifth client experiences is unstated (best inference: silently not registered). A band gig routinely has X32-Edit at FOH plus several X32-Mix/Mixing-Station phones for personal monitor mixes.

**On a real desk:** With FOH laptop + 3 musicians' phones connected, the MCP server never receives pushes: every get_* answer can be up to 2 s stale with no DEGRADED indication, the web dashboard's live view freezes while status says CONNECTED/heartbeat_ok, and feedback_watch's operator-driven master_db tracking lags.

**Offline test:** Start five X32Connection clients against FakeDesk (cap already modelled) and assert the fifth reports status().heartbeat_ok False / a 'no pushes (client table full?)' warning after fakedesk.set() changes a value it has cached; today it stays CONNECTED and silent. Mitigation to test for: detect absence of the echo of a deliberate write on a second socket (transport.md §12 step 4) or periodically diff a cheap leaf.

> **Verifier 1: PARTIAL (low)** — Core claim holds: transport.md §2 (line 148, DOC 446-455) and §4.1 (lines 229-279, section marked CONFIRMED) state /xremote pushes go to "maximum four active clients", /xremote is never acked (line 245), and the verified emulator code returns 0 silently when the table is full ("no room for new clients! (todo; another return status?)"). FakeDesk models exactly this (fakedesk.py:98 MAX_XREMOTE_CLIENTS=4; :845-853 _h_xremote logs a warning and does not register). No test exercises a fifth client: the only tests touching fakedesk.clients wait for 1 or 2 registrations (tests/integration/test_desk.py:108,161; test_fakedesk.py:225,368). X32Connection cannot detect non-registration: _heartbeat_loop (connection.py:891-899) sets _heartbeat_ok=True on a successful local sendto; status.heartbeat_ok (:459) is that flag AND tasks alive AND CONNECTED; the watchdog (:908-935) only probes /info on silence, and since get/node replies keep _last_rx fresh it never even fires. Nothing in HANDOVER/DESIGN/REVIEW_BRIEF acknowledges the limitation; README:891-892 promises operators that "the server's cache is 2 s and is invalidated by pushed updates, so reads reflect their changes".

Fallback the claimant did account for: both caches are TTL-bounded (device.yaml:739 read_cache_ttl_s 2.0; desk.py:212,313; connection.py:581-605), and our own writes invalidate via the 'write' event, so the damage is bounded to <=2 s staleness of other operators' changes plus a silent 'update' event stream — which is why 'low' (already mitigated) is the right severity, as self-rated.

Overstated/inaccurate parts of the failure narrative: (1) "the web dashboard's live view freezes" — the dashboard's live content is RTA frames from the /meters subscription (webui.py:298 frames.subscribe) and CFS state from an internal provider on a ticker (webui.py:455-474); neither depends on /xremote registration. Only the pushed-'update' entries in the event feed (webui.py:449-452) would go missing. (2) "feedback_watch's operator-driven master_db tracking lags" — there is no such tracking: cfs.py subscribes to no 'update' events (only connection.state at :522 and frames at :920); in WATCH mode ses.master_db is set once from preflight (:892-896) and only ring-out's own RAISE writes change it (:1191-1195). So nothing lags; it was never tracked. The realistic gig failure is narrower than stated: get_* tools and the README's concurrent-operator promise silently degrade to 2 s-TTL polling with connection_status reporting heartbeat_ok:true.

> **Verifier 2: PARTIAL (low)** — The assumption is real and genuinely unexercised, but the fake is correct and two of the three claimed gig consequences are wrong; what remains is bounded by design.

What holds up: transport.md §2 (table rows 147-148) and §4.1 give a DOC-confirmed 4-client /xremote cap with no ack (§4.1 line 245, §11 item 7), and fakedesk.py:98 + _h_xremote (fakedesk.py:845-853) model exactly that — so the FakeDesk matches research. Every test registers one or two clients (tests/integration/test_fakedesk.py:219-250 waits for len(fakedesk.clients)==2; test_desk.py:108,161 likewise; no test anywhere references MAX_XREMOTE_CLIENTS or a full table). X32Connection._heartbeat_loop (connection.py:892-899) sets _heartbeat_ok=True on a successful sendto and nothing ever checks that pushes actually arrive; the watchdog (connection.py:908-937) probes /info, which answers regardless of registration (§4.3), so a 5th client stays CONNECTED/heartbeat_ok with zero pushes. A FOH X32-Edit plus 3+ musicians' X32-Mix/Mixing-Station phones is a normal band-gig topology, so being client #5 is plausible.

What does not hold up: (1) 'the web dashboard's live view freezes' — the dashboard's live content is the RTA (from this client's own /meters subscription, webui.py:22-24,298) and CFS state polled from the manager (webui.py 'State is derived by polling'); nothing in webui.py renders xremote pushes except the generic event log, so only 'update' log lines go missing. (2) 'feedback_watch's operator-driven master_db tracking lags' — cfs.py has no on_update/'update' subscriber at all (only 'connection.state', cfs.py:522); in WATCH mode ses.master_db is the preflight value and is never tracked from pushes, so losing pushes changes nothing there. (3) 'every get_* answer can be up to 2 s stale with no DEGRADED indication' — true, but that is the designed correctness bound, not a dependency on pushes: DESIGN.md §0.6 line 24 'Read cache TTL <= 2 s; invalidated by pushed...' and desk.py:16-19 make the TTL (device.yaml:739 read_cache_ttl_s 2.0, desk.py:212, desk.py:313; connection.py:615-620) the guarantee and pushes an early-invalidation optimisation; our own writes still invalidate via the 'write' event (desk.py:233-235,286-289). The only consumer of on_update is Desk._on_push (desk.py:232,282-284).

Residual real-world bite: as a 5th client, reads inside the 2 s window after a front-panel/X32-Edit move return the old value more often, and adjust_level (desk.py:1007-1009) computes base+delta from a possibly <=2 s-stale cached 'before', so an LLM that reads then nudges the same fader an operator just moved could land it at stale+delta — but that race is already accepted by the TTL design (it exists with pushes too, just narrower), is bounded by check_relative (+/-6 dB) and ramped, and requires an LLM tool pair inside 2 s coinciding with a human move on the same control. heartbeat_ok cannot mean 'registered' under this protocol (/xremote is unacked by the real desk too), so the status is not lying about anything it could know. Net: a valid untested-scenario note with an easy offline test (5 conn_factory() clients, fakedesk.set_value, assert the 5th sees nothing and status gives no hint) and a cheap mitigation (periodic diff of a cheap leaf, or §12 step-4 second-socket echo check), but cosmetic/already-mitigated in effect. Low, as the finder rated it.

## E108. [low] (unconfirmed-hunter, confirmed) The 32 channel meters in /meters/0 (and /meters/1 [0-31]) are post-fader/post-mute levels: a muted channel or one with its fader down reads silence.

**Encoded at:** src/x32mcp/fakedesk.py:930-941 (_strip_level returns SILENCE_LIN when mix/on is 0 or fader <= 0 and scales by fader dB), 957-962; tests/integration/test_fakedesk.py:284-285 asserts muting ch 2 drives /meters/0[1] < 1e-4.

**Code depends on it at:** src/x32mcp/server.py:1419-1457 get_meters('channels') documents '-90 = silence' and feeds the LLM's reasoning about which inputs carry signal; HANDOVER §4b proposes cross-checking discover_mics candidates 'against actual meter activity (an unplugged input reads near-silent, a live mic picks up room noise)' - a check that would be developed and certified against this fake.

**Reality:** meters.md §3 only says '/meters/0 [0-31] 32 input channels' / '/meters/1 [0-31] 32 input channels (level)' next to their gate/dyn GR words; /meters/6 distinguishes [0] pre-fade from [3] post-fade explicitly; Automix.c (meters.md sources) reads /meters/1 as channel INPUT level on a real console. X32 channel strip/METERS-page channel meters are input (pre-fader) meters; pre/post is not stated in the research either way, so the fake picked the reading reality is least likely to honour.

**On a real desk:** A meter-activity mic check tuned on the fake ('muted or fader-down => silent => no mic') inverts on the desk: muted live vocal mics show room noise and are declared connected/active, or - if the logic keys on silence - nothing is ever silent; get_meters tells the operator a muted channel 'has signal at -30 dB', read as a routing fault.

**Offline test:** Decide from a 30-second real-desk capture (mute a channel with a live mic, watch /meters/0 and /meters/1 index) and encode it; meanwhile make FakeDesk channel entries of /meters/0,/1,/13 pre-fader (post-preamp, ignore mix/on and fader) like /meters/6[0], keep bus/main entries post-fader, and flip test_fakedesk.py:285. Any future discover_mics activity check must be tested against that model.

> **Verifier 1: CONFIRMED (low)** — Both citations check out and there is no fallback the claimant missed. (1) Encoding: src/x32mcp/fakedesk.py:930-941 `_strip_level` returns SILENCE_LIN whenever `<prefix>/mix/on` is 0 or the fader is <= 0 and otherwise scales the level by the fader dB; lines 957-962 apply that post-fader/post-mute model to every channel word of /meters/0, /meters/13 and /meters/1 [0-31] (only /meters/6 word 0 is generated with pre_fade=True, line 967-970). tests/integration/test_fakedesk.py:285-286 certifies it (`fakedesk.set('/ch/02/mix/on', 0)` -> `/meters/0` value[1] < 1e-4) and cites 'meters.md §6.3' for it, but §6.3 (meters.md:467-469 item 3) only says float-meter silence is ~1e-5..4e-7, not that channel meters follow the mute; the one muted -> -128 dB observation in the research (meters.md §2.2 line 196, §4.1 line 277) is explicitly the /meters/6 *post-fade* word [3]. (2) Research: meters.md §3 lines 241-242/254 describe /meters/0, /1, /13 channel entries only as '32 input channels' / '(level)' with no pre/post statement, while /meters/6 (line 247) explicitly separates [0] 'post gain/trim (pre-fade)' from [3] 'post-fade' — so the fake chose an unverified reading. (3) Reality evidence is actually stronger than the claimant stated: meters.md lists X32Automix.c as 'a real client that subscribes /meters/1 against a real console' (line 12); I fetched it — at start it drives every channel to its pre-recorded LOW fader value (lines 551-552, header comment line 22: 'low position (no sound)') and then opens a channel only when its /meters/1 level exceeds X32sensitivity=0.005 (lines 626-635). That algorithm cannot work if /meters/1 [0-31] were post-fader (a channel parked at -oo could never cross the threshold), so on real hardware the channel words are pre-fader, i.e. the FakeDesk's mute/fader-following channel meters are wrong. This also matches the X32 surface/METERS-page channel meters being input (pre-fader) meters. (4) HANDOVER §4b (docs/HANDOVER.md:184-187) does propose exactly the meter-activity cross-check for discover_mics that would be developed against this fake. Caveat on impact: no shipped logic keys on the post-fader model today — get_meters (server.py:1419-1457, METER_GROUPS meters.py:101-107 -> /meters/0) is a pass-through and its docstring makes no pre/post claim, CFS uses only /meters/15 (cfs.py:508), so on a real desk get_meters simply reports true pre-fader levels; the harm is that the emulator teaches the wrong model (muted/fader-down => silent) to any future activity heuristic (discover_mics cross-check, 'is this channel contributing' reasoning) and the LLM may misread a muted channel's non-silent reading. That is correctly rated low.

> **Verifier 2: PARTIAL (low)** — The encoded assumption is real and most likely wrong, but nothing shipped depends on it today, so it stays low and is only partially a "code depends on it" finding.

(1) Encoded: fakedesk.py:930-941 `_strip_level` returns SILENCE_LIN when `mix/on`==0 or fader<=0 and scales the level by fader dB; fakedesk.py:956-962 uses that post-fader model for every channel word of /meters/0, /meters/13 and /meters/1[0-31]; only /meters/6[0] is modelled pre-fade (line 970). tests/integration/test_fakedesk.py:283-285 certifies it ("muted: silence level (meters.md §6.3)") — a miscitation: meters.md §6 item 3 only says silence is not 0.0; the sole mute-related datum in the research is the DOC /meters/6 capture (§2.2/§4.1) where the *post-fade* word [3] reads -128 dB while the *pre-fade* word [0] of the same idle channel reads -100 dB. The research (§3 table) says nothing about pre/post for /meters/0,/1,/13 channel entries, so the fake generalised the /meters/6[3] behaviour to all channel meters without evidence.

(2) Reality: not stated in docs/research, but the weight of evidence is pre-fader. X32Automix.c — which meters.md lists as "a real client that subscribes /meters/1 against a real console" — reads /meters/1[ch] (line 630) and, when it exceeds X32sensitivity, raises /ch/NN/mix/fader from a pre-recorded "low position (no sound)" (header lines 15-22, loop 632-647). That design is a latch if the meter were post-fader (a channel parked at its silent low fader could never cross threshold again), so /meters/1 channel levels must be pre-fader input levels on real hardware. This matches the physical desk: X32 channel-strip LED meters and the METERS->CHANNEL page (which the DOC says /meters/1 feeds) are post-preamp, pre-fader, and the console offers no post-fader channel-meter option.

(3) Dependence / gig consequence: the only consumer is get_meters (server.py:1418-1457, Tier 0, read-only, /meters/0 slices via METER_GROUPS meters.py:101-108). Its docstring says "Signal levels ... -90 = silence" and claims neither pre nor post, so on a real desk it simply returns pre-fader input levels — arguably the more useful answer to "which inputs carry signal". No write, no safety path, CFS does not use these meters (cfs.py:508 uses /meters/15). The HANDOVER §4b meter-activity cross-check for discover_mics does not exist yet; the risk is that it (or an LLM narrative "muted => meter silent") would be developed and certified against a fake that inverts the real behaviour — notably, real pre-fader metering is exactly what would make that check work on muted-but-connected mics, whereas the fake would report them silent and steer the design wrong. That is a development-fidelity trap, not a tool that lies at a gig today.

Net: assumption confirmed as encoded and probably contrary to the real desk; current real-world impact cosmetic/future-facing. Severity low as the finder rated. Fix as proposed: make /meters/0,/1[0-31],/13 channel (and aux/fx-return) words pre-fader like /meters/6[0], keep /meters/6[3] (and main) post-fader, flip test_fakedesk.py:285, and confirm with a 30 s real-desk capture (mute a live-mic channel, watch /meters/1[idx]).

## E109. [low] (unconfirmed-hunter, confirmed) The Solo-Priority bit can always be read and cleared through the leaf /-prefs/rta/options, and once cleared at arm time nothing re-routes the analyser to the solo bus.

**Encoded at:** src/x32mcp/fakedesk.py: the leaf exists under exactly that spelling (device.yaml:564) and solo has no effect on frames; tests/integration/test_fakedesk.py:395-397 clears bit 5 happily.

**Code depends on it at:** src/x32mcp/meters.py:885,899-903 (read options; on read failure opts=None -> silently not cleared, options_cleared False, no warning beyond the generic read log); cfs never re-checks /-stat/solo or options during the session.

**Reality:** meters.md §5.1/§7: 'which leaf spelling (options/option) the console accepts' is UNCONFIRMED (X32DeskRestore lists /-prefs/rta/option; DOC node list prints -prefs/rta/option); §5.3 bit 5: 'the RTA source will be replaced with the monitor solo bus whenever a channel solo is active ... affects both the GEQ RTA view and the dedicated RTA tab view'. The M5 sweep only proved the 10-field /-prefs/rta NODE parses, not the leaf GET/SET.

**On a real desk:** If the desk only answers /-prefs/rta/option, Solo Priority stays on unnoticed; the engineer PFLs a channel mid ring-out (normal habit) and the analyser jumps to the solo bus: detections/verification now describe whatever is solo'd while the master keeps rising.

**Offline test:** Parametrise FakeDesk to expose the leaf as 'option' only (node unchanged) and to swap /meters/15 to the solo'd strip while /-stat/solo is on and bit 5 set. Test: set_rta_source must fall back to writing the whole '/-prefs/rta' node line via '/' (spelling-independent) or raise when it cannot prove bit 5 is clear; and CFS must pause on a /-stat/solo push. Fails today (silent).

> **Verifier 1: CONFIRMED (low)** — Both citations check out and the code has no fallback. (1) Research: docs/research/meters.md line 405 says verbatim "Try `options` first; UNCONFIRMED which the console actually accepts as a leaf — the `/node ,s -prefs/rta` group form avoids the question", and line 526 lists "which leaf spelling (`options`/`option`) the console accepts" among the items still UNCONFIRMED after verification; §5.3 (line ~444) quotes the manual for bit 5: "the RTA source will be replaced with the monitor solo bus whenever a channel solo is active … This affects both the GEQ RTA view and the dedicated RTA tab view" and line ~452 "Solo Priority (bit 5) overrides everything while any solo is active". HANDOVER §4a only records that the full /node sweep parsed (group node), and §4b (M7) records autogain/det fixes but nothing about the options leaf, so the leaf GET/SET was never directly verified on the real desk. (2) Code: meters.py:885 takes opt_addr from descriptor (device.yaml:564 declares only `rta/options`); meters.py:899-903 reads it via _read(), which swallows any exception/timeout into None with only a generic log.warning, then `cleared` stays False — indistinguishable in RtaSourceResult from "bit 5 was already clear"; no alternative spelling, no group-node ('/' ) write, no raise. tests/test_meters.py:689-692 ("deaf" conn with get_fail on /-prefs/rta/options) explicitly certifies this silent-degrade path as passing. cfs.py has zero references to solo (/-stat/solo, solosw) — grep confirms — so nothing pauses or re-checks during a session. (3) Fake: fakedesk.py:160 defaults "rta/options": 0 and exposes exactly the `options` spelling; _mirror_rta_stat/_refresh_cuts (fakedesk.py:1094-1135) derive the analysed strip solely from /-prefs/rta/source — /-stat/solo and options bit 5 have no effect on /meters/15 frames, so no test can observe a solo hijack; tests/integration/test_fakedesk.py:395-397 sets 0b100000 and asserts it clears, as cited. Mitigating context (why severity stays low, as the claimant rated it): the weight of documentary evidence (emulator X32.c command table quoted at meters.md:377, DOC table at :400) favours `options`, the sibling leaves /-prefs/rta/autogain and /det demonstrably worked as leaf GET/SET at M7, and the failure needs Solo Priority to be on plus an operator solo mid-session. But per the task's rule (dependence on an UNCONFIRMED item without a fallback is a finding) and the un-modelled solo override, the finding stands as stated.

> **Verifier 2: PARTIAL (low)** — Two claims are bundled; they fare differently.

(A) Leaf-spelling dependency — CONFIRMED as a genuine UNCONFIRMED-item dependency, but low real-world weight. set_rta_source (src/x32mcp/meters.py:885,899-903) reads and writes the leaf '/-prefs/rta/options' (device.yaml:760 options_param; device.yaml:564 declares the leaf, and FakeDesk builds its address tree from that declaration, so the emulator can only ever answer the 'options' spelling — the suite cannot detect a wrong spelling). meters.md §5.1 (line 405) and §7's still-UNCONFIRMED list (line 526) explicitly say which leaf spelling the console accepts is unverified and that the spelling-independent route is the '/-prefs/rta' group node (7th field %options, VERIFIED format) / '/ ,s' node write. The code does not use that route, so if a real desk only answered 'option', bit 5 would silently stay as-is and RtaSourceResult.options_cleared=False is indistinguishable from 'was already clear'. HOWEVER: (1) the code follows the research's own recommendation ('Try options first'); (2) it is not without a fallback — a failed read is caught, logged at WARNING ('rta: reading /-prefs/rta/options failed'), nothing wrong is written, and arming proceeds (this degradation is deliberately encoded in tests/test_meters.py:689-692, the 'deaf' case); (3) the balance of evidence favours 'options': Maillot's DOC 4.09 parameter table (pp.59-60), the emulator's PrefStat.h, and fx_routing_scenes.md:640 all use 'options', while the only 'option' evidence is a commented-out DeskRestore.c block that also contains the known-wrong '/-stat/rtaeqpost'; (4) set_rta_source ran repeatedly against the real FW 4.13 desk at M5/M7 (HANDOVER §4b — the sibling leaf /-prefs/rta/autogain was read and written successfully there), and a wrong spelling would have produced a ≥1 s stall plus a WARNING on every arm in sessions whose logs were combed finely enough to count 337 detections — not proof, but it did not surface among nine real-desk defects. (5) Even if it bit, harm needs a conjunction (wrong spelling × Solo Priority enabled on that desk × operator PFLs during an armed session), and CFS writes are bounded (−3 dB steps, −9 dB max, 4-notch budget) with growth+persistence gating, so 'CFS acts on garbage' is limited to wasted budget / a few dB of wrong cut and lying verification — the hunter's own 'low' is right.

(B) 'Nothing re-checks /-stat/solo during the session' — REFUTED as a defect. meters.md §5.3 (bit-5 row and 'Consequences' bullets) says solos replace the RTA source ONLY when Solo Priority is set (or source=1 Monitor); set_rta_source writes a fixed strip index and clears bit 5, after which the manual says solos do not touch the RTA-tab analysis. FakeDesk's 'solo has no effect on /meters/15' therefore matches documented real-desk behaviour for the state CFS puts the desk in. Pausing CFS on every /-stat/solo push (the proposed test) would be an over-reaction that fights a normal engineer habit for no gain; the residual risk (operator re-ticks Solo Priority or moves RTA encoder 6 on the console mid-session) is a different, operator-interference finding, not this one.

Net: the finding correctly identifies an UNCONFIRMED protocol detail hard-coded identically in fake and product, with a reporting gap (read-failure conflated with already-clear) and a cheap robust alternative left unused (read %options from the VERIFIED '/-prefs/rta' node line, or write it via '/'). But it already degrades safely with a logged warning, the evidence leans toward the spelling being right, live runs did not flag it, and half the finding (solo re-check) contradicts the research. PARTIAL, low. Worth a one-line hardening: on leaf-read failure fall back to parsing field 7 of `node('-prefs/rta')` and, if bit 5 is set, clear it via `slash('-prefs/rta ... %0xxxxx ...')`, and report options_read_failed distinctly in RtaSourceResult / session warnings.

## E110. [low] (unconfirmed-hunter, confirmed) A GEQ band cut of c dB lowers every RTA band within that 1/3-octave by exactly c dB (rectangular, non-interacting bands on the ISO centre list), so mapping an RTA band to the nearest GEQ centre and cutting -3 dB always removes 3 dB of loop gain at the ring frequency.

**Encoded at:** src/x32mcp/fakedesk.py:1124-1130 (nearest-centre lookup, full-depth attenuation of every RTA band mapped to that GEQ band); src/x32mcp/meters.py SyntheticRta cut model ('level -= c per frame'); tests/test_meters.py:436-448, tests/integration/test_fakedesk.py:419-427, and every CFS notch/verify test.

**Code depends on it at:** src/x32mcp/cfs.py NotchController band mapping (RTA band -> nearest geq band_hz, device.yaml:775) and the -3 dB step / 6 dB verify expectation (device.yaml:816-821); merge_adjacent_bands 1.

**Reality:** fx_routing_scenes.md §2.3/§13 items 1-3 and scales_params.md §14/§17: the 31 centres are the ISO list by inference (web-corroborated) and the desk's gain quantisation is UNCONFIRMED; physically a graphic-EQ band is a bell filter: a ring sitting between two ISO centres (RTA is 1/10-octave, GEQ 1/3-octave, so 2 of every 3 RTA bands are off-centre by ~1/10 oct) receives noticeably less than the nominal cut from one band and GEQ2 (non-'True' EQ) bands interact; TEQ compensates. Mitigated in practice by deepen-on-failed-verify.

**On a real desk:** Rings between centres need one extra -3 dB step (audibly wider tonal hole than necessary) and occasionally hit -9 dB/ABORT where cutting the two adjacent bands -3 dB each would have held; verify thresholds tuned on the rectangular fake are optimistic.

**Offline test:** Replace the fake's rectangular coupling with a constant-Q bell per GEQ band (e.g. RBJ peaking, Q~4.3 for 1/3 oct) summed in dB across bands, evaluated at each RTA centre; add a test with a ring at 2.24 kHz (between 2k and 2k5) expecting the controller to split the cut across both neighbours or to reach kill within budget. Today's controller assumes full depth at the nearest centre.

> **Verifier 1: CONFIRMED (low)** — The assumption is genuinely encoded and the code genuinely depends on it; the claimant's characterisation of the research docs is accurate and the physics is sound; the mitigation (closed-loop verify + deepen) was correctly acknowledged and the low severity is appropriate. Two pointer slips do not change the substance: NotchController.band_for_freq lives in src/x32mcp/detector.py:538-543 (cfs.py:507/888 only builds _geq_hz from device.yaml and hands it to NotchController), and the ISO band_hz list is device.yaml:773 (775 is par_a_master).

Encoded: fakedesk.py:_refresh_cuts (lines ~1124-1130 in the file as read) maps every RTA band to the single nearest GEQ centre in log-frequency and calls rta.attenuate(i, cut) with the full band gain (+master) — rectangular, non-overlapping, non-interacting, identical for GEQ/GEQ2 and TEQ/TEQ2. SyntheticRta (meters.py:572-578 docstring, :661-666 set_geq_gain applies the full gain to every RTA band within ±1/6 oct, :707/:716-717 subtracts the full cut from the displayed level and from the ring's per-frame loop gain). tests/test_meters.py:441-447 asserts set_geq_gain(2500,-3) -> cuts {69:3.0,70:3.0,71:3.0}; tests/integration/test_fakedesk.py:419-424 asserts a -6 dB write to the 2.5 kHz GEQ par yields rta.cuts[band(2400 Hz)] == 6.0 exactly. Depends: detector.py:538-543 band_for_freq (nearest centre), :551-565 plan() opens/deepens exactly one band in notch_step_db=-3 steps to notch_max_db=-9 (device.yaml:816-817), merge_adjacent_bands=1 (:819) deepens the already-cut neighbour rather than splitting, and cfs.py:1200-1219/_verify_decay expects decay_verify_db=6 within 1.5 s (device.yaml:820-821); cfs.py:1160-1163 ABORTs the ring-out when the single band reaches -9 without taming.

Reality: fx_routing_scenes.md §2.3 and §13 items 1/3, scales_params.md §14/§17 say exactly what is claimed (ISO centre list CONFIRMED-by-inference/web only; 0.5 dB step UNCONFIRMED); none of the research describes filter shape, so the bell-filter/band-interaction point rests on engineering common sense, which the brief admits as a source — and it is correct (a 1/3-oct graphic band is a peaking filter; a ring at the 2k/2.5k edge ≈2.24 kHz, or RTA band 68 ≈2.18 kHz which is 0.12 oct off the 2 kHz centre, receives well under the nominal cut; non-'True' GEQ bands interact, TEQ compensates). HANDOVER §4b item 4 even corroborates it on the real desk: a -15 dB PRE cut moved the three RTA bands by only -5.9/-6.0/-3.9 dB, far from the rectangular fake's -15/-15/-15.

No missed fallback: the controller never splits a cut across two neighbours; its only recourse is deepen-then-ABORT (ABORT backs the master off 6 dB, so it is safe). Because VERIFY is closed-loop on the measured band level, the practical cost is an extra -3 dB step (wider tonal hole) or an earlier per-band -9 dB exhaustion/ABORT for between-centre rings, plus verify timing tuned on an optimistic fake — a gig-time efficiency/spurious-abort issue, not a wrong or unsafe write. Low severity as claimed. Offline test as proposed (constant-Q bell per GEQ band summed in dB at each RTA centre in FakeDesk._refresh_cuts/SyntheticRta.set_geq_gain, ring at ~2.24 kHz) would fail today's exact-6.0 assertions and exercise the deepen/abort path.

> **Verifier 2: PARTIAL (low)** — The encoded assumption is real: FakeDesk._refresh_cuts (src/x32mcp/fakedesk.py:1124-1129) maps every RTA band to the nearest ISO GEQ centre in log-f and applies the full -(gain+master) dB there via SyntheticRta.attenuate, i.e. a rectangular, non-interacting 1/3-octave brick per GEQ band; SyntheticRta.set_geq_gain (src/x32mcp/meters.py:661-667) does the same (+-1/6 oct, full depth) and the ring model subtracts the full cut from loop gain each frame (meters.py:716-718). tests/test_meters.py:436-448 and tests/integration/test_fakedesk.py:419-427 assert exactly that (cuts == {69:3,70:3,71:3}; ring at 2400 Hz gets the full 6 dB of the 2.5 kHz band). NotchController.band_for_freq (src/x32mcp/detector.py:538-543) picks the single nearest GEQ band and _apply steps it -3 toward -9 (detector.py:566-567; device.yaml notch_step_db/notch_max_db), never splitting across neighbours. docs/research/fx_routing_scenes.md 2.3/13 only establishes the ISO centre list (by inference) and says nothing about filter shape, so the fake cannot be REFUTED as 'matching research'; physically a GEQ band is a bell, and with a 1/3-oct RBJ peaking model a ring 1/6 oct off-centre receives ~50% of the nominal cut (-1.5 of -3, -4.5 of -9), ~73% at the median RTA-to-ISO offset of 0.078 oct (30% of RTA bands in 200 Hz-10 kHz sit >0.12 oct from the nearest centre). HANDOVER 4b item 4 (a -15 dB PRE cut read only -5.9/-6.0/-3.9 dB on the real RTA) is weak corroboration that 1:1 coupling is optimistic, though confounded by music content.

However, arguing from the gig consequence, the code's correctness does not actually depend on full-depth coupling: it depends only on 'a cut at the nearest band monotonically reduces loop gain at the ring; if the ring does not decay, deepen; if -9 dB is reached, ABORT and back the master off 6 dB' - which a bell filter honours. In ring_out mode the master rises 1 dB per 1.5 s dwell, so a fresh ring's loop-gain excess is ~<=1 dB and even the worst-case 1.5 dB effective cut breaks the loop; re-rings at higher master are merged into the same band (merge_adjacent_bands 1) and deepened. The real-desk M7 session (HANDOVER 4b) is direct evidence: two genuine rings were each killed by a single nearest-band notch. Nearest-1/3-octave-slider, -3 dB at a time, is the industry-standard manual GEQ ring-out procedure; not splitting across two sliders is the accepted limitation of a 31-band GEQ, not a defect. The 'verify thresholds are optimistic' part is speculative: on a real desk post-notch decay is governed by the acoustic loop break and /-prefs/rta/decay, not by rectangular-vs-bell coupling. Net effect at a gig: occasionally one extra -3 dB step (a slightly deeper hole at one ISO band) and ~3-4 dB less achievable gain-before-feedback for a ring that sits exactly between centres before the session ends via the designed ABORT/backoff path. No wrong write, no safety exposure, no tool reporting false state. The proposed offline test (bell-shaped coupling in the fake) is a worthwhile fidelity improvement, but 'controller should split the cut across both neighbours' is a feature request. Confirmed as an unphysical fixture assumption; downgraded to PARTIAL because the claimed dependency and failure are largely mitigated by design and contradicted in part by real-desk results. Severity low stands.

## E111. [none] (transport-connection, partial) Datagrams arrive in the order they were sent (the shim states 'unordered delivery is not simulated'), so the last ramp step sent is the value the desk ends on and RTA frames are consumed in emission order.

**Encoded at:** tests/conftest.py:6-7 (explicitly not simulated); FakeDesk latency_ms is a constant delay (fakedesk.py:778-781) so order is preserved; ramp tests in tests/integration/test_desk.py assert the final desk value equals the target.

**Code depends on it at:** src/x32mcp/desk.py:26-27 docstring ('after_db is what the desk received. No sleep after the final step') and the ramp writer (steps ~15 ms apart, fire-and-forget); src/x32mcp/connection.py:782-795 FIFO matching; meters.LiveMeters/detector consume frames without a sequence number (the /meters blob has none, transport.md §8).

**Reality:** UDP gives no ordering guarantee; Wi-Fi link-layer retransmission and AP power-save buffering reorder datagrams sent milliseconds apart. transport.md §8: meter blobs carry no timestamp/sequence, so the receiver cannot re-order.

**On a real desk:** A 300 ms fade to −10 dB ends at the penultimate step (e.g. −10.7) when the last two datagrams swap; the tool reports after_db −10.0. A swapped pair of RTA frames shows the detector a spurious dip-then-jump in a ring's growth (minor with the current 3-frame growth estimate).

**Offline test:** Add a jitter fault to FakeDesk (per-datagram random inbound delay 0-30 ms) and assert a ramp's final read-back equals the target — fails unless the final step is re-sent after a settle or verified by read-back; assert detector output is invariant to adjacent-frame swaps.

> **Verifier 1: PARTIAL (low)** — Code/test citations check out: tests/conftest.py:6-7 literally says "unordered delivery is not simulated"; fakedesk.py:772-781 `_send` applies a constant `call_later(latency_ms)` so order is always preserved; tests/integration/test_desk.py:167 asserts the FakeDesk's final fader == target and :171 asserts the 15 pushed steps are monotonic (`pushes == sorted(pushes, reverse=True)`); desk.py:25-26 docstring says "after_db is what the desk received. No sleep after the final step"; desk.py:922-946 `_run_ramp` fires `conn.set` per step with no read-back, and `_move_level` (desk.py:969-974) reports `after_db = after` (the intended target) whenever not superseded; connection.py:520-530 `set` is fire-and-forget; connection.py:782-795 `_pop_waiter` is FIFO per key; transport.md §8's verbatim blob layout (<int1><int2><floats>) indeed has no sequence/timestamp field. No fallback was missed: nothing re-reads the fader after a ramp (server.py:892 set_fader just returns desk.set_level's dict).

Why only PARTIAL: (1) the 'reality' mechanism is overstated — 802.11 ARQ (stop-and-wait, or block-ack with a receiver reorder buffer) and AP power-save queues deliver MSDUs in order within a traffic class, and a single-hop Ethernet path does not reorder; the ramp's last two datagrams are 20 ms apart (policy.ramp_step_ms=20, 300 ms → 15 steps; the finding says ~15 ms), so a swap needs >20 ms differential delay on one 5-tuple — implausible at FOH. No research or HANDOVER text reports reordering; transport.md §2/§10 document silent LOSS over Wi-Fi, not reordering, and 'so the receiver cannot re-order' is the claimant's inference, not §8's words. (2) The concrete failure described (desk parks at the penultimate step while the tool reports the target) is real for this code path but is far more likely to be caused by the final datagram being dropped (transport.md §2) than swapped — i.e. the genuine baked-in assumption is 'every fire-and-forget step arrives', of which ordering is a minor sub-case. (3) The RTA adjacent-frame-swap effect is self-admittedly negligible, and FIFO reply matching only mis-pairs replies for the same address, which carry the same parameter anyway. HANDOVER §4a shows ramps landing on target on the real desk (−22.8 → −15.0 confirmed). Net: assumption genuinely encoded and depended on, practical impact near-nil; low severity is correct.

> **Verifier 2: REFUTED (none)** — The claimed mechanism (adjacent-datagram reordering within a single unicast UDP flow, 20 ms apart, PC-to-desk) does not occur on the documented deployment and is close to non-existent even on the secondary Wi-Fi host, and the consequence if it did occur is sub-dB and self-correcting. (1) Deployment: README.md:289 requires 'a PC on the same LAN as the desk'; HANDOVER.md:118-120/README.md:874 show the M5 desk was on a wired cable (cable-pull test), PC 192.168.1.231 / desk 192.168.1.139 on one subnet. A single switch hop does not reorder frames of one flow; arrival order == send order, which is exactly what FakeDesk's constant latency_ms (fakedesk.py:771-781) and the conftest shim model. (2) Research: docs/research/transport.md §2 (line 149) and §10 (line 649) document the real Wi-Fi hazard as silent datagram LOSS under /node//showdump bursts, never reordering; nothing in docs/research or HANDOVER §4a/§4b reports or predicts out-of-order delivery. The 802.11 MAC delivers MSDUs in order per station/access-category (stop-and-wait ARQ on legacy, block-ack reorder buffer on n/ac; power-save buffers are FIFO), so 'link-layer retransmission reorders datagrams sent milliseconds apart' is not how a single STA-AP flow behaves; reordering needs multipath/ECMP or mixed QoS classes, neither present here. (3) Spacing: consecutive ramp writes are >= ramp_step_ms = 20 ms apart (desk.py:935-945 sleeps to the wall-clock slot; policy token bucket also caps 50 writes/s), and /meters frames are 50 ms apart, so a swap needs >20 ms (>50 ms for RTA) of differential one-way delay between two back-to-back packets of the same flow on a LAN. (4) Consequence even if it happened: the desk lands one step short — for the default 300 ms/15-step ramp of a 10 dB move that is ~0.7 dB, inaudible on a wedge and invisible to the audience; conn.set invalidates the cache (connection.py:528, desk.py:883) so the next get_channel shows the true value; no safety/CFS write is driven by after_db. The RTA half is self-described as 'minor' and the detector's 3-frame growth estimate absorbs a single adjacent swap. (5) HANDOVER.md:99-100,110 verified ramps on the real desk land on target (−22.8 → −15.0, 15 s full travel) with no ordering anomaly. The genuinely credible adjacent hazard — the fire-and-forget FINAL step being LOST over Wi-Fi so after_db over-reports — is a different finding (loss, which FakeDesk.drop_next only applies to replies, not inbound SETs) and is not what is claimed here. Net: the FakeDesk's in-order behaviour matches what the research and the real-desk session say the target network does; this would not bite at a gig.

The analyser lands on strip /fxrtn/0n — the strip the operator named — whatever its L/R identity. The token is a private intermediary the desk never sees (device.yaml:140 'Tokens are ours (desk prints the int)').

(fxrtn n -> 65+n)' (fx_routing_scenes.md:398), the scene-safe bitmap b8-15 FX1L-4R (line 516/534), Xisel/Xinsel, and the real scene naming /fxrtn/01 'Reverb L'. The one residual UNCONFIRMED item (scales_params.md §11.3 line 726-729 / §17 line 1044-1047) is narrowly the sub-order of the /ch/NN/config/source int block 41..48, which the research itself calls 'UNCONFIRMED-but-standard' and 'the only consistent expansion' of the PDF text. Code touching that (desk.py:731 get_routing label, patches.py:243-279 normalise_source, set_source) would at worst mislabel/mis-set a channel deliberately sourced from an FX-return tap — a routing almost nobody uses live (FX returns have their own strips), with no safety, feedback-suppression or gain consequence, and no evidence anywhere that Behringer uses a different FX order in that one enum than in the six others. Nobody rings out an FX return (no mic, no loop), and even if they pointed the RTA at one the index would be right. The finding also concedes no offline test exists. FakeDesk behaviour matches what docs/research say the real desk does; this is theoretical, not a gig-biting assumption.

The claimant themselves rated it low and 'low risk for GEQ use'. With the research VERIFIED, a real-desk scene line, and a live FW-4.x Main LR run all confirming the 4-char token, this is not an emulator-certified false belief; REFUTED.

That set is not an emulator artefact the FakeDesk merely mirrors: fx_routing_scenes.md §3.2 marks it VERIFIED from four independent sources (X32.c:328 Xisel, X32Fx.h:58 Sinsel printer copy, X32SetScene.h:5097, and DOC p.25/33/35/36/38 — explicitly including /main/st and /main/m), the node printer for every insert block including main/st is `Sinsel[sel]` (X32.c:3959, §3.3), and transport.md §6.3 carries a verbatim real-desk node line `/ch/01/insert ON PRE FX4L`. The wire value is an int 0..22, so there is no representable 'pair token'. §13 item 6 (UNCONFIRMED) asks whether the R side auto-inserts and whether sel reads back FXnL — any answer the enum can encode (FXnL or FXnR) is still a 4-char token that _insert_side maps to (slot, side); it cannot produce (None, None). Decisively, HANDOVER §4b (M7, X32 Rack FW 4.13) ran CFS² end-to-end with 'GEQ2 already in FX slot 5, inserted on Main LR' and applied notches: cfs.py:885 asserts ins.fx_slot is not None from validate_ringout_eqs → Desk._insert_dict → _insert_side on the real /main/st/insert read-back, so the exact 'paired insert on a stereo strip' case the finding worries about was parsed correctly on real hardware. The FakeDesk therefore prints exactly what research and the real desk print; the parse covers every documented token (checked all 23: FXnL→(n,'A'), FXnR→(n,'B'), OFF/AUXk→(None,None); case-insensitive via nodes.py:329-338; an out-of-range OSC int raises ScaleError rather than yielding a bogus token). The secondary point about per-effect A/B par splits is unreachable: provision.py:399-402 rejects any slot whose type is not in fx_types_dual/stereo before _side_gains runs, and set_geq_band (desk.py:1417-1424) does the same. What remains — 'an undocumented future token would be treated as no insert instead of a distinct validation reason' — is defensive hardening with no documented or observed trigger, and even then the overwrite is a Tier-2 plan the operator must confirm (it would show a type_load GEQ→GEQ2 on the slot). The genuinely risky Main-LR behaviour (a dual GEQ2 via FX5L notching only side A while the desk feeds R through side B) is a different finding already filed in this slice (commit 25babfb 'Main LR consuming both FX sides'), not this one.

## E114. [none] (scales-nodes, refuted) GEQ band gains live on a 0.5 dB grid (61 values), so reads may be snapped to it and writes quantised to it.

**Encoded at:** device.yaml:72 `geq_gain: {kind: lin, lo: -15, hi: 15, steps: 61}  # 0.5 dB grid inferred (§14)`; src/x32mcp/scales.py:376-382 `Scale.to_value` for `lin` with steps SNAPS the raw read to the grid before converting; FakeDesk `_quantise_raw` stores GEQ pars on the same 61-grid (fakedesk.py docstring :15-16), so a value between grid points can never be observed in tests.

**Code depends on it at:** desk.get_fx/GEQ band decode and CfsManager.gains bookkeeping (cfs.py:413 `validate_notch(self.gains.get(band, 0.0), gain_db)` cuts-only/≤ current comparison), provision 'existing cuts' reporting, diff of `/fx/N/par` tokens.

**Reality:** scales_params.md §14 and fx_routing_scenes.md §2.2: 'Step size: not documented in DOC (linf [-15…+15] with no step) … UNCONFIRMED … the wire value is a continuous float and the desk will quantize on display'; the 0.5 figure is inferred from one FW 2.7 scene. Another OSC client (Mixing Station, TheatreMix) or a future CFS step can leave a band at −2.75; the desk may store it exactly.

**On a real desk:** A band at −2.75 dB reads as −3.0 (or −2.5): existing-cut reports and the notch ledger are off by ≤0.25 dB and validate_notch's 'new ≤ current' can accept a 0.25 dB boost relative to the true value. Small, bounded — but it is a read path that silently rewrites what the desk said.

**Offline test:** Let FakeDesk store GEQ pars unquantised (flag), set par/27 raw to (15-2.75)/30, assert get_fx reports −2.75 (fails: −3.0/−2.5). Fix: do not snap on READ for scales whose grid is UNCONFIRMED (keep quantisation on write only), or mark `steps` as write-only in the yaml.

> **Verifier 1: REFUTED (none)** — The research citations check out (fx_routing_scenes.md §2.2 line 237: "Step size: not documented in DOC ... UNCONFIRMED ... the wire value is a continuous float and the desk will quantize on display"; scales_params.md §14 line ~933: "Step size therefore appears to be 0.5 dB (61 values) — UNCONFIRMED"), device.yaml:72 does declare `geq_gain: {kind: lin, lo: -15, hi: 15, steps: 61}` with the "0.5 dB grid inferred" comment, Scale.to_value for `lin` with steps does snap (scales.py:375-381; verified: Scale(lin,-15,15,61).to_value((15-2.75)/30) == -2.5), and FakeDesk._quantise_raw does force GEQ pars onto the 61-grid (fakedesk.py:623-627). So the fixture/fake half of the claim is accurate.

But the claimed product dependency is wrong. The GEQ READ path never goes through Scale.to_value: device.yaml:288-291 declares `/fx/N/par/NN` as `{osc: f, scale: raw01, node: token}` (raw01 = lin 0..1 with NO steps, device.yaml:91), nodes.py:325-326 returns `token` node text verbatim, and Desk.get_fx (desk.py:669-699) builds `bands_db` via `_geq_token_db` (desk.py:702-709), which is a plain `float(str(tok))` of the desk's own one-decimal dB text — no grid snap. provision._side_gains (provision.py:328-338) and CFS `existing` (cfs.py:886) and hence `_DeskGeqWriter.gains`/validate_notch (cfs.py:413, policy.py:405-422) all consume those verbatim floats. The only call to `_geq_scale.to_value` in product code is desk.py:1431, decoding the tool's OWN just-quantised write raw for the event payload (self-consistent by construction). Therefore on a real desk a band left at -2.75 dB by another client would be reported as whatever the desk prints (-2.8 or -2.7 at one decimal, per §2.2), not -3.0/-2.5; the ≤0.25 dB ledger error and the 'validate_notch accepts a 0.25 dB boost' scenario do not arise from this code (residual error ≤0.05 dB comes from the desk's own text formatting, and CFS only ever writes -3/-6/-9 which are on any plausible grid). Write-side quantisation to 0.5 dB remains, which the claimant themselves deems acceptable and which set_geq_band discloses in its returned gain_db. Net: the assumption is encoded in yaml/Scale/FakeDesk, but no read path depends on it, so the stated failure is not real. Per the skeptical default (dependent-code citation wrong), REFUTED.

> **Verifier 2: REFUTED (none)** — The finding's central mechanism does not exist in the production read path, and its residual is below the desk's own display resolution.

1. The read path does NOT snap GEQ gains to the 0.5 dB grid. Desk.get_fx (src/x32mcp/desk.py:669-699) reads the `/node fx/N/par` TEXT reply and decodes each band with `_geq_token_db` (desk.py:701-709), which is a plain `float(tok)` — no Scale.to_value, no grid. That is the only source of GEQ gains for provision.geq_status (provision.py:336) and hence for CFS `existing` (cfs.py:886) → NotchController/_DeskGeqWriter.gains (cfs.py:407/413). The `geq_gain` scale's `to_value` is used in exactly one production place: desk.py:1431, to echo the value just written (already on-grid because to_raw quantised it). So 'reads may be snapped to it' is false for every path the finding names as dependent.

2. Empirical probe (worktree $SP/worktrees/verifier-geq-grid, commit d1000c3, tests/integration/test_verifier_geq_offgrid.py): bypassing FakeDesk._quantise_raw and storing par/27 raw = (15−2.75)/30 exactly, `desk.get_fx(5)` reports −2.8 — the desk's own one-decimal print parsed verbatim — not the −3.0/−2.5 the finding predicts. The 0.05 dB residual is the real desk's node-text resolution (fx_routing_scenes.md §2.2 'the desk prints dB with one decimal'), not a code artefact; the tool reports exactly what the desk says.

3. The premise that a real desk would even hold −2.75 is itself against the verified general rule: scales_params.md §0 (VERIFIED, PDF p.12-13) 'The console only stores a finite set of floats per parameter; any float sent is rounded to the nearest known value. Reading back returns the stored value.' The only real-console GEQ data (scene1.scn:1900/1902, §14) shows every value a multiple of 0.5. The 'continuous float, quantize on display' line in fx_routing_scenes.md §2.2 is the researcher's UNCONFIRMED speculation, weaker than §0.

4. Even granting the hypothetical, no wrong/unsafe write results: NotchController._apply (detector.py:568-569) only ever writes current+(−3) or the −9 clamp; with current known to ≤0.05 dB (or even ≤0.25 dB), every write is still a strict cut relative to truth, and all writes (−3/−6/−9, 0.5-grid via to_raw) land on any plausible desk grid (0.5 or 0.25). validate_notch can never be induced to pass a boost by this. Consequence at a gig: nobody hears anything; existing-cut report is off by at most the desk's own print rounding.

FakeDesk quantising GEQ stores to 61 steps (fakedesk.py:624-625) matches the best available real-desk evidence and the verified store-quantisation behaviour; it is not encoding a belief reality contradicts. Not a finding.

Dropped ~9 weaker items: (a) set_main_fader's signature default db=-90 means a call that omits db proposes 'Main LR -> -oo' (gated by the confirmation summary); (b) restore_snapshot's confirmation preview shows only 15 of N changes, so a whole-desk restore that releases /config/mute groups or rewrites /config/routing can hide that below the fold; (c) EQ gain ±15 dB (the desk's full range) is Tier 1 on mains/wedge buses while a 0.5 dB main fader move is Tier 2 — a +15 dB 3 kHz bell on a wedge is a more reliable feedback trigger than any fader move (likely covered by the redteam-clamps agent); (d) adjust_fader from -oo writes -87 dB and reports success ('-oo -> -87.0') — inaudible 'done'; (e) RATE_LIMITED raised mid-ramp (e.g. while a restore runs) leaves the fader at an intermediate value without the RAMP_ABORTED 'read it back' hint; (f) _show_control() treats a timed-out GET as SCENES (desk.py:1256 'sc is None or'), so on the CUES desk one lost datagram re-enables the meaningless 2 s pointer poll; (g) X32 Rack/Compact/Producer have 16 local preamps and Core none (scales_params §12.2) — set_phantom(16..31) writes to head amps with no hardware and reports on:true; (h) meters.md §5.3: what /meters/15 carries while X32-Edit (which Jim keeps open) shows a channel PEQ or FX GEQ page is UNCONFIRMED — the analyser CFS listens to may silently switch source mid-session (meters/CFS slice); (i) the FakeDesk deliberately decouples bus fader/mute from ring growth (fakedesk.py docstring), so no test can express 'raising the master causes the ring' or 'muting/panic stops it' — ring_out's causal premise is only ever simulated by test-injected rings (CFS slice). Lead's leads, status in this slice: decay/peakhold — FakeDesk stores them, SyntheticRta ignores them and autogain/det/gain too (finding 9); CUES vs SCENES — handled in desk.py for current/recall but snapshot scene labels and 'verified' semantics still assume SCENES (finding 7); slash()/send_raw publish no write event — Desk.restore and panic invalidate explicitly afterwards, so within this slice the gap only bites other modules' slash/send_raw users. Commit in the worktree was made with -c commit.gpgsign=false because the SSH signing agent refuses in this sandbox; nothing was pushed.

Run the probes with: $SP/runtests.sh $SP/worktrees/assumptions-cfs-detector-fixtures tests/integration/test_assumptions_cfs.py tests/test_assumptions_detector.py  -> '12 failed, 1 passed' at HEAD a408a2a (the pass is the 60 dB/s boundary case). Findings 1,2,3,4,9,10,11 and the detector half of 5 are demonstrated by those failing tests; 6 (ballistics), 7 (bus link), 8 (RTA gain), 12, 13 are by code reading + research and each names the FakeDesk change that would make them testable. Note on finding 5's integration probe: SyntheticRta's cut term is only physical when loop_period_s = tau (level += (excess-cut)*period/tau); the stock FakeDesk leaves loop_period_s = 50 ms, i.e. it models a 17 m loop for cuts while tests inject 15-20 dB/s growth (= 0.75-1 dB excess at that tau) - so the fake is pessimistic for fast rings (a -3 dB cut cannot tame >= 60 dB/s there) and the 'one -3 dB step kills any ring < 60 dB/s' sentence in meters.py:577 is a statement about tau=50 ms, not about desks. Dropped as weaker/duplicative (7): (a) cooldown_s=1.0 sets the watch-mode deepening cadence, so a ring that survives -3 dB (excess > 3 dB => >100 dB/s) howls at the limiter for 1 s per step, 3 s to reach -9 - fixtures never survive the first cut; (b) FX-slot type change / insert bypass mid-session (same 'desk frozen at preflight' class as 1-2: notch writes then fail NOT_A_GEQ or go to a bypassed GEQ and ring_out ABORTs after VERIFY); (c) cfs.py:1186 comment calls `after` a read-back but desk.py returns the requested value - the 'master clamped' branch only ever sees the local policy clamp (folded into 1); (d) persistence/override/verify expressed in frames not seconds (folded into 14); (e) the fake applies 100% of a GEQ cut to the displayed band while the desk showed ~40% (folded into 13; nothing but VERIFY-via-loop-break depends on it); (f) SyntheticRta's base spectrum is ~30 dB hotter at LF (-19 dBFS at 39 Hz) than the M7 studio WITH music (-51.7), which would drive any max-band calibration to ~-8 dB (folded into 11); (g) NTP/sleep-wake wall-clock steps (folded into 14). Calibration status discrepancy worth flagging to the lead: HANDOVER/commit 60b86d5 say arm-time calibration was backed out, but _calibrate_floor is live in cfs.py:824-890 and enabled by device.yaml floor_margin_db: 8; it is merely unreachable on the real arming path (finding 11), which is also the likely root of REVIEW_BRIEF §4's confusion. Commits in the worktree were made with `git -c commit.gpgsign=false` because the SSH signing agent refuses in this sandbox; nothing was pushed and <repo> was not modified.
